“对了，毒雾纪的毒雾是怎么消失的？我听到过好多个版本，不知道你们这边是怎么说的。”

村长没有怀疑，笑着说道：“是的，关于毒雾消失这件事确实有很多个版本说法，每个还都不一样。不过毒雾纪距离我们现在的新生纪已经过了两百多年，那时留存下来的记录也不多，我们现在人推测不出真实原因也很正常。”

“按照我们村的说法，毒雾是在活尸消失后的某一天突然消失的。我们这里的人都说是那位大祭司献祭自身才让毒雾消失，但外面人最常见的说法则说毒雾是被自然净化掉的。”

商非凡和村长又聊了一会儿，他故意引着村长说话，期间还承诺村长会做一件比镰刀更有效率的收割工具。

村长特别高兴和期待。他觉得自己说得并不是什么秘密，只当平时和游商侃大山，和商非凡聊得特别好。

商非凡则从村长的聊天中，摸出了一点游戏世界隐藏的大背景。

现在是新生纪，往前推似乎还有四个纪元，分别是毒雾纪、战毁纪、大战纪、大繁华纪。

在大繁华纪之前是不是还有其他纪元，他暂时没打探到，也不好打探。

大繁华纪维持的时间非常长，现在留下的知识、遗迹等全都是那时候留下。

之后就发生了长达一百年的大战，因为大战彻底毁灭了兽人世界，那在历史中不算长的一段时间就被单独拎出来算作大战纪。

当大型战争结束，兽人世界就进入了战毁纪，那时的兽人们顾不上重新建设家园，他们还在和敌人持续不断地进行小型战斗。

战毁纪持续了三百多年，兽人世界混乱不堪，也导致大繁华纪遗留下来的知识和物品被进一步摧毁。

直到一场蔓延整个世界的毒雾突然降临。

毒雾笼罩整个兽人世界长达近两百年，那时的兽人们只能躲进地下、躲进山洞才能勉强活下来。

但也有一些兽人适应了毒雾的毒性，甚至后来生育的孩子天生就自带抗毒性。

可天残也增加了。

原本兽人生育的天残幼崽只是极少数，可毒雾纪中和毒雾纪过后，天残幼崽逐渐增多。

当时的兽人认为天残是不祥的象征、是祸乱的开端，发现天残幼崽九成会直接杀死，剩下的一成一多半会被抛弃，只有极少数才会被父母保护。

村长说到这里就咬牙切齿，对正常兽人带着一点固执的仇恨和反感。

“现在都新生纪两百多年了，还是有不少老古董会把天残幼崽当做不祥！但好在能接受天残幼崽的父母也越来越多，他们就算不想留下天残幼崽，也不会直接杀了，一般都是托人或自己亲自把天残幼崽送来类似我们这样的天残村。”

“有的父母亲人还有点良心，会支付这类收容天残幼崽的村子一些养育费，但大多数都是丢下就走。”

村长看向商非凡，感叹：“你运气还算不错，能在外面健康长这么大。”

商非凡看到村长的目光才想起来他现在的模样也是天残。

进而他就想到这个天残村的村长和村民能这么容易让他进入村子，还跟他侃大山，恐怕不止是因为他会修理东西，更大原因应该是因为看到他没尾巴？

The village chief waved his hand, "I don't know either. Legend has it that before the Heaven-Defying High Priestess could finish her words, she vanished. Some say too much time has passed, and the original words weren't passed down accurately. Later generations made up quite a few prophecies based on what she supposedly said, but in our Heaven-Defying Valley, we have records left behind by the First Chieftain. He recorded the High Priestess's exact words and explicitly noted that she hadn't finished speaking. That's why our people have never believed those fake prophecies."

The village chief even chuckled at Shang Feifan, "You've lived out in the outside world—you must have heard plenty of similar prophecies, right?"

Shang Feifan hadn't heard any, but he couldn't deny it outright, so he just nodded vaguely.

The village chief continued, "Even though the High Priestess didn't finish her words, we can all guess it couldn't have been anything good."

"So that's why you're all so wary of the living corpses walking out of that temple? But how do you even know those beastmen coming out are living corpses and not normal beastmen?"

"Because the records state that the only things that emerge from that temple are living corpses!" the village chief blurted out.

Shang Feifan really wanted to take a look at those records, so he cautiously probed about them.

Without a shred of tact, the village chief flatly refused, "Those records left by the First Chieftain can only be viewed by the village priest and the village chief."

The village chief chuckled again, "Actually, there's nothing classified in there, nor does it involve treasures or ancient ruins. If it did, our village wouldn't be living in such poverty. We don't let outsiders see them simply because they were written by the First Chieftain. Out of respect, we prefer not to show them to outsiders. You can understand that, right?"

Shang Feifan indicated that he understood.

"Right, how did the toxic mists of the Miasma Era disappear? I've heard quite a few versions of the story. I wonder what the tale is around here."

The village chief didn't harbor any suspicions and smiled as he said, "Ah, yes, there are indeed many different versions about the disappearance of the toxic mists, and every single one is different. But more than two hundred years have passed since the Miasma Era gave way to the New Era. With so few surviving records from back then, it's only natural that people today can't figure out the true cause."

"According to our village's tradition, the toxic mists vanished suddenly one day after the living corpses disappeared. The people here all claim that the High Priestess sacrificed herself to make the mists dissipate, while the most common story in the outside world is that the mists were naturally purified."

Shang Feifan chatted with the village chief a bit longer, intentionally steering the conversation while promising to build the chief a harvesting tool far more efficient than a sickle.

The village chief was exceptionally delighted and full of anticipation. Feeling that he wasn't divulging any state secrets and merely shooting the breeze with a traveling merchant as usual, he hit it off wonderfully with Shang Feifan.

From the village chief's chatter, Shang Feifan managed to piece together a bit of the hidden grand backdrop of this game world.

It was currently the New Era. Pushing backward in time, there appeared to be four preceding epochs: the Miasma Era, the War-Ravage Era, the Great War Era, and the Grand Prosperity Era.

Whether there were other epochs before the Grand Prosperity Era, he hadn't managed to find out yet, nor was it easy to pry into.

The Grand Prosperity Era had lasted for a tremendously long time; all the knowledge, ruins, and artifacts remaining today were left over from that period.

Afterward came a century-long grand war. Because the war completely devastated the beastman world, that relatively short span of history was singled out and designated as the Great War Era.

When the massive war concluded, the beastman world entered the War-Ravage Era. The beastmen of that time had no leisure to rebuild their homes; they were still locked in continuous, small-scale skirmishes with their enemies.

The War-Ravage Era lasted for over three hundred years, plunging the beastman world into absolute chaos and leading to the further destruction of knowledge and items inherited from the Grand Prosperity Era.

Until a world-spanning wave of toxic mists suddenly descended.

The mists shrouded the entire beastman world for nearly two hundred years. The beastmen of that era could only survive by retreating underground or hiding in mountain caves.

Yet, some beastmen adapted to the toxicity of the mists, and the children born to them later even possessed innate resistance to the poison.

However, the number of Heaven-Defying ones—those born with physical abnormalities—also surged.

Originally, deformed newborns among the beastmen were exceedingly rare. But during and after the Miasma Era, these infants gradually increased in number.

The beastmen of that time viewed physical abnormalities as symbols of inauspiciousness and the harbingers of disaster. Nine out of ten times, they would kill such newborns outright; of the remaining tenth, well over half would be abandoned, and only a tiny fraction would be protected by their parents.

At this point, the village chief grit his teeth, harboring a stubborn, residual hatred and resentment toward normal beastmen.

"Even though it's been more than two hundred years into the New Era, there are still plenty of old fossils who treat deformed infants as bad omens! Fortunately, the number of parents willing to accept them is growing. Even if they don't want to keep a disabled child themselves, they won't kill them outright; instead, they usually entrust them to others or personally bring them to Heaven-Defying villages like ours."

"Some parents and relatives still have a sliver of conscience and pay these child-rearing villages some upbringing fees, but the majority simply drop them off and leave."

The village chief looked at Shang Feifan and sighed, "You're actually quite lucky to have grown up healthy in the outside world."

Only upon seeing the chief's gaze did Shang Feifan remember that his current appearance in this world was also that of a Heaven-Defying one.

This led him to realize that the reason the village chief and villagers had so easily let him into the village and chatted with him wasn't just because he knew how to fix things—the bigger reason was probably because they saw he didn't have a tail?

chunks.chineseText:
第15章 日常

天黑前，商非凡利用长镰刀做了个掠子。

为了展示掠子的功效，商非凡带着掠子和村长来到村里的麦地。

这时节正是麦子成熟的时候，莫约山谷那一带已经收过麦子，但天残谷这边则是刚开始收。

在一片金黄的麦地里，商非凡展示了掠子的用法。

正在田地里忙活的兽人看到，纷纷围拢过来。

看到掠子大片大片割下麦子，一个个都想试试手。

掠子使用时需要一点技巧，但只要有力气、愿意学，多试几次就能上手。

十来个兽人排队试用掠子，只要是能上手的，试用了都说好。

没有用掠子的兽人眼馋，追着村长问，能不能给他们也做一个。

商非凡大方地表示，他可以教大家怎么制作，这东西的制作方法并不难，重点就在于那把长镰刀。

村里那么长的镰刀不多，村长临时调配过来，打算先做几个掠子给大家紧急割麦用。

商非凡就在田埂边坐下，一边制作掠子，一边跟大家说明掠子怎么做。

村里负责制作工具的兽人和几个手巧的就在一边跟着学。

大家一边制作掠子，一边说说笑笑，一时气氛极好。

阿呆寸步不离商非凡，就在他脚边跟来跟去，还会帮忙叨材料给他。

有兽人开玩笑：“阿呆这么亲近你，要么你就把他带走吧。”

“喂！”有人捣说话的兽人。

说话的兽人干咳，忙说：“我不是非要让你收-养他，我就是随便说说。我们村的孩子，外面人轻易带不走，我也就是见你人挺不错，也是天残……”

说话的兽人大概觉得自己越说越错，说到后来就尴尬地笑起来。

商非凡手上动作不停，“没事，我懂。只是我生计不定，需要到处跑，有时候吃了上顿也不知道下顿在哪。阿呆很好，带走他，我怕自己养不好。”

阿呆仰头看着他。

商非凡腾出一只手揉揉他的方脑袋。

村长妻子给商非凡送来晚餐，这次不仅有死面饼，还有一大块新鲜的烤肉和半瓦罐蔬菜汤。

商非凡在田埂边的水沟里洗了洗手，把烤肉撕下一小块，又把面饼撕碎泡在汤里，分给阿呆。

阿呆埋头就吃。

村长妻子轻哎，“这孩子有饭吃，我正准备带他回去。”

商非凡摆手表示没事。

学做掠子的兽人看天色不早，也都回家吃饭。

走之前，帮着商非凡把用具和材料都收拾干净，一起抬回村长家的谷仓。

在村里负责打铁的兽人还招呼商非凡：“诺曼兄弟，明天早上你去我那儿看看？你不是想要收集矿石吗，我那儿有一些，你可以看看有没有你想要的。”

打长镰刀不难，但打铁的兽人怕自己弄错尺寸和模样，希望做模子的时候，商非凡能帮忙确定。

“好啊。”商非凡一口答应。

今天他靠给村里兽人制作连枷和掠子，从两个游戏系统那里分别赚到十五铜达铢和两个贡献点。

就是十五铜达铢需要到玩家营地的杂货铺领取，无法直接给到他手上。

商非凡：玩游戏竟然没有空间背包，差评！

有村里兽人帮忙收拾，商非凡吃完饭啥都不用干，在村里略微走了走消食，阿呆就跟在他脚边。

商非凡看阿呆脏得不成样子，他自己忙了一天也想冲个澡，问了村里兽人在哪里洗澡后，抓起阿呆一起去了村东头的池塘。

给村里做了更好用的工具，村里人现在看他不但不警惕，还很亲热，不但愿意回答他的问题，还会主动跟他搭话。

池塘连接着活水，流淌进村里田地沟渠。

傍晚，不少忙完回来的兽人都在池塘里清洗身体，顺便洗衣服。洗好的兽人大多只穿着一条短裤，手里拿着洗好的衣服回家。

有不少小兽人跳进池子里玩耍。

女兽人不在这儿洗澡，她们另外有自己的地方。小孩子不分男女，七八岁以下两边随便跑。

阿呆似乎不爱洗澡，不愿进水池。

商非凡不惯着他，把他丢进水池就一阵搓揉。

阿呆发出喵嗷喵嗷叫声，还会用小爪子拍打。

其他兽人看了哈哈笑：“这些小东西都不太爱洗澡，喊他们洗澡就跟要他们命似的。”

“也有特别喜欢泡水的，成天泡在水池里不愿意出来。”

商非凡笑：“天性。”

“也是啊。你们那里不排斥天残吗？如果有天残去你们那里做工，他们愿意要么？”有兽人试探地问。

商非凡回忆，因为没有特别留意，他也不知道莫约镇的天残多不多，只能含糊说：“哪里都差不多。”

几个兽人叹息，聊起等农忙结束就去附近挖遗迹的事。

有人借了类似肥皂的块状物给商非凡。

商非凡道谢，给不爱洗澡的阿呆打上肥皂，随口问：“附近还能挖到东西吗？”

阿呆不挣扎了，乖乖待在老商的手掌心，任他搓揉。

借肥皂的兽人也随口回：“往下深挖总还是能挖到一点，反正冬天闲着也没事干，我们出去找活也不容易，如果能挖到一点大繁华纪的东西，就算残破的，也能卖给游商换点物资。”

“除了你们，还有人去挖遗迹里的东西吗？”

“有啊，我们这儿附近有不少村镇，大家农忙过后没事都会提着锄头去挖遗迹，算是我们这儿的普遍活动。你要是没事，也可以跟着过去挖挖看，不过你要是冲着有大收获，那还不如继续到处跑给人修理东西。”

商非凡点点头，见阿呆脏得连泡沫都打不出来，给他冲洗干净，又打了一遍肥皂。

这次总算能搓出泡沫。

阿呆身上不再油腻泛黑，但毛发摸到手上特别干涩。洗完澡，还掉了不少毛，身上看起来更秃。

商非凡在阿呆身上发现不少伤口和已经痊愈的疤痕。

旁边的兽人看到，习以为常地说：“都这样，小崽子欺负起人有时候比大人还狠。有父母照顾的还好一些。没父母照顾的，都是这么磕磕绊绊长大。不过小时候挨揍多了，长大至少知道怎么保命。村里幼崽都被教训过，不准弄出人命、不准致残。”

“弱肉强食。我们是天残，本来就不容易在这世界活下去，如果连同类的欺负都挨不住，也学不会抗争，那还不如早点死掉。”

话语说得冷漠，但周围兽人却纷纷点头，说就是这么个理，他们都是这么被教育长大。

商非凡没说什么，一个地方有一个地方的习俗，就算是现实世界管理不错的福利院，也有受宠爱的、强大的、被欺负的。

天残村愿意收留被人抛弃的孩子，愿意挤出原本就不太丰富的食物去养育不是自己的血脉，已经比一般兽人好得多。

他们恐怕连自己的孩子都是放养式，别人的孩子更不可能去精心养育。

被洗干净的阿呆也并不可爱，因为毛发稀疏，反而看着更怪异，甚至是丑陋，抬着方脑袋就那么呆愣愣地看着商非凡。

“叮铃铃！”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 15: Daily Life

Before dark, Shang Feifan used the long sickle to construct a cradle scythe.

To demonstrate its effectiveness, Shang Feifan brought the cradle scythe and the village chief to the village's wheat fields.

This season was precisely when the wheat ripened. The Moyue Valley region had already harvested its wheat, but the Heaven-Defying Valley was just beginning.

Amidst a sea of golden wheat, Shang Feifan demonstrated how to use the cradle scythe.

The beastmen busy working in the fields immediately crowded around to watch.

Seeing the cradle scythe slice down vast swaths of wheat in one go, every single one of them itched to try it out.

Operating the cradle scythe required a bit of technique, but as long as one had strength and a willingness to learn, a few attempts were enough to get the hang of it.

A dozen or so beastmen lined up to test out the tool, and anyone who managed to get the hang of it praised its efficiency.

The beastmen who hadn't gotten a turn looked on with envy, pestering the village chief to ask if he could make one for them as well.

Shang Feifan generously offered to teach everyone how to make it; the fabrication method wasn't difficult, with the key component being the long sickle itself.

Long sickles were scarce in the village, but the village chief temporarily pooled them together, planning to make a few cradle scythes immediately so everyone could harvest the wheat in a hurry.

Shang Feifan sat down on the ridge of the field, crafting the cradle scythes while explaining the manufacturing process to everyone.

The village's resident tool-making beastmen and a few dexterous hands followed along by his side, learning as he went.

As everyone worked on making the tools amidst laughter and chatter, the atmosphere for a time became exceptionally warm and harmonious.

Ah Dai stuck to Shang Feifan like a shadow, following him back and forth around his feet, even helping to fetch and pass materials to him.

A beastman joked, "Ah Dai is so attached to you—why don't you just take him with you?"

"Hey!" Someone nudged the speaking beastman.

The beastman gave a dry cough and hurriedly explained, "I didn't mean you *have* to adopt him; I was just casually talking. The children of our village aren't easily taken away by outsiders. It's just that I see you're a really good person, and you're also Heaven-Defying..."

Realizing perhaps that the more he spoke, the worse it sounded, the beastman ended up chuckling awkwardly.

Shang Feifan didn't stop his hands. "It's fine, I understand. It's just that my livelihood is unsettled, and I need to travel everywhere. Sometimes I eat this meal without knowing where the next one is coming from. Ah Dai is a good kid, but if I take him with me, I'm afraid I won't be able to raise him properly."

Ah Dai looked up at him.

Shang Feifan freed a hand to rub the boy's square head.

The village chief's wife brought Shang Feifan his dinner. This time, there wasn't just unleavened flatbread, but also a large piece of fresh roast meat and half an earthen jar of vegetable soup.

Shang Feifan washed his hands in the irrigation ditch by the field ridge, tore a small piece off the roast meat, and broke the flatbread into pieces to soak in the soup, dividing it for Ah Dai.

Ah Dai buried his head and began to wolf it down.

The village chief's wife let out a soft "Oh," saying, "The child has his meal now; I was just about to take him back."

Shang Feifan waved a hand to indicate it was no trouble.

Seeing that it was getting late, the beastmen learning how to make the cradle scythes also headed home for dinner.

Before leaving, they helped Shang Feifan clean up all the tools and materials, carrying them back together to the granary at the village chief's house.

The village blacksmith even called out to Shang Feifan, "Brother Norman, why don't you come over to my place tomorrow morning? Didn't you want to collect ores? I have some over there—you can take a look and see if there's anything you want."

Forging a long sickle wasn't difficult, but the blacksmith was afraid he'd mess up the dimensions and shape, and hoped Shang Feifan could help verify them when making the molds.

"Alright," Shang Feifan agreed without hesitation.

Today, by crafting flails and cradle scythes for the village beastmen, he had earned fifteen copper Da-coins and two contribution points from the two game systems respectively.

The only catch was that the fifteen copper Da-coins had to be collected at the player camp's grocery store; they couldn't be deposited directly into his hands.

Shang Feifan thought: *To think a game doesn't even have an inventory space—one-star review!*

With the village beastmen helping to clean up, Shang Feifan didn't have to lift a finger after finishing his meal. He took a brief stroll around the village to aid digestion, with Ah Dai trotting closely at his heels.

Noticing how utterly filthy Ah Dai was—and feeling sticky and grimy himself after a full day of hard work—Shang Feifan asked where the villagers bathed, then grabbed Ah Dai and headed straight for the pond at the east end of the village.

Having built vastly superior tools for them, the villagers not only lacked any wariness toward him but were now extremely warm. Not only were they willing to answer his questions, but they also took the initiative to strike up conversations.

The pond was fed by running water that flowed into the ditches of the village fields.

At dusk, quite a few beastmen returning from a hard day's work were scrubbing themselves in the pond and washing their clothes by the side. Most of the washed beastmen wore only a pair of shorts, carrying their clean garments back home in their hands.

Numerous little beastmen were splashing and playing in the water.

Female beastmen did not bathe here; they had their own separate area. As for the children, gender didn't matter below the age of seven or eight, and they ran freely between both sides.

Ah Dai seemed to dislike bathing and resisted entering the pool.

Shang Feifan wasn't about to indulge him, picking the boy up and tossing him right into the water for a vigorous scrub.

Ah Dai let out mewling, meowing cries, swatting weakly with his little paws.

The other beastmen looked on and laughed heartily. "These little runts all hate taking baths; telling them to wash up is like asking for their lives."

"Some of them are obsessed with soaking, though—staying in the pool all day long and refusing to come out."

Shang Feifan smiled, "It's in their nature."

"True enough. Don't people in your parts discriminate against the Heaven-Defying? If a Heaven-Defying person goes to your place to look for work, are they willing to hire them?" a beastman asked probingly.

Recalling his experiences, and realizing he hadn't paid much attention, Shang Feifan had no idea whether Moyue Town had many Heaven-Defying individuals, so he could only reply vaguely, "Everywhere is pretty much the same."

Several beastmen sighed, chatting about how they planned to dig around nearby ruins once the farming busy season ended.

Someone lent Shang Feifan a bar of soap-like block.

Shang Feifan expressed his thanks, lathered up the bath-hating Ah Dai with soap, and casually asked, "Can you still dig up useful things around here?"

Ah Dai stopped struggling, behaving obediently in Old Shang's palm as he let himself be scrubbed.

The beastman who lent the soap casually replied, "If you dig deep enough, you can still unearth a bit of stuff. Besides, winter is idle anyway, and it's not easy for us to find outside labor. If we can dig up even a little something from the Grand Prosperity Era—even if it's broken and ruined—we can sell it to traveling merchants in exchange for supplies."

"Besides you guys, do other people go digging for stuff in the ruins?"

"Of course. There are quite a few villages and towns around our parts; after the farming rush, everyone grabs a hoe and heads out to dig ruins. It's pretty much a common pastime around here. If you're bored, you can tag along and dig around too. But if you're holding out for a big haul, you'd be better off continuing to travel around and fix things for people."

Shang Feifan nodded. Seeing that Ah Dai was so filthy that suds wouldn't even form, he rinsed him off and lathered him with soap a second time.

This time, he finally managed to work up a lather.

Ah Dai's body was no longer greasy and blackened, but his fur felt exceptionally coarse and dry to the touch. After the bath, a significant amount of fur shed off, making him look even more bald and patchy.

Shang Feifan discovered numerous wounds and healed scars scattered across Ah Dai's body.

Seeing this, the beastman nearby remarked with jaded familiarity, "They're all like that. When little runts bully people, they can sometimes be even more vicious than adults. Those with parents to look after them have it a bit better. The ones without parents grow up through all these bumps and bruises. Still, after taking enough beatings in childhood, at least they know how to preserve their lives when they grow up. The little ones in the village are taught strict rules: no taking lives, and no permanent mutilation."

"The law of the jungle. We are Heaven-Defying; it's already hard enough to survive in this world. If we can't even withstand bullying from our own kind and can't learn to fight back, we might as well just die early."

The words sounded cold and heartless, but the surrounding beastmen nodded one after another, agreeing that this was simply how things were and that they had all been raised with this mindset.

Shang Feifan didn't say anything. Every place had its own customs; even in the relatively well-managed welfare institutions of the real world, there were favorites, the strong, and the bullied.

The Heaven-Defying village's willingness to take in abandoned children and scrape together their already meager food to raise blood that wasn't their own already made them far better than average beastmen.

They probably practiced a hands-off, free-range approach even with their own children; it was practically impossible for them to meticulously nurture other people's kids.

Even after being washed clean, Ah Dai didn't look cute. Because of his sparse fur, he looked even more bizarre—almost ugly—as he lifted his square head and stared blankly at Shang Feifan.

*Jingle bell!*

chunks.chineseText:
商非凡脑子里传来传统的电话铃声，这是外面在提醒他，让他赶紧下线。

商非凡跟周围兽人打了招呼，从池子里出来，穿着湿淋淋的背心短裤，把阿呆放到肩膀上，回去谷仓休息。

阿呆似乎第一次待在这么高的地方，之前眯着的眼睛睁大，居高临下地俯视周围几个小兽人。

几个同样没有父母的小兽人看到阿呆被成年兽人放在肩膀上，露出羡慕妒忌的目光。

阿呆咧嘴，像是在笑。

但等其他兽人看过来，他又变得呆愣愣的。

谷仓里铺好了一张临时的床铺，就是用干草铺在地上，上面什么都没有，旁边放了一壶清水。

商非凡躺到干草堆上，戳戳阿呆的脑门：“你想待着就待着，我睡着了喊不醒，有什么事就去找村长。记住了？”

阿呆点头。

商非凡觉得这小东西一点都不呆。

商非凡闭上眼睛立刻陷入深眠。

阿呆先原地不动了片刻，过了一会儿伸出小爪子试探地拍了拍睡着的大人，见商非凡没反应，他就一点点往商非凡身上挪动，顺着他的胳膊爬到他的肩颈处，身体团成一小团，也闭眼睡了。

中途，谷仓大门被推开一条缝，村长在外面往里看了看。

干草堆上，那名外来的兽人睡得很熟，谷仓里还有一道更弱更轻的呼吸声。

村长静悄悄地合上谷仓大门，放心回去睡了。

现实世界，商非凡睁开眼睛就看到了伏向军的大脸。

“到了？”

“到了。马上就要下船，你准备一下。”

商非凡摘下游戏头盔，麻利起身。

长时间玩游戏，他的身体竟然并不僵硬，只随便活动几下就像是做了半个小时的热身运动。

商非凡记下这个变化。

两人不能走正常途径下船，得先偷偷潜入水中，再游到附近已经准备好的渔船，从渔船返回陆地。

因为他的护照上只有入境记录，没有出境记录。

上陆的大陆并不是他们的母国。

商非凡在这边买了一个带葡萄园的中型农庄，明面上他在这个国家是一名拥有五千亩田地、不算太起眼的投资型农场主。

就是投资不太顺利，农庄买下后就年年亏损。

这也是大多数外国人在该洲买农庄牧场会遇到的事情，光是处理农庄牧场里的兔子狐狸就能让他们头疼死。加上其他频出的环境问题，比如龙卷风、干旱之类，都会造成绝收，导致投资大、收获小，很多人都是表面光鲜辛苦经营。

因为知道农场经营不易，当地政府对这些农场主盯得就不算严，只要他们愿意交足税、对农场土地不搞大肆破坏，其他就不会多管。

农庄距离海岸线不太远，直线距离只有十公里不到，开车十分钟就能到。

渔船上负责接应他的人都是他的老兄弟，在这边开了一家渔业公司。

从渔船下来，再转乘一辆给农庄送海鲜的小货车。

十分钟后，商非凡和伏向军安全回到了农庄。

农庄一间隐秘地下室内已经准备好了全套检测仪器，还有两名负责跟商非凡解说仪器使用说明的特派员。

为了不引起注意，没有专家跟着过来，但两人上游戏时的身体数据会实时传回研究所，由那边的专家分析，有任何情况都会随时通知两人。

仪器和专家都由组织提供，另外还有丰厚的试验费。

回到自己地盘，商非凡和伏向军明显放松了许多。

到这里，他们就算彻底安全了。

“老大，你以后……”

“我退役了，现在就是一个农场主。”商非凡正对游戏上头，而且他确实想要好好休息一段时间，不想工作。

再说农场的活就不是活了？

伏向军心想一个在各个地方都挂名的军火商想要金盆洗手哪有那么容易，但他也觉得他老大应该休息一段时间，就说：“那我也在你农场里留一段时间吧。”

“你打过报告了？”

“嗯，他们对这个突然出现的全息游戏也特别感兴趣，目前能查出来的国内玩家不多，找普通人，也怕他们胡思乱想，就先只是暗中监控。现在已经安排人想法申请游戏资格，在其他人申请到游戏资格前，就我们两个。”

商非凡对此无所谓，只要报酬到位，什么都好说。伏向军想要留下来也不难，他在他农场原本就有身份，学化肥制作的研究生，毕业后就来投奔他，已经在农场待了五六年。
chunks.englishText:
The traditional sound of a telephone ring echoed in Shang Feifan's mind—this was the reminder from the outside world telling him to log off immediately.

Shang Feifan exchanged parting words with the surrounding beastmen, climbed out of the pond, and wearing his wet undershirt and shorts, hoisted Ah Dai onto his shoulder before heading back to the granary to rest.

Ah Dai seemed to be experiencing being at such a height for the very first time. His previously squinted eyes widened as he looked down condescendingly at several little beastmen nearby.

Those few young beastmen, who likewise lacked parents, revealed looks of envy and jealousy upon seeing Ah Dai perched on the shoulder of an adult beastman.

Ah Dai grinned, as if smiling.

Yet the moment other beastmen looked over, he reverted to his dull, blank expression.

A temporary bed had been made inside the granary by spreading dry straw across the ground, with nothing else on top except for a pitcher of clean water placed nearby.

Shang Feifan lay down on the hay pile and poked Ah Dai on the forehead. "Stay if you want to. Once I fall asleep, you won't be able to wake me up—if anything comes up, go find the village chief. Got it?"

Ah Dai nodded.

Shang Feifan decided this little creature wasn't dull at all.

Closing his eyes, Shang Feifan instantly plunged into a deep sleep.

Ah Dai remained motionless in place for a moment. After a little while, he extended a tiny paw to test-pat the sleeping adult. Seeing that Shang Feifan didn't react, he inched bit by bit over Shang Feifan's body, climbed up his arm to his shoulder and neck, curled his body into a small ball, and closed his eyes to sleep as well.

Halfway through, the granary doors were pushed open a crack, and the village chief peeked inside from the outside.

On the bed of straw, the foreign beastman was sleeping soundly, accompanied by an even softer, lighter sound of breathing within the granary.

Quietly, the village chief closed the granary doors and went back to sleep with peace of mind.

In the real world, the moment Shang Feifan opened his eyes, he was greeted by Fu Xiangjun's oversized face.

"We here?"

"We're here. We'll be disembarking shortly, get ready."

Shang Feifan took off his gaming helmet and briskly stood up.

Despite playing games for such a long time, his body didn't feel stiff at all; a mere stretch and a few casual movements made it feel as though he had just completed half an hour of warm-up exercises.

Shang Feifan mentally noted this physical change.

The two of them couldn't disembark through normal channels; they had to covertly slip into the water first, swim over to a pre-arranged fishing boat nearby, and return to land from there.

After all, his passport only contained an entry record, with no departure record.

The continent they were stepping onto was not their home country.

Here, Shang Feifan had purchased a medium-sized farm with a vineyard. On paper, he was an unremarkable, investment-oriented farm owner in this country with five thousand mu of land.

It was just that his investment wasn't going particularly smoothly; ever since purchasing the farm, it had operated at a loss year after year.

This was a common predicament faced by most foreigners buying ranches and farms in this region. Merely dealing with the rabbits and foxes plaguing the property was enough to give them splitting headaches, not to mention other frequent environmental problems like tornadoes and droughts that could trigger total crop failures—resulting in heavy investments for meager yields, forcing many to maintain a glamorous facade while struggling through arduous management.

Knowing that farm operations were no easy task, the local government kept a fairly relaxed eye on these landowners. As long as they paid their taxes in full and didn't wreak massive destruction on the farmland, everything else was left alone.

The farm wasn't far from the coastline, with a straight-line distance of less than ten kilometers—a mere ten-minute drive away.

The people responsible for picking them up on the fishing boat were his old brothers-in-arms, who ran a fishery company around these parts.

Stepping off the fishing boat, they transferred to a small delivery truck that supplied seafood to the farm.

Ten minutes later, Shang Feifan and Fu Xiangjun safely returned to the farm.

A set of comprehensive testing equipment had already been prepared in a concealed basement on the farm, accompanied by two special agents tasked with explaining the instrument operating instructions to Shang Feifan.

To avoid drawing attention, no experts had accompanied them here, but the physical data of the two men while playing the game would be transmitted back to the research institute in real-time for analysis by experts stationed there, and any anomalies would be reported to them immediately.

Both the equipment and the experts were provided by the organization, complemented by generous experimental stipends.

Back on familiar turf, Shang Feifan and Fu Xiangjun visibly relaxed a great deal.

At this point, they could consider themselves completely safe.

"Boss, what are you going to do in the future..."

"I've retired. Right now, I'm just a farm owner." Shang Feifan was thoroughly hooked on the game, and furthermore, he genuinely wanted to take a nice, long break and avoid working.

Besides, wasn't managing a farm considered work?

*As if an arms dealer whose name is flagged all over the place can wash his hands of it that easily,* Fu Xiangjun thought to himself. Still, he felt his boss deserved a break, so he said, "Then I'll stay at your farm for a while too."

"Did you file your report?"

"Yeah. They're extremely interested in this sudden holographic game, and right now there aren't many domestic players they've managed to trace. They're worried that recruiting ordinary people might make their imaginations run wild, so for now, they're only keeping it under covert surveillance. They've already arranged for people to apply for game qualifications. Until others secure access, it's just the two of us."

Shang Feifan didn't mind either way; as long as the pay was right, anything was fine. Having Fu Xiangjun stay behind wasn't difficult; he already had a pre-established cover identity on the farm as a graduate student specializing in fertilizer production who had come to work under him after graduation, having already spent five or six years on the farm.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第16章 开启铁匠职业 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第16章 开启铁匠职业

次日天没亮，商非凡就睁开眼睛爬起来。

一团软软暖暖的小东西从他脖子处咕噜噜滚到草堆上。

商非凡揉揉脖子，没管那小东西，径直打开谷仓大门，先活动身体，再一路小跑到沟渠边操水洗漱。

阿呆爬起来跟在他后面追。

村里没有水井，用水全都是用沟渠里引来的活水。

商非凡漱口时发现这里的水有点苦涩，还有点怪味，就像是放多了漂白-粉。

莫约镇那边的水质要比这里的好，至少没有怪味。

阿呆跑得一头撞在他小腿上。

商非凡扭头，弹弹他的方额头：“你老跟着我做什么？我不是你爸，不会管你吃喝，更不会养你。”

阿呆昂起头，小小声说：“我能找到能吃的果子和野菜，你带我走，不亏。”

商非凡似笑非笑：“就知道你不是一个真正的小呆子。为什么要装呆？为什么非要和我离开？村里待你不好吗？”

阿呆：“聪明健壮的孩子会被领养走。”

“那不好吗？你不就想要离开村子？”

阿呆摇头，“每年来领养的兽人都是同一批人。”

商非凡转过身，半蹲在地上看小崽：“你是说村里在进行人口买卖？会把健壮的幼崽卖出去？”

阿呆没说是也没说不是，只说：“每年秋收完没多久他们就会来，今年能合格的幼崽不多，有时候数量不够，他们也会带上体弱的。”

商非凡发现阿呆不但不呆，兴许智商还很高，至少这么点大的幼崽就跟四五岁的小孩子一样，压根什么都不懂，阿呆却观察仔细、说话也条理分明，还知道自救。

“我九岁了。因为又弱又呆，他们才看不上我。但一直这样，我就是对村里没用的废物，等他们想起我的年龄，我很有可能还是会被带走。”

“你有九岁？”商非凡惊讶，他怎么看阿呆都像是刚出生没几个月，身体又瘦又小，比三四个月的猫仔大不了多少。

阿呆：“我也不知道为什么我长不大，大人说我可能天生就体弱，长不大就会死。”

“那你又怎么知道我不会出卖你，不会在路上把你杀了卖了？”商非凡说话时特别观察周围，也有早起的兽人，但都离得远。

阿呆：“我原本还想找那些活尸带我走，但他们身上有一股很奇怪的味道。”

商非凡懂了，小家伙不挑人，只要对方肯带他离开。也许小家伙还有自保的办法。

带不带小家伙离开的问题先放一边，他比较感兴趣的是：“什么味道？”

阿呆不知道该怎么形容：“就是……死掉的尸体的味道。”

他见过死掉的猎物和牲畜，也见过村里死去的兽人，活的生命死后就会发出一股奇怪的味道，哪怕是刚死，和腐烂味不同，很轻微，他能闻到。

商非凡：“其他兽人也能闻出来？”

阿呆再次摇头，“我不知道，没有问过，但村里人都不喜欢那些活尸。”

“那些活尸身上都有那股味道？”

“嗯！”阿呆重重点头。

商非凡想问我身上就没有那股味道吗，但这样问太直接，他就换了个方式：“你是不是看到我从神殿那边走过来，但没有闻到我身上有怪味，所以才敢接近我？”

阿呆又点头，但紧接着就说：“你是活尸也没关系，只要你肯带我离开。”

商非凡发现了自己和玩家的第二个不同，他不但有两套游戏系统，很可能他的这具游戏身体材料或者说制作方法也有点不一样。

“你知道村里人把那些健壮的幼崽卖给了谁，又是做什么用的吗？”

阿呆摇头，他确实不知道。

商非凡总觉得这村子里的兽人不像那种卖孩子的丧天良人渣，也许有人带走健壮的天残小孩另有隐情，但……虽然知道了这么一个也许有问题的秘密，他也并不打算插手，甚至不打算再多询问，他怕系统给他发任务。

换成一般玩家，说不定就兴冲冲去找线索、主动探索有没有做大任务的可能。

但他上游戏是悠闲放松的，现在还背着两套游戏系统，真不想给自己找麻烦。

想了想，商非凡特别没人情味地对小孩说：“我不会收-养你，但我可以把你带到其他兽人的聚集地，你可以看看那里有没有人愿意和你一起生活。如果没有，我也不会继续带着你，你得自己养活自己，懂？”

阿呆严肃脸，点头：“好。只要你肯带我去你的家乡莫约镇，以后不管怎样，我保证不纠缠你。”

商非凡捏捏小东西的后脖颈皮，心想这小家伙真的很聪明，还知道限定一个地点。可能在小家伙的认知里，能让一个天残长大的地方，至少不像其他地方那么危险。

一大一小就这么说定。

天蒙蒙亮，有早起的兽人扛着农具往这边走过来。

阿呆两只小爪子吧唧抱住商非凡的小腿，很大声地喊：“爸爸！”

商非凡也用平常声音无奈地说：“我不是你爸。”

“爸爸！”

“哈哈，被缠上了是吧？没事，把他踢开就好。这些没父母的小崽子都这样，谁对他们好一点，就会缠上去。但你对他们凶一点，他们就不敢再缠了。”走过来的兽人笑着说。

“算了，随他去。”商非凡一脸无奈地站起身，“早，我想去铁匠家里，说好了今天去他那里和他一起打制刀片，请问他家要往哪个方向走？”

兽人很热情地指明方向，告诉商非凡：“铁匠家很好认，他家大门上画着一只大铁锤，一看就知道。”

商非凡把阿呆放到肩头，很顺利地找到了铁匠家。

铁匠看到商非凡如约而至，很高兴，把商非凡迎入隔壁的打铁坊，问他会不会打铁。

商非凡不会单纯打铁，他只会用工业化手段制造出他想要的零配件。

在战区，在他自己的房子里，他准备了或简单或精密的制造小工厂，可以把原始的生铁块制作成他想要的东西。

但他真的没有用过这么原始的炼铁炉去炼化矿石，练出生铁，再把生铁弄成熟铁，再打制成自己想要的东西。

“我和你用的炼制工具不一样。”商非凡委婉地说。

铁匠笑呵呵：“你们大地方用的东西肯定和我的不一样，我这就是自己拼凑出来的。听说外面有那种很高很大的炼铁炉，铁矿石倒进去没一会儿就能自动炼制成熟铁，我这里不行，得一点点来。”

商非凡不想干看着：“我帮你，你说要怎么做，我给你打下手。”

“好啊。”铁匠认定商非凡原本就会打铁，只不过用的手段和工具都比他高明，且商非凡也不会留在村里，也就没有藏私的想法。

叮咚。

脑载系统和笔记本系统同时有了反应。

两个系统给他布置了相同的任务，都是让他帮助铁匠制作掠子刀片，成功就奖励开启铁匠职业技能。

商非凡笑，这就是个意外之喜了。

虽然不是炼金术，但技多不压身，多一个铁匠职业技能也挺好。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 16: Unlocking the Blacksmith Profession (Part 1)

Before dawn the next day, Shang Feifan opened his eyes and scrambled up.

A soft, warm little bundle rolled over from his neck like a roly-poly right onto the straw mat.

Shang Feifan rubbed the back of his neck, ignoring the little creature. He strode over to open the barn doors, stretched his limbs first, and then broke into a jog all the way down to the irrigation ditch to splash water on his face and wash up.

Ah Dai scrambled up and trotted along right behind him, giving chase.

There were no wells in the village; all the water used came from the flowing streams diverted from the ditch.

As Shang Feifan rinsed his mouth, he noticed that the water here tasted slightly bitter with a strange, off taste—resembling water with an overdose of bleaching powder.

The water quality over in Moye Town was much better than this, at least lacking any weird chemical aftertaste.

Ah Dai ran up and bumped his little head right against Shang Feifan's shin.

Shang Feifan turned his head and flicked Ah Dai's square forehead. "Why do you keep following me around? I'm not your dad. I won't worry about feeding you, and I certainly won't raise you."

Ah Dai raised his head and spoke in a tiny, quiet voice, "I can find edible fruits and wild vegetables. If you take me with you, you won't lose out."

Shang Feifan wore a half-amused, half-mocking expression. "I figured you weren't truly a little dull-wit. Why pretend to be slow? Why are you so insistent on leaving with me? Has the village not treated you well?"

Ah Dai replied, "Smart and strong children get adopted and taken away."

"Isn't that a good thing? Don't you want to leave the village?"

Ah Dai shook his head. "Every year, the beastmen who come to adopt are the exact same group of people."

Shang Feifan turned around, half-squatting on the ground to look at the little cub. "Are you saying the village is running some kind of human trafficking operation? They sell off the strong pups?"

Ah Dai neither confirmed nor denied it, merely stating, "They always come shortly after the autumn harvest. The number of qualified pups isn't high each year, and sometimes when the numbers fall short, they take the frail ones along too."

Shang Feifan realized that far from being dull, Ah Dai's intelligence might actually be quite high. At least, while a cub this small should be like a four- or five-year-old child who understood nothing at all, Ah Dai possessed sharp powers of observation, spoke with distinct logic, and even knew how to save himself.

"I'm nine years old. Because I'm weak and slow-witted, they didn't want me. But if things keep going like this, I'm just useless trash to the village. Once they remember my age, there's a strong chance I'll still get hauled away."

"You're nine?" Shang Feifan asked in astonishment. No matter how he looked at Ah Dai, the kid seemed like he had been born just a few months ago—skinny and tiny, barely bigger than a three- or four-month-old kitten.

Ah Dai answered, "I don't know why I can't grow up either. The adults say I might be sickly by nature, and if I don't grow up, I'll die."

"Then how do you know I won't sell you out, or kill and sell you along the road?" As he spoke, Shang Feifan deliberately scanned his surroundings. There were other early-rising beastmen about, but they were all far off.

Ah Dai replied, "I originally thought about finding those living corpses to take me away, but they have a very strange smell on them."

Shang Feifan understood. The little fellow wasn't picky about who he chose, as long as the other party was willing to take him away. Perhaps the little guy even possessed some means of self-preservation.

Putting aside the question of whether or not to take the kid along for the moment, what interested him more was: "What kind of smell?"

Ah Dai didn't know how to describe it. "It's just... the smell of a dead corpse."

He had seen dead prey and livestock, as well as dead beastmen in the village. Once a living lifeform died, it would emit a strange odor—even if it had just passed away. It was different from the smell of rotting flesh; it was very faint, but he could smell it.

Shang Feifan asked, "Can other beastmen smell it too?"

Ah Dai shook his head again. "I don't know. I've never asked, but the people in the village all dislike those living corpses."

"Do all those living corpses carry that smell?"

"Mhm!" Ah Dai nodded heavily.

Shang Feifan wanted to ask if he carried that smell on himself, but asking so directly felt too blunt. Instead, he changed his approach: "Did you see me walk over from the shrine, but notice that I didn't have any weird smell on me, which is why you dared to approach me?"

Ah Dai nodded again, but immediately added, "It doesn't matter if you're a living corpse either, as long as you're willing to take me away."

Shang Feifan discovered the second difference between himself and ordinary players: not only did he possess two game systems, but there was a high likelihood that the material or manufacturing method of his game body was somewhat unique as well.

"Do you know who the villagers sold those strong pups to, and what they're used for?"

Ah Dai shook his head; truly, he didn't know.

Shang Feifan had a lingering feeling that the beastmen in this village didn't look like heartless scumbags who sold children. Perhaps there was an unspoken reason behind someone taking away strong, disabled children, but... even though he had stumbled upon a potentially problematic secret, he had no intention of meddling, nor did he plan to ask any further questions. He was terrified the system would issue him a quest.

An average player might eagerly go hunting for clues, proactively exploring the possibility of triggering a major questline.

However, he logged into the game to relax and unwind. Right now, he was already weighed down by two game systems; he genuinely didn't want to invite trouble upon himself.

After a moment's thought, Shang Feifan said to the child with utter lack of sentimentality, "I won't adopt you, but I can take you to another gathering place of beastmen. You can see if anyone there is willing to live with you. If not, I won't keep dragging you along either—you'll have to support yourself. Understand?"

Ah Dai wore a solemn face and nodded. "Okay. As long as you're willing to take me to your hometown, Moye Town, I promise I won't pester you anymore no matter what happens in the future."

Shang Feifan pinched the loose skin at the back of the little fellow's neck, thinking to himself that this little guy was truly sharp; he even knew how to specify a destination. Perhaps in the little fellow's cognition, a place capable of letting a disabled child grow up at least wasn't as dangerous as other places.

Thus, the adult and the child reached an agreement.

With the sky just turning bright, some early-rising beastmen were walking past carrying farming tools.

Ah Dai clamped his little paws tightly around Shang Feifan's calf and shouted at the top of his lungs, "Daddy!"

Shang Feifan replied in a normal tone, helplessness tinged in his voice, "I'm not your dad."

"Daddy!"

"Haha, you've been latched onto, haven't you? Don't worry, just kick him away. These parentless little brats are all like this; whoever treats them a bit nicely, they'll stick to them. But if you act a bit fierce with them, they won't dare pester you anymore." A passing beastman laughed and said.

"Forget it, let him be." Shang Feifan stood up with an expression of pure resignation. "Morning. I want to head over to the blacksmith's place. We agreed today to go over and forge knife blades together. Could you tell me which direction his house is?"

The beastman enthusiastically pointed out the direction and told Shang Feifan, "The blacksmith's house is very easy to recognize. There's a big iron hammer painted on his front door, you'll know it at a glance."

Shang Feifan hoisted Ah Dai onto his shoulder and successfully located the blacksmith's house.

Seeing Shang Feifan arrive as promised, the blacksmith was overjoyed. He welcomed Shang Feifan into the adjoining smithing workshop and asked if he knew how to blacksmith.

Shang Feifan didn't know traditional blacksmithing; he only knew how to manufacture the precise components he wanted through industrialized methods.

In the war zone, inside his own home, he had prepared simple or sophisticated small manufacturing workshops capable of turning raw pig iron blocks into whatever items he desired.

Yet he truly had never used such primitive smelting furnaces to refine ores, produce pig iron, convert pig iron into wrought iron, and then hammer it into the desired items.

"The smelting tools I use are different from yours," Shang Feifan said tactfully.

The blacksmith laughed heartily. "The things you use in big cities must certainly be different from mine. What I have here is just cobbled together myself. I've heard there are huge, tall smelting furnaces out there where you can dump iron ore in, and it automatically refines into wrought iron in no time. My setup here doesn't work like that; I have to do it bit by bit."

Shang Feifan didn't want to just stand around watching. "I'll help you out. Tell me what needs to be done, and I'll be your assistant."

"Alright." Convinced that Shang Feifan originally knew how to blacksmith—just that his methods and tools were more sophisticated than his own, and knowing Shang Feifan wouldn't stay in the village anyway—the blacksmith harbored no thoughts of hiding his trade secrets.

*Ding-dong.*

Both the brain-link system and the notebook system reacted simultaneously.

The two systems issued him identical quests: both instructed him to help the blacksmith manufacture raider knife blades, with success rewarding him with the unlocked Blacksmith profession skill.

Shang Feifan smiled. This was a pleasant surprise.

While it wasn't alchemy, one could never have too many skills; acquiring an extra Blacksmith profession skill was quite nice.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第16章 开启铁匠职业 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
商非凡确实不会最原始的打铁手法，他有冲床车床，根本不需要自己辛辛苦苦打制，但有经验的人和没有经验的人还是不一样的。

在问清楚铁匠都是用哪些材料来炼制熟铁后，商非凡略微改换了一下配方的材料配比，这次炼制出来的熟铁不但保留了原先的坚硬度，还多了几分柔韧，这也就代表刀锋和刀身都更不容易损坏。

铁匠听商非凡说这个配方可以免费送给他，差点高兴疯，无法报答下恨不得把自己会的全都教给商非凡，还非要把家里储存的矿石送老商一半。

商非凡就在铁匠铺待了一天，中午饭也是在铁匠家吃的。

他也因此顺利完成两个系统的任务，成功开启了铁匠职业技能。

以后他学习铁匠技艺，虽然还是要自己多动手动脑，但系统有辅助加成的效用，可以让他更快地掌握打铁技术，就跟初级骑乘术一样。

换言之，他学习铁匠技能就没有所谓的瓶颈，只要他动手，随着熟练度加成，他可以从初级技能一路往上升。

就是炼合金的方子需要他自己寻找、购买。

不过炼制不同种工具、武器、装备的合金配方，脑载系统的游戏商城里都有，只要舍得花贡献点，就能买得到。

开启铁匠职业技能还有两个好处，那就是对矿石的分辨能力也会随之提高，力气值也会跟着增大。

铁匠技能还附赠两个主动技能，分别是铜皮铁骨和耐灼烧。

总之，这个技能开启还是很划算的，尤其没花一个铜达铢，也没花贡献点！

铁匠看他动作越来越娴熟，也没多想，还以为商非凡原本就擅长打铁，一开始不熟练只是用的工具不习惯。

铁匠婆娘给他们送来饭菜，不算多好，但勉强能让成年兽人吃饱。

阿呆被所有大人忽略，他就窝在打铁坊的角落里，不注意都发现不了他。

商非凡把自己的饭菜分给他，铁匠家这才注意到阿呆。

村长从铁匠那里得知这名外来的天残兽人不仅教他们制作更好用更有效率的新农具，还给了铁匠一个珍贵无比的新打铁配方，对商非凡的印象更是好得不得了。

晚上，村长从家里带了饭菜过来，加上其他两个兽人，和铁匠、商非凡一起吃晚饭。

饭桌上，村长和铁匠不住感谢商非凡。

新农具暂且不说，只那个炼制熟铁的方子就价值千金。

这么一个配方，商非凡如果拿出去卖，能卖不少钱，可他说送就送。

商非凡见气氛正好，“凑巧”阿呆又凑上来抱他腿叫爸爸，就举了举装了蔬菜汤的大碗说：“谢谢你们的照顾，我明天就得离开，家里还等着我回去。”

“是你照顾我们！”村长真心实意地说。

“你放心，村里已经帮你凑了一些盘缠，还有一套换洗衣服和一些干粮之类。武器，铁匠这边的东西你看着拿，只要合手的你都可以带上，我们村不会让你空手上路。东西不多，就是我们一点心意。”

下午铁匠跟他们说了配方的事，村长就召集村里几个骨干商量，给商非凡准备了一包相对于村子来说很丰厚的送行礼。

这会儿，村长就把这个包裹拿给了商非凡。

商非凡没有拒绝，利益要有来有往才能长久，否则谁都会不安心。

“爸爸~不要丢下阿呆……”阿呆眼睛红通通，眼泪鼻涕一起流下来。

“阿呆，一边玩去！这不是你爸，不要纠缠！”身上长鳞片的兽人呵斥。

阿呆紧紧抱着商非凡小腿不放。

商非凡眼中流露出无奈和怜悯，叹了口气，面向村长几人说：“算了，我家也不差他一口吃的，如果你们放心，我就带他回去。”

村长没想到商非凡会愿意带上阿呆，但他和其他村人也听到看到阿呆是怎么纠缠商非凡的，这会儿听到外来兽人心软，也没怎么惊讶。

村长和其他几个兽人互看。

铁匠开口：“如果诺曼兄弟真的不介意多养一个孩子，那就把阿呆带走吧。”

鳞片兽人也跟着点头：“这样。如果以后诺曼兄弟不打算再养阿呆，就麻烦你把他再送回来，你没空，托人带回来也行。”

村长叹气：“你真决定了？阿呆跟正常孩子不一样，他不但不能变身，脑子也不是很好。”

商非凡：“算我和他有缘吧。反正兽人孩子都皮实，他在村里吃百家饭都能长这么大，到我们那里，怎么也不会饿死。”

村长他们就这么同意了，还又给商非凡的包裹里多塞了一些干粮。

商非凡心里越发觉得这里的兽人不像是阿呆说的会卖孩子的类型，但他也不觉得阿呆在说谎，也许有人来带走健壮小兽人另有内情？
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 16: Unlocking the Blacksmith Profession (Part 2)

Shang Feifan indeed did not know the most primitive manual blacksmithing techniques. With punch presses and lathes at his disposal, he had no need to painstakingly hammer things out by hand. However, an experienced person still differed from an inexperienced one.

After clarifying the various materials the blacksmith used to refine wrought iron, Shang Feifan slightly altered the ingredient proportions of the formula. The wrought iron refined this time not only retained its original hardness but also gained a touch of flexibility, which meant both the blade edge and the sword body would be far less prone to damage.

When the blacksmith heard Shang Feifan offer to gift him this formula for free, he was nearly beside himself with joy. Unable to repay the kindness, he wanted nothing more than to teach Shang Feifan everything he knew, and even insisted on giving Old Shang half of the ores stored in his household.

Shang Feifan spent the entire day at the smithy, eating lunch right there at the blacksmith's home.

As a result, he smoothly completed the quests from both systems and successfully unlocked the Blacksmith profession skill.

From then on, while learning blacksmithing techniques would still require him to apply his own manual labor and brainpower, the system provided an auxiliary bonus that allowed him to master smithing technology much faster—just like the Primary Riding skill.

In other words, he would have no bottleneck when learning blacksmithing skills. As long as he got his hands dirty, following the proficiency bonuses, he could climb all the way up from novice skills.

The only catch was that alloy formulas for smelting different tools, weapons, and equipment required him to find and purchase them himself.

However, alloy recipes for refining various tools, weapons, and equipment were available in the brain-link system's game mall; as long as one was willing to spend contribution points, they could buy them.

Unlocking the Blacksmith profession skill came with two additional perks: his ability to distinguish ores would correspondingly improve, and his strength stats would increase as well.

The blacksmith skill also came bundled with two active skills: "Copper Skin and Iron Bones" and "Scorch Resistance."

All in all, unlocking this skill was an absolute bargain—especially since it didn't cost a single copper Dazhu, nor a single contribution point!

Seeing his movements grow increasingly adept, the blacksmith didn't think much of it, assuming Shang Feifan had always excelled at blacksmithing and was merely unaccustomed to the tools at first.

The blacksmith's wife brought them their meals. It wasn't anything lavish, but it was barely enough to fill an adult beastman's stomach.

Ah Dai was ignored by all the adults, curling up quietly in a corner of the smithing workshop where he wouldn't even be noticed unless one paid close attention.

Shang Feifan shared his meal with him, which finally drew the blacksmith household's attention to Ah Dai.

Having learned from the blacksmith that this foreign disabled beastman had not only taught them how to make better, more efficient new farming tools, but had also given the blacksmith a wildly precious new iron-smelting recipe, the village chief's impression of Shang Feifan was exceptionally favorable.

That evening, the village chief brought food from home. Together with two other beastmen, the blacksmith, and Shang Feifan, they sat down for dinner.

At the dinner table, the village chief and the blacksmith showered Shang Feifan with endless gratitude.

Leaving aside the new farming tools for the moment, the wrought iron refining recipe alone was worth a fortune.

If Shang Feifan took such a formula out to sell, he could command a hefty sum, yet he had given it away simply because he wanted to.

Seeing the atmosphere just right—and "coincidentally" having Ah Dai trot over to hug his leg and cry "Daddy"—Shang Feifan raised his large bowl filled with vegetable soup and said, "Thank you for your hospitality. I have to leave tomorrow; people are waiting for me to return home."

"It is you who are taking care of us!" the village chief said with utmost sincerity.

"Rest assured, the village has already pooled together some travel funds for you, along with a change of clothes and some dry rations. As for weapons, feel free to take whatever catches your eye here at the blacksmith's; as long as it's comfortable in your hand, you can take it. Our village won't let you set off empty-handed. It's not much, just a token of our appreciation."

That afternoon, after the blacksmith told them about the recipe, the village chief had gathered several core members of the village to discuss and prepare a farewell package for Shang Feifan that was quite generous by village standards.

Right then, the village chief handed this parcel over to Shang Feifan.

Shang Feifan did not refuse. Benefits required mutual give-and-take to be sustainable; otherwise, no one would feel at ease.

"Daddy~ Don't leave Ah Dai behind..." Ah Dai's eyes were red and swollen, tears and snot streaming down together.

"Ah Dai, go play somewhere else! This isn't your dad, stop pestering him!" a scale-covered beastman scolded.

Ah Dai hugged Shang Feifan's shin tightly and refused to let go.

A look of helplessness and pity crossed Shang Feifan's eyes. He sighed, turned to the village chief and the others, and said, "Forget it. My home isn't short of one extra mouth to feed. If you all trust me, I'll take him back with me."

The village chief hadn't expected Shang Feifan to be willing to take Ah Dai along, but he and the other villagers had seen and heard how Ah Dai clung to Shang Feifan. Hearing the foreign beastman's heart soften now, they weren't too surprised.

The village chief and the other beastmen exchanged glances.

The blacksmith spoke up, "If Brother Norman truly doesn't mind raising another child, then take Ah Dai with you."

The scaled beastman nodded along as well. "That works. If Brother Norman doesn't plan on raising Ah Dai anymore in the future, just trouble yourself to bring him back. If you don't have time, entrusting someone else to bring him back works too."

The village chief sighed. "Are you really sure? Ah Dai is different from normal kids. Not only can he not transform, but his head isn't too bright either."

Shang Feifan replied, "Consider it fate between him and me. Beastman children are tough anyway; he's managed to grow this big eating from a hundred families in the village, so coming with us, he certainly won't starve to death."

The village chief and the others agreed on the spot, and even stuffed a few more dry rations into Shang Feifan's parcel.

Deep down, Shang Feifan felt all the more that the beastmen here didn't seem like the type to sell children as Ah Dai had claimed. Yet he didn't think Ah Dai was lying either—perhaps there was some hidden story behind someone coming to take away strong little beastmen?

chunks.chineseText:
第17章 得到狰爷

在村长等人同意他带走阿呆的同时，两个游戏系统又同时给他发了相同的任务。

但任务内容却略有不同。

脑载系统：【任务十六，接受阿呆委托，带阿呆离开天残谷天残村至莫约山谷镇，成功后奖励贡献点2点。】

笔记本系统：【任务五，请玩家‘你皇退休了’带阿呆离开天残村送至玩家自建一号营地，完成后奖励50铜达铢。】

比起脑载系统的要求，笔记本系统发布的任务难度要低得多。莫约山谷镇距离这里还不知道有多远，但玩家营地应该就在附近。

哦，笔记本系统附带的地图页面还出现了玩家一号营地的坐标，只要按照地图指示走过去都不用担心迷路。

晚饭后，商非凡带着阿呆在村长家的谷仓里再次休息一晚。

次日一大清早，商非凡再次上游戏。

游戏世界的时间和现实世界的时间流速等同，只时差不一样。

天残村这边早上六点，现实世界农场那边则是深夜十二点。

这个时差不算完美，但也勉强能让商非凡两头兼顾。

不过商非凡觉得游戏世界的时间流速还是太慢，跟现实世界一样的话，游戏体验感就差了不少，不知道游戏开发商以后会不会修改这一点。

村长、铁匠和几名兽人来给商非凡送行。

商非凡脚上穿着一双村长妻子送的草鞋，肩膀上背着包裹，一手提着一把造型奇怪的铁铲，跟村长等人告辞。

阿呆就趴在包裹上。

村长摸摸阿呆的方脑袋：“以后你就离开村子了，要好好听你诺曼爸爸的话。如果你在外面待不下去，能找回来就找回来，村里不缺你一口饭吃。”

阿呆呆呆地看着村长。

村长看阿呆这副呆样，很为他的未来担忧。

村长又对商非凡特意叮嘱：“那群活尸在天残谷南面平原建立了营地，好在他们没有堵在谷口，你出去时最好避开他们，那就是一群脑子不正常的。”

商非凡一本正经点头：“好的，我知道了。”

村长又让鳞片兽人给商非凡带路，让他一直把商非凡送出天残谷。

村长和铁匠都很忙，村长得忙着带村人抢收，铁匠得忙着赶紧打制更多的掠子刀片，并带人制作掠子和改良连枷。

农收时分真的是一分都不敢耽误，否则秋后一场雨下来，收成得完蛋大半。

鳞片兽人一口答应，经过一天半相处，鳞片兽人现在看商非凡很顺眼。

出村时，村里的大小兽人基本都已经起床出门干活。

小兽人们看到阿呆趴在那个外来兽人的包裹和肩膀上，一副要跟他离开的模样，都十分好奇。

有小兽人追在几个人后面跑，大声询问阿呆要去哪里。

阿呆突然张口，用很大的声音说：“我要跟爸爸回家了。”

十几个追逐的小兽人呆住，先是不信，等到跟身边大人确定后，几个同样被抛弃的小兽人眼中顿时浮现浓浓的妒忌和羡慕。

阿呆昂起头，看那些经常欺负他的小兽人，整个意气风发。

商非凡虽然没有看到阿呆的表情，但是……人生经验丰富的他抬手摸了摸趴在包裹上的阿呆，跟阿呆说：“儿砸，跟你的朋友们好好道别，等以后有机会，你再带礼物来见他们。”

礼物？做梦！阿呆抬起小爪子，表情特别欠揍地挥了挥。

“哇！我也要爸爸来接我！我爸爸为什么不来接我？”一个小兽人突然嚎啕大哭。

好几个小兽人跟着哭嚎起来。

村里成年兽人就看着笑，劝慰哄孩子的一个没有。

商非凡让阿呆充分体会了凌驾其他小兽人的优越感，这才扛着小家伙离开。

鳞片兽人跟在旁边噗噗笑：“没想到啊，阿呆还有这么一面。”

另一个兽人也笑着说：“再呆也知道好歹啊。何况阿呆只是反应慢一点，也不是真的脑子不行。”

商非凡听出来兽人后面那句话是特意对他说的。这越发让他不觉得这村里的兽人是卖孩子的人渣。

出谷的路比较长，商非凡就引送行的两个兽人跟他聊天，聊这附近的历史，补充自己对这个游戏世界的背景知识。

等快要走到谷外，商非凡看到了一片树林。

“这片树林也算是我们天残谷的防御带之一，里面生活着好几种巨虫，那些巨虫杀伤力很大，不过那些巨虫只吃泥土石头和植物和一些小虫子，只要你不招惹它们，它们也不会理睬兽人。”鳞片兽人跟他介绍。

商非凡跟着两个兽人走进树林，猜测他们应该有办法和树林里的巨虫和谐相处。

鳞片兽人突然说：“你家乡距离我们这里不知道有多远，我建议你最好能弄一只坐骑。”

另一名兽人也说：“我们出远门都会骑上巨虫。但那些巨虫从小和我们一起长大，才会听我们的话。如果你想获得一只巨虫坐骑，得自己想办法获得巨虫同意。”

商非凡觉得这个村子的兽人真的很朴实，这么机密的事也跟他说。

鳞片兽人看看阿呆，再想到商非凡对村子的贡献：“我们可以把你介绍给巨虫，但能不能说服巨虫做你的坐骑，就得看你自己的本事。前提是你决不能伤害它们！”

商非凡神色不动：“谢谢，如果能有一只巨虫坐骑那真是帮上大忙了，请让我试试。”

另一名兽人没反对鳞片兽人的提议，两人带着商非凡就朝巨虫巢穴走去。

不过他们没有深入巢穴，而是发出一种像是虫子振翅的声音，引来两只大虫子。

商非凡抬头看两只巨虫。

这两只巨虫和他在莫约镇看到的巨虫完全不一样，莫约镇的巨虫长得像放大版的天牛，而这两只巨虫长得更像是陆地巨蟹，一双大钳子极具威胁力。它还有一对翅膀，不过翅膀不大，像是断掉一样，没有翅尖。

鳞片兽人上前，轻轻拍抚其中一只巨虫，口中发出声音，就像是在和巨虫交谈。

过了一会儿，长得像巨蟹的巨虫敲击两只大钳子，发出召唤。

第三只和它们体型不相上下的巨蟹虫出现。

鳞片兽人转头看商非凡：“我们和它们商量好了，你可以试试驯服这只巨虫。如果它愿意载你，它会跟着你一起离开。将来如果你对它不好、或者它不再喜欢你，就会自己回来族地。”

商非凡把行李和阿呆暂时交给另外一名兽人，走近巨蟹虫。

他对巨虫不了解，他现在唯一可以依仗的就是刚学会没多久的初级骑乘术。

手掌碰到巨蟹虫的虫腿，一股明悟从脑中升起，他就像是之前骑过巨蟹虫，下意识就知道该如何安抚它，以及该如何和它交流。

商非凡心惊。他是不是太小看那个初级骑乘术？

早知道这个初级骑乘术这么有用……幸好他选择了这个奖励。

商非凡口中模仿出振翅声，又让上下两排牙齿互相敲击，发出特殊频率。

三只巨蟹虫一起看向他。

鳞片兽人和另一名兽人面露惊讶。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 17: Acquiring Lord Zheng (Part 1)

While the village chief and the others agreed to let him take Ah Dai away, both game systems simultaneously issued him identical quests.

However, the quest objectives differed slightly.

Brain-link System: [Quest 16: Accept Ah Dai's commission, take Ah Dai away from the disabled valley's Disabled Village to Moye Valley Town. Reward upon success: 2 contribution points.]

Notebook System: [Quest 5: Player 'Your Emperor Has Retired' is requested to take Ah Dai away from Disabled Village and deliver him to Player's Self-built Camp No. 1. Reward upon completion: 50 copper Dazhus.]

Compared to the brain-link system's requirements, the quest published by the notebook system was vastly lower in difficulty. Moye Valley Town was an unknown distance away, but the player camp should be quite nearby.

Oh, the map page attached to the notebook system also displayed the coordinates of Player Camp No. 1; as long as he walked according to the map's instructions, he wouldn't have to worry about getting lost.

After dinner, Shang Feifan took Ah Dai to rest for another night in the village chief's barn.

Early the next morning, Shang Feifan logged back into the game.

The time flow in the game world ran parallel to the real world, differing only in time zones.

It was six in the morning here in Disabled Village, while back at the farm in the real world, it was midnight.

This time difference wasn't entirely seamless, but it barely allowed Shang Feifan to manage both ends.

Still, Shang Feifan felt the time flow in the game world was a bit too slow; if it matched the real world completely, the gaming immersion would drop significantly. He wondered if the game developers would modify this in the future.

The village chief, the blacksmith, and several beastmen came to see Shang Feifan off.

Shang Feifan wore a pair of straw sandals gifted by the village chief's wife, carried a parcel on his shoulder, and held a strangely shaped iron shovel in one hand as he bid farewell to the village chief and the others.

Ah Dai was perched right atop the bundle.

The village chief patted Ah Dai's square head. "You're leaving the village from now on. You must listen well to your Norman Daddy. If you can't survive out there and manage to find your way back, the village will always have a bowl of rice for you."

Ah Dai stared blankly at the village chief.

Seeing Ah Dai's dull expression, the village chief felt deeply concerned for his future.

The village chief specifically exhorted Shang Feifan, "That group of living corpses has built a camp on the southern plains of the disabled valley. Fortunately, they aren't blocking the valley entrance. When you head out, it's best to avoid them; they're a bunch of screw-loose lunatics."

Shang Feifan nodded with a straight face. "Got it, I understand."

The village chief then had the scaled beastman guide Shang Feifan, escorting him all the way out of the disabled valley.

Both the village chief and the blacksmith were rushed; the village chief had to lead the villagers in harvesting crops, while the blacksmith was busy hammering out more raider knife blades and leading people to make raiders and improved flails.

During harvest season, not even a single minute could be wasted; otherwise, if an autumn rainstorm hit afterward, more than half the crop yield would be ruined.

The scaled beastman readily agreed. After a day and a half of mingling, he now looked upon Shang Feifan quite favorably.

As they left the village, most of the big and small beastmen in the village were already up and out working.

When the young beastmen saw Ah Dai perched on the foreign beastman's bundle and shoulder, looking like he was about to leave with him, they were filled with curiosity.

Several young beastmen chased after the trio, loudly asking where Ah Dai was going.

Ah Dai suddenly opened his mouth and shouted at the top of his lungs, "I'm going home with Daddy!"

The dozen or so chasing young beastmen froze in their tracks. At first they didn't believe it, but after confirming it with the adults beside them, several other abandoned little beasts felt a wave of intense jealousy and envy well up in their eyes.

Ah Dai raised his head, looking at the little beastmen who used to bully him, radiating supreme swagger and pride.

Although Shang Feifan couldn't see Ah Dai's expression, his... life-experienced self reached out to pat Ah Dai perched on the bundle, telling him, "Little buddy, properly bid farewell to your friends. If there's a chance in the future, come back and visit them with gifts."

*Gifts? In your dreams!* Ah Dai raised his little paw and waved it with a hilariously punchable expression.

"Waah! I want Daddy to come pick me up too! Why won't my daddy come pick me up?" One young beastman suddenly wailed aloud.

Several other young beastmen burst into tears and howls along with him.

The adult beastmen in the village merely looked on and laughed; not a single one stepped forward to comfort or coax the children.

Shang Feifan let Ah Dai fully experience the superiority of lording it over the other little beastmen before shouldering the little guy and walking away.

The scaled beastman walked alongside him, chuckling softly. "Who would've thought? Ah Dai has a side like this to him too."

Another beastman chimed in with a smile, "No matter how slow-witted, he still knows what's good for him. Besides, Ah Dai is just a bit slow in his reactions; he's not actually lacking in brains."

Shang Feifan caught that the beastman's latter sentence was spoken specifically for his benefit. This made him even less inclined to believe the village's beastmen were child-selling scum.

The path out of the valley was quite long, so Shang Feifan engaged the two seeing-off beastmen in conversation, asking about the local history to supplement his background knowledge of this game world.

As they neared the exit of the valley, Shang Feifan spotted a stretch of woodland.

"This forest can be considered one of the defensive belts of our Disabled Valley. Several kinds of giant insects live inside. Those giant insects are extremely lethal, but they only eat mud, rocks, plants, and some small bugs. As long as you don't provoke them, they won't bother the beastmen either," the scaled beastman introduced.

Shang Feifan followed the two beastmen into the forest, guessing they must have a way to coexist peacefully with the giant insects within.

The scaled beastman suddenly said, "Who knows how far your hometown is from here? I suggest you'd better acquire a mount."

Another beastman added, "Whenever we go on long journeys, we ride giant insects. But those giant insects only obey us because they grew up alongside us. If you want to get a giant insect mount, you'll have to figure out a way to win its consent yourself."

Shang Feifan felt the beastmen of this village were truly straightforward to share such confidential matters with him.

The scaled beastman glanced at Ah Dai, then thought of Shang Feifan's contributions to the village. "We can introduce you to the giant insects, but whether you can convince one to be your mount depends entirely on your own capability. The prerequisite is that you must never harm them!"

Shang Feifan maintained a calm expression. "Thank you. If I could get a giant insect mount, it would truly be a huge help. Please let me give it a try."

The other beastman didn't oppose the scaled beastman's proposal. The two led Shang Feifan toward the giant insect nest.

However, they didn't venture deep into the nest, instead emitting a sound resembling insect wings vibrating, which summoned two large bugs.

Shang Feifan looked up at the two giant insects.

These two giant insects looked completely different from the ones he had seen in Moye Town. The giant insects in Moye Town resembled oversized longhorn beetles, whereas these two looked much more like land-dwelling giant crabs, armed with a pair of menacing, massive pincers. They also possessed a pair of wings, though the wings were small and looked clipped, missing their tips.

The scaled beastman stepped forward, gently patting one of the giant insects while making sounds with his mouth, as if conversing with the insect.

After a moment, the crab-like giant insect clicked its two giant pincers and let out a summoning call.

A third giant crab-insect, identical in size to the other two, emerged.

The scaled beastman turned to look at Shang Feifan. "We've discussed it with them. You can try taming this giant insect. If it's willing to carry you, it will leave with you. In the future, if you treat it poorly or it no longer likes you, it will return to its homeland on its own."

Shang Feifan temporarily handed his luggage and Ah Dai over to the other beastman and walked closer to the giant crab-insect.

He knew nothing about giant insects. The only thing he could rely on right now was the Primary Riding skill he had just learned not long ago.

The moment his palm brushed against the giant crab-insect's leg, a wave of sudden enlightenment welled up in his mind. It was as if he had ridden giant crab-insects countless times before; instinctively, he knew how to soothe it and how to communicate with it.

Shang Feifan was inwardly startled. Was he underestimating that Primary Riding skill?

If he had known this Primary Riding skill was so useful... Fortunately, he had chosen this reward.

Shang Feifan mimicked the wing-vibrating sound in his mouth, then made his upper and lower rows of teeth click together in a specific rhythm.

All three giant crab-insects turned to look at him simultaneously.

The scaled beastman and the other beastman wore expressions of utter astonishment.

chunks.chineseText:
鳞片兽人直接说：“你知道如何和巨蟹断翅虫交流？难道你们那里也有这种巨虫？”

商非凡模糊说：“我到处跑，以前见过类似的巨虫，跟当地人学会怎么和它们交流，但从没有骑过它们。”

“厉害！”鳞片兽人真心夸赞：“巨虫的交流方法可难了，我们从小学，还不一定学得好。”

另一名兽人喜悦地说：“你能和它们交流就已经成功大半，现在就看你能不能适应它们。”

商非凡拍拍巨蟹虫的长腿，见它不排斥自己，当即翻身一跃。

这次他就有数多了，跳上去的高度恰恰好。

巨蟹断翅虫的背部很宽阔，与其说是骑乘它们，不如说是坐在它们背上。如果技术好，还能直接站在它们身上。

实际上天残村的兽人骑乘巨蟹虫时就是站在巨蟹虫的背部。

鳞片兽人还特意在边上做了个示范，教商非凡怎么骑、怎么操控巨蟹虫。

巨蟹虫讨厌缰绳，好在它背部有两个像是骨刺的突起，可以方便兽人抓住，确保自己不会被甩掉下来。

操纵巨蟹虫得用敲击声。

鳞片兽人用左脚敲击巨蟹虫背部左边，就是让巨蟹虫往左走。反之就是向右。如果敲击中间则是停下。

还有加速、变速、慢跑、慢走等几种示意方法，鳞片兽人全都不藏私地交给商非凡。

商非凡跟着学习，他有初级骑乘术加成，加上鳞片兽人的认真指点，很快就掌握了巨蟹虫的骑乘方法。

商非凡骑着巨蟹虫在树林里跑了两圈。

巨蟹虫身体庞大，但动作极为灵活，并不是真的大螃蟹，也不会一个劲横行，它甚至能跳起来，还跳得很高。在茂密的树林里，上上下下爬来跑去，没有任何阻碍。

这只巨蟹虫似乎也不反感商非凡。

鳞片兽人抓了一大把叶子过来，让商非凡喂给巨蟹虫。

“平时你并不需要怎么喂养它们，它们自己会找吃的。但如果你愿意给它们提供食物，会让它们更高兴。这种叶子是巨蟹虫最喜欢吃的，其他植物的叶子它也不排斥，越鲜嫩越好。你要记得经常抓一些小虫子喂给它，什么小虫子都可以，它们不挑。你还可以给你的巨蟹虫取名字，让它记住你。”

商非凡看看这只面目狰狞的巨蟹断翅虫，一个名字脱口而出：“狰爷！”

鳞片兽人两个没听懂。

商非凡解释说就是特别凶悍特别厉害的大佬的意思。

巨蟹虫似乎对这个名字的发音有点喜欢，在商非凡几次对它喊出“狰爷”后，它的巨钳蹭了蹭商非凡的胳膊，似乎接受了这个名字。

“恭喜你，你获得了这只巨蟹断翅虫的认可。”鳞片兽人脸色变得严肃：“兄弟，你一定要记得，它们已经记住你的味道，如果你敢伤害这只巨蟹虫，甚至杀害它，它的族虫一定会知道并一定会为它复仇，除非你永远不接触巨蟹虫。”

“不要问我它们怎么知道伤害它们族虫的仇家是谁，因为我也不知道，但它们就是知道。”

商非凡握拳点了点心脏部位，算是做出保证。

“兄弟，一路小心！”鳞片兽人和另一名兽人与商非凡郑重道别。

“谢谢你们赠送的坐骑。”商非凡接过行李和阿呆，跳上狰爷的背。

鳞片兽人摇头：“不用道谢，你也帮了我们很多，这是互换。而且狰爷也不是赠送给你，它是自由的，如果它不高兴，随时都会离开你。”

真是一只有个性的虫。商非凡右拳按胸：“有缘再见。”

鳞片兽人再次叮嘱：“千万不要靠近那些活尸的营地，他们就在谷口往南走不到千米的地方。”

商非凡挥手，没有给出明确回应，但两名兽人都以为他记住了。

两名兽人不知道的是，商非凡在骑着巨蟹虫离开谷口树林带后，就往南边拐，正正向他们口中的活尸营地跑去。

隔着老远，商非凡就看到了在营地附近活动的玩家。

几名玩家瞪大了眼睛。

“卧槽！那是什么？”

“怪物？敌袭？野外boss来了？”

“等等！那巨虫上面有人！还有个幼崽！”

“哇，肯定是NPC小boss！那巨虫是坐骑吧？我看到天残村的NPC兽人骑着这种巨虫去打猎。”

“他们不是看我们不顺眼吗？怎么会突然跑来我们这里？”

“说不定是来找我们麻烦的，快去频道喊人！打野外boss了！”

“人家带着幼崽呢，打个屁打！”

“去问问有什么事，说不定就是什么大型任务。”

“走走走！”

一群玩家兴冲冲地奔着商非凡而去。
chunks.englishText:
The scaled orc directly asked, "You know how to communicate with a Giant-Winged Crab-Bug? Could it be that your people also have these giant insects?"

Shang Feifan answered vaguely, "I travel around quite a bit and saw similar giant insects in the past. I learned how to communicate with them from the locals, but I've never ridden one before."

"Impressive!" the scaled orc praised sincerely. "The communication methods for giant insects are extremely difficult. We start learning from childhood, and even then, there's no guarantee we'll master it."

Another orc said happily, "Being able to communicate with them means you've already succeeded more than half the way. Now it just depends on whether you can adapt to them."

Shang Feifan patted the long leg of the Giant Crab-Bug. Seeing that it didn't reject him, he immediately leaped up onto its back.

This time he had a much better sense of scale, and his jumping height was just right.

The back of the Giant-Winged Crab-Bug was very broad. Rather than saying one was riding them, it was more like sitting on their backs. If your skills were good enough, you could even stand directly on them.

In fact, when the orcs of Tiancan Village rode the crab-bugs, they stood right on their backs.

The scaled orc even went out of his way to give a demonstration on the side, teaching Shang Feifan how to ride and control the giant insect.

The crab-bug hated reins, but fortunately, it had two bone-spur-like protrusions on its back that the orcs could grab onto to ensure they wouldn't be thrown off.

Controlling the crab-bug required tapping sounds.

The scaled orc used his left foot to tap the left side of the crab-bug's back, which signaled it to move left. Doing the opposite meant going right. Tapping the middle meant stopping.

There were also several signal methods for accelerating, changing speed, jogging, and walking slowly, all of which the scaled orc taught Shang Feifan without holding anything back.

Shang Feifan followed along, learning as he went. With his beginner riding skill bonus and the scaled orc's earnest guidance, he quickly mastered the method of riding the crab-bug.

Shang Feifan rode the crab-bug around the woods for a couple of laps.

Although the crab-bug possessed a massive body, its movements were exceptionally agile. It wasn't truly a giant crab, nor would it blindly walk sideways; it could even jump, and jumped very high at that. Within the dense forest, it climbed up and down and scurried back and forth without any obstruction.

This particular crab-bug also seemed to feel no aversion toward Shang Feifan.

The scaled orc grabbed a large handful of leaves and had Shang Feifan feed them to the crab-bug.

"Normally, you don't really need to feed them; they'll forage for food on their own. But if you're willing to provide them with food, it will make them even happier. This kind of leaf is the crab-bug's favorite, and it doesn't reject the leaves of other plants either—the fresher and more tender, the better. You must remember to frequently catch some small bugs to feed it; any small bugs will do, as they aren't picky. You can also give your crab-bug a name so that it remembers you."

Shang Feifan looked at this ferocious-looking Giant-Winged Crab-Bug, and a name slipped out of his mouth: "Lord Zheng!"

The two scaled orcs didn't understand.

Shang Feifan explained that it meant an exceptionally fierce and formidable big boss.

The crab-bug seemed to somewhat like the pronunciation of this name. After Shang Feifan shouted "Lord Zheng" to it a few times, its giant pincers rubbed against Shang Feifan's arm, as if it had accepted the name.

"Congratulations, you have gained the recognition of this Giant-Winged Crab-Bug." The scaled orc's expression turned serious. "Brother, you must remember, they have already remembered your scent. If you dare to harm this crab-bug, or even kill it, its clan members will definitely know and will certainly avenge it—unless you never interact with crab-bugs again."

"Don't ask me how they know who the enemy that harmed their clan member is, because I don't know either, but they just know."

Shang Feifan clenched his fist and tapped his chest, considering it a guarantee.

"Brother, take care along the way!" The scaled orc and the other orc bid a solemn farewell to Shang Feifan.

"Thank you for the mount you gifted me." Shang Feifan took his luggage and A-Dai, then jumped onto Lord Zheng's back.

The scaled orc shook his head. "No need to thank us; you helped us a lot too, so it's a fair exchange. Besides, Lord Zheng wasn't gifted to you—it is free. If it becomes unhappy, it will leave you at any time."

What a bug with personality. Shang Feifan pressed his right fist to his chest. "We shall meet again if fate allows."

The scaled orc gave another earnest admonition: "Make sure you don't approach the living corpses' camp. They are located less than a thousand meters south of the valley entrance."

Shang Feifan waved his hand without giving a definite response, but both orcs assumed he had taken it to heart.

What the two orcs didn't know was that after riding the crab-bug out of the forest belt at the valley entrance, Shang Feifan turned south, heading straight for the living corpse camp they had mentioned.

From quite a distance away, Shang Feifan spotted players moving around near the camp.

Several players widened their eyes in shock.

"What the hell! What is that?"

"A monster? Enemy attack? Is a field boss here?"

"Wait! There's someone on top of that giant bug! And there's a child cub too!"

"Whoa, it's definitely an NPC mini-boss! That giant bug must be a mount, right? I saw the NPC orcs from Tiancan Village riding these kinds of giant bugs to go hunting."

"Don't they hate the sight of us? Why would they suddenly run over to our place?"

"Could be here to cause trouble for us! Quick, go shout in the channel! We're fighting a field boss!"

"The guy is carrying a kid, fight my ass!"

"Go ask what's going on; it might just be some large-scale quest."

"Let's go, let's go!"

A crowd of players rushed enthusiastically toward Shang Feifan.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第18章 玩家一号营地 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第18章 玩家一号营地

商非凡靠近营地才发现玩家们正在用大块石砖修建城墙。

“嗨，朋友，你来这里有什么事吗？”

一名脸上有斑马兽纹的瘦高玩家用结结巴巴不太熟练的当地语言大声询问。

老婆是熊猫是第一批玩家，他也是接触NPC并被迅速取了一血的倒霉蛋中的一个，事后分析觉得应该是语言不通造成，之后就开始积极学习当地语言。

但NPC不爱跟他们玩，又没有专门的教材，搞得他们这些玩家想要学习当地语言也比较吃力。

玩游戏还得学习外语这一点让玩家们抱怨无尽，纷纷在论坛留言要求能一键学会兽人语言。

据说游戏策划已经接受大家意见，但不打算修改。

这种劝退行为逼得玩家们对游戏策划破口大骂，但也没有一个人真的因为这点就退游。

商非凡低头：“我来找杂货铺兑换任务奖励。”

“卧槽！”几个听到的玩家大吃一惊。

“他竟然是玩家？！”

“什么时候玩家竟然能有坐骑了？”

“他还有宠物！”

“好丑的宠物。”

“那叫丑吗？那叫丑萌！只要让我能拥有宠物，蟑螂我也愿意要！”

“呕！等等，游戏系统已经开启坐骑和宠物玩法了吗？”

“不知道啊，我笔记本上面没写。不过坐骑和宠物是不是要自己抓？毕竟这是开放型自由全息游戏世界……”

“完全没听到风声。这人太他妈碉了，他谁啊？”

伏向军也在营地门口搬砖顺便等待他老大，见到一只巨虫跑过来，他也好奇地看过去。

这一看，伏向军呆滞了。

他老大是不是很多事没跟他交代？

一群玩家排排站在巨蟹虫前，满眼羡慕妒忌，好几个上手就去摸巨蟹虫。

巨蟹虫大钳子一挥，就要夹人。

商非凡操纵巨蟹虫跳起来，躲开玩家的手，也避免巨蟹虫伤害这些玩家。

“哇，好凶！”

“酷~”

商非凡从巨蟹虫身上跳下来，拍拍巨蟹虫的腿，口中发出振翅声。

巨蟹虫掉身就走，转眼就跑得看不见身影。

“啊，它跑了。”

“临时坐骑？我说兄弟，你是怎么驯服它的？有什么诀窍么？”

“这只方脑袋小兽是什么？跟宠？战宠？哪里能弄到？”

“大佬！求攻略啊！我感觉我们玩的不是一个游戏。”

“哇，这张脸极品，现实中是不是也长得这么帅？”

“兄弟，要不要进帮会？我们‘啥都不干就挣钱’帮会正在征人，看兄弟就是我们正在找的副帮主人选！”

“大佬，加个朋友，以后一起玩啊。”

一堆玩家城墙也不堆了，一窝蜂地跑来围住商非凡，吵吵囔囔，喊什么的都有，还是几国语言交杂。

伏向军跑过来对商非凡挥手。

商非凡看到了，对老伏打了个手势。

阿呆紧张地盯着这群活尸，他听不懂这些活尸在说什么，就看到一堆活尸围着他们不放，好些个活尸还用看大肥肉的馋涎目光盯着他。

诺曼爸爸为什么要来活尸的营地？他走错路了吗？

商非凡提着工兵铲一指前方，惊讶：“NPC攻城了？”

“什么？！”众玩家纷纷回头。听不懂的也会被商非凡的手势吸引。

商非凡扛着阿呆拔腿就跑。

等众玩家发现后方一个NPC都没看到时，再转头已经找不到刚才的玩家。

众玩家骂骂咧咧，有人迅速发出世界消息，有人到处询问朋友有没有见过类似的玩家。

也有智商流玩家露出若有所思的神情，也不知道想到了什么。

没一会儿九成以上玩家都知道了玩家中-出现了一个碉货，在其他人都还在辛苦搬砖赚钱币赚经验值时，人家已经左手巨虫坐骑、右手跟宠，长得还贼他妈帅！

商非凡在伏向军引领下，从还没有修建好的城墙缺口中跑进了营地。

伏向军不住看阿呆，忍不住问：“这小家伙从哪儿弄来的？你什么时候愿意养宠物了？”

“他叫阿呆，不是我的宠物，是我的任务对象。”商非凡介绍。

“任务对象？你竟然能跟当地NPC接到任务？还和小兽人有关？”伏向军更惊讶。

“运气。”商非凡的眼神告诉伏向军，有些事不适合在游戏中说。

伏向军懂了，猜测商非凡能跟玩家顺利交流，很可能和他的另一个游戏系统有关。但两人约定，在游戏中不会提到商非凡有两个游戏系统的事，伏向军还会帮他掩护。

伏向军用当地语言跟阿呆打招呼：“日安。”

阿呆有点不安。

商非凡拍拍他，跟他介绍伏向军：“这是我的好兄弟，他叫十面埋伏，你叫他老伏就好。”

阿呆表情变得呆愣：诺曼爸爸为什么有个活尸好兄弟？

阿呆比较引人注意，但他比较小号，只带着他，比骑着一只巨虫大摇大摆地进入营地要低调得多。

路人玩家虽有注意，顶多也就是指指点点，再没有一堆人围过来看稀奇。

刚进入营地，笔记本系统就通知商非凡，他的任务五完成了，让他去杂货铺领取奖励。

同时又给他发布一个任务，就是给阿呆找到一个领养人。

给阿呆在玩家中找一个领养人，这个任务一点都不难。

不说喜欢毛茸茸幼崽的玩家，有些玩家冲着能养一个跟宠，说不定还是游戏中第一个跟宠，也愿意领养阿呆。

但商非凡并不打算强制阿呆必须留在玩家营地，他决定让阿呆自己选。

“阿呆，如果途中你看到合适的人，想要跟随ta的话，就跟我说。”

阿呆歪头，“你不想带我去你的家乡了吗？”

商非凡：“我只是想给你多一些选择机会。”

阿呆斩钉截铁地：“不要。我要跟你去莫约山谷镇。”

商非凡知道了阿呆的决心。

伏向军带商非凡前往杂货铺，一路顺便介绍正在建造中的玩家营地。

商非凡打量这个营地，简单说这就是一个大型工地，所有建筑物都需要从砖瓦地基开始建造，没有其他经营建造类游戏中的建筑模块给他们使用。

从营地建造规模看来，玩家的野心不小，而且应该是有一张建造规划图纸。

“如果没有奖励，加上很难从NPC那里领到任务，大家早就跑出去随便玩了。现在也就是一些在现实中学习建筑学的人对建造这座营地感兴趣，据说这些人都领到了相关任务，完成会有很好的奖励。”

伏向军告诉商非凡，“游戏要求达到五级才能开启职业技能系统，天赋技能的进修拜师则需要达到十级，所以绝大多数玩家都在肝经验值，想要快点升到五级。另外这里拜师学艺需要大量游戏币，所以前期赚钱也很重要。”

“还有，很多装备、武器、衣服、食物、材料等需要在杂货铺购买，这些也都需要钱。”

商非凡问：“这么说营地里就有开启职业技能和天赋技能的NPC师父？”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 18: Player Camp Number One

Only when Shang Feifan approached the camp did he discover that the players were building city walls using large stone bricks.

"Hi, friend, what brings you here?"

A tall, thin player with zebra orc patterns painted on his face shouted loudly in a stuttering, unpolished local dialect.

"Wife Is Panda" was among the first batch of players, and he was also one of the unlucky fellows who had interacted with an NPC and promptly taken his first death. After analyzing the incident afterward, he figured it must have been caused by a language barrier, so he immediately started actively learning the local language.

However, NPCs didn't like to hang out with them, and there were no specialized textbooks, making it quite arduous for players who wanted to learn the local language.

The fact that playing a game required learning a foreign language drew endless complaints from the players, who flooded the forum comments demanding a one-click button to learn orc language.

It was said that the game planners had accepted everyone's opinions, but had no intention of modifying it.

This dissuasive behavior forced players to curse the game planners to high heaven, yet not a single person actually quit the game over this minor detail.

Shang Feifan lowered his head. "I'm here at the grocery store to redeem quest rewards."

"Holy shit!" Several players who overheard this were taken aback.

"He's actually a player?!"

"Since when can players have mounts?"

"He even has a pet!"

"Such an ugly pet."

"Do you call that ugly? That's called ugly-cute! As long as I can have a pet, I'd even take a cockroach!"

"Ugh! Wait, has the game system already unlocked the mount and pet features?"

"I don't know, it wasn't written in my patch notes. But do mounts and pets have to be tamed yourself? After all, this is an open, free-form holographic game world..."

"Didn't hear a peep about this at all. This guy is way too fucking badass—who is he?"

Fu Xiangjun was also moving bricks by the camp entrance while waiting for his boss. Seeing a giant bug trudge over, he curiously looked in that direction.

At this single glance, Fu Xiangjun froze.

Did his boss leave out a whole bunch of details when briefing him?

A bunch of players stood in a row in front of the Giant Crab-Bug, their eyes filled with envy and jealousy, and quite a few reached out to touch the crab-bug.

The crab-bug swung its large pincers, threatening to snap at them.

Shang Feifan manipulated the crab-bug to jump up, dodging the players' hands while also preventing the crab-bug from injuring them.

"Whoa, so fierce!"

"Cool~"

Shang Feifan jumped down from the crab-bug, patted its leg, and emitted a fluttering wing-sound with his mouth.

The crab-bug wheeled around and left, vanishing from sight in the blink of an eye.

"Ah, it ran away."

"A temporary mount? Tell me, brother, how did you tame it? Any secret tricks?"

"What is this square-headed little beast? A follower? A battle pet? Where can you get one?"

"Big Boss! Begging for a guide! I feel like we aren't even playing the same game."

"Wow, this face is top-tier. Does he look this handsome in real life too?"

"Brother, want to join a guild? Our 'Earn Money Without Doing Anything' guild is currently recruiting. Looking at you, brother, you're just the candidate we're looking for as vice-guild master!"

"Big Boss, add me as a friend! Let's play together sometime."

A throng of players stopped stacking city walls and swarmed over to surround Shang Feifan, chattering noisily. Everyone was shouting different things, and several languages were even mixed together.

Fu Xiangjun ran over and waved at Shang Feifan.

Shang Feifan saw him and flashed a hand gesture toward Lao Fu.

A-Dai stared nervously at this group of living corpses. He couldn't understand what these living corpses were saying; he only saw a bunch of living corpses surrounding them relentlessly, with quite a few staring at him with the greedy, salivating gazes people reserve for a fat piece of meat.

Why did Papa Norman want to come to the living corpses' camp? Did he take the wrong road?

Shang Feifan brandished his entrenching tool and pointed forward, acting surprised. "Did the NPCs launch a siege?"

"What?!" The players all turned around. Even those who didn't understand were drawn in by Shang Feifan's gesture.

Shang Feifan hoisted A-Dai onto his shoulder and took off running.

By the time the players realized not a single NPC was to be seen in the rear and turned back around, they couldn't find the player from a moment ago anywhere.

The players cursed up a storm; some quickly broadcasted world messages, while others scurried about asking friends if they had seen a similar player.

There were also intelligent, analytical players who wore thoughtful expressions, wondering what they had just deduced.

Before long, over ninety percent of the players knew that a badass had appeared among the players. While everyone else was still bitterly moving bricks to earn game coins and experience points, this guy already had a giant bug mount in his left hand, a companion pet in his right hand, and to top it all off, he was ridiculously, insanely handsome!

Led by Fu Xiangjun, Shang Feifan ran through the gap in the unfinished city wall and into the camp.

Fu Xiangjun kept glancing at A-Dai, finally unable to hold back his question: "Where did you fish this little guy out from? Since when were you willing to raise a pet?"

"His name is A-Dai. He's not my pet; he's my quest target," Shang Feifan introduced.

"A quest target? You can actually take on quests from local NPCs? And it involves a young orc?" Fu Xiangjun was even more surprised.

"Luck." Shang Feifan's gaze signaled to Fu Xiangjun that some things weren't appropriate to discuss within the game.

Fu Xiangjun understood, guessing that Shang Feifan's ability to communicate smoothly with players was likely related to his other game system. However, the two of them had agreed not to mention the fact that Shang Feifan possessed two game systems while in the game, and Fu Xiangjun would help cover for him.

Fu Xiangjun greeted A-Dai in the local dialect: "Good day."

A-Dai felt somewhat uneasy.

Shang Feifan patted him and introduced Fu Xiangjun: "This is my good brother. His name is Ten-sided Ambush, you can just call him Lao Fu."

A-Dai's expression turned blank and stunned: Why does Papa Norman have a living corpse as a good brother?

A-Dai was quite eye-catching, but since he was small and just tagged along, bringing only him was vastly more low-profile than swaggering into the camp riding a giant insect.

Though passing players noticed him, at most they would point and gossip, and a crowd no longer gathered around to gawk at a novelty.

Right as they entered the camp, the notebook system notified Shang Feifan that his fifth quest was complete and instructed him to go to the grocery store to claim his reward.

At the same time, it issued him a new quest: to find an adoptive parent for A-Dai.

Finding an adoptive parent for A-Dai among the players was not difficult at all.
