Restricted by raw materials and time constraints, Xiao Yan employed the most primitive sourdough fermentation method.

That is, using old dough as the starter.

Actually, the current orc world did possess old dough, but the orcs generally loathed wasting it; they would simply mix the old dough into fresh flour without allowing sufficient time for complete fermentation. Coupled with the fact that most orcs had exceptionally tough teeth, dense wheat cakes provided strong satiety and a long shelf life, making them ideal for long-term storage and arduous journeys. Consequently, no one ever bothered to improve the flour's fermentation method.

Furthermore, additives were scarce. Due to a lack of ingredients, orcs who made food with wheat flour never added things like milk, white sugar, or butter.

Generally speaking, the scarcer food was, the more reluctant people were to waste it, and naturally, no one would casually add or subtract ingredients to experiment with new flavors out of fear of spoiling or ruining the food.

That night, Xiao Yan did not make any wheaten staple foods. Instead, he mixed the flour with the purchased sourdough, covered it with a damp cloth, and placed it in a warm spot to ferment thoroughly.

He only prepared three dishes and one soup.

One dish was stir-fried mushrooms with sliced meat; another was braised pork with dried vegetables; a third was a cold mixed assorted vegetable dish; and the soup was a vegetable and meat nugget dough-drop soup.

These three dishes and one soup required no delicate plating; they were suited for bulk communal cooking, and a single wok stir-fry yielded enough portions to feed over a dozen big-bellied men at once.

When Hu Bushuai watched Xiao Yan haul an iron wok out of his giant insect mount and proceed to flip the wok using a stir-frying technique he found incomparably familiar, his gaze toward Xiao Yan shifted entirely.

Could this be... a fellow countryman?

The orc world did have iron woks, but the ones they used were either jar-shaped, mostly utilized for stewing meats and vegetables, or flat-bottomed, used for pan-frying meat and pancakes. The latter were more common, though people preferred clay pots for the former.

An arched, round-bottomed iron wok like this—he had never laid eyes on one.

Not to mention this cooking technique of flash-frying with added oil; it possessed far too much distinctive character.

As Hu Bushuai trailed at Xiao Yan’s heels, watching him rummage through ingredient shops and herbal shops in search of seasonings, he suspected the man was hunting for chili peppers, though regrettably, none were found.

At the thought of the texture and flavor of chili-stir-fried dishes, Hu Bushuai's mouth instantly flooded with saliva. He truly missed spicy food beyond measure.

In his past life, he had managed to find a substitute, but in this lifetime, within this orc world, he had yet to discover any ingredient resembling chili peppers.

Damn the insect curse! Damn the Poison Fog Era!

If this world possessed fine cuisine, he believed he would live a much happier life.

Solely based on Xiao Yan's wok-flipping technique, Hu Bushuai resolved to treat him a bit better.

What malicious intentions could a master chef possibly harbor?

As long as the man didn't plan on using orcs as raw materials, they could definitely get along.

By the time Xiao Yan served the three dishes and one soup onto the table, the dozen or so orcs in the courtyard were already on the verge of losing control.

Had Xiao Yan not kept the dishes inside the kitchen, and had Hu Bushuai not barred others from entering the kitchen to help (and steal bites), these dishes would never have made it to the present moment.

The only ones helping in the kitchen were Hu Bushuai and Wolf Four. Even Wolf Four could not resist sneaking tastes, let alone the others.

A crowd of orcs sat tightly clustered around the table, their eyes locked intently onto the large vegetable basin and large soup basin resting in the center.

Orcs did not use chopsticks; everyone was more accustomed to... using their own claws, only resorting to knives, forks, and spoons when being particularly formal.

Inside the dish-filled basins were several spoons and flat spatulas, allowing everyone to scoop their desired portions onto their personal plates.

"Dig in," Hu Bushuai said softly.

Swish! The entire table sprang to life, and the orcs fighting over the spoons nearly came to blows.

A'Dai was taken care of by Lao Shang, eating without even raising his head.

The evening's three dishes and one soup completely conquered every single orc in this expeditionary team.

Savoring the delicious stir-fried dishes—whose textures were completely different from roasted or stewed meat—washed down with the rich and mellow vegetable-and-meat-nugget dough-drop soup, and punctuated by bites of the sweet, sour, salty, and savory mixed vegetable dish, the orcs present experienced for the very first time the intense happiness brought by fine cuisine.

So meat, vegetables, and mushrooms could be stirred together to burst forth with such extraordinary flavors.

So vegetables could be blanched, stir-fried, and served cold as a salad. Whether they liked or loathed vegetables, none of these orcs had ever known that vegetables could be made to taste so delectable.

Not to mention the dough-drop soup. They had eaten soups made from wheat flour paste before, but this soup... how should he put it? The taste was extraordinarily rich and savory; it felt as though, even without eating anything else, they could drink this dough-drop soup every single day for a month without growing tired of it.

Hu Bushuai's dining etiquette was far more refined than that of the other orcs—this had been specially trained and corrected by his original body's mother, giving it a distinctively aristocratic air—though his eating speed was not a whit slower.

Hu Bushuai’s expression remained unchanged, but with every bite of food and every sip of soup, a little flower blossomed within the depths of his heart.

It tastes better than what I make!

It was hardly inferior to what he had eaten at grand restaurants in his pre-pre-life. Moreover, because it had been such a long time since he last tasted such flavors, coupled with the fact that this body had not yet grown accustomed to such multi-layered sensory explosions, it actually tasted even better than he remembered.

At the dining table, Xiao Yan announced that tomorrow morning he would make dry rations that were easier to carry on the road, and all the orcs immediately volunteered to help.

Naturally, Xiao Yan did not refuse.

After finishing dinner, Xiao Yan sat in the courtyard doing manual woodwork with rattan vines.

Watching for a moment, Hu Bushuai guessed what the man was making: he was weaving steaming baskets (steamers).

Ninety-nine percent chance he was a fellow countryman, no doubt about it.

Early the next morning, before the sky had even brightened, all the orcs in the courtyard were already up.

Xiao Yan divided the helping orcs into several groups: whipping cream, beating eggs, kneading dough, tending the fires, chopping vegetables... everything was arranged in an orderly fashion.

"What can I do?" Hu Bushuai approached and asked.

"This morning we're steaming a few batches of steamed buns (baozi) for breakfast." Yesterday, Xiao Yan had searched for soybeans but found none. Otherwise, they could have had soybean milk and tofu pudding this morning as well.

Baozi to eat! Hu Bushuai’s eyes lit up with a liveliness surpassing their usual state.

"I know where we can buy beans," Hu Bushuai couldn't help whispering. He had guessed what Xiao Yan had wanted to buy most yesterday.

"Oh? Then when we have time, you can take me to take a look." Not all beans were suitable for making tofu and soybean milk.

Hu Bushuai had never attempted to develop byproducts from local beans either; he had only ever eaten bean gruel, and it had been utterly foul-tasting.

chunks.chineseText:
商非凡并没有奇怪虎不帅会提到要帮他找豆子，因为他昨天就问过食材店的老板有没有豆类卖。

做包子需要包子皮，还要会包。

虎不帅不会擀皮，但他会包。但他不想暴露，就假装跟商非凡学习，还故意包出好几个丑里吧唧的。

商非凡就手把手教他怎么包出不露馅又好看的包子褶。

伪装笨拙的虎不帅：“……”我太难了！

但想到今后就能吃到各种美食，他又平静了。

随着肉包子和菜包子上锅，蒸腾出的香味就闹醒了周围居民。

阿呆也是第一次吃暄软的肉包子，小爪子抱着大大的肉包子，吃得脸都要埋进包子里。

商非凡看到虎不帅眯起眼睛小口小口咬着包子，特别想捏捏他的脸。

他做这些是为了赚钱，可看到虎不帅吃得这么幸福，他忽然觉得这些忙碌更加值得，甚至不赚钱也值得。

攻陷一个男人就得先抓住他的胃，嗯，他似乎知道该怎么拿下这个NPC了。

但不得不再说一次，这个世界的NPC也太灵动，连吃东西时的小表情都各不一样，你甚至能从他们身上体会到喷喷而出的幸福感。

数据编程真的能做到这么真实的程度吗？

商非凡第一次不希望虎不帅只是一段数据和程序。

等帮忙的兽人们吃上热腾腾香喷喷还特别暄软的大肉包子和菜包子时，他们后面干活就更来劲了。

商非凡给做的干粮是锅盔，这种能长时间摆放，携带也方便，且烤烤就能复软的食物很适合当干粮。

另外他还打算做一些五香肉干和泡一天以上就能吃的泡菜。

除了干粮，他今天重点要做的就是奶味小面包和蜂蜜小面包。

蛋糕就算了，奶油和糖都不够，可以等下次。

奶味小面包和蜂蜜小面包被烤熟后的香味非常霸道，能强势掩盖很多种早点香味，还能传出老远。附近居民大多都是被这股奶香和甜香味给诱惑得打开家门，循着香味找根源。

“啊。”商非凡示意。

正在揉面的虎不帅下意识张开嘴巴。

一个香软甘甜奶味浓郁的小面包被塞入口中。

这是第一板出炉的小面包。

强烈的香味惹得帮忙的兽人们蠢蠢欲动。

“好吃吗？”商非凡笑眯眯地问。

虎不帅两口就把小儿拳头大的小面包给咽下肚，虽然不习惯商非凡的亲昵，但他还是诚实地点头：“好吃。”

“你都说好吃，那我们可以开门营业了。”

这将是炒作的第一步。

嗡东亭那边正在帮他联系城中食品相关业者、酒馆旅馆老板、家中富裕且喜欢吃的老饕，以及富商和有脸面的小贵族。

嗡东亭甚至通过关系给彘庞男爵的长子彘圭也发了一张请柬。

请柬的名头就是【美食品鉴及食谱拍卖会】。
chunks.englishText:
Xiao Yan wasn't surprised that Hu Bushuai mentioned helping him find beans, because he had already asked the grocery store owner yesterday whether any beans were for sale.

Making baozi required wrappers, and one had to know how to wrap them.

Hu Bushuai didn't know how to roll out wrappers, but he knew how to wrap them. However, not wanting to expose himself, he pretended to learn from Xiao Yan, intentionally folding several unsightly, ugly-looking buns.

Xiao Yan patiently taught him hand-in-hand how to pleat the wrapper so the filling wouldn't leak out and the bun would look attractive.

Hu Bushuai, feigning clumsiness: "..." This is too hard for me!

Yet, thinking of the various delicacies he would be able to eat henceforth, his heart grew calm once more.

As the meat and vegetable baozi were placed into the steamers, the billowing fragrance awakened the surrounding residents.

It was also A'Dai's first time eating soft, fluffy meat baozi. Holding a large meat baozi in his little claws, he ate with such enthusiasm that his entire face was practically buried inside the bun.

Seeing Hu Bushuai narrow his eyes and take tiny, delicate bites of his baozi, Xiao Yan felt a strong impulse to pinch his cheeks.

He was doing all this to make money, but seeing Hu Bushuai eating with such sheer happiness, he suddenly felt that this busyness was all the more worthwhile—it would even be worth it without making a profit.

To conquer a man, you must first capture his stomach. Ah, he seemed to know how to capture this NPC now.

Yet he had to say it once more: the NPCs in this world were far too vivid. Even their tiny, varied expressions while eating allowed one to palpably experience a bubbling, overflowing sense of happiness.

Could data programming genuinely reach such a realistic degree?

For the very first time, Xiao Yan found himself wishing that Hu Bushuai wasn't merely a block of data and code.

When the helping orcs got to eat piping hot, fragrant, and exceptionally soft big meat baozi and vegetable baozi, they threw themselves into the subsequent labor with even greater vigor.

The dry rations Xiao Yan made for them were guokui (crusty flatbreads); such food could be kept for long periods, was convenient to carry, and could be softened back up simply by toasting—making it ideal as field rations.

Additionally, he planned to make some five-spice dried jerky and pickled vegetables that would be ready to eat after pickling for over a day.

Aside from dry rations, his primary focus today was baking milk-flavored mini bread rolls and honey-flavored mini bread rolls.

As for cakes, forget it; the cream and sugar were insufficient. That could wait for next time.

The fragrance of the milk and honey mini bread rolls, once baked, was utterly overbearing. It forcefully drowned out the scents of many other breakfast items and carried to great distances. Most of the nearby residents were lured by this milky and sweet aroma to open their front doors and track the scent back to its source.

"Ah," Xiao Yan signaled.

Hu Bushuai, who was in the midst of kneading dough, instinctively opened his mouth.

A fragrant, soft, sweet, and intensely milky mini bread roll was popped right in.

This was the first tray of freshly baked mini bread rolls.

The intense aroma set the helping orcs' hearts stirring restlessly.

"Is it delicious?" Xiao Yan asked with a beaming smile.

Hu Bushuai swallowed the child's-fist-sized mini bread roll in two bites. Although unaccustomed to Xiao Yan's affectionate gesture, he nodded honestly: "Delicious."

"Since you say it's delicious, then we can open our doors for business."

This would be the first step in the hype campaign.

Weng Dongting was currently helping him contact food-related business owners in the city, tavern and inn proprietors, wealthy gourmands who loved good food, as well as rich merchants and influential minor nobles.

Weng Dongting had even used his connections to send an invitation letter to Zhi Pang, the eldest son of Baron Zhi Pang.

The title of the invitation read: [Gourmet Food Tasting and Recipe Auction].

chunks.chapterTitle: 第51章 卖小面包配方 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第51章 卖小面包配方

摩罗城第九街这几天特别热闹，来来往往的人数都快赶得上商业街在办大小集时的流量。

先是有个小道消息在城中中层人士家中流传，说是有一个从大繁华纪就流传下来的千年厨艺世家子弟来到摩罗城。

而这名子弟从小听着祖上传说长大，一心想要恢复大繁华纪时代那水陆毕陈、琳琅满目、百花齐放，传说中的饕餮盛宴。

为此，这位千年厨艺世家子弟到处冒险挖掘废墟，就想从废墟中找出大繁华纪时代遗留下来的食谱以及还有活性的食物种子。

可谁都知道冒险和探宝旅程花费巨大，为了养活自己的队伍，也为了持续自己的目标，他不得不贩卖自己寻找到的一些食谱。

好在这位只是想要恢复大繁华纪时的无数美食，并不打算把这些食谱全都据为己有。只要有人能出得起价，任何食谱他都可以卖。

为了证明自己即将拍卖的食谱是真货，这位姓商的厨艺世家子弟决定先亮出自己的手艺，复现食谱上的食物，并以半卖半送的方式给摩罗城的居民们品尝。

紧接着第九街附近的居民就你传我、我传你，传出了他们街区来了一名大师级大厨的传言。

证据就是第九街每天早上都会飘出来的诱人香味。

而那户人家拿出来的食物也都是大家从没有见过、吃过的。

且他们第一天敞开门做生意，就有第五街的炼药师学徒们携伴前来品尝和购买。

每一个吃过他们家美食的炼药师学徒和他们的家人都赞不绝口，并且恨不得把那家的食物全都打包。

众所周知，炼药师包括炼药师学徒都是一群生性高傲的职业者，更爱惜自己的羽毛。他们也许会偷偷摸摸找人宣传自己的药剂效果更好，但极少会给别人抬轿子、吹嘘别人的东西。

对于入口的东西，他们更是谨慎，极少会表达意见，就算有那特别爱吃的炼药师也不过是经常光顾某家店，或者让家里的仆人经常购买，但也不会随意帮人宣传。

所以这帮第五街的炼药师学徒，其中还有名头比较响亮的，竟然集体前来第九街品尝一家压根没有挂招牌的小食铺里的食物，那效果堪比他们公开为这家店做宣传。

当然，这些炼药师中级和高级学徒一开始只是看在嗡东亭和他老师的面子上，只打算过来走一趟，如果好吃就买一点回家，如果不好吃，他们也算全了嗡东亭的人情——好歹来过。

没想到这家看着毫不起眼……实际上连店铺名都没有，只是打开院门，摆了几张桌子就开始营生的野店，竟然真的拿出了让他们完全预想之外的美食。

确实称得上美食。

不但外形看着小巧可爱，让人下意识就想要捏一捏尝一尝。那色泽、那香味，更是诱人至极。

等尝到嘴里，那香甜暄软、充沛的蜜香和奶香味，还带着一点点麦粉食物特有的焦香和麦香，更是让人吃了一个还想再吃一个。

这种口感和他们往日吃的硬麦饼完全不同。

他们吃的麦饼都是用麦粉和水做成面团，然后直接放在火上烘烤。讲究的人家会有一个烤炉，但烤出来的麦饼都是死面饼。

这时，绝大多数兽人还没有麦粉会发酵这个概念，也不知道发酵的面粉做出来的饼更好吃。

“这也是用麦粉做出来的？”品尝食物的老炼药师学徒手里托着小巧喷香的奶香小面包惊讶。

跟他一起来玩的小孙子不断蹦跶，想要从爷爷手里把那个奶香小面包给抢过来。他刚才一口气吃了两个，真的好好吃。

可惜这些叫做小面包的小点心份量非常少，店家说是限量，每个人都只能买一个送一个。

“爷爷，给我吃，给我吃~”

“好好好，给你给你。”老炼药师学徒被孙子缠得没办法，给了……半个。还有半个，他放自己嘴里了，随即他就被奶香小面包的味道给惊艳。

眼看袋子里只剩下一个小面包，他舍不得给孙子了。

今天愿意过来的炼药师除了看在人情份上，还有就是本身也比较爱吃，而老炼药师学徒就是一个隐藏的吃货，他对美食没有任何抵抗力。

“主材料应该就是麦粉，只是不知道添加了什么，让硬麦饼变得这样蓬松柔软。”嗡东亭适时回应。

“我之前接到男爵府邸的请柬，参加男爵的新年宴会，在宴会中也看到一种膨胀的麦饼，他们叫布洛驮。制作工艺保密，听说只有贵族家世代相传的厨娘才知道制作这种布洛驮的手艺。但布洛驮外壳很硬，不像这种小面包从里到外都很软还很香。”说话的炼药师高级学徒带着几分炫耀。

“啊，我也听过这种布洛驮，说是贵族家的特色食物，而且传承时间短的贵族都不知道布洛驮的做法。这种布洛驮的特色就是用同样多的面粉可以做出比正常麦饼要膨胀很多的食物，还抵饱。”

“能让食物变多的制作方法就应该传出来，那些贵族……”

“好了，这种话就不要在外面说了。而且现在不是已经有了比布洛驮更好的食物做法？”

老炼药师学徒很想多买一些，但刚才店家就跟他们说明白，因为人手不够，加上烤炉也小，他们做出的小面包不多，为了让更多人品尝到，只能限量。

既然不能多买，那就直接问配方能不能卖吧。

老炼药师学徒心中有数，之前嗡东亭就跟他们透露过食谱可以买的事。虽然说要放到拍卖会上，但卖谁不是卖，大家都是熟人，可以一起报个价嘛。

其他炼药师学徒也都起了心思，都是现场品尝，好不好吃，自己心知肚明。

有些精明的炼药师还想到：这么好吃的东西如果自家学会制作，不止可以满足口腹之欲，说不定还能给家里某些不擅长炼药的子孙谋一条新出路。

“买小面包的制作配方？”商非凡被叫出来，他身上一股子烘烤面包的香味。

大家推了老炼药师学徒出来说话。

“日安，商先生。我是皮翰。”老炼药师学徒微笑道。

商非凡挑眉，这名字可真熟悉，他和这位皮翰炼药师也算十分有缘分。

“日安，皮翰炼药师，久仰大名。”

“我还不是炼药师，只是一名学徒。”老皮翰客气地道。

当然，这话大家都是听听就算，不管在哪里，就算是低级炼药师学徒都会被尊称为炼药师，区别炼药师等级的是他们别在胸前的徽章。

“我听说你的这些食物配方都打算拍卖？”

“是的，拍卖会的时间就定在五天后的下午三点，拍卖场地就在商业街的献宝楼。”商非凡还特意指了指门口竖起来的牌子。

上面写了相关内容，包括他的来历介绍。

老皮翰摆摆手：“冲着你今天拿出来的小面包，五天后的拍卖会我一定会过去捧场。不过在这之前，这小面包的配方你不考虑先卖一卖吗？”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 51: Selling the Mini Bread Recipe

The Ninth Street of Wu Tan City had been exceptionally bustling over the past few days. The volume of people coming and going was almost on par with the foot traffic during a commercial street bazaar.

First, a rumor began circulating among the middle-class households of the city: a descendant of a millennial culinary family dating back to the Great Flourishing Era had arrived in Wu Tan City.

Growing up listening to ancestral legends, this descendant was single-mindedly determined to restore the legendary, opulent banquet of the Great Flourishing Era—a time when delicacies of land and sea were presented in their entirety, dazzling the eye and blooming in a hundred styles.

To this end, this scion of the millennial culinary family adventured everywhere, excavating ruins in search of surviving recipes and viable food seeds left behind from the Great Flourishing Era.

Yet everyone knew that adventure and treasure-hunting journeys required vast expenditures. To sustain his team and pursue his goal, he had no choice but to sell some of the recipes he had discovered.

Fortunately, this young man merely wished to revive the countless delicacies of the Great Flourishing Era and had no intention of hoarding all these recipes for himself. As long as someone could meet his price, he was willing to sell any recipe.

To prove that the recipes he was about to auction were genuine, this culinary family scion surnamed Xiao decided to first showcase his skills, recreate the dishes from the recipes, and offer them semi-gratis for the residents of Wu Tan City to taste.

Immediately following this, residents near Ninth Street passed the word back and forth until the entire district was abuzz with the rumor that a master-level chef had taken up residence in their neighborhood.

The proof was the enticing aroma that drifted out of Ninth Street every single morning.

Moreover, the food produced by that household consisted of items no one had ever seen or tasted before.

On their very first day throwing open their doors for business, apothecary apprentices from the Fifth Street came in groups to taste and purchase the goods.

Every single apothecary apprentice—and their families—who tasted the food there could not stop praising it, to the extent that they practically wanted to pack up and take away every single dish the place had to offer.

As everyone knew, apothecaries, including their apprentices, were a notoriously arrogant breed of professionals who cherished their reputations dearly. They might secretly hire people to spread the word that their own potions were superior, but they rarely stooped to acting as hype-men to praise someone else's wares.

When it came to things ingested into the body, they were even more cautious, seldom voicing opinions. Even if a particular apothecary was a massive foodie, they would merely frequent a certain shop often or send their servants to buy items regularly, never casually helping others publicize their business.

Thus, for this group of mid-level and senior apothecary apprentices from Fifth Street—some of whom held quite prominent reputations—to collectively visit an unnamed, un-signboarded little eatery on Ninth Street to sample its food had an effect comparable to publicly endorsing the establishment.

Of course, these intermediate and senior apothecary apprentices had initially come merely as a favor to Weng Dongting and his teacher, planning only to make a brief appearance: if the food tasted good, they would buy a little; if it didn't, they would still have honored Weng Dongting by showing up.

To their utter astonishment, this thoroughly unremarkable shop—which in reality didn't even have a store name, merely opening its courtyard gates and setting out a few tables to conduct business—actually produced gourmet food that completely shattered their expectations.

It genuinely deserved to be called fine cuisine.

Not only were the pastries small and cute in appearance, making one instinctively want to pinch and taste them, but their color and aroma were also intensely alluring.

Upon tasting them, the sweet, soft, and fluffy texture, laden with rich honey and milky fragrances and accompanied by the distinctive, toasted aroma of wheat flour, made people want to eat one after another.

This texture was entirely different from the hard wheat cakes they ate on a daily basis.

The wheat cakes they ate were made by mixing wheat flour and water into dough, then baking it directly over a fire. Affluent households might possess an oven, but the wheat cakes baked in them were always unleavened flatbreads.

At this point in time, the vast majority of orcs had yet to grasp the concept that wheat flour could be fermented, nor did they know that cakes made from fermented flour tasted vastly superior.

"This is also made from wheat flour?" the veteran apothecary apprentice asked in astonishment, holding the small, fragrant milk-flavored mini bread roll in his palm.

His young grandson, who had accompanied him, bounced up and down, trying to snatch the milk bread right out of his grandfather's hand. He had just eaten two in one breath, and they were truly delicious.

Regrettably, these pastries called mini bread rolls came in extremely limited quantities; the shopkeeper stated they were strictly limited edition, with a "buy one, get one free" limit per person.

"Grandpa, give it to me, give it to me~"

"好好好,给你给你." The veteran apothecary apprentice, badgered relentlessly by his grandson with no other choice, handed over... half of it. The other half went straight into his own mouth, whereupon the flavor of the milk bread blew him away.

Seeing that only one mini bread roll remained in the bag, he couldn't bear to give it to his grandson anymore.

Aside from honoring a favor, the apothecaries who had been willing to come today were also inclined toward good food by nature. The veteran apothecary apprentice was a hidden foodie with zero resistance against fine cuisine.

"The main ingredient should be wheat flour, though I don't know what was added to make a hard wheat cake become so fluffy and soft," Weng Dongting remarked smoothly at the right moment.

"I previously received an invitation to the Baron's New Year banquet, where I saw a kind of expanded wheat cake called a Buluotuo. The production technique is kept secret; I hear only the family chefs passed down through generations in noble households know how to make them. However, the crust of a Buluotuo is quite hard, unlike these mini bread rolls, which are soft and fragrant from the inside out," said a senior apothecary apprentice with a hint of boastfulness.

"Ah, I've also heard of this Buluotuo. They say it's a specialty food of noble houses, and nobles with short ancestral lineages don't even know how to make it. The special feature of the Buluotuo is that the same amount of flour can produce a food much more puffed up and filling than regular wheat cakes."

"Methods that can make food yield more ought to be shared with the public. Those nobles—"

"Alright, best not to say such things outside. Besides, isn't there already a better way to make bread than the Buluotuo?"

The veteran apothecary apprentice desperately wanted to buy more, but the shopkeeper had made it clear to them earlier: due to a shortage of manpower and the small size of their ovens, they could not bake many mini bread rolls. To allow more people to sample them, purchases had to be restricted.

Since he couldn't buy in bulk, he might as well ask straight out if the recipe could be bought.

The veteran apothecary apprentice had his calculations. Weng Dongting had previously dropped hints that the recipes could be purchased. While they were meant for the auction, who wasn't willing to sell to a willing buyer? They were all acquaintances here; they could always make a collective offer.

The other apothecary apprentices also had their minds stirred—they had tasted the goods on the spot, and whether they were good or not, they knew best in their own hearts.

Some shrewd apothecaries even thought: If their own households could learn to make such delicious food, it wouldn't just satisfy their cravings; it might even forge a brand-new path for descendants who lacked aptitude in pharmacy.

"You want to buy the recipe for the mini bread rolls?" Xiao Yan was called out, carrying a distinct aroma of freshly baked bread on him.

Everyone pushed the veteran apothecary apprentice forward to speak.

"Good day, Mr. Xiao. I am Pihan," the veteran apothecary apprentice said with a smile.

Xiao Yan raised an eyebrow. This name sounded truly familiar; he and this apothecary Pihan shared quite a deep bond of fate.

"Good day, Apothecary Pihan. I've heard a great deal about you."

"I am not yet an apothecary, merely an apprentice," Old Pihan said modestly.

Naturally, everyone took those words with a grain of salt. Regardless of the setting, even a low-level apothecary apprentice would be respectfully addressed as an apothecary; the distinction in rank lay in the insignia pinned to their chests.

"I heard you plan to auction all these food recipes?"

"Indeed. The auction is scheduled for 3:00 PM five days from now, and the venue will be the Treasure-Offering Pavilion on Commercial Street." Xiao Yan even specifically pointed toward the sign erected by the doorway.

It listed the relevant details, including an introduction to his background.

Old Pihan waved a hand. "For the sake of the mini bread rolls you brought out today, I will definitely show up to support the auction five days from now. However, before that, won't you consider selling the mini bread roll recipe beforehand?"

chunks.chapterTitle: 第51章 卖小面包配方 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
不等商非凡给出回答，老皮翰就侃侃说道：“我们一个人给出的价格也许不比拍卖会上的拍卖价格，但如果我们好些人购买，加起来的钱也不会少。而且你不觉得这样的美食不应该只被一家一店垄断，而是应该让所有人都品尝到吗？”

商非凡“动摇”了。

嗡东亭很懂地也跟着劝慰几句。

其他想购买配方的炼药师纷纷开口，表示不会让商非凡吃亏。

商非凡貌似碍于情面，也像是被打动了，松口：“我当然愿意让大家都品尝到美食，我到处跑寻找食谱也是为了恢复大繁华纪时期的无数美食。诸位炼药师大人肯捧场，也是给鄙人面子。好吧，小面包配方不会卖独家，只要想买的人都可以买到！”

十几位炼药师连同他们的家人发出矜持的小小欢呼。

看热闹的人群把这处院落附近围得水泄不通。

狼四他们帮忙让客人排队，并不断说他们限量，每个人只能买一个再送一个。

小面包价格对比麦饼不算便宜，小儿拳头大的一个就要五个铜达铢。

但想到这是从没有见过吃过的新鲜食物，又是买一送一，也就是五铜可以买两个，且这小面包看起来闻起来也着实诱人，来排队的还是有不少。

一些舍不得花钱的兽人看到其他人买到吃到嘴里，幸福得眯起眼睛的样子，也忍不住心动。

小孩子更直接，都蹦跶着说好吃，还央求家人再买一点。

没吃到的小孩眼馋急了，就差打滚撒泼。

很多舍不得花钱的大人被闹腾得没办法，只能过去排队。但等把小面包拿到手里再吃进嘴里，他们心里也没多少后悔，虽然会嘟囔这小面包要比麦饼贵多了。

皮翰等炼药师这时也和商非凡商量出了一个适宜价格，一份奶香或蜜香小面包的配方，定价为二十个银达鲁。

这个价格绝对不算高，属于普通人家也能买得起的价格。

商非凡还拿了个喇叭，大声告诉所有人：买配方，他还附赠详细的烘烤方法，保证大家都不会走弯路。

“另外，我再告诉大家一个秘密。面食的制作方法都是一通百通，你们购买了小面包的制作方法，就相当于也知道了其他面食的制作方法。就算你们想不到其他面食怎么做，但你们在小面包上涂抹奶油，那就是奶香小面包。切开面包，里面涂抹果酱或者夹杂坚果水果等食物，那就是另一种新式面包。面包可以玩出的花样很多，一张价值二十银的配方，就足够让人开出一家面包店。”

这下人群轰动了。

舍不得或拿不出二十银的人在听说这不止是一张配方的价格，而是可以当做一门营生来做的价格后，都恨不得马上借钱去把小面包的制作配方买下来。

还有更“聪明”的人想要花二十银把配方买下来，再用更低的价格大量卖出去。

商非凡当然也考虑到这一点，他选择把他的防盗措施告诉所有人。

“诸位，这是我冒着生命危险从废墟里挖出来的配方，如今我愿意用低廉的价格把它卖出去，但如果有人不讲规矩，把配方另外转手，包括免费赠送和标价另卖，那就不要怪我诅咒这样做的人不但会失去通过小面包配方获得的一切，还需要赔偿我相等价格的损失。”

听到的兽人们不少人脸色变了，还有人当场就想骂人。

兽人们讨厌的技能之最就是诅咒，一听诅咒就暴躁。

商非凡做了个下压的手势，竖起一根手指：“只要一年！我只要你们遵守一年的时间。一年后，你们是免费赠送也好，是贩卖也好，都和我无关。”

“好哎！”嗡城用力鼓掌。

在场的兽人恢复和善，大多露出笑容，只是一年时间，那谁都能等得。

只有想要赚快钱的兽人在翻白眼。

商非凡被鼓掌，半点不觉得尴尬，还能保持笑容，对众人说：“想要购买小面包配方的人，可以到这条队伍来排队。记住，我的一年期限诅咒不是开玩笑。我们这种古老的厨艺家族，为了保下家传的秘密食谱，怎么可能没有一点防盗绝活？”

有兽人相信，也有兽人不信。

商非凡也不管他们信不信，该给的警告他已经给了，他也会保证向每个买配方的人都说明情况。如果这样还有人要违反一年的保密契约时间，那就不要怪诅咒内容灵验。

虎不帅在旁边用欣赏的目光看商非凡。

他觉得这个老乡人品不错。

一年时间，可以保障他本人的利益，至少能借这些食物配方赚一些钱。

而一年时间又如此短暂，相信等一年后，面食需要发酵的常识就会飞速传遍整个兽人世界。

面包的香味也会就此传进千家万户。

多好啊。

商非凡正在头疼，他应该提前去印刷一批配方和烘烤说明，而不是现场手写。

有没有人的天赋技能是复制？

不过老商也很快找到了解决办法，他跟所有想要购买配方的人约定，先交一半定金，晚上来拿配方。

买配方的人也表示理解，毕竟这位千年厨艺世家传人也是临时决定要低价卖配方给所有人。

“印刷？没有印刷，只有找手抄匠。”虎不帅非常残念地告诉商非凡这个事实。

商非凡：所以我现在还要现场diy出印刷术吗？

虎不帅很是期待地看着这位老乡，快点把印刷术搞出来吧！

嗡东亭在旁边说：“听说王室宫廷图书馆有一位可以复制文字的天赋者……”

商非凡给了他一个无语的眼神：“就聘请抄写匠人。”

在说印刷时，商非凡脑中就浮出一种最简单的印刷方法，这种方法他曾教给某些部落的学校，简称蜡纸油印法。

只要有一张蜡纸和一张白纸，再找一个钢笔尖，白纸在下蜡纸在上铺在钢板上，用钢笔尖在蜡纸表面刻写上要印刷的内容，需要把蜡纸刻透。

然后把新的白纸铺到蜡纸下面，中间垫上防溢出的纱网，用油墨滚筒对着蜡纸一滚，油墨就可以透过刻透的缝隙，把字印到下面的白纸上。

这种方法虽然简单，但没有蜡纸和油墨滚筒也不行。

而且刻写蜡纸的过程也很麻烦，很容易刻坏，刻这个需要经验。

商非凡不想给自己找这样的麻烦，最后还是决定花钱请抄写匠帮忙。

还好这个世界已经发明出纸张，大战纪和毒雾纪也没让纸张的制作工艺失传。

不过凡是用植物做出来的东西都很贵，纸张在这里就属于高价货。

大约A4大小的纸张，工艺一般，售价就要一铜一张。

比成年人巴掌还大的麦饼的价格才一铜一个。

抄写匠人找来了，小面包的名气也传出了第九街，往其他街区蔓延。

因为生意太好，狼四他们在收到所有药剂后都不想立刻离开，而是想要留下来帮忙。他们不要工钱，只要商非凡管饭就行。

如果不是大家都挂心镇子那边的疫情，他们真的会留下来。
chunks.englishText:
Before Shang Feifan could give an answer, Old Pihan chimed in smoothly, "The price each of us offers might not match a high-stakes auction, but if a good number of us buy it together, the total sum won't be small. Besides, don't you think such a delicacy shouldn't be monopolized by just a single shop, but rather shared so everyone can taste it?"

Shang Feifan appeared "swayed."

Weng Dongting was perceptive enough to offer a few words of persuasion as well.

The other alchemists who wished to purchase the recipe quickly spoke up, assuring him that they would not let Shang Feifan suffer a loss.

Acting as though he were pressured by social pressure and genuinely moved, Shang Feifan relented: "Of course I want everyone to taste good food. The reason I traveled around searching for recipes was precisely to revive the countless delicacies of the Great Prosperous Era. Since all you esteemed Alchemist Lords are willing to grace me with your presence, you're doing me a great honor. Very well! The little bread recipe will not be sold exclusively; anyone who wants to buy it can have it!"

A dozen or so alchemists, along with their families, let out restrained, dainty cheers.

The crowd of onlookers packed the area around the courtyard so tightly that not even water could leak through.

Lang Si and his men helped keep the customers in line, constantly announcing that supplies were limited and it was a buy-one-get-one-free deal—one person could only buy one and get another free.

Compared to wheat cakes, the little bread wasn't cheap; a piece the size of a child's fist cost five copper dalus.

However, thinking that this was a fresh food they had never seen or tasted before, and that it was buy-one-get-one-free—meaning five coppers could buy two—plus the fact that the little bread looked and smelled utterly enticing, quite a few people still joined the queue.

Some stingy beastmen, watching others buy it and eat it with looks of blissful squinting, couldn't help but feel tempted.

The children were even more direct, jumping up and down, declaring how delicious it was, and begging their families to buy a little more.

Those kids who hadn't gotten a bite were green with envy, practically rolling on the ground and throwing tantrums.

Many adults who hated spending money were pushed to their wits' end by the commotion and had no choice but to go queue up. Yet once they held the little bread in their hands and ate it, they didn't feel much regret—even though they muttered that this little bread was far more expensive than wheat cakes.

By this time, Pihan and the other alchemists had also negotiated a suitable price with Shang Feifan: a single recipe for milk-flavored or honey-flavored little bread was priced at twenty silver dalus.

This price was definitely not high; it belonged in the category of what ordinary families could afford.

Shang Feifan even took out a megaphone and shouted to everyone: for those who bought the recipe, he would throw in detailed baking instructions for free, guaranteeing that no one would take any detours.

"Also, let me tell you a secret. The methods of making wheat-based foods are all interconnected. Once you purchase the method for making little bread, you are equivalent to knowing the methods for making other wheat-based foods as well. Even if you can't think of how to make other wheat-based foods, if you spread butter on this little bread, it becomes milk-flavored little bread. Slice the bread open and smear it with jam or stuff it with nuts and fruits, and it becomes a completely new style of bread. There are countless ways to play with bread. A recipe worth twenty silvers is enough for someone to open a bakery."

The crowd erupted at this.

Those who were reluctant or unable to scrape together twenty silvers, upon hearing that this wasn't just the price of a single recipe, but rather the price to establish a livelihood, all wished they could immediately borrow money to buy the little bread recipe.

There were even "smarter" people who wanted to spend twenty silvers to buy the recipe and then resell it in large quantities at a lower price.

Of course, Shang Feifan had considered this possibility, and he chose to inform everyone of his anti-piracy measures.

"Ladies and gentlemen, this is a recipe I risked my life to dig out from the ruins. Now, I am willing to sell it at a low price, but if anyone breaks the rules and resells the recipe—including giving it away for free or pricing it for separate sale—then don't blame me for cursing whoever does so. Not only will they lose everything they gained through the little bread recipe, but they will also be required to compensate me for an equivalent loss."

Hearing this, the expressions of quite a few beastmen changed, and some even wanted to start cursing on the spot.

The skill beastmen hated the most was cursing; the moment they heard the word "curse," they grew irritable.

Shang Feifan made a pressing gesture with his hand and raised a single finger: "Just one year! I only ask you to abide by it for one year. After one year, whether you give it away for free or sell it has nothing to do with me."

"Hooray!" Weng Cheng clapped vigorously.

The beastmen present returned to their amiable demeanors, mostly revealing smiles. It was only a year, after all; anyone could wait that long.

Only the beastmen who wanted to make a quick buck rolled their eyes.

Shang Feifan didn't feel awkward in the slightest from receiving applause; he maintained his smile and said to the crowd, "Those who wish to purchase the little bread recipe can come line up in this queue. Remember, my one-year time-limit curse is no joke. As an ancient culinary family, how could we not have a few anti-theft secret techniques to protect our ancestral secret recipes?"

Some beastmen believed him, while others did not.

Shang Feifan didn't care whether they believed him or not; he had already given the warning he needed to give, and he would also ensure that every single buyer was informed of the situation. If anyone still chose to violate the one-year confidentiality contract after that, they shouldn't blame the curse for taking effect.

Hu Bushu looked at Shang Feifan with appreciative eyes from the side.

He felt that this fellow countryman had good character.

A year's time could safeguard his own interests, allowing him to at least earn some money through these food recipes.

And a year was such a short period; he believed that after a year, the common knowledge that wheat dough required fermentation would rapidly spread across the entire beastman world.

The fragrance of bread would likewise find its way into thousands of households.

How wonderful.

Shang Feifan was currently suffering from a headache over the fact that he should have gone ahead to print a batch of recipes and baking instructions instead of hand-writing them on the spot.

Did anyone happen to have copying as a innate talent?

However, Lao Shang quickly found a solution. He made an agreement with everyone who wanted to buy the recipe that they would pay half the deposit first and come back in the evening to collect the recipe.

The buyers expressed their understanding, considering that this descendant of a millennial culinary dynasty had also made a sudden decision to sell the recipe cheaply to everyone.

"Printing? There's no printing here, only copyists," Hu Bushu regretfully informed Shang Feifan of this reality.

Shang Feifan: *So now I have to DIY movable-type printing on the spot?*

Hu Bushu looked at his fellow countryman with high anticipation. *Hurry up and invent printing!*

Weng Dongting chimed in from the side, "I heard the Royal Palace Library has a talented individual who can copy text..."

Shang Feifan gave him a speechless look. "We'll just hire copyists."

When discussing printing earlier, a primitive method of printing had surfaced in Shang Feifan's mind—a method he had once taught to certain tribal schools, commonly known as mimeographing or stencil printing.

As long as one had a wax stencil and a piece of white paper, along with a steel pen nib, the white paper was placed underneath and the wax stencil on top upon a steel plate. One would use the steel pen nib to carve and write the content to be printed onto the surface of the wax stencil, making sure the stencil was pierced through.

Then, a new sheet of white paper was placed beneath the wax stencil, with an anti-overflow gauze net padded in between. By rolling an ink roller over the wax stencil, the ink could penetrate through the carved openings and print the characters onto the white paper below.

Although this method was simple, it was useless without wax stencils and ink rollers.

Moreover, the process of carving the wax stencil was quite troublesome and very easy to ruin; carving it required experience.

Shang Feifan didn't want to invite such trouble upon himself, so he ultimately decided to spend money to hire copyists for help.

Fortunately, paper had already been invented in this world, and neither the Great War Era nor the Poison Fog Era had caused the papermaking craft to be lost.

However, anything made from plants was expensive, and paper belonged to the luxury tier here.

A piece of paper roughly the size of A4, with ordinary craftsmanship, cost one copper per sheet.

Meanwhile, a wheat cake larger than an adult's palm only cost one copper each.

The copyists were summoned, and the fame of the little bread also spread out of the Ninth Street, rippling into other districts.

Because business was so booming, Lang Si and his men didn't want to leave immediately after receiving all the potions; instead, they wanted to stay and help out. They didn't want wages, as long as Shang Feifan provided their meals.

If everyone hadn't been worried about the plague back in the town, they really would have stayed.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第51章 卖小面包配方 (Part 3)
chunks.chineseText:
狼四带着队伍和买到的药剂，以及商非凡给他们做的大量干粮，在当天下午就离开了摩罗城。

虎不帅暗中送行，跟了他们一段路，见没有人盯上他们，这才回转。

商非凡这边继续待在小院里制作面包，他打算头两天就销售面包，后面做油条和烧饼，等拍卖会时再做一些小炒菜。

现实世界那边的美食太多，他不可能全拿出来，就先卖几样常见的，且这边也有原材料的再说。

嗡城主动留下来打下手，商非凡干脆通过嗡东亭的关系，找了十来个老实可靠的兽人过来帮忙做杂活。

他跟这些帮忙的人也都说好，一年之内不允许对外透露出他的配方，如果泄露就会遭到诅咒。

这些人都忙不迭地答应，他们来帮忙，不但有工钱，还能偷学手艺，只要等一年时间，他们就可以拿出来自用或盈利，这样的好处到哪里找？

虎不帅在下午回来，也加入了打杂中。

小面包烘烤好一批就往外卖一批。

院子外面排队的人络绎不绝，且人数越来越多。

商业街那边的人消息最灵通，尤其是那些做食品行业的，听到消息后，立刻就亲自或派伙计过来打探。

等尝到小面包的味道后，哪怕为了不落于人后，他们也会报名购买配方。

二十银，对于吃了上顿不知道下顿在哪里的穷人来说很难掏出这么一笔钱，但对于城中的中产人士，这笔钱真的不算什么。

钱赚多了，自然会惹得别人眼红。

虽然才只是第一天，找麻烦的人也上门了。

一群地痞流氓一脚踹开了院门。

“谁让你们在这儿开店了！不知道这里是居民区吗？你们开店的手续呢？拿出来看看！”

“有人来找事？”商非凡兴奋得眼睛都亮了，提起一根擀面杖就往厨房外面跑。

谁爱当厨子谁当，他要打架！
chunks.englishText:
CHINESE SOURCE TEXT (第51章 卖小面包配方 (Part 3)):
"""
Lang Si led his squad, along with the acquired potions and a large amount of dry rations prepared for them by Shang Feifan, and left Molo City that very afternoon.

Hu Bushu escorted them in secret, tailing them for a stretch of the road. Seeing that nobody was trailing them, he turned back.

Shang Feifan remained in the small courtyard to continue making bread. He planned to sell bread for the first two days, make fried dough sticks (*youtiao*) and baked sesame flatbreads (*shaobing*) afterward, and whip up some quick-stir-fried dishes when the auction arrived.

There were simply too many delicacies in the real world; he couldn't possibly bring them all out. He would just sell a few common ones for which the raw materials were readily available here first.

Weng Cheng voluntarily stayed behind to lend a hand, and Shang Feifan simply used Weng Dongting's connections to find a dozen or so honest and reliable beastmen to come over and help with odd jobs.

He made it clear to all these helpers that they were not allowed to reveal his recipe to the outside world for a full year, and that anyone who leaked it would suffer a curse.

These people agreed without a moment's hesitation. Coming to help not only earned them wages, but they could also secretly learn the craft. They only had to wait a year before they could use it themselves or turn a profit—where else could they find such a sweet deal?

Hu Bushu returned in the afternoon and also joined in the odd-job brigade.

A fresh batch of little bread was baked and immediately put up for sale.

Outside the courtyard, the queue of waiting people stretched endlessly, and the crowd was only growing larger.

News traveled fastest in the commercial district, especially among those in the food industry. Upon hearing the news, they immediately came in person or sent their apprentices to investigate.

Once they tasted the flavor of the little bread, even just to avoid falling behind the competition, they would sign up to purchase the recipe.

Twenty silvers was a hard sum to scrape together for poor folks who lived from hand to mouth, but for the middle class in the city, this amount of money was truly nothing.

When one earns too much money, it naturally invites the jealousy of others.

Even though it was only the first day, troublemakers had already come knocking.

A group of ruffians and scoundrels kicked open the courtyard gate.

"Who told you bastards to open a shop here! Don't you know this is a residential area? Where are your business permits? Hand them over and let's see!"

"Someone's here to look for trouble?" Shang Feifan's eyes lit up with excitement as he grabbed a rolling pin and bolted out of the kitchen.

Whoever wanted to be a chef could be one; he wanted to fight!
