chunks.chineseText:
“饿吗？”

“还好。你饿了？”商非凡抬手就要从雕像广场找吃的。

虎不帅忙摇头：“我不饿，我是怕你饿了。你胃口那么好，刚才还来回变身。”

变身非常消耗能量。

商非凡笑，自从上次升级，他的力量值大幅度提高，他的食量也翻倍上涨。过不了多久就会感到饿，每次都会吃很多。

但真的只是因为这样？

不帅实际上是在担心他饥饿会变身幼崽这点吧？

会主动担心他了。第二大进步，很好！

“我在储物空间里准备了很多食物，不会饿着自己。”

“哦。”

两人短暂陷入沉默。

虎不帅感到有人在碰自己的手指。

“这条通道有点暗，我有点看不清。”手指勾住他。

虎不帅嗤笑：胡扯，我们兽人除了少数种族，绝大多数都能在黑暗中视物。

虎不帅用力想要甩开勾住他手指的手指。

没甩掉。

挣扎了几次，虎不帅……放弃了。

但很快他就为自己的放弃而后悔。

因为某个家伙显然非常懂得什么叫得寸进尺。

刚刚还只是手指勾住他的手指，现在整个手掌都握了上来。

虎不帅刚要挣脱。

“如果这里真是一个真实世界，我会留下。”

“……我不需要任何人为我做出牺牲。”

“这怎么能叫牺牲呢？我是想告诉你，有你的世界才精彩又让我充满期待。”

这话，商非凡并不是哄人。

他不是一个冲动的人，他说出的话都经过深思熟虑。

在听到脑载系统跟他说的那句话后，他就在认真考虑一个可能：我是否能真正进入这个世界。

为此，他加快了在现实世界寻找游戏服务器和头盔制作商的速度。

他坚信，就算这个游戏和头盔都是外星人做的，只要它们出现在地球，就不可能做到不留下一点痕迹。

他现在寻找游戏商的下落，除了想要给自己留个后手——以防不帅还是一段数据，更是为了找出事实来证明这不是一个游戏。

如果这真的不是一个游戏世界，那他就会为真正进入这个世界做好准备。

如果不能，他会用尽方法把不帅从这个世界带到地球。

如果这两点都不能做到……

他不知道自己会做出什么事情。

“你想了解我吗？真正的我。”虎不帅突然说。

商非凡侧头看他：“当然。”

虎不帅不看他，只看着前面的路：“那你就去找十一年前你错过的那个人。”

嗯？商非凡心里冒出问号。不帅这是吃醋？

不对，不帅这是在说……艹！不会吧？！

紧接着，不帅又冒出一句：“你说这个世界是游戏，也就是说你是玩家。那么你每次睡觉睡得那么死，是不是就是下线了？”
chunks.englishText:
"Hungry?"

"Not really. You hungry?" Shang Feifan raised a hand, making as if to pull food out of the statue plaza.

Hu Bushuai hurriedly shook his head. "I'm not hungry, I'm worried *you're* hungry. With an appetite as big as yours, you were shifting back and forth earlier, too."

Shifting consumed a massive amount of energy.

Shang Feifan chuckled. Ever since his last upgrade, his strength stat had soared dramatically, and his food intake had doubled right along with it. It didn't take long before he'd feel hungry, and he always ate a mountain of food when he did.

Was it really just because of that, though?

Bushuai was actually worried he'd turn back into a little cub if he got too hungry, wasn't he?

He was starting to proactively worry about him. Step two of progress achieved—marvelous!

"I've prepared plenty of food in my storage space. I won't starve myself."

"Oh."

A brief silence fell between them.

Hu Bushuai felt someone brushing against his fingers.

"This passage is a bit dim; I can't see very well." A finger hooked into his.

Hu Bushuai sneered internally: *Absolute bullcrap. Aside from a tiny minority of species, the vast majority of us orcs can see perfectly in the dark.*

Hu Bushuai forcefully tried to shake off the finger hooked around his.

It didn't budge.

After struggling a few times, Hu Bushuai... gave up.

Yet, he instantly regretted giving up.

Because this certain someone clearly understood the art of inching forward to take a mile.

A moment ago it had merely been a single finger hooked around his; now, an entire palm had wrapped completely over his hand.

Hu Bushuai moved to yank his hand free.

"If this place really is a real world, I'm staying."

"......I don't need anyone making sacrifices for me."

"How could that possibly be called a sacrifice? I'm trying to tell you that a world with you in it is the only one that's brilliant and full of expectations for me."

Shang Feifan wasn't just sweet-talking him with these words.

He wasn't an impulsive man; everything he said had been thoroughly deliberated.

The moment he heard what the in-brain system told him, he began seriously contemplating a single possibility: *Could I truly enter this world?*

To that end, he had accelerated his search in the real world for the game's servers and helmet manufacturers.

He firmly believed that even if this game and those helmets were crafted by extraterrestrial beings, the moment they manifested on Earth, it was simply impossible for them to leave behind zero traces.

His current hunt for the game developers—aside from wanting to leave himself a safety net just in case Bushuai turned out to be nothing more than a string of data—was driven even more by the desire to unearth facts proving this wasn't a game.

If this truly wasn't a game world, then he would ready himself to enter this world for real.

If he couldn't...

He had no idea what he might end up doing.

"Do you want to get to know me? The *real* me?" Hu Bushuai blurted out suddenly.

Shang Feifan turned his head to look at him. "Of course."

Hu Bushuai didn't look back at him, keeping his eyes fixed on the path ahead. "Then go find the person you missed out on eleven years ago."

*Huh?* A question mark popped up in Shang Feifan's mind. *Is Bushuai jealous?*

No, wait. Was Bushuai implying... *Holy shit! No way?!*

Immediately following that, Bushuai tossed out another sentence: "You claim this world is a game, which means you're a player. So every time you fall sound asleep like a log... does that mean you're logging off?"
"""

chunks.chapterTitle: 第84章 带我老婆回家 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第84章 带我老婆回家

商非凡正乘坐飞机前往华夏。

不过不是以回国的名义，而是以Y国旅游者的身份。

Y国护照持有者可以免签进入华夏待上半个月。

这么绕一圈，也是为了确保不会有人把商非凡这个军火贩子的身份和华夏联系到一起，就算有些人有怀疑，但只要没有抓到证据，他和华夏就是没关系。

飞机上的时间很无聊，商非凡很想进入游戏，但他忍住了，改为拿出电脑处理一些工作。

在外面这么多年，官方的、非官方的，他认识了很多人。

这些人和他们的朋友以及朋友的朋友形成一张巨大网络，这张网络上的人可以以发布任务的方式互助互利。

商非凡就在通过这张庞大的人脉网络重金查找《天河星争霸》这首款百分百全息游戏的相关信息。

知道这个游戏的人不少，但至今为止没有任何一个人表示他们有收到过该游戏的任何重要信息。

而这在现实世界几乎不可能。

一个游戏，还是一个大型多人同时上线的全息游戏，哪怕是内测，想要推出来也要拿到官方许可，其中更包括多种必要证书。

比如营业执照、软件著作权、游戏版号、运营备案、网络经营许可等等。

可那张遍及全世界的庞大人脉网络竟然没有一个人提供相关消息。

就算那家游戏开发商再能保密，在网络时代，她也瞒不住一些必要信息。

对此，商非凡不得不得出结论：除非《天河星争霸》这款全息游戏压根就没有注册。

他再查游戏头盔，先从游戏头盔的运送商查起。

这个倒是有一点线索。

先是各地配送公司收到货物，再按照货物上标明的地址送到各个玩家手中。

再查这些头盔是从哪里寄到各地配送公司，就这样一层层递进，最终查到一个内乱国家的码头仓库。

管理仓库的一对兄弟在收钱后告诉调查者，所有头盔都是从这里发出。

而他们则是在某天接到一封电子邮件，说他们应聘上了仓库管理员和寄送员的工作。

正在到处投简历找工作的兄弟也没有多怀疑，他们确实也找了几个仓库方面的工作岗位，当看到邮件中提到的薪水和福利待遇都远超他们期待后，两兄弟毫不犹疑地收拾行李就来到了这个工作地点。

他们的工作内容就是按照邮件要求，在邮件吩咐的时间打开仓库大门，拿出里面已经准备好的头盔，包装，并把邮件发给他们的地址打印出来，贴到纸箱上，把头盔寄出。

因为头盔看起来平平无奇，他们也不想丢掉这份收入不菲还特别轻松的工作，就一直没有打这些头盔的主意，更没有深究这些头盔的来源和雇主身份。

头盔的线索到这里就断了。

调查者依旧不知道这些头盔是怎么进入的这个仓库。

而就在调查者发现这个仓库不久，那对兄弟就收到了一封辞退邮件，表示他们的工作已经结束。

再查这个仓库的拥有者，竟是一个已经死了四五年、却没有注销身份的人。

对方无子无女，死亡后的遗产就只有一栋房子和这个仓库。

对方很可能是突发疾病死亡，尸体就在他自家的地下室里。

调查者查到死者的住房，在地下室发现其尸体。死者尸体头朝下，身体还搭在地下室的阶梯上，看着很像是突发疾病倒下死亡。

因为尸体在地下室，紧闭的空间遮掩住了他尸体腐烂的臭味，附近邻居也不是特别讲究的人，就算闻到一点味道也没怎么在意。

再加上死者没有亲人，这个国家内部管理也比较混乱，最后竟然没有谁注意到这个人已经死亡，更没有注意到死者名下的仓库在被人使用。

商非凡又调查给那对兄弟发邮件的邮箱地址，查来查去查到一家图书馆。

现在商非凡就在派人盯着这家图书馆，目前还没有发现问题。

另外商非凡重点盯的就是给那对兄弟账户打钱的账户。

那个账户属于某家国际银行，是一个已经超过十年都没有转账进账的‘遗忘’账户。

每家银行都有这样的账户，要么是账户主人突然死亡，没有来得及立遗嘱。要么就是账户主人患病遗忘或无法处理自己的财产。还有失踪者、犯罪者、不能动的钱……

十年没有人动过的账户突然再次开始转账，银行方面也稍微关注了一番。

但后来发现那就是固定转账，还注明是酬薪，个人网银也重新人脸认证过，确认是本人，银行方面就以为账户主人终于想起了这笔钱，就没有再多注意。

商非凡通过个人渠道拿到了这个账户主人的信息，就如他一开始预料的，这个账户主人早已失踪。

有意思的是，账户主人的妻子和孩子都不知道他有这么一个秘密账户，这也让做妻子的越发确定她丈夫压根就不是失踪，而是转移财产打算和她离婚。

至于为什么在离婚前人就失踪了，被转移财产的账户也十年没有人动用，就成了一个未知答案。

做妻子的报警了，她不是想要找回失踪的丈夫，而是想要把这个账户里的钱拿回来。

现在这个案件正在受理中。

不想卷进这个案子的商非凡消失得干干净净，任凭警察怎么查，都无法找到那个找上门的律师。

如此，看起来他没有查到多少线索，但通过他找到的这些线索，一个答案逐渐浮出水面。

这么一个伟大的、卓绝的全息游戏，为什么要通过这么神秘的方式出现？

什么样的人见不得人？

又是什么样的人拥有这么非凡的手段？

商非凡心中已经有所猜测，他只是还需要一些事实证据来验明。

还有一个小时就能抵达他想要前往的N城。

商非凡打开了电脑邮件，他没有用网络，这些邮件内容都已经下载下来。

鼠标转移到一封十一年前发给他的邮件上。

实际上早在他第一次碰到那人时，他就通过身上微型摄像头拍下了对方的面貌。

和那人分开不久，他产生了想要了解那人的想法，就请人帮忙，搜索华夏大使馆驻意国的国人护照信息库，经过照片对比，很快就找到了那人的身份信息。

在朋友把调查到的身份信息发给他后，他在电脑前坐了好一会儿，最终没有打开那封邮件。

十一年！

他怎么也没想到，十一年后，他会选择点开这封邮件。

邮件内容他在上飞机前就看过了，否则他也不会买前往N城的机票。

商非凡点击鼠标，再次打开了邮件。

邮件里附带了一份证件照。

他一点开邮件就出现在他眼前。

就是那个人，五官很年轻，神情却没有年轻人的毛躁和锐利，笑容温和，但也明显缺乏了一些年轻人特有的进取心和朝气。

乍一看，他的五官似乎和不帅有那么一点想象。但仔细看，就会发现两者区别很大。

再点开另一个附件，里面是照片中人的详细个人信息。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 84: Bringing My Wife Home

Shang Feifan was currently aboard a flight heading toward China.

However, he was not traveling under the guise of returning home, but rather as a tourist from Country Y.

Holders of Country Y passports were granted visa-free entry into China for a stay of up to half a month.

Making such a roundabout detour was to ensure that no one could ever link Shang Feifan the arms dealer to China. Even if certain people harbored suspicions, as long as there was no hard evidence, he and China remained completely unconnected.

Time on the airplane was excruciatingly dull. Shang Feifan desperately wanted to log into the game, but he restrained himself, opting instead to pull out his laptop to handle some work matters.

Having spent so many years operating in the shadows, he had forged connections with countless individuals across official and unofficial channels.

These people, along with their friends and friends of friends, formed a massive network. Individuals within this network could assist and mutually benefit one another by posting tasks.

Shang Feifan was currently utilizing this sprawling network of personal connections, throwing heavy sums of money around to hunt down information regarding *Starry River Hegemony*, the very first hundred-percent holographic game.

Quite a few people knew of this game, yet up to this day, not a single soul had reported receiving any substantive intelligence about it.

In the real world, this was virtually impossible.

A game—especially a large-scale multiplayer online holographic game—required official authorization just to be pushed out, even during closed beta testing, which naturally encompassed a variety of mandatory certifications.

Things like business licenses, software copyright registrations, game publication numbers, operational filings, and internet business licenses, among others.

Yet not a single person across his worldwide network of connections could provide any relevant news.

No matter how capable that game developer was at keeping secrets, in the modern internet age, it was impossible to conceal every necessary piece of information.

Faced with this, Shang Feifan was forced to reach a conclusion: unless the holographic game *Starry River Hegemony* had never been legally registered in the first place.

He then shifted his investigation to the game helmets, starting his search with their delivery service providers.

This yielded a slight lead.

First, regional distribution companies received the cargo, then dispatched them to individual players based on the addresses marked on the goods.

Tracing these helmets backward to find where they had been shipped from to the regional distribution companies, layer by layer, he ultimately tracked them down to a dockside warehouse in a war-torn country.

The pair of brothers managing the warehouse pocketed the cash and informed investigators that every single helmet had been dispatched from right here.

As for themselves, they had simply received an email one day stating that they had been hired for the jobs of warehouse manager and shipping clerk.

Since the two brothers were actively sending out resumes and looking for work, they hadn't suspected much. They *had* indeed been searching for warehouse positions, and upon seeing that the salary and welfare benefits mentioned in the email far exceeded their expectations, they packed their bags without the slightest hesitation and moved to this workplace.

Their job duties were simple: according to the email's instructions, open the warehouse doors at the designated times, take out the pre-packaged helmets, box them up, print out the shipping addresses sent to them via email, stick them onto the cardboard boxes, and ship the helmets out.

Because the helmets looked utterly unremarkable, and they had no desire to lose such a well-paying and remarkably easy job, they never bothered to mess with the helmets, let alone dig into their origins or the identity of their employer.

The trail of the helmets went cold right here.

Investigators still had no clue how those helmets had managed to enter that warehouse in the first place.

And shortly after investigators discovered the warehouse, that pair of brothers received a dismissal email stating that their employment had come to an end.

When they investigated the owner of the warehouse, they discovered it belonged to someone who had been dead for four or five years without having their identity deregistered.

The deceased had no children, and his sole inheritance upon death was a single house and this warehouse.

The man had most likely died of a sudden illness, and his corpse was still lying right there in his own basement.

Investigators tracked down the deceased's residence and discovered his remains in the basement. The corpse was face down, with the upper body still draped across the basement steps—looking precisely like someone who had collapsed and died from a sudden medical emergency.

Because the body was in the basement, the enclosed space had stifled the stench of putrefaction, and the nearby neighbors weren't particularly fastidious people; even when they caught a faint whiff of something, they hadn't paid it much mind.

Coupled with the fact that the deceased had no surviving relatives, and the internal administration of that country was rather chaotic, no one had ever noticed that this person had passed away, let alone that the warehouse under his name was being actively utilized.

Shang Feifan then investigated the email address that had sent instructions to the two brothers, tracing it back and forth until it led to a public library.

Right now, Shang Feifan had operatives staking out that library, though no issues had been uncovered as of yet.

Additionally, Shang Feifan's primary focus was pinned on the account that deposited funds into the brothers' bank accounts.

That account belonged to a certain international bank—a 'forgotten' account that hadn't seen a single outgoing or incoming transfer in over ten years.

Every bank had accounts like this: either the account holder died suddenly without leaving a will in time, or the account holder fell ill, forgot about it, or lost the ability to manage their assets. There were also missing persons, criminals, frozen funds...

For an account left untouched for ten years to suddenly resume transfers caught the bank's attention as well.

However, they later discovered it was simply a scheduled transfer designated as a salary payment, and the personal online banking had even gone through facial re-verification to confirm the identity of the account holder. Assuming the owner had finally remembered this stash of money, the bank didn't pry any further.

Through personal channels, Shang Feifan managed to acquire the information of this account holder. Just as he had anticipated from the start, the account owner had gone missing long ago.

Curiously enough, neither the account holder's wife nor children had any idea he possessed such a secret account, which drove the wife to become increasingly convinced that her husband hadn't gone missing at all, but had deliberately hidden his assets with the intention of divorcing her.

As for why he vanished right before the divorce, or why the asset-shifted account had sat untouched for a decade, it remained an unanswered mystery.

The wife had called the police—not to find her missing husband, but to reclaim the money locked within that account.

Presently, the case was under active investigation.

Unwilling to become entangled in this mess, Shang Feifan vanished completely off the grid; no matter how thoroughly the police investigated, they could never track down the lawyer who had stepped forward.

Thus, while it seemed he hadn't reaped many clues, a single answer was gradually rising to the surface through the fragments he *had* gathered.

Why would such a magnificent, peerless holographic game need to manifest through such mysterious means?

What kind of person couldn't bear to show their face in public?

And what kind of person possessed such extraordinary methods?

Shang Feifan already harbored a suspicion in his heart; he simply needed a few factual pieces of evidence to verify it.

With just one hour left before arriving at his destination, N City,

Shang Feifan opened his email client. He wasn't connected to the network; these email contents had already been downloaded beforehand.

His mouse hovered over an email sent to him eleven years ago.

In truth, long before he first bumped into that person, he had already captured the man's facial features using a micro-camera on his person.

Shortly after parting ways with the man, driven by a sudden urge to understand him better, he had asked a favor to search the passport database of Chinese nationals stationed at the embassy in Italy. Through a facial match, he quickly retrieved the man's identity information.

After his friend sent him the compiled investigative profile, he sat before his computer for a long while, ultimately failing to open that email.

Eleven years!

Never in his wildest dreams had he imagined that eleven years later, he would actually choose to click open this email.

He had already read the contents before boarding the plane; otherwise, he wouldn't have purchased a ticket to N City.

Shang Feifan clicked his mouse, reopening the email.

Attached to the email was an ID photograph.

The moment he clicked it, the image sprang into view right before his eyes.

It was that exact same man—with a youthful face, yet lacking the restlessness and sharp edge typical of youth. His smile was gentle, though it distinctly lacked the proactive drive and vitality native to young men.

At a glance, his facial features seemed faintly reminiscent of Bushuai's. But upon closer inspection, one would realize the differences between them were vast.

Clicking open the next attachment, he found the detailed personal background information of the person in the photograph.
"""

chunks.chapterTitle: 第84章 带我老婆回家 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
郎沐，三十岁，华夏N城人，飞跃重工汽车制造集团下属发动机研发公司的AI系统工程师……

商非凡盯着资料上的名字，眼神有点可怕。

郎沐。

拉斐尔郎沐。

在不帅说出那句话后，他就有了预感。

但是！当他看到这个名字时，他脖颈和手臂上的汗毛还是全都倒竖了起来。

如果郎沐真的是不帅……

其实已经不用怀疑。

在不帅对他说出游戏、玩家和下线这些词语后，他就不可能是纯种的兽人世界的土著。

他记得很清楚他只对不帅说过游戏和数据这两个词。

当然也不排除法德尔大陆和兽人大陆已经出现游戏和玩家的概念，甚至已经有了网络游戏。

但不帅当时对他说的是华夏语，最标准的官方发音，想要错听都不可能。

恍然间，时间过得飞快。

等商非凡回过神，空姐已经在通知飞机即将降落。

商非凡没有行李可取，背着单肩背包按照机场指示牌找到地下停车场。

在那里他打了个电话。

对方告诉他车牌号码，让商非凡在原地等候。

不到十分钟，一辆黑色越野车慢慢驶近商非凡。

商非凡拉开车门坐进副驾驶。

车门刚关上，越野车就丝滑地往前流入车群。

“你怎么弄了一个老头的样子？”魏轲叼着烟一边转动方向盘一边含糊不清地说。

商非凡：“我要的东西呢？”

魏轲翻了个白眼，按灭香烟：“你昨天晚上才打电话给我，现在就要我交货，你以为我……”

“就用电脑查个资料有多难？”商非凡不耐烦地说。

“你以为全国信息都是互通的吗？我压根不在N城工作，为了你的事，老子不但要找人情帮忙，还特地请假跑来接你。你他么就对我这态度？”魏轲对老兄弟凶狠竖起中指。

“六星级自助餐一顿。”

“呸！你以为老子这么好打发？还是你想坑老子？”

“那买只N城特产盐水鸭请你啃？”

“……我以后要是再帮你，我就是狗！”

“小龙虾随便吃。”

魏轲挑眉，手指一转：“在后面文件袋里，你自己拿。”

商非凡转身，伸手从后座上拽过文件袋。

有时候纸质资料交付反而比电子的形式更安全。

商非凡手指快速绕开线头，打开文件袋，倒出里面的文件。

只有两张纸。

商非凡在心里一遍遍告诉自己：我知道的，我已经预料到了，所以不管看到什么都不用惊讶。

唰！两张A4资料纸翻到正面。

商非凡的目光在资料上快速浏览，等看到一个明晃晃的名词时，就算已有心理准备，他还是感到刺眼。

“好端端的，怎么突然要查这个人？大佬你还为此特意回国？对方犯了什么事？我看过他的资料，他以前去过意国，难不成他和那边的……”

“别乱猜。和公事无关，只是私事。”

魏轲撇嘴，表情摆明不信，方向盘一打，驶出机场收费处，拐向高速。

商非凡正在看郎沐的死因。

【死因：他杀】

【凶手：朗岸】

商非凡一看到凶手和郎沐同样的姓氏，就感到不妙。再看案件详细。

不到五百字，他看了足足有十分钟。

魏轲在一边偷瞄他，被老商的表情有点吓到。

“你认识他？”

过了好一会儿，才听到老商回：“嗯。”

“关系很好？”

“我老婆。”

轰——！

魏轲一脚油门差点踩到底，眼看就要撞上前面的车屁股，又赶紧松开油门踩刹车，再打灯转向转到路边，停下车辆打开双闪。

商非凡无视魏轲盯着他的不可思议的双眼，只继续看着那内容不多的资料。

“你老婆？你什么时候有的老婆？为什么我们没有一个人知道？不对！我看过资料，那个郎沐，他明明是男的！男的！带把的！”

“我又没要睡你，你那么激动干什么？”

“艹！”魏轲猛拍方向盘。手指到处摸，摸到一包烟，从里面胡乱抽出一根塞进嘴里。

啪嚓啪嚓，魏轲点燃香烟，深深吸了一口。

“要来吗？”魏轲叼着烟问。

商非凡摆摆手，把两张纸重新装回文件袋里。

“你刚才没开玩笑？你说真的？”魏轲仍旧不敢置信。

商非凡抬起头：“你看我像开玩笑吗？”

魏轲半晌没能给出答案。

商非凡打开手机地图APP，“去铁衣寺公墓。”

魏轲：“……你不会不知道他已经死了吧？”

“昨晚之前。”

魏轲低骂一声。他知道老商在说什么，他在说昨晚之前他都不知道他老婆已经死了，还是被人杀死的。

而等老商得到消息，就立刻让人调查，又立即冒险回国。

魏轲没有再详细追问，他脑中已经自动编织出一个关于等待到白头再相守的凄美爱情约定。

两人性别相同，相爱本来就不容易。

偏偏老商因为工作缘故，不得不常年待在国外，甚至因为某些事情，有家也归不得。

嫂子……那个郎沐很可能不知道老商的真实工作，只能留在国内长期等待。

也许两人已经做好约定，等到两人年岁大了，等到老商可以没有任何顾忌地回国的那一天，他们会借口互相照顾而住到一起，共同相扶到老。

谁想，天有不测风云，郎沐就那么倒霉，还没有等到老商回来的那一天，就被人杀死，还是被同父异母的亲兄弟杀死。

老商在国外那么拼，他心中的支撑是不是就是郎沐？

可现在等待他的人却先一步成了黄土……

魏轲鼻头一酸，借着夹烟的动作掩饰地抹了抹眼角。

商非凡：“你哭屁啊！我老婆在另外一个世界活得好好的，我很快就会去找他。”

“别啊，老大！”魏轲都小抽泣了。他这个人看着凶，但感情特别充沛。

“……我不是要去寻死。”

魏轲：我不信！老伏已经几次跟我们唠叨说你心理疾病严重需要看医生！

以前他一心以为老商心理不正常是因为工作缘故。

实际上做那份工作的，几乎没有心理正常的，很多人都需要长时间接受心理按摩师的调养。

更多人因为扛不住压力，不得不做个两三年就转职。

可老商却把这份工作做得那么出色，出色到有家都回不得了。

现在他明白了，老商哪里是被工作熬出来的心理不正常，他根本就是想老婆想出精神病了！

现在老大老婆死了，老大他不会真的……疯死吧？

“行了！赶紧开车。我时间紧急。”商非凡催促。

魏轲暗中打了个激灵，打算找几个老兄弟好好聊聊，尤其要让老伏多盯着点某人。

一个小时后，两人在铁衣寺停车场下车。

魏轲能力很强，资料上连郎沐的坟墓门牌号码都有。

在往山坡走的路上，很久没有说话的商非凡突然问道：“朗岸被放出来了吗？”

魏轲神经一路紧绷，听到商非凡询问，条件反射地回答：“我现在就去查。”
chunks.englishText:
Lang Mu, thirty years old, a native of City N in Huaxia, AI systems engineer at the engine R&D company under the Feiyue Heavy Industry Automobile Manufacturing Group...

Shang Feifan stared at the name on the document, his gaze somewhat terrifying.

Lang Mu.

Raphael Lang Mu.

Ever since Bu Shuai uttered those words, he had harbored a premonition.

Yet! When he actually saw this name, the hairs on the back of his neck and arms still stood completely on end.

If Lang Mu truly was Bu Shuai...

In truth, there was no longer any need for doubt.

After Bu Shuai spoke words to him like "game," "players," and "logging off," it was impossible for the other party to be a pure-bred native of the Orc World.

He remembered very clearly that he had only ever mentioned the words "game" and "data" to Bu Shuai.

Of course, one could not entirely rule out the possibility that the concepts of games and players—or even online games—had already emerged on the Fader Continent and the Orc Continent.

However, the language Bu Shuai had used with him back then was Huaxia Chinese, spoken with the most standard official pronunciation; it was utterly impossible to have misheard it.

In a flash, time flew by.

By the time Shang Feifan snapped out of his thoughts, a flight attendant was already announcing the plane's impending landing.

Shang Feifan had no luggage to claim. Slinging his single-shoulder backpack over his shoulder, he followed the airport's directional signs down to the underground parking lot.

There, he made a call.

The person on the other end gave him a license plate number and told Shang Feifan to wait right where he was.

In less than ten minutes, a black off-road vehicle slowly approached Shang Feifan.

Shang Feifan pulled open the door and climbed into the passenger seat.

The moment the door closed, the SUV smoothly merged forward into the stream of traffic.

"Why the hell did you dig up the look of some old codger?" Wei Ke muttered indistinctly, a cigarette clamped between his lips as he turned the steering wheel.

Shang Feifan: "Where is the stuff I asked for?"

Wei Ke rolled his eyes and stubbed out his cigarette: "You only called me last night, and now you want me to deliver the goods immediately? Do you think I..."

"How hard is it to just look up some info on a computer?" Shang Feifan said impatiently.

"You think all information across the country is seamlessly interconnected? I don't even work in City N! For your sake, I not only had to call in favors, but I even took special leave just to come pick you up. And this is the damn attitude you give me?" Wei Ke fiercely thrust his middle finger at his old buddy.

"One six-star buffet dinner."

"Bah! You think I'm that cheap to buy off? Or are you trying to screw me over?"

"Then how about buying a specialty City N salted duck for you to chew on?"

"—If I ever help you out again, I'm a dog!"

"All-you-can-eat crawfish."

Wei Ke raised an eyebrow, his fingers flicking the steering wheel: "It's in the document envelope in the back. Get it yourself."

Shang Feifan turned around, reached out from the back seat, and yanked the document envelope into his hands.

Sometimes, physical paper documents were actually safer than electronic formats.

Shang Feifan quickly unwrapped the string tied around the clasp, opened the envelope, and tipped out the contents.

There were only two sheets of paper.

Shang Feifan told himself over and over in his heart: I already know. I've already anticipated this, so no matter what I see, there is no need to be surprised.

Swish! The two sheets of A4 data paper were flipped to the front.

Shang Feifan's gaze swept rapidly over the documents. When his eyes caught a glaringly obvious term, even though he was mentally prepared, a harsh sting still pierced his vision.

"Out of nowhere, why'd you suddenly want to look up this guy? Big Boss, you even flew all the way back to the country just for this? What crime did he commit? I looked at his file; he went to Italy before. Could it be that he and those guys over..."

"Don't guess blindly. It has nothing to do with official business—just personal matters."

Wei Ke curled his lips, his expression clearly showing he didn't believe a word of it. He spun the steering wheel, drove out of the airport toll booth, and merged onto the highway.

Shang Feifan was currently reading about the cause of Lang Mu's death.

[Cause of Death: Homicide]

[Assailant: Lang An]

The moment Shang Feifan saw that the killer shared the same surname as Lang Mu, a bad premonition gripped him. He read on into the case details.

It was less than five hundred words long, yet he stared at it for a full ten minutes.

Wei Ke glanced sideways at him, somewhat spooked by Old Shang's expression.

"You know him?"

After quite a while, Old Shang's reply finally came: "Mn."

"Close relationship?"

"My wife."

Boom—!

Wei Ke slammed his foot down so hard he nearly floored the accelerator. Seeing that he was about to plow straight into the rear of the car ahead, he frantically lifted his foot to brake, flicked on his turn signal, pulled over to the roadside, and hit the hazard lights.

Shang Feifan ignored Wei Ke's incredulous, wide-eyed stare and continued reading through the sparse documentation.

"Your wife? When the hell did you get a wife? Why doesn't any of us know about this? No, wait! I read the file—that Lang Mu, he's clearly a man! A man! With a dangling piece!"

"I'm not asking to sleep with you, why are you getting so worked up?"

"Fuck!" Wei Ke slammed a heavy hand against the steering wheel. His fingers groped around blindly until they brushed against a pack of cigarettes, from which he savagely yanked one out and shoved it into his mouth.

Click, click. Wei Ke lit the cigarette and took a deep, heavy drag.

"Want one?" Wei Ke asked, the cigarette clamped between his teeth.

Shang Feifan waved a hand and slid the two sheets of paper back into the document envelope.

"You weren't joking just now? You're serious?" Wei Ke still found it hard to believe.

Shang Feifan raised his head: "Do I look like I'm joking?"

Wei Ke couldn't spit out an answer for the longest time.

Shang Feifan opened the map app on his phone: "Drive to Tieyi Temple Cemetery."

Wei Ke: "...You can't possibly not know he's already dead, right?"

"Before last night."

Wei Ke let out a low curse. He knew what Old Shang meant; he meant that until last night, he hadn't even known his wife was dead—let alone murdered by someone else.

And the moment Old Shang got the news, he immediately had people investigate, then risked everything to rush back to the country.

Wei Ke didn't press for further details; his brain had already automatically woven a poignant, tragic romance story of waiting until their hair turned white to be reunited.

The two of them were of the same sex, and loving each other was already difficult enough.

Yet because of his work, Old Shang had no choice but to stay abroad year-round, unable to even return home due to certain constraints.

Sister-in-law... that Lang Mu probably didn't even know Old Shang's true line of work, forced to remain in China for a long-term vigil.

Perhaps the two of them had made a pact: once they grew old, once Old Shang could return to the country without any lingering apprehensions, they would use the excuse of taking care of each other to move in together and support one another through their twilight years.

Who could have foreseen that heaven is fickle and storms arise unexpectedly? Lang Mu was so profoundly unlucky that before he could even wait for Old Shang to return, he was murdered—and by his own half-brother, no less.

With Old Shang fighting so desperately abroad, wasn't Lang Mu the very pillar of support sustaining him in his heart?

Yet now, the person waiting for him had turned to dust a step ahead...

Wei Ke felt a sudden sting in the bridge of his nose and used the motion of holding his cigarette to covertly wipe the corner of his eye.

Shang Feifan: "What the hell are you crying for? My wife is living just fine in another world; I'm going to go find him very soon."

"Don't do it, Boss!" Wei Ke was practically letting out little whimpers. He might look fierce on the outside, but he was exceptionally emotional on the inside.

"...I'm not going to go kill myself."

Wei Ke: I don't believe you! Old Fu has already nagged us several times about how your psychological disorder is severe and you need to see a doctor!

In the past, he used to blindly think that Old Shang's mental abnormality stemmed from his line of work.

In truth, practically no one who did that kind of work had a normal psychological state; many required long-term maintenance and conditioning from psychological therapists.

Even more people couldn't bear the pressure and were forced to transfer to other jobs after two or three years.

Yet Old Shang had performed that job with such excellence—excellence to the point where he couldn't even return to his own home.

Now, he finally understood. Old Shang's mental unsteadiness wasn't wrung out of him by his job at all; he had literally gone psycho from missing his wife!

Now that the Boss's wife was dead, wouldn't the Boss actually... go crazy and die?

"Alright, step on the gas. I'm pressed for time." Shang Feifan urged.

Wei Ke gave an inward jolt, resolving to have a good chat with some of the old brothers—especially making sure Old Fu kept a close eye on a certain someone.

An hour later, the two of them got out of the car in the parking lot of Tieyi Temple.

Wei Ke was exceptionally capable; the file even listed the exact plot and niche number of Lang Mu's grave.

On the way walking up the hillside, Shang Feifan, who had been silent for a long time, suddenly asked: "Has Lang An been released?"

Wei Ke's nerves had been strung tight all the way. Hearing Shang Feifan's query, he replied by reflex: "I'll check right now."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第84章 带我老婆回家 (Part 3)
chunks.chineseText:
说完，他真的打电话找监狱系统的人帮他调查了。

郎沐的坟墓到了。

商非凡看到了熟悉的证件照，就是之前他在飞机上看到的那一张。

从墓碑上的刻字来看，为郎沐收尸立碑的人是他亲生父亲。

呵！商非凡发出一声极淡极淡的冷笑。

魏轲站在一边，心里特别不是滋味。

就算郎沐是男的，完全出乎他们对于“嫂子”这个角色的设想，但是……那是商老大喜欢的人啊。

换言之，郎沐就是自己人。

“那个案情描述说的不是很详细，给我两天时间，我会给你最详细的调查报告。”

商非凡沉默一会儿，“好。辛苦你。”

“喂！这种事说什么辛苦。”魏轲心里更不是滋味。

这他么都是什么破事！

他调查前再怎么也没想到……嗐！

商非凡跟魏轲借了打火机，在郎沐的墓碑前把文件袋里连同里面的两页纸都烧了。

上面的内容他已经全部记下来。

“走吧。”

“去哪？”

“去附近的五金店，我要买把凿子和锤子。”

“老大，你想干嘛？”魏轲迟疑。

商非凡淡淡说：“不干什么。带我老婆骨灰回家，他不喜欢这里。”
chunks.englishText:
CHINESE SOURCE TEXT (第84章 带我老婆回家 (Part 3)):
"""
Speaking, he actually made a phone call to someone in the prison system to help him look into it.

Lang Mu's grave had arrived.

Shang Feifan saw the familiar ID photo—it was the exact same one he had seen earlier on the plane.

Judging from the engraving on the tombstone, the person who had collected Lang Mu's remains and erected the monument for him was his biological father.

Heh! Shang Feifan let out a cold, faint, feather-light laugh.

Wei Ke stood off to the side, feeling a terrible, churning knot in his heart.

Even though Lang Mu was a man—completely shattering any preconceived notions they had about the role of a "sister-in-law"—nevertheless... that was the person Old Shang loved.

In other words, Lang Mu was one of their own.

"That case summary wasn't very detailed. Give me two days, and I'll get you the most comprehensive investigative report."

Shang Feifan fell silent for a moment. "Alright. Hard work for you."

"Hey! What are you talking about hard work for this kind of thing." Wei Ke felt even more wretched inside.

What kind of bloody mess was all this!

Before he started investigating, no matter how he racked his brain, he never could have imagined... sigh!

Shang Feifan borrowed a lighter from Wei Ke, and right in front of Lang Mu's tombstone, he set fire to the document envelope along with the two sheets of paper inside.

He had already memorized every single word written upon them.

"Let's go."

"Where to?"

"To a nearby hardware store. I need to buy a chisel and a hammer."

"Boss, what are you trying to do?" Wei Ke hesitated.

Shang Feifan said indifferently: "Nothing much. Taking my wife's ashes home. He doesn't like it here."
"""

chunks.chineseText:
第85章 甥婿上门

虎不帅侧头看了看躺在简易铺盖上睡得死沉的商非凡。

在风洞山通道内他说了那几个词语后，两人就像是有了一种默契，他们没有互相询问，就这么一路沉默着绕到莫约镇西边荒原，找到那群休息的迁徙兽人。

那些兽人不知道是出于警惕，还是旅途疲累，彼此都没说什么重要的话。

只领头的青壮和一名老人提到迪莉娅夫人，担心迪莉娅夫人不肯见他们。

老人只让青壮耐心等待，多余的话什么都没说。

虎不帅打算在这边留上一晚上，窃-听本来就是需要花时间的事，极少会有那种窃-听者刚来就能听到重要对话的时候。

商非凡自然想要留下来陪他。

等天色彻底暗下来，两人用了一点干粮和水，商非凡就很坦然地说他要睡觉。

虎不帅秒懂，让他放心睡。

作为当地人，不帅选择的地点很隐蔽，也很安全。

他们待的这个半地穴就是莫约镇猎人特意挖出来的安全洞，用来观察和躲避荒原中的猛兽。

不帅放空自己的大脑，让自己的注意力全都集中在那群迁徙兽人那里。

凌晨四点，正是夜色最深，也是万籁俱寂的时候。

就连喜欢夜行的野兽这时候也会结束游荡和狩猎。

天上七个月亮全部消失，连星星都藏在了云层后。

天空颜色有点泛红，不帅猜测明天九成会下雨，还不是小雨。

那群迁徙兽人也很安静，偶尔能听到有兽人做梦的呓语声，负责守夜的兽人坐在火堆边，偶尔会起身巡逻。

太-安静，让他都能清楚听到火堆木柴被烧出来的噼啪声。

不帅有点走神，眼睛不由自主瞟向身边。

那人的侧脸很立体，只要审美没问题，绝大多数人看到他大概都会说一声超帅。

商的英俊和帅气属于很硬气的那种，还有点黑暗，更带着战火之气。

这也是他会猜测商不是兵就是匪的原因，且不是普通的兵和匪，而是长期待在硝烟战火中，多次见过血和尸体的老兵和恶匪。

以前的不帅绝对看不出这点，顶多会觉得这人不太好惹。

但经历过第二世，亲身经历并参与了大量战斗，最后也算战死的他，已经能清晰分辨出谁生活在安逸的环境中，谁又走在危险的边缘。

他被这个人吸引了吗？

虎不帅迷茫，他也不知道。

但他知道他已经不再排斥这个人，甚至能很自然地守在熟睡的对方身边，半点不觉得别扭和尴尬。

就算是关系特别好的好友，也极少有人能做到这一点，不信试试？

人睡着时看起来毫无防备，其实会自然释放出一种排他磁场，这是历经无数年刻印在基因中的本能。人们渴望和需要睡眠，但人们也知道当他们睡着时也是最危险的。

而醒着的人会无意识地接收到这种排他磁场，会自然而然地选择远离，比如去隔壁的房间，或者坐得更远一点。

除非关系特别亲密，彼此之间极为信任的情况下，才会无视或消融这种磁场。比如夫妻、父母与孩子。

走一步看一步吧。不帅无奈地想。

“啊啊啊——！”

前方营地突然传出刺耳的惨叫。

这声惨叫打破了原有的安寂，整个营地的兽人似乎都被惊醒。

不帅听到奔跑声，听到焦急的询问声。

“老样子，他们又发作了。我们该怎么办？让他们沉睡的药物已经不够了！”

“我去找迪莉娅！这次无论他们说什么，我都要见到她！”

“别去！你这是想要结仇吗？”

“可是我父亲和叔叔，还有卡罗尔他们都已经挺不住了！”

“呃啊啊啊——！”

更多更刺耳的惨叫响起。

这是好几个不同的人在同时惨叫。

他们叫的就像是正在被剥皮，又像是正在被缓慢的五马分尸。

那种绝对会撕破喉咙的惨叫，让听到的人都能替他们感到极致痛楚。

“如果这是我们家的血脉诅咒，谁也无法逃脱，为什么迪莉娅就能摆脱？”属于青壮的声音压低声音怒吼。

“她能好好地活到现在，她一定有办法逃离家族的血脉诅咒！她必须救我们，她不能这么躲着不见面……”

“为什么不能？凭什么不能？”老人的声音很冷漠。

“当年，迪莉娅父亲死于非命，母亲失踪，她们姐妹也曾来求过我们，希望我们能帮忙查清她们父亲的死因，还有找到她们失踪的母亲，但我们做了什么？”

“我们什么都没做。不，我们做的事比什么都没做更残忍。”

老人声音变得略微尖锐：“当年就是你的亲祖父逼迫安妮塔和迪莉娅这对姐妹，逼迫她们分别嫁给她们一点都不想嫁的男人。逼得那对姐妹不得不逃离家族！而那时安妮塔才十六岁，迪莉娅更才只有十四岁！”

青壮沉默了一会儿，“我祖父当年那么做，你们这些族老也没有反对。”

“是。所以今日我们也没脸来求她们。如果不是实在没有人救我们，我又怎么会同意让你带领全部族人千里迢迢来找迪莉娅？”

“然后呢？就因为当年族里没有……帮她们，现在我们也只能在这里等死，哪怕明知道迪莉娅有办法解决血脉诅咒？”

“这只是一个猜测。说不定迪莉娅也不知道……”

“她知道！安妮塔死了，但她还活得好好的！这就是证据。”

虎不帅一惊。什么意思？难道原身母亲不是故意拖死自己，而是死于血脉诅咒？

原身母亲到底隐瞒了他多少事情？

对方为什么会把他的灵魂从法德尔大陆召来？

为什么要让他顶替原身？

归根究底，对方到底希望他做什么？

虎不帅轻轻吐气。

自从认识商非凡后，他发现他的两世穿越，尤其是第三世，简直就跟洋葱一样，剥了一层还有一层，谁也不知道一层层的外皮下隐藏着怎样的内芯。

那边营地里越发混乱，因为缺乏安抚手段，那些兽人没办法让受到诅咒折磨的族人安生下来，导致惨叫声也一直没有消失。

好些兽人都在陪着哭泣，也有人像没头苍蝇一样地跑来跑去，更有人在暴躁地发火怒骂。

这么大的动静自然也惊动了莫约镇的守镇者。

虎不帅又侧耳细听了一会儿，没再听到其他能称得上重要的消息，他决定回去镇子，先找他姨父问一问。

不帅推了推熟睡如死人的商非凡，并小声叫他的名字。

商睡着前曾特意跟他说：如果有急事就叫醒他，用精神力叫，他会醒得更快。

不帅不禁猜测商那边是不是有一个随身终端，就算离开游戏头盔或游戏仓，依然能接收到游戏世界的“信号”。

商非凡啪地睁开眼睛，没有半点熟睡者醒来时的慵懒和迟钝。

不帅：这是说破了干脆不装了吗？

商非凡坐起身：“怎么了？有什么紧急事情发生？”

“我听到一些消息，需要找我姨父和小姨确认。”

商非凡跳起来：“那走吧。”

CHINESE SOURCE TEXT (第85章 甥婿上门 (Part 1)):
"""
Chapter 85: The Nephew-in-Law Comes Calling

Hu Bushuai turned his head to glance at Shang Feifan, who was sleeping soundly as if dead on the makeshift bed.

Back inside the Wind Cave Mountain passageway, after he spoke those few phrases, it was as if an unspoken tacit understanding had formed between the two of them. Without questioning one another, they had remained silent all the way around to the wasteland west of Moyue Town, locating that group of resting, migrating orcs.

Whether out of vigilance or sheer travel fatigue, those orcs exchanged no words of any great importance.

Only the leading young adult and an old man mentioned Madam Delia, expressing concern that Madam Delia might refuse to see them.

The old man simply told the young adult to wait patiently, saying nothing more.

Hu Bushuai intended to stay here for the night; eavesdropping inherently required time, and it was exceedingly rare for an eavesdropper to stumble upon crucial dialogues the moment they arrived.

Naturally, Shang Feifan wanted to stay and accompany him.

As day faded completely into night, the two of them consumed a bit of dry rations and water, after which Shang Feifan stated very frankly that he was going to sleep.

Hu Bushuai understood instantly, telling him to rest easy.

As a local, the spot chosen by Bushuai was both well-hidden and secure.

The semi-dugout they stayed in was a safety cave specifically excavated by Moyue Town hunters, meant for observing and evading ferocious beasts roaming the wasteland.

Bushuai emptied his mind, concentrating all his focus on that group of migrating orcs.

Four in the morning—the deepest part of the night, when all creation lay in absolute stillness.

Even nocturnal beasts would finish their prowling and hunting by this hour.

All seven moons in the sky had vanished, and even the stars hid behind layers of clouds.

The sky possessed a faintly reddish hue; Bushuai guessed there was a ninety percent chance it would rain tomorrow, and not a light drizzle either.

That group of migrating orcs was also dead quiet. Occasionally, one could hear a orc muttering in a dream; the orcs assigned to keep watch sat by the campfire, standing up from time to time to patrol.

It was so quiet that he could clearly hear the crackle of firewood burning in the flames.

Bushuai's mind drifted slightly, his eyes involuntarily glancing toward his side.

The man's profile possessed sharp, chiseled contours; as long as one's aesthetic judgment wasn't broken, the vast majority of people laying eyes on him would likely exclaim that he was drop-dead handsome.

Shang's handsomeness and striking features belonged to a very rugged breed, tinged with a touch of darkness and reeking of the fires of war.

This was precisely why he had guessed that Shang was either a soldier or a brigand—and not an ordinary soldier or bandit either, but a veteran and hardened criminal who had spent prolonged periods amidst gunsmoke and warfare, witnessing blood and corpses time and time again.

In the past, Bushuai absolutely would not have been able to discern this, at most thinking the man wasn't someone to be trifled with.

Yet, having gone through a second lifetime, having personally experienced and partaken in massive battles, and ultimately perishing in combat himself, he was now fully capable of clearly distinguishing who lived in an environment of comfort and who walked on the razor's edge of danger.

Had he been drawn to this person?

Hu Bushuai felt a sense of bewilderment; he didn't know either.

Yet he knew that he no longer felt any repulsion toward this man. He could even naturally stand guard by the sleeping form of the other party without feeling the slightest bit awkward or out of place.

Even among exceptionally close friends, very few could achieve this—if you don't believe it, try it out yourself!

When a person sleeps, they appear utterly defenceless, but in reality, they naturally emit an exclusionary magnetic field—an instinct branded into their genes over countless eons. People yearn for and require sleep, yet they also know that sleep renders them most vulnerable.

Meanwhile, a waking person unconsciously registers this exclusionary magnetic field and naturally chooses to keep their distance, such as moving to an adjacent room or sitting further away.

Unless the relationship is exceptionally intimate and mutual trust is absolute, this field will be ignored or dissolved—such as between spouses, or between parents and children.

*We'll cross that bridge when we come to it,* Bushuai thought helplessly.

"Ah-ah-ah—!"

A piercing, agonizing shriek suddenly erupted from the camp ahead.

This scream shattered the original dead silence, and orcs throughout the entire camp seemed jolted awake.

Bushuai heard the sound of running feet, followed by anxious inquiries.

"Same as before, their affliction is flaring up again. What should we do? The medicine to make them sleep is already running out!"

"I'm going to find Delia! This time, no matter what they say, I'm going to see her!"

"Don't go! Are you trying to make an enemy of her?"

"But my father, my uncle, and Carol—they can't hold on much longer!"

"Urgh-ah-ah-ah—!"

More and even more piercing screams rang out.

These were several different individuals screaming in agony simultaneously.

Their cries sounded as though they were being flayed alive, or perhaps slowly torn apart by chariots.

That kind of scream—one that would undoubtedly shred vocal cords—made anyone who heard it feel the peak of excruciating pain by proxy.

"If this is our family's bloodline curse, and no one can escape it, why is it that Delia was able to break free?" A young adult's voice dropped to a low, angry roar.

"She's able to live safely right up to now, so she must have a way to escape the family's bloodline curse! She has to save us; she can't just hide like this and refuse to see us..."

"Why can't she? What right do you have to say she shouldn't?" The old man's voice was frigid.

"Back then, Delia's father met a violent end, her mother went missing, and their sisters even came to beg us, hoping we could help investigate the cause of their father's death and find their missing mother. But what did we do?"

"We did nothing. No, what we did was far more cruel than doing nothing."

The old man's voice grew slightly sharp: "Back then, it was your own biological grandfather who forced Anita and Delia—that pair of sisters—forcing them to marry men they didn't want to marry in the slightest! He forced that pair of sisters to flee the family! And at that time, Anita was only sixteen, while Delia was merely fourteen!"

The young adult fell silent for a moment. "When my grandfather did that back then, none of you clan elders raised any objections."

"True. Therefore, today we have no face to beg them either. If not for the fact that literally no one else can save us, how could I have possibly agreed to let you lead all our clansmen thousands of miles to find Delia?"

"And then what? Just because the clan didn't... help them back then, are we just supposed to wait here and die now—even knowing full well that Delia has a way to resolve the bloodline curse?"

"That's merely a guess. Who's to say Delia even knows..."

"She knows! Anita is dead, but Delia is still alive and well! That's the proof."

Hu Bushuai gave a start. What did that mean? Could it be that the original owner's mother hadn't intentionally dragged herself to death, but had instead died from the bloodline curse?

Just how many things had the original owner's mother hidden from him?

Why did the other party summon his soul from the Fader Continent?

Why make him take the place of the original owner?

When it all boiled down to it, what on earth did the other party want him to do?

Hu Bushuai exhaled softly.

Ever since meeting Shang Feifan, he discovered that his two traversals—especially the third one—were simply like an onion; peel away one layer and there was another underneath, and no one could tell what kind of core was hidden beneath all those outer skins.

The camp over there grew increasingly chaotic. Lacking soothing methods, the orcs had no way to calm their clansmen suffering under the curse, causing the screams to persist without end.

Quite a few orcs were weeping in accompaniment, while others ran around like headless flies, and some flared up in volatile, furious curses.

A commotion of this scale naturally alarmed the town guards of Moyue Town.

Hu Bushuai leaned his ear close to listen a moment longer, but caught no further news that could be deemed important. He decided to head back to the town first and consult his uncle.

Bushuai nudged Shang Feifan, who was sleeping as soundly as a corpse, and called his name in a low voice.

Before falling asleep, Shang had specifically instructed him: If anything urgent happened, wake him up using spiritual energy, and he would wake up even faster.

Bushuai couldn't help but guess whether Shang possessed some sort of portable terminal on him, allowing him to receive "signals" from the game world even when away from his gaming helmet or gaming pod.

Shang Feifan snapped his eyes open, devoid of any of the languor or sluggishness typical of someone newly awakened from deep sleep.

Bushuai: Is this a case of "the secret's out, so I won't pretend anymore"?

Shang Feifan sat up: "What is it? Did some urgent matter happen?"

"I overhead some information. I need to find my uncle and aunt to confirm it."

Shang Feifan leaped to his feet: "Then let's go."

chunks.chineseText:
虎不帅很想问他“现实世界”那边的事情，强行忍住。

商非凡暂时也没什么重要的事需要告诉不帅。

他刚开始调查，刚买了飞机票准备回国。

只是这时他已经点开了十一年前那封邮件。

这让他看眼前的不帅老是有种在看重影的错觉。

“我只有两个小时。”商非凡垂下眼眸。

两个小时后他就要赶往机场。还要给自己留点时间做外表伪装。

虎不帅：“哦，了解。不用你陪我去找我小姨他们。我喊你，也是想你回镇子睡会更安全一些。”

商非凡也没强求，他和不帅也不争这点时间。目前对他来说最重要的事就是弄清楚郎沐是怎么死的。

嗯，都穿越了。肯定已经死了。

最好的情况也是变成植物人。

商非凡非常希望是后者，但他也知道这个可能性非常非常小。

镇长家大宅。

镇长被半夜叫醒，脸上没有丝毫怒气，反而用最快速度跑到一楼客厅。

“你听到他们说什么了？知道他们为什么要找你小姨吗？”镇长上来就问。

虎不帅起身，先行礼。

镇长摆手，让跟过来的管家赶紧给准备一些吃的喝的，两人份。

商非凡说是不陪，还是来了。

他跟不帅说好了，如果途中他到了需要下线的时间，就由不帅把他背回风洞山洞屋。

虎不帅……很想拒绝，但他心里又有一点希望商非凡能陪他一起。

只有一点点！

不帅讨厌自己这种依赖心，但他心底深处又不得不承认他很高兴商总是会想尽办法留在他身边，试图了解他的一切。

这真是一个糟糕的心理偏向。

不帅在心里用力抽打自己，表面却神色严肃地跟镇长重复了他听到的部分内容。

“家族血脉诅咒？”镇长明显很惊讶。

“你小姨从来没有跟我提过这事。”

虎不帅：“我听他们的意思，似乎我母亲……的死亡也和家族血脉诅咒有关？”

“听他们放屁！”

三个大男人一起转头看向客厅入口。

迪莉娅夫人穿着一身鲜红的睡衣就这么走入客厅。

镇长叹口气，摇铃让女仆进来。

他不是觉得他夫人穿的少，而是怕他夫人冻到！

这时镇长完全无视他自己就穿了一条睡裤的事实。

镇长一边叮嘱女仆去拿厚实衣服，一边亲自动手把客厅里的壁炉点起来。

迪莉娅夫人突然抬起修长的手指，点了点商非凡：“第二次。”

商非凡坦然：“两天内。”

镇长看妻子和商非凡打哑谜，用眼神询问虎不帅。

虎不帅做口型：当初解开诅咒需要的物品。

镇长恍然大悟。

关于商非凡，镇长也有很多事要询问自家外甥，比如这家伙不是叫诺曼霍希尔吗？怎么又改名叫商非凡？

但这时显然还是血脉诅咒这件事更重要。

迪莉娅夫人无视了商非凡，在铺着厚厚皮毛的宽椅子上坐下。

镇长理所当然地坐到自家夫人身边。

不帅和商非凡则坐到两人对面。

“那您知道家族血脉诅咒这件事吗？”虎不帅主动询问迪莉娅夫人。

迪莉娅冷笑：“知道。”

“那您也已经知道您家族的人跑来找您的事？”

“嗯。狼守什么都不会瞒我。”迪莉娅昂头。

镇长无奈又宠溺地看向妻子。

“那不见他们，也是您的意思？”

“对。”

“那您能告诉我，您为什么不愿见他们吗？原因真的就是他们说的那个？”虎不帅把他听到的内容又大致重复一遍。

迪莉娅目光转移，盯住商非凡：“下面我们要说的都是我们的家事。你是以什么身份坐在这里？”

“甥婿的身份？嗷！”商非凡捂住小腿，幽怨地瞅虎不帅。

虎不帅不看他：让你胡说八道！

商非凡：我用的词他们肯定听不懂。

迪莉娅夫人和镇长确实没听懂，因为商非凡说的是华夏语。

迪莉娅看到外甥的小动作和商非凡的表情，手指突然掐了丈夫大腿一把。

镇长忍住，按住妻子的手。

迪莉娅用审视的目光把商非凡看了一遍又一遍，如果她的眼睛会透视，商非凡的骨头大概都被她看透。

虎不帅干咳一声：“商先生他也……懂一点诅咒。”

迪莉娅看向外甥，目光像是在嘲笑：这也算是理由？

镇长似乎也想到了什么，同样开始打量商非凡，随后他眼中流露出欣慰神色。

据他了解，他这个外甥性格略微有些孤僻，自从被儿时好友坑害，就更不想再交朋友。他之前的侍卫同伴来看望他，他也没怎么亲近，反而一个劲赶人离开。

就算在莫约镇，不帅也没有什么特别亲近的人，就是对他和他小姨也同样。

没想到不帅竟然会把商非凡带回家，还愿意让他参与家族谈话，这是多大的信任？

虎不帅注意到镇长的眼神，再看到迪莉娅夫人眼中的嘲讽，他尴尬得蜷曲起手指。

可能是对现在这个身份认同感还不够高，也可能是他从来没有把原身母亲和迪莉娅夫人的家族当做自己的家族看，所以当商非凡提出要和他一起过来时，他完全没想到让一个外人知道家族秘密是多么不妥当的事情。

现在，虎不帅尴尬又充满歉意。

就算他是魂穿来的，对原身母亲家族认同感不高，但这件事已经牵涉到迪莉娅夫人，属于迪莉娅的私事。

他带商非凡过来，相当于是要让迪莉娅夫人把自己的私事告诉亲人以外的人。

换了他，他也会超级生气。

“抱歉，是我考虑不周到。我……”

“是我蛊惑了不帅，他只是希望我能帮助他小姨也就是迪莉娅夫人您。他这人不会说话，他绝对没有伤害你们的意思。你们别责怪他，我现在就走。”商非凡一眼就看出不帅在想什么，立刻打断他，主动站起来，就要离开。

迪莉娅更不爽。

这小子这语气是什么意思？

搞得像是他和不帅才是一家人，而她这个亲小姨却是个小鸡肚肠只会挑外甥刺的外人？

真的好想再揍这小子一顿！

镇长的脸部肌肉有一点点扭曲，他挚爱的亲爱的妻子又开始拧他的大腿肉。

好、好疼！

迪莉娅夫人拍拍丈夫的大腿，语气冷漠：“我让你走了吗？不过是一点狗屁倒灶的往事，有什么不能说？就算是丑事，那也是林格莱特家族，不是我！”

管家悄无声息地进来，送来了丰盛的宵夜。

管家的大女儿也给迪莉娅夫人送来了厚实的外套，辅助她穿上，又静悄悄地退下。

管家出门时还体贴地关上了客厅大门，确保里面的声音不会泄露出去。

虎不帅悄摸摸地把盘子推到商非凡面前。

迪莉娅夫人：……她是不是得庆幸她姐死得早？

镇长却笑呵呵：外甥有亲近好友了，真好。
chunks.englishText:
Hu Bushuai desperately wanted to ask him about the "real world," but forced himself to hold back.

Shang Feifan didn't have anything particularly important to tell Bushuai for the time being either.

He had only just begun his investigation and had just bought a plane ticket to return to his home country.

Except, by this point, he had already opened that email from eleven years ago.

This gave him the recurring illusion of seeing double whenever he looked at Bushuai before him.

"I only have two hours," Shang Feifan said, lowering his eyes.

In two hours, he would have to rush to the airport, leaving himself just enough time to disguise his appearance.

Hu Bushuai: "Oh, got it. You don't need to come with me to see my aunt and the mayor. I called you out mainly because I thought sleeping back in town would be safer for you."

Shang Feifan didn't insist. He and Bushuai didn't need to squabble over this bit of time. For him, the most critical task at hand was figuring out how Lang Mu had died.

Well, since he had transmigrated, he was definitely dead.

The best-case scenario would be ending up in a vegetative state.

Shang Feifan deeply hoped for the latter, though he knew the possibility was infinitesimally small.

***

The Mayor's Manor.

Woken in the middle of the night, the Mayor didn't display the slightest trace of anger. Instead, he sprinted to the first-floor living room at top speed.

"Did you hear what they said? Do you know why they're looking for your aunt?" the Mayor asked the moment he arrived.

Hu Bushuai stood up and gave a polite greeting first.

The Mayor waved his hand, ordering the butler who had followed him down to quickly prepare food and drink for two.

Though Shang Feifan had said he wouldn't tag along, he ended up coming anyway.

He had agreed with Bushuai that if his time to log off arrived along the way, Bushuai would carry him back to the wind cave on the mountain.

Hu Bushuai... desperately wanted to refuse, but deep down, a tiny part of him wished Shang Feifan would accompany him.

Just a tiny, tiny bit!

Bushuai hated his own dependency, yet in the deepest recesses of his heart, he had to admit he was glad Mr. Shang would always try every possible way to stay by his side, attempting to understand everything about him.

This was truly a terrible psychological inclination.

Bushuai gave himself a firm mental thrashing while maintaining a solemn expression as he repeated the bits of conversation he had overheard to the Mayor.

"A family bloodline curse?" The Mayor was clearly astonished.

"Your aunt has never mentioned this to me."

Hu Bushuai: "From what I gathered, it seems my mother's... death was also connected to this family bloodline curse?"

"Bullshit!"

The three grown men turned simultaneously to look at the living room entrance.

Lady Delia walked into the living room clad in a vibrant scarlet nightgown.

The Mayor sighed and rang the bell to summon a maid.

It wasn't that he thought his wife was underdressed, but rather that he was afraid she would catch a cold!

At that moment, the Mayor completely ignored the fact that he himself was wearing nothing but a pair of sleep pants.

While instructing the maid to fetch thick clothing, the Mayor personally stoked and lit the fireplace in the living room.

Lady Delia suddenly raised a slender finger and pointed at Shang Feifan. "The second time."

Shang Feifan replied composedly, "Within two days."

Seeing his wife and Shang Feifan speaking in riddles, the Mayor threw an inquiring glance at Hu Bushuai.

Hu Bushuai mouthed silently: *The items needed to break the curse back then.*

Enlightenment dawned on the Mayor.

Regarding Shang Feifan, the Mayor also had many questions for his nephew—for instance, wasn't this guy named Norman Horshill? Why had he changed his name to Shang Feifan?

But right now, the bloodline curse was clearly more urgent.

Ignoring Shang Feifan, Lady Delia sat down on a wide armchair covered in thick fur.

Naturally, the Mayor sat down beside his wife.

Bushuai and Shang Feifan sat opposite the two.

"Then do you know about this family bloodline curse?" Hu Bushuai took the initiative to ask Lady Delia.

Delia sneered. "I do."

"And you already know that members of your family came looking for you?"

"Mm. Lang Shou hides nothing from me." Delia held her head high.

The Mayor looked at his wife with helpless doting.

"And refused to meet them—was that also your decision?"

"Yes."

"Then could you tell me why you're unwilling to meet them? Is the reason truly what they claimed?" Hu Bushuai roughly summarized what he had overheard.

Delia shifted her gaze, locking onto Shang Feifan. "What we're about to discuss next is family business. In what capacity are you sitting here?"

"As your nephew-in-law? Ow!" Shang Feifan clutched his shin and looked resentfully at Hu Bushuai.

Hu Bushuai didn't look at him: *That's what you get for talking nonsense!*

Shang Feifan: *They definitely won't understand the term I used.*

Lady Delia and the Mayor indeed didn't understand, because Shang Feifan had spoken in Huaxia language.

Seeing her nephew's small action and Shang Feifan's expression, Delia suddenly pinched her husband's thigh hard.

The Mayor endured it and held his wife's hand.

Delia scrutinized Shang Feifan over and over again. If her eyes had x-ray vision, Shang Feifan's bones would likely have been picked clean by her gaze.

Hu Bushuai cleared his throat. "Mr. Shang also... knows a bit about curses."

Delia looked at her nephew, her expression mocking: *And that counts as a reason?*

The Mayor seemed to have thought of something as well, examining Shang Feifan in turn before a look of relief and gratification surfaced in his eyes.

From what he knew, his nephew had a somewhat solitary personality, and after being betrayed by his childhood friend, he was even less inclined to make friends. When his former guard companion came to visit him, he hadn't grown close either, instead repeatedly urging him to leave.

Even in Moyue Town, Bushuai had no one he was particularly close to—the same went for his relationship with the Mayor and his aunt.

Who would have thought Bushuai would actually bring Shang Feifan home and even allow him to sit in on a private family conversation? What an immense level of trust!

Hu Bushuai caught the Mayor's gaze and then saw the mockery in Lady Delia's eyes, making his fingers curl in embarrassment.

Perhaps he still lacked a strong sense of identity with his current self, or perhaps he had never viewed his original body's mother's family—or Lady Delia's family—as his own. Thus, when Shang Feifan proposed coming along, it hadn't crossed his mind how inappropriate it was to let an outsider in on family secrets.

Now, Hu Bushuai felt awkward and deeply apologetic.

Even though his soul had transmigrated here and he felt little connection to the original body's maternal family, this matter now involved Lady Delia and was her personal affair.

Bringing Shang Feifan along was equivalent to asking Lady Delia to disclose her private matters to someone outside the family.

Had he been in her shoes, he would be furious too.

"I'm sorry, I didn't think this through. I..."

"It was me who coaxed Bushuai. He only hoped I could offer help to his aunt, Lady Delia. He's not good with words, but he definitely didn't mean any harm to you. Please don't blame him—I'll leave right now." Shang Feifan saw through Bushuai's thoughts in a flash, cutting him off immediately as he stood up to take his leave.

This made Delia even more displeased.

What was with this kid's tone?

Making it sound as if he and Bushuai were a family, while she, the biological aunt, was a petty outsider who did nothing but pick on her nephew?

She really wanted to beat this kid up again!

The Mayor's facial muscles twitched slightly as his beloved, darling wife began twisting the flesh on his thigh again.

Ouch, that hurts!

Lady Delia patted her husband's thigh and said coldly, "Did I say you could leave? It's just a bunch of rotten old stories—what's so secret about it? Even if it's a disgrace, it belongs to the Linglete family, not me!"

The butler entered silently, bringing a sumptuously prepared late-night snack.

The butler's eldest daughter also brought a thick coat for Lady Delia, helping her put it on before quietly taking her leave.

Upon stepping out, the butler thoughtfully closed the living room door to ensure no sound would leak out.

Hu Bushuai stealthily pushed a plate toward Shang Feifan.

Lady Delia: ...Should she consider herself lucky that her sister died early?

The Mayor, on the other hand, grinned warmly: *It's so wonderful that my nephew has a close friend now.*

chunks.chineseText:
第86章 家族秘密

商非凡也没客气，大口大口吃得很香。

不帅发现他吃东西很快，示意他吃慢一点。

商非凡果然放慢了一点速度，但也只是一点点。他除了伪装的时候，平时吃东西速度都很快，但该有的餐桌礼仪也刻在了骨子里。

“你也吃。”

“嗯。”不帅也看饿了，跟着吃了一点。

两个小的吃着夜宵，两位大人……至少镇长看得很开心。

迪莉娅夫人虽然没有正眼看商非凡，却一直在暗地里观察他，通过对方的一举一动来判断对方的家世身份。

迪莉娅夫人也不知得出了什么判断，冷哼一声。

镇长悄悄对外甥歉意地笑，给妻子倒了一杯热饮。

不帅和商两人一起看向迪莉娅。

迪莉娅抱着杯子，两腿蜷曲到椅子上，很不文雅地撇撇嘴：“我和你母亲没跟你说林格莱特家的事，只是因为不值得说。”

“也没有什么所谓的诅咒，只是他们非要这么认为。因为林格莱特家不能承认雄性兽人的天赋和身体素质都要远远弱于家中雌性，也只有雄性兽人会遗传一种家族疾病，雌性兽人则极少。”

虎不帅惊讶：“家族疾病？”

“对，应该是跟虫毒有关，也有传说是跟毒雾纪的毒雾有关。但那时世道混乱，就算有人发病也只会以为是别的原因。”

“但新生纪来临，等林格莱特家族安顿下来后，发现家族雄性兽人基本只要到四十岁以后就会出现严重的骨骼病，疼起来比生扯四肢还要痛苦。”

“为此，林格莱特家族到处寻找治疗系的大祭司和高级药剂师，可问题总是无法解决。一次又一次，林格莱特家族便开始怀疑家族血脉受到诅咒。”

“家族中有不少人也因此去接触诅咒术，有的人成功，有的人失败。”

迪莉娅微微抬起下巴，傲气尽露：“我承认我也是因此对诅咒感兴趣，但我跟那些失败的蠢货不一样，我只用了五年时间就成为初级诅咒术士。”

商非凡想到自己现在也是正式的诅咒祭司，他才花了多长时间？

算了，这种事还是不说出来刺激不帅的小姨了。

而且诅咒祭司比诅咒术士更讲究天赋？

说白了，就是能成为祭祀的人会更受相关神灵的青睐。

商非凡碰碰不帅的手臂：偶不骄傲。

不帅：？

迪莉娅并不知道某人的内心戏有多丰富，继续述说家族秘密：“我检查过我和安妮塔的血液，我可以很负责地告诉你们，我们家族并没有任何被诅咒的痕迹，全都是林格莱特家族自己给自己加戏。”

虎不帅：“……”

迪莉娅又不屑地说：“自从那群白痴不知从哪里知道我成为诅咒师后，就想找我帮他们破解诅咒。他们之前就派人来找过我，我已经跟他们说得很清楚，他们那是遗传疾病，不是诅咒。但他们就是不信！”

迪莉娅冷笑：“可怜的雄性兽人的自尊。”

在场的雄性兽人们：“……”

“至于你母亲，”迪莉娅看向虎不帅：“她是怎么死的，你应该比我更清楚。”

虎不帅苦笑，他还真的不是很清楚。

或者说他之前以为自己很清楚，但最近发生的一连串事情已经让他不确定之前的判断。

“她生病了，拖了很长时间。”

“什么病？”这个问题，迪莉娅在第一次见到不帅时也问过。

不帅给出和当初一样的回答：“肺病。”

“你觉得肺病在王城无法治疗吗？”这个问题迪莉娅同样问过不帅。

虎不帅还真无法回答，因为肺病也有轻有重，他觉得当时原身母亲死亡并不完全是因为肺病，而是因为她自己不想活了。

迪莉娅看不帅沉默，尖锐道：“安妮塔那么早死全是因为你！”

镇长头大地想要阻止妻子。

虎不帅的手下意识按住商非凡的胳膊。

商非凡：“……”有点怪怪的，但心里有点窃喜是怎么回事？

迪莉娅无视丈夫打圆场，提高声音：“如果不是为了你这个……，她怎么会年纪轻轻就放弃自己的生命？安妮塔是那么坚强的人，当年没有父母依靠的我们在家族中有多难，她当时也只有十六岁，可她还是带我逃了出来！”

迪莉娅咬住嘴唇，过了好一会儿才说道：“安妮塔不是那种会轻易放弃生命的人，除非有人拿我或者你威胁他。”

虎不帅深吸气：“让我猜测一下，您是不是在想，我是王的私生子，我的存在威胁到了那些有继承权的王子和公主，尤其在虎王对我还算不错的情况下，更是让大家担心虎王会在晚年脑子发晕把我这个私生子给推上位。”

“有人认为我母亲会是我上位的最大臂助。因为她一直和虎王保持着情人关系，她又长得那么美。”

只看迪莉娅夫人，就知道原身母亲有多美。甚至比起迪莉娅，原身母亲的容貌更上一层楼。

而兽人的青壮期可以维持很长时间，换言之，原身母亲可以保持很长时间的美貌。

“虽然我已经表示出对王位毫无意思的想法，就连王也没有把我往那个方向培养。但依然有人觉得我们母子是威胁。”

“于是，有人找到我母亲，大约是五年多前，也是我重伤后。对方跟我母亲说，如果她不死，死的就是我。说只要她活着，对正统继承人就是威胁。很可能对方还答应我母亲，只要她肯放弃自己的生命，我这个儿子的生命就会得到保障，甚至除了王位以外还能得到一些普通人得不到的优待，比如爵位和领地。”

“然后就是我们看到的了。我母亲因为一场普通的受凉，就莫名其妙转为肺病，且怎么都看不好。坚持到今年初，终于坚持不下去，最终病得撒手人寰。”

虎不帅直视迪莉娅：“以上，是不是就是您的猜测？”

迪莉娅夫人伸直腿放到地上，挺直背脊：“我猜错了吗？”

虎不帅轻声叹了口气，“我不知道。”

实际上，这也是他的猜测。

否则无法解释原身母亲那么厉害的一个人，竟然会被一个不算很严重的肺病给拖到药石无效的地步。

迪莉娅想说什么，却发现那个姓商的家伙脑袋竟然靠到了她外甥的肩膀上，眼睛还闭了起来。

听他的鼻息，他竟然睡着了？！

“这是什么病吗！”迪莉娅指着睡着的商非凡骂。

虎不帅刚刚已经接到商的暗示，这时只能帮助遮掩：“我们赶路很累，这几天他为了保护我们，几乎没怎么合眼，昨天到达镇子后本想让他好好休息，但他担心我，跟我一起去窃-听那群迁徙者说话，现在只是支持不住了。”

镇长不等自家夫人开口，就抢先站起来说：“送他去客房吧，这样也休息不好，你也累。”

虎不帅摇头，“我等会儿带他回去风洞山。他带着的幼崽也在那边。”

“他的崽？”

“不是。是他捡的。”

“穷好心！”迪莉娅夫人嗤笑。

镇长不赞成地看妻子：“迪莉娅。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 86: Family Secret

Shang Feifan didn't stand on ceremony either, digging in heartily.

Bushuai noticed he was eating very fast and gestured for him to slow down.

Shang Feifan indeed slowed down a bit, though only slightly. Except when he was in disguise, he usually ate quite fast, yet proper table manners were etched into his very bones.

"You eat too."

"Mm." Bushuai felt his appetite stoked as well and joined in with a few bites.

While the two youngsters ate their late-night snack, the two adults... well, at least the Mayor was enjoying the sight immensely.

Though Lady Delia didn't look Shang Feifan directly in the eye, she was observing him covertly, judging his family background and standing through his every gesture.

Whatever conclusion Lady Delia reached, she let out a cold snort.

The Mayor offered his nephew an apologetic smile in secret while pouring his wife a cup of hot drink.

Both Bushuai and Shang looked over at Delia.

Delia clutched her cup and curled her legs onto the chair, curling her lip ungracefully. "Your mother and I never spoke to you about the Linglete family simply because it wasn't worth mentioning."

"There is no so-called curse either; it's just that they insist on thinking so. That's because the Linglete family refuses to acknowledge that the male beastmen's talent and physical fitness are vastly inferior to the females in the family, and only male beastmen inherit a certain familial disease, while females rarely do."

Hu Bushuai was surprised. "A hereditary disease?"

"Yes. It's likely related to insect venom, though rumors say it might be tied to the toxic fog from the Toxic Fog Era. But back then, the world was in chaos, so even if someone fell ill, people would attribute it to other causes."

"When the New Era arrived and the Linglete family settled down, they discovered that almost all male beastmen in the family developed a severe bone disease after reaching forty. The pain was worse than having one's limbs ripped off alive."

"To address this, the Linglete family searched everywhere for high priests of the healing branch and advanced pharmacists, yet the problem remained unsolved. Time and again, the Linglete family began to suspect that their bloodline was cursed."

"Many in the family went on to dabble in curse arts because of this—some succeeded, while others failed."

Delia raised her chin slightly, her pride laid bare. "I admit I turned to curse arts for that reason too, but I'm not like those failed idiots. It took me only five years to become a novice curse practitioner."

Shang Feifan recalled that he was currently an official Curse Priest as well—and how long had it taken him?

Forget it, better not speak up and provoke Bushuai's aunt.

Besides, aren't Curse Priests even more reliant on innate talent than curse practitioners?

To put it plainly, those who can become priests are simply favored more by the relevant deities.

Shang Feifan nudged Bushuai's arm: *I'm not proud.*

Bushuai: *?*

Unaware of how melodramatic a certain person's inner monologue was, Delia continued recounting the family secret: "I examined both my blood and Anita's. I can tell you with complete certainty that our family bears not a single trace of a curse. It's all the Linglete family making drama out of nothing."

Hu Bushuai: "..."

Delia added disdainfully, "Ever since those idiots somehow learned I had become a curse master, they wanted me to help them lift the curse. They sent people to find me before, and I made it abundantly clear to them that theirs was a hereditary disease, not a curse. But they just wouldn't believe it!"

Delia sneered, "Pathetic male beastman pride."

The male beastmen present: "..."

"As for your mother," Delia looked at Hu Bushuai, "you ought to know how she died better than I do."

Hu Bushuai let out a bitter smile. In truth, he really wasn't clear about it.

Or rather, he used to think he was clear on it, but the series of recent events had cast doubt on his previous judgment.

"She fell ill, and it dragged on for a long time."

"What illness?" Delia had asked Bushuai this very question the first time she met him.

Bushuai gave the same answer as before: "A lung affliction."

"Do you think a lung affliction is untreatable in the royal capital?" Delia had likewise asked him this before.

Hu Bushuai really couldn't answer that. Lung afflictions varied in severity, and he felt that the original body's mother hadn't died solely from the illness, but because she no longer wished to live.

Seeing Bushuai fall silent, Delia said sharply, "Anita dying so young was entirely because of you!"

The Mayor felt a headache coming on and tried to stop his wife.

Hu Bushuai subconsciously pressed his hand against Shang Feifan's arm.

Shang Feifan: "..." *This feels a bit weird, but why am I feeling a subtle thrill inside?*

Ignoring her husband's smooth-over attempt, Delia raised her voice: "If not for a... like you, how could she have given up her life at such a young age? Anita was such a strong person! Back then, without parents to rely on, life in the family was so brutal for us. She was only sixteen, yet she still managed to escape with me!"

Delia bit her lip, and only after a long pause did she speak again: "Anita was not someone who would give up her life so easily—unless someone threatened her using me or you."

Hu Bushuai took a deep breath. "Let me take a guess. Are you thinking that since I am the King's illegitimate son, my presence threatened the princes and princesses who hold rights of succession? Especially since the Tiger King treated me decently, which led everyone to fear he might suffer a lapse of mind in his late years and push me, an illegitimate son, onto the throne."

"Someone believed my mother would be my greatest benefactor in ascending the throne, because she had always maintained a lover's relationship with the Tiger King, and she was so breathtakingly beautiful."

Just looking at Lady Delia was enough to gauge how beautiful the original mother had been. In fact, compared to Delia, the original mother's looks were even a notch above.

Beastmen remained in their prime for a very long time, meaning the original mother could maintain her beauty for many years.

"Although I had already expressed having zero interest in the throne, and the King never groomed me in that direction either, there were still those who viewed us, mother and son, as a threat."

"So, someone approached my mother roughly five years ago—right after I was severely injured. They told my mother that if she didn't die, I would be the one to die instead. They said that as long as she lived, she remained a threat to the legitimate heirs. They likely also promised my mother that if she gave up her life, my safety would be guaranteed, and I would even receive special privileges beyond ordinary reach—such as a title and a fiefdom—everything except the throne."

"And then we arrived at what we witnessed. From a simple cold, my mother mysteriously developed a lung affliction that defied all treatment. She held on until early this year before finally giving out, passing away from her illness."

Hu Bushuai looked directly at Delia. "Is the above... your guess?"

Lady Delia lowered her legs to the ground and straightened her back. "Did I guess wrong?"

Hu Bushuai let out a soft sigh. "I don't know."

In truth, this was his guess as well.

Otherwise, there was no way to explain how someone as formidable as the original mother could be dragged down to the point of incurable ruin by an illness that shouldn't have been so severe.

Delia was about to say something when she noticed that guy named Shang had actually leaned his head onto her nephew's shoulder, his eyes closed.

Judging by his breathing, he had actually fallen asleep?!

"What kind of affliction is this?!" Delia pointed at the sleeping Shang Feifan and yelled.

Having just received Shang's hint moments ago, Hu Bushuai could only help cover for him: "We've had an exhausting journey. Over the past few days, he barely closed his eyes to protect us. After reaching town yesterday, I wanted him to rest well, but he was worried about me and came along to eavesdrop on those migrants. He's simply reached his limit now."

Before his wife could speak, the Mayor stood up first and said, "Take him to a guest room. He won't rest well like this, and you're tired too."

Hu Bushuai shook his head. "I'll take him back to Wind Cave Mountain in a bit. The cub he brought along is over there too."

"His cub?"

"No. He picked it up."

"Softhearted fool!" Lady Delia sneered.

The Mayor looked at his wife disapprovingly: "Delia."

chunks.chineseText:
迪莉娅还是很尊重以及爱护这位丈夫的，看他阻止，到底没再说什么。

镇长转头又对虎不帅说：“大致情况你已经了解了。虽然你是安妮塔的孩子，但我建议你不要和林格莱特家族接触，那是一群会上杆子爬的亲戚。”

“他们可是靠一代又一代的嫁女儿才保住那个农庄。”迪莉娅夫人无限讽刺。

“林格莱特家女兽人生的孩子也会遗传那个家族疾病吗？”虎不帅冷不丁问。

迪莉娅冷笑：“如果是这样，谁还敢娶林格莱特家的女兽人？”

“只有男兽人的后代才有这样的问题？”

“对。”

“那林格莱特家族有没有考虑过，不让家族直系的男兽人结婚生子，而是只让女兽人传宗接代，同样都是林格莱特家族血脉，还能洗脱这种家族遗传疾病。”

“你真是太不了解某些固执的老古董。”迪莉娅重重嗤声：“让他们放弃雄性继承人，不如让他们去死。他们宁可家族血脉彻底消失，也不愿意让延续了几百几千年也许更久的‘传统’消失。懂吗？”

“很多种族的雌性兽人都比雄性更强。而且从遗传角度来看，孩子遗传母亲的天赋和身体素质更多。”虎不帅中肯地说。

镇长也连连点头：“我们兽人一般都不重视性别，如果真要说重视，反而很多种族更重视雌性。”

“但你们也得承认这世上就是有某些雄性兽人越是比雌性弱，就越是要打压雌性，就生怕雌性爬到他们头上。当然，我不是说全部，只是林格莱特家族就是这么一群依靠雌性却又要打压雌性的卑劣兽人。”迪莉娅还是给了丈夫几分面子，没有开地图炮。

虎不帅挑眉。他小姨都用上卑劣这个词了，可见对林格莱特那群亲戚有多么厌恶。

“小姨，能说说我……外公外婆的死亡和失踪是怎么一回事吗？还有当初的族长为什么不肯帮助你们，他们是不是知道什么？”

虎不帅也不知道自己为何会问出这个问题，他只是觉得原身家的秘密一环套一环，表面上看起来毫无关系的几件事，说不定在后面就能纠缠在一起。

虽然迪莉娅说林格莱特家族的遗传疾病不是诅咒，但这个病也太古怪了。

也许他该找商去看看那些犯病的林格莱特兽人。

不是他偏心，他见识过商的能力，他感觉商的诅咒术很可能要比他小姨厉害得多。

迪莉娅皱眉，但没有马上拒绝回答。

商非凡的脑袋偏了一下，虎不帅连忙用手扶住，担心对方睡得不舒服，干脆就把对方身体放倒，让他睡在长椅上，还不见外地拉了一条毯子给商盖上。他自己则坐到了扶手上。

镇长：睡得这么死吗？兽人能睡得这么死，要么就是极度信任身边环境和身边人，要么就是真累狠了。

看到外甥忙活了好一会儿把好友安顿好，迪莉娅夫人心中不快。

这人睡着都让她不爽！

“详细的事情我也不太清楚，那时我还小，想要了解也没有渠道。他们绝对知道什么，但一直没有对我和安妮塔说真话，甚至怕我们闹腾，一心要把我和安妮塔嫁出去。”

“后来我长大有能力了，也去找过他们几次，但还是没有从他们口中问出实话。包括安妮塔也一样。”

虎不帅试探地问：“您没有对他们使用诅咒？”

“你是说威胁他们？”迪莉娅昂头：“我当然做了。可当年的族长和知道详细的族老都死得太早，而年轻那一辈压根就不清楚情况，还活着的少数老人则什么都不知道。”

虎不帅：“除了林格莱特家族那边，还有其他人知道外祖父母的事情吗？”

迪莉娅夫人沉默片刻：“我和你母亲只查到一个线索。”

“什么线索？”

“虎国王后。她是你外祖母的堂姐妹。据说，我母亲失踪前曾见过一个来自王城的大人物。”

虎不帅愕然。

他再怎么也没想到原身母亲一脉竟然还能和堂堂虎国王后扯上关系。

如果按辈分算起来，这算不算姑妈和侄女共侍一夫？

虎王知道这件事吗？

如果知道，只能说这位虎王口味好重。

虎不帅忽然想到一点，脱口问出：“我母亲接触虎王，成为他的情人，不会就是想要接近王后吧？还是你们怀疑外祖父母的死亡和失踪和王族有关？”

迪莉娅夫人神色不动，“那位王后一开始确实不知道安妮塔的身份。但后来她应该知道了，可她依然没有同意见我们。”

虎不帅：果然复杂了！

“等等，王后可是黑森林城主的亲妹妹。那不就是说你们的母亲、我外祖母也是黑森林城主的堂姐妹？”

迪莉娅摆摆手：“再是大贵族大富豪，谁还没有几个穷亲戚？你外祖母只是前代黑森林城主第三子的孩子。”

“前代黑森林城主把爵位和领地以及绝大部分财产都传给了最能干的长子。其他子女根据能力高低和受欢迎程度，共同分不到十分之一的财产。”

“你外祖母的父亲算是丹顿家最不受重视的一个，他得到的也最少，他甚至没有弄到爵位，连最低的勋爵都没有弄到。最后只分到一个小型农庄就被打发。”

“否则你以为林格莱特家族的雄性兽人怎么可能娶到丹顿家的女儿？”

虎不帅举手，又问：“外祖母和王后少时感情如何？她们后来还有联系吗？”

“谁知道呢。”迪莉娅夫人懒懒地靠在丈夫身上：“我和安妮塔能查到我们母亲和堂堂王后殿下有亲戚关系，还是因为一个偶然的机会。”

虎不帅心中还有许多疑问：“王后为什么不肯见你们？难道她真的心中有鬼？”

“这件事……”迪莉娅想说这事就需要你这个虎王私生子进行调查了。但想到她姐姐并不想这唯一的儿子被卷入王位之争，甚至为此付出生命，就把这句话又咽了回去。

迪莉娅一瞪眼：“总之，长辈的事，你们小孩别管。包括镇子外面那群林格莱特，当不认识就好。不要和他们说话，不要和他们接近！还有王后那边，你也别给我乱调查，全都当做不知道！记住了？”

虎不帅是记住了。但他怎么可能不管、不调查？

他确实可以无视。

但他现在用的是原身的身体，血脉关系就在那里，真出了事、真有人进行清算，他能逃脱？

而想要知道这些被隐藏在幕后的秘密，他恐怕得回去王城一趟才行。
chunks.englishText:
Delia still respected and cherished her husband deeply, and seeing him stop her, she ultimately said nothing more.

The Mayor turned his gaze back to Hu Bushuai and said, "You already have a general understanding of the situation. Although you are Anita's child, I advise you not to have any contact with the Lingelate family. They are a pack of relatives who will climb all over you if you give them an inch."

"They've only managed to hold onto that manor by marrying off their daughters generation after generation," Madam Delia remarked with boundless sarcasm.

"Do the children born to female beastmen of the Lingelate family also inherit that familial disease?" Hu Bushuai asked out of the blue.

Delia sneered, "If that were the case, who would ever dare to marry a female beastman of the Lingelate family?"

"So only the descendants of the male beastmen suffer from this issue?"

"Correct."

"Then has the Lingelate family ever considered forbidding the direct male descendants of the family from marrying and having children, allowing only the female beastmen to pass down the bloodline? Since they all share the same Lingelate blood, wouldn't that wash away this hereditary family disease?"

"You truly have no idea how stubborn certain old fossils can be," Delia scoffed heavily. "Making them give up male heirs is no different from asking them to die. They would rather their family bloodline vanish completely than let a 'tradition' that has lasted for hundreds, thousands, or perhaps even longer, disappear. Understand?"

"The females of many beastman races are stronger than the males. Moreover, from a genetic standpoint, children inherit more of their talent and physical fitness from their mothers," Hu Bushuai said objectively.

The Mayor also nodded repeatedly. "We beastmen generally do not place much emphasis on gender; if anything, many races actually value females more."

"Yet you must also admit that there are certain male beastmen in this world who become all the more desperate to suppress females the weaker they themselves are, terrified that females might ride roughshod over them. Of course, I'm not speaking of all of them, but the Lingelate family is precisely that kind of despicable bunch of beastmen who rely on females while simultaneously trying to crush them." Delia still granted her husband a modicum of face and refrained from generalizing to all males.

Hu Bushuai raised an eyebrow. Since his own aunt had resorted to using the word "despicable," it was clear just how much she loathed those Lingelate relatives.

"Auntie, could you tell me... what happened with my grandfather and grandmother's death and disappearance? And why didn't the clan head at the time help you two? Did they know something?"

Hu Bushuai didn't even know why he was asking this question; he simply felt that the secrets of the original body's family were nested within one another like interlocking rings. Several matters that looked completely unrelated on the surface might very well entangle in the end.

Although Delia claimed that the Lingelate family's hereditary disease wasn't a curse, this illness was altogether too bizarre.

Perhaps he should find Shang to examine those afflicted Lingelates.

It wasn't that he was biased, but having witnessed Shang's capabilities, he felt that Shang's curse arts were likely far more formidable than his aunt's.

Delia frowned, but did not immediately refuse to answer.

Shang Fanfan's head tilted to one side, and Hu Bushuai hurriedly steadied it with his hand. Fearing that the other man was sleeping uncomfortably, he simply laid Shang's body flat so he could sleep on the bench, and unceremoniously pulled a blanket over him. As for himself, he sat on the armrest.

The Mayor thought: *He can sleep this soundly? For a beastman to sleep this deeply, it either means he has extreme trust in his surrounding environment and companions, or he is truly exhausted to the bone.*

Seeing his nephew bustling about for quite a while to settle his friend in, Madam Delia felt a wave of displeasure in her heart.

The mere fact that this man was asleep annoyed her!

"I don't know the detailed circumstances either. I was too young back then and had no channels to find out. They definitely knew something, but they never told me and Anita the truth; they were even terrified of us making a fuss, and were dead set on marrying both me and Anita off."

"Later, when I grew up and gained the ability, I went to look for them a few times, but still couldn't pry the truth out of their mouths. Anita was the same."

Hu Bushuai probed tentatively, "You didn't use curses on them?"

"Are you talking about threatening them?" Delia lifted her chin. "Of course I did. But the clan head of that era and the clan elders who knew the details died much too young, while the younger generation was completely clueless about the situation, and the few surviving old folks knew nothing at all."

Hu Bushuai asked, "Aside from the Lingelate family, is there anyone else who knows about my grandparents?"

Madam Delia fell silent for a moment. "Your mother and I only managed to track down a single clue."

"What clue?"

"The Queen of the Tiger Kingdom. She is your grandmother's first cousin. It is said that before my mother disappeared, she once met a prominent figure from the Royal City."

Hu Bushuai was dumbfounded.

No matter how he thought about it, he never expected that his original body's maternal lineage could actually be connected to the dignified Queen of the Tiger Kingdom.

If calculated by seniority, did this count as an aunt and a niece sharing the same husband?

Did the Tiger King know about this?

If he did, one could only say that this Tiger King had a rather heavy palate.

A thought suddenly struck Hu Bushuai, and he blurted out, "My mother approaching the Tiger King and becoming his mistress... couldn't it be that she wanted to get close to the Queen? Or did you suspect that my grandparents' death and disappearance were related to the royal family?"

Madam Delia's expression remained unchanged. "That Queen indeed did not know Anita's identity at first. But later on, she should have figured it out, yet she still refused to agree to see us."

Hu Bushuai thought: *As expected, things are complicated!*

"Wait, the Queen is the biological younger sister of the Lord of the Black Forest. Doesn't that mean your mother—my grandmother—is also a first cousin of the Lord of the Black Forest?"

Delia waved a hand. "No matter how great the noble family or wealthy the clan, who doesn't have a few poor relatives? Your grandmother was merely the child of the previous Lord of the Black Forest's third son."

"The previous Lord of the Black Forest passed down his peerage, territory, and the vast majority of his wealth to his most capable eldest son. The other children, based on their abilities and popularity, shared less than one-tenth of the estate."

"Your grandmother's father could be considered the least valued of the Denton family, and he received the least. He didn't even secure a peerage, not even the lowest barony. In the end, he was brushed off with just a small manor."

"Otherwise, how do you think the male beastmen of the Lingelate family could possibly have married a daughter of the Denton family?"

Hu Bushuai raised his hand and asked again, "How was the relationship between your grandmother and the Queen in their youth? Did they maintain contact afterward?"

"Who knows." Madam Delia leaned lazily against her husband. "The only reason Anita and I were able to discover we had blood ties to Her Majesty the Queen was by pure coincidence."

Hu Bushuai still had many doubts in his heart. "Why is the Queen unwilling to see you? Could it be that she really has a guilty conscience?"

"This matter..." Delia wanted to say that this was something for him, the illegitimate son of the Tiger King, to investigate. But recalling that her older sister did not want this only son to be dragged into the struggle for the throne—and had even paid with her life for it—she swallowed those words back down.

Delia glared at him. "In short, matters of the elders are not for you kids to meddle in. That includes those Lingelates outside the town; just treat them as strangers. Do not speak to them, and do not get close to them! As for the Queen's side, don't you go launching any reckless investigations either—treat everything as if you know nothing! Understood?"

Hu Bushuai noted it down. But how could he possibly ignore it and not investigate?

He could indeed choose to turn a blind eye.

However, he was currently using the original body, and the blood ties were right there. If something really happened and a reckoning came, could he escape?

And if he wanted to uncover these secrets hidden behind the scenes, he would likely have to make a trip back to the Royal City.
