The young beastman let out a light snort, took the bone staff, gave it a casual wave, and continued walking without stopping his pace.

The receptionist hurried to push open the doors, bowing as he welcomed in this young master whose very appearance screamed trouble.

The last servant to enter casually slipped a coin to the receptionist.

The receptionist looked down, only to find that it was actually a ten-value Silver Daru!

Noticing a guest of formidable air entering, the hotel manager rushed over immediately.

The manager’s eyes were far sharper than the receptionist's. With a single sweeping glance, he deduced that this young, decadent master undoubtedly hailed from a wealthy household—and perhaps even held a noble title, and not a low one at that.

Although the young master was dressed loosely and carelessly, every single piece of his clothing, shoes, and socks was of top-tier quality. The materials used were among the most exorbitant on the market, many of them natural fibers.

In the Beastman Continent, natural materials were notoriously rare and expensive. Beast furs were costlier than stone-cloth, but silk textiles were vastly more precious than fur.

Yet the inner garments worn by this young master were entirely made of silk!

The uppers of his boots even featured embroidery, yet such precious footwear had been stained with mud.

Then there was the bone staff he carried. Setting aside the exquisite carvings etched into its surface, the material of the staff head and shaft alone revealed a vintage of many years.

While the manager could not immediately identify the guest's lineage from the patterns on the bone staff or the style of its head, he dared not show the slightest negligence.

Despite the young master's seemingly lax demeanor and arrogant posture, his spine remained straight and his gaze looked down upon nothing. This was the mark of a refined upbringing deeply ingrained into his very bones—a true aristocratic bearing.

From the moment the young master entered the lobby, he showed no interest whatsoever in the hotel's decor, nor did he display the slightest regard for anything he passed. He didn't even spare a single extra glance at the other guests lingering in the lobby.

This was clearly the behavior of a noble young master who frequently frequented luxurious estates and had long since grown blasé to the extravagant lifestyle of the upper crust.

Furthermore, he cared not a whit about the gazes of others.

Acting as if he hadn't noticed the young man's sloppy attire or mismatched boots, the manager bowed with utmost politeness and greeted him, "Greetings, esteemed guest. How may I be of service to you?"

The noble young master crooked a finger.

The middle-aged female beastman stepped forward to address the manager. "The finest suite. Quiet, clean, spacious. No disturbances. The top floor is preferred."

"Very well. Please follow me." Without even bothering with the check-in formalities, the manager led them directly to the entrance of the mechanical elevator.

The receptionist opened the elevator doors.

Finally showing a glimmer of interest, the young noble glanced slightly at the lift. "An alchemical elevator?"

The manager smiled proudly and gave a slight nod.

Striding into the elevator, the young noble drawled lazily, "Such a waste."

The manager’s face twitched slightly. The Twin Lamps Hotel only stood four stories tall. Given the robust physique of beastmen, using an alchemical elevator here did indeed border on extravagant, but wasn't it all for the sake of appearances?

The elevator ascended to the top floor.

This floor apparently contained only three large suites.

Someone was just emerging from the right-hand room.

Guiding the young noble to the central VIP suite, the manager reached out to unlock the door.

However, the young noble pointed his bone staff toward the leftmost room. "Has anyone taken the rooms over there?"

The manager replied apologetically, "Yes, sir. Guests are already checked in."

"So you're saying my room is flanked on both sides?" The young noble adopted an entitled, matter-of-fact tone. "Have them leave. I'll cover their room fees."

"Young Master!" The middle-aged female beastman seemed on the verge of intervening.

Seeing the female beastman speak up, the hotel manager lowered his gaze and remained silent.

The young noble shot a sidelong glance at the female steward and curled his lip. "We'll stay for a day first. If I'm not satisfied, we leave."

"Understood, Young Master." The middle-aged female beastman exhaled softly and signaled the hotel manager.

The manager hurriedly handed the keys over to her.

Stiding into the suite, the young noble slammed the door shut with a loud *bang* before anyone else could step inside.

 Wearing an expression of helpless resignation, the middle-aged female beastman handed the keys to the two male beastmen, then accompanied the manager downstairs to complete the check-in procedures.

The hotel manager also noted that apart from the two male servants who each carried a single trunk, this entourage brought no extra luggage whatsoever.

When filling out the registration forms, the middle-aged female beastman entered only a single character: "Shang." The number of occupants was listed as one, accompanied by three attendants.

The manager harbored no suspicions regarding such sparse information, especially after the female beastman directly prepaid five gold Darud.

Neither nobles nor the immensely wealthy favored exposing their whereabouts, let alone being pried into. The reason the Twin Lamps Hotel had become the premier establishment in the Royal City—aside from its top-notch hardware facilities—was its supreme, discreet service. One of its golden rules was simple: never ask what shouldn't be asked, and never look at what shouldn't be seen.

"Should your master have any requests, please feel free to inform us. We will do our utmost to satisfy his every demand," the manager said with a polite smile.

A subtle expression crossed the middle-aged female beastman's face. "Keeping our young master satisfied won't be easy. Let me see your menu first."

While the middle-aged female beastman busied herself worrying over her master's three daily meals, that very same "spoiled scoundrel" had already leaped off the balcony, swaggering toward the Royal City's most bustling red-light district—without taking a single servant along.

chunks.chineseText:
第124章 假亦真来

一个纨绔少爷在王城消费最昂贵的销金窟撒下大把金钱，只为见到王城最美、名头最大的“多丽丝王妃”。

多丽丝王妃当然不是真正的王妃，虎国只有王后，没有王妃。

多丽丝之所以被称为王妃，是因为传说她出身贵族，身份高贵，却因家道中落沦于风尘。

多丽丝气质神秘自带忧郁，她的容貌、气质和身材都能满足普通人对于贵族千金的幻想。

而富豪和一些贵族也喜欢她，因为她有着优雅的风范、让人称赞的容貌，却可以做到贵族千金和夫人们做不到的事情。

但自称阿瑞斯商的纨绔少爷在见到多丽丝后却失望地说了一声“就这”，然后扭头就走。

多丽丝气到脸蛋扭曲，她从没有受到过这样的侮辱！

阿瑞斯商丢在桌子上的金达盾没有带走，但这在多丽丝看来更像是对她的羞辱。

到她现在的地位，金钱已经不是那么重要，她能拥有现在的地位和名气，就是因为受到众人追捧。

可一个不知道哪里来的纨绔少爷在花了那么多金达盾后，却对她表现得不屑一顾，摆在桌上的金达盾简直就像是在打发垃圾。

这件事传出去，对她的名气损害无疑会很大。

但无论是多丽丝，还是她的背后老板都已经无法阻止这件事传出去。

因为那个纨绔少爷为了见到多丽丝，闹得很大，就在大厅里，不断在桌子上加码金达盾。不止店内员工知道，很多客人也听到看到了。

而老板会让多丽丝出面，不只因为对方拿出的越来越多的金达盾，更是看到对方没有携带任何背包。

换言之，这是一个拥有空间储物工具的豪门少爷！

哪怕他来历不明，也没有人敢得罪他。很多人都在猜测他会不会是异国贵族，或者某个古老家族的后代。

多丽丝原本可以让这位少爷前往贵宾室与她相见，但她希望和这名纨绔的见面能更有戏剧性。

她盛装出面，未尝没有震慑和魅惑住这名纨绔少爷的意思。顺便也让大厅的其他客人看看她是多么受人追捧和欢迎。

可谁能想到戏剧性是有了，但完全不是她想要的那种。

多丽丝一回到房间，就变了脸孔。

她脸上的怒意消失。

老板进来。

“查清那人的来历。”多丽丝下令。

“是。”老板当即找人吩咐下去。

商非凡找上多丽丝自然不是随便找的，他问过天眼系统，从天眼系统那里得知王城名头最大的交际花其实是王后的眼线。

在得知王后竟然掌控着红灯区最火爆最有名的销金窟后，商非凡也没有太过意外。

妓-院、赌场、酒馆……这些地方原本就是最容易收集消息，也最容易散播谣言的地方。几乎每个当权者都不会放过这样的地方，就算不会直接掌控，也会通过某些手下来间接掌控。

商非凡相信，不仅王后在这些地方有安插人手，虎王肯定也有。

而几位王子公主只要对权力有野心，对这些地方也不可能不注意。

同样，王城的某些官员也会把目光放在这些地方。

所以只要在这里闹事，做得夸张一点、让人印象深刻一点，一定会给王城的头头脑脑们留下印象。

商非凡……阿瑞斯商在离开红灯区后，又走入了王城最大赌场的大门。

赌场和红灯区向来相隔不远，关金娱乐场灯火辉煌，里面的客人全都打扮得人模狗样，这就不是穷鬼能来的地方。

阿瑞斯商一进门，立马就有管事迎上前来。

这些地方消息流通很快，阿瑞斯商过来的路上都有人盯着，他刚接近赌场大门，就有人把消息传递给了赌场管事。

不是没有人想要打劫这位连仆人没带一个的少爷，但某些人下了命令，暂时不准动这个来历不明的纨绔。

如果这个纨绔只是家里有钱，或者只是一个小贵族之子，那被打劫了也只能怪他自己太过高调。

可如果对方身后有个庞大家族，甚至是来自异国的大贵族呢？

毕竟，普通贵族有几个能拥有空间储物工具？

况且，这么一个少爷就这么自己一个人跑出来，还没有人保护，谁信？

就算要摸底，也不是现在。

阿瑞斯商一脸无聊，单手提着骨杖晃来晃去，整个人都透着一股“爷有钱有势，生命的每一天就在花钱中，真的无趣啊”的找刺激作死感。

“尊贵的客人，您好。欢迎来到……”

“废话少说，爷是赌钱的，哪种游戏最有趣最刺激？”阿瑞斯商不耐烦地打断管事。

管事立刻换了话语，恭敬地说：“那要看您喜欢哪一种，我们这里有轮-盘、骨牌、骰子……等常规玩法。还有兽人与兽人的竞技、兽人与野兽的竞技、野兽与野兽的……，甚至您还能亲自参与。”

“有推荐吗？”

“有的。今晚有一个已经准备了半年的赛事，还有半个小时就要开启。您可以自由选择其中一个参赛者，赌对方是第一个死，还是能活到最后，不同赌局，收获也不一样。”

“什么赛事？”

管事对附近的侍者打眼色。

两名美艳女兽人神色婉转地走过来，想要挽起阿瑞斯商的胳膊。

阿瑞斯商提起骨杖轻轻推开女兽人，神色恹恹地说：“滚远一点。”

管事连忙再次打眼色。

两名美女迅速离开。

“抱歉，我们只是希望您能宾至如归。”管事充满歉意。

阿瑞斯商不屑地撇嘴：“宾至如归？只怕你们还做不到。好了，爷不是来跟你聊天的，赛事在哪里？没有你说的那么有趣刺激，爷就走人。”

片刻后，阿瑞斯商在管事的引领下进入娱乐场地下。

王城下面可没有一个地下城，但有四通八达的地下排水设施。

地下排水渠道甚至形成了一条小河。

阿瑞斯商下来后就看到一条小船停在排水渠上，船上还有一名戴着头罩的船夫。

“一般客人来到这里，都会被蒙上眼睛。我们要去的地方……不适合外传。”管事道。

阿瑞斯商看都不看他，一副谁敢蒙他眼睛，他就要谁死的神情。

管事：讨厌的纨绔。希望你背后的身份足够撑得住你如此嚣张，否则……他真的很期待看到这个纨绔惊恐求饶痛哭涕流的模样。

“你身上有挥之不去的血腥味。”阿瑞斯商忽然道。

“什么？”管事不确定地问。

阿瑞斯商转头看他：“我的经验告诉我，你杀过很多人，甚至是虐杀。你喜欢看到别人在你面前痛苦喊叫求饶的模样，喜欢掌握别人的生死。你痛恨权贵，却又不得不跪舔他们。每天在权贵和上司面前不得不毕恭毕敬，一心为他们做事，却还会遭受他们的羞辱和斥责。”

“这种愤怒、痛苦，要怎么发泄呢？你不敢对权贵和你的上司报复，你只能把这些愤怒和报复的欲望全都发泄到其他人身上。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 124: False Becomes True (Part 1)

A dissolute young master scattered piles of gold in the royal city’s most extravagant pleasure den, all simply to catch a glimpse of the capital’s most renowned and celebrated beauty: "Princess Doris."

Of course, Princess Doris was not a true princess. The Tiger Kingdom only had a queen, not a princess.

The reason Doris was called a princess was because rumor had it she came from an aristocratic background with a noble lineage, only to be reduced to the mortal dust of the brothels after her family’s fortunes declined.

Doris possessed a mysterious, melancholic aura. Her looks, temperament, and figure could effortlessly fulfill any commoner’s fantasies of a noble daughter. 

Wealthy magnates and various nobles were also fond of her because she carried herself with an elegant demeanor and possessed universally praised beauty, yet she was willing to do things that true noble daughters and matrons never would.

However, after catching sight of Doris, the profligate young master—who called himself Ares Shang—uttered a disappointed "Is that it?" and turned on his heel to leave.

Doris’s pretty face twisted in fury! She had never suffered such an insult in all her days!

Ares Shang hadn't even bothered to take back the golden shields he had tossed onto the table, but to Doris, this felt even more like a humiliation.

At her current standing, money was no longer all that important. She owed her current status and fame entirely to the adoration and pursuit of the masses.

Yet a profligate young master who had materialized out of nowhere, after spending so many golden shields, had looked at her with utter disdain. The golden shields left lying on the table were practically treated like garbage tossed at a beggar.

If this matter spread, the damage to her reputation would undoubtedly be immense.

Yet neither Doris nor her behind-the-scenes boss could stop the news from leaking.

This was because the arrogant young master had made quite a scene just to see Doris. Right there in the main hall, he had continuously piled more and more golden shields onto the table. Not only the venue's staff knew about it, but countless patrons had seen and heard the entire spectacle as well.

The reason the boss had allowed Doris to step forward wasn't merely because of the ever-growing stack of golden shields the fellow produced, but also because he noticed the guest wasn't carrying any sort of luggage or pack.

In other words, this was a scion of a wealthy, powerful clan who possessed spatial storage tools!

Even though his origins were shrouded in mystery, not a single soul dared to cross him. Many were already speculating whether he might be a foreign aristocrat or the descendant of some ancient clan.

Doris could easily have had the young master brought to a VIP room for a private meeting, but she had wanted their encounter to carry a touch of theatrical drama.

By stepping out in full, resplendent attire, she had half-intended to overawe and charm this dissolute young master, while incidentally showing the other patrons in the hall just how adored and sought-after she truly was.

Who could have predicted that while there was indeed drama, it was completely opposite to the kind she wanted?

The moment Doris stepped back into her private chambers, her expression morphed.

The anger vanished from her face.

The boss walked in.

"Investigate that man's origins," Doris commanded.

"Understood." The boss immediately turned to give instructions to his subordinates.

Shang Feifan’s approach to Doris was certainly no random whim. He had consulted the Heavenly Eye system, learning from it that the royal city’s most famous courtesan was, in fact, an informant planted by the Queen.

Upon discovering that the Queen actually controlled the red-light district’s most explosive and famous pleasure den, Shang Feifan hadn't been overly surprised.

Brothels, casinos, taverns... these places had always been the easiest breeding grounds for gathering intelligence and spreading rumors. Almost no person in power would ever let such a place slip through their fingers; even if they didn't control it directly, they would pull strings through underlings to manage it indirectly.

Shang Feifan believed that not only did the Queen plant people in these locations, but the Tiger King undoubtedly did as well.

As for the various princes and princesses, any of them with ambitions for the throne couldn't possibly ignore such establishments.

Likewise, certain officials in the royal city would inevitably cast their gaze in these directions.

Therefore, as long as one caused a commotion here—doing it with enough flair and extravagance to leave a deep impression—it would inevitably leave a mark on the bigwigs pulling the strings in the royal city.

After leaving the red-light district, Shang Feifan—now operating as Ares Shang—strode through the doors of the royal city's largest casino.

Casinos and red-light districts always sat close to one another. The Golden Glow Entertainment House blazed with brilliant lights, its patrons all dressed to the nines. This was hardly a place where destitute beggars could set foot.

The moment Ares Shang stepped through the threshold, a manager hurried forward to greet him.

Information flowed at lightning speed in these places; Ares Shang had been watched all the way along his route. The moment he approached the casino gates, word had already been passed to the floor manager.

It wasn't that no one wanted to rob this young master who hadn't even brought a single servant along, but higher-ups had issued strict orders temporarily forbidding anyone from touching this mysterious, profligate youth.

If this young man was merely backed by wealth or was simply the son of some minor noble, getting robbed would only prove he had been far too arrogant and high-profile for his own good.

But what if he had a colossal family clan standing behind him, or hailed from a formidable foreign house of high nobility?

After all, among ordinary nobles, just how many possessed spatial storage tools?

Besides, for a young master like this to wander out entirely on his own without a single bodyguard—who would believe it?

Even if they wanted to test the waters, now was not the time.

With a bored expression, Ares Shang twirled a bone staff in one hand, radiating the classic aura of a man who thought: *This young master has money and power, and every day of my life is spent burning cash—it is truly, unbearably dull.* It was the epitome of a seeker of thrills courting death.

"Respected guest, greetings. Welcome to—"

"Cut the crap. This lord is here to gamble. Which game is the most interesting and thrilling?" Ares Shang impatiently interrupted the manager.

The manager instantly switched tactics, speaking deferentially, "That depends on your preferences. We offer roulette, dominoes, dice, and other conventional games. We also feature beast-versus-beast combat, beast-versus-monster combat... and you can even participate personally if you wish."

"Any recommendations?"

"Indeed. Tonight, we have a tournament that has been half a year in the making, and it starts in half an hour. You can freely choose one of the contestants and wager whether they will die first or survive to the very end. The payouts vary depending on the specific stakes."

"What kind of tournament?"

The manager cast a sidelong glance at nearby attendants.

Two ravishing beast-folk women swayed over with alluring expressions, attempting to link arms with Ares Shang.

Ares Shang raised his bone staff and gently pushed the beast-folk women away, saying with a listless expression, "Get lost."

The manager hurried to exchange another glance.

The two beauties quickly retreated.

"Apologies. We merely wished to make you feel at home," the manager said, full of remorse.

Ares Shang curled his lip in disdain. "Make me feel at home? I'm afraid your establishment lacks the competence for that. Enough, this lord didn't come here to chat with you. Where is the tournament? If it's not as interesting and thrilling as you claim, this lord is walking out."

A short while later, guided by the manager, Ares Shang descended into the underground depths of the entertainment house.

Beneath the royal city lay no sprawling underworld city, but rather an intricate, labyrinthine network of drainage facilities.

The underground drainage channels even formed a miniature subterranean river.

Upon descending, Ares Shang saw a small boat moored along the drainage channel, manned by a hooded boatman.

"Ordinary guests coming here are usually blindfolded. The place we are heading... is not meant for outsiders to know," the manager said.

Ares Shang didn't even deign to look at him, wearing the expression of a man who would gladly put anyone to death if they dared to blindfold him.

*What an obnoxious profligate,* the manager thought. *Let's just hope the power backing you is enough to sustain such arrogance of yours, otherwise...* He genuinely looked forward to seeing this young master screaming, begging for mercy, and weeping tears of terror.

"There is a lingering stench of blood clinging to your body," Ares Shang suddenly remarked.

"What?" the manager asked, uncertain.

Ares Shang turned his head to look at him. "My experience tells me that you've killed many people—tortured them to death, even. You enjoy watching others shriek in agony and beg for mercy before you, and you revel in holding the power of life and death over others. You loathe the powerful and elite, yet you have no choice but to grovel before them. Every day, you are forced to act utterly deferential to your superiors and aristocrats, working your heart out for them, only to be subjected to their humiliation and scolding."

"How does one vent such fury and torment? Lacking the courage to exact revenge on the nobility and your masters, you can only channel all that rage and desire for retaliation onto everyone else."

chunks.chineseText:
“这个其他人，有你们娱乐场里的员工，有权贵不要的奴隶，有欠了债的赌鬼，有赌鬼的家人，还有得罪你们老板的人……”

管事脸色丕变，差点脱口问出“你是谁”，强忍住，话出口改为：“我不知道您在说什么。客人，船要出发了，您还去不去赛场？”

“赛场当然要去。”阿瑞斯商露出冷漠又残忍的笑容：“可我看你不顺眼，你说我该怎么办？”

管事往后退了一步。

阿瑞斯商提起骨杖：“我有没有跟你说过，我无聊的时候也喜欢杀人玩？你刚才说要让我宾至如归？那么你一定可以满足我这个愿望了？”

管事神色凝固，转身就跑。

噗嗤。

锋利的剑尖从管事的心脏部位露出。

阿瑞斯商轻轻抽出锋利的长剑，看着上面的血液滑落，剑身不留半丝血液，这才重新插回骨杖中。

管事的尸体倒在地上。

戴着头罩的船夫就那么站在船上，不知道是吓傻了，还是无动于衷。

阿瑞斯商跳到船上，不耐烦问：“还要等谁？”

船夫立刻用撑杆推动小船进入水道。

小船远去，这才有人过来收拾管事的尸体。

“马金完全被镇住了。他甚至没有来得及使用自己的天赋能力。”

“不是没有来得及，是他压根没有机会使出。那个纨绔少爷出剑非常快，我甚至没有看清他是什么时候拔-出的剑。”

“怪不得他敢一个人乱跑。他根本不像看上去的那么弱。”

“妈的！这家伙就是个疯子，说杀人就杀人。”

“你说那个纨绔少爷会不会是看出马金要送他去当羊仔……”

“不可能。如果他看出来，为什么还要上船？”

“因为他……无聊？想要找刺激？”

又一名兽人快跑过来，“上面有令，什么都不要做！就把他当普通贵客对待。”

正在处理尸体的兽人当即变成一只黑色蝙蝠飞了出去。

小船上，阿瑞斯商感知到什么，抬头就看到一只蝙蝠划过通道顶部。

郊外的一栋庄园。

一名又一名客人被从不同通道接入观赛场地。

这些客人无一例外都戴着精致的面具。

送阿瑞斯商前来的船夫全程非常安静和老实，把人送到地点，就静静地等在原地。

岸上有另外的侍者负责接待和引路。

他从排水渠过来，但上岸的却是庄园内一个小湖泊。

客人先被引入一辆兽车。

车内放着许多面具，任由客人挑选。

阿瑞斯商随意选取了一个眼罩型面具。

车辆停下，已经在庄园内。

但他们没有进入任何庄园内建筑，而是进入了一个开阔的宛如斗兽场一样的赛场。

阿瑞斯商到达时，看台上已经坐了七八成客人。

他被引入贵宾席，这让附近的客人多看了他两眼。

十分钟后，两支队伍进入比赛场地，每队十二人，全部二十四人。

一开始，这场比赛还算正常，只不过是两支队伍的兽人在争夺一只皮球。

形式有点像橄榄球，但这些兽人身上没有护具，只要能把球送入对方球门，不管是头顶脚踢还是手抛，都可以。

这个被称为“兽球”的球类活动在陆地兽人中非常受欢迎，有正规的赛事。

但现在他们看的这一场显然不是正规赛事，因为这场比赛没有犯规，你可以用各种方式让对手受伤甚至死亡。

阿瑞斯商看出来两只队伍的参赛队员虽然都在拼命，但并没有想要把另一支队伍的成员置于死地的意思。

只要对方伤到爬不起来，攻击方就会停止攻击，专心把球送向对方球门。

姑且称两队为红队和蓝队。

三十分钟的比赛，最后的比赛结果是红队输了。

主持人宣布蓝队获胜，并获得五百金达盾的奖励，蓝队队员只要能动的都在欢呼。

阿瑞斯商以为这场比赛到此就结束。比赛开始前他随便买红队赢，比赛结果出来，他失去了十枚金达盾。

“是不是觉得这场比赛很无聊很普通？根本没必要搞得这么神秘？”一名宾客忽然侧头对阿瑞斯商说话。

阿瑞斯商轻哼。

“不要失望。接下去才是这场比赛的精华，现在只是小小的热身而已。”宾客轻笑。

果然，就在蓝队成员准备离开之际，主持人忽然询问蓝队成员愿不愿意和红队再打一场附加赛。

只要蓝队成员能再次赢下比赛，就能额外再获得一千金达盾。

同样红队队员如果能反败为胜，也能获得这一千金达盾。

两队成员的呼吸都变得粗重。

五百金达盾已经是足够丰厚的奖金，分给队内每一个人，不敢说能让每一个队员都能在今后的人生中衣食无忧，但最短保证十年二十年的优质生活是没问题的。

如果能在这个基础上，再得到一千金达盾，那就等于每个人能获得125金达盾。

按照金达盾的购买力，他们能在王城非中心区域买下一栋独栋房屋还能做个小买卖，如果到别的城市生活，他们能买下更大的房屋、获得更优质的生活。

可以说他们和他们家人的人生都会因此改变。

赢球的蓝队成员还好，他们有五百金达盾打底。可输球的红队……哪怕胜率不大，他们还是想赌一赌机会。

那可是一千金达盾！

蓝队中有人动心，也有人只想见好就收，拿着刚得到的奖金立刻走人。

红队同样，他们不少人受了重伤，认为就算再比一场，胜率也极小，还容易造成无法治疗的极重伤势，运气不好，小命送掉都有可能。红队一半的人都想离开，不想再来一场附加赛。

主持人微笑表示：“想要走的人请站到左边，想要留下比赛的人请站到右边。”

两队队员面面相觑，他们心中有些担忧，比较敏感的更是心跳加快。

但这时他们不得不做出选择。

有人动了，在队友搀扶下走到左边，这是重伤者，不想再继续参赛。

也有人走到右边，想要继续比赛。

两支队伍重新分成了两堆。

想走的人有十七人，有一人已经走进左边队伍，又迟疑，重新回到右边队伍中。

想留下的人一共七个人。

两队队员看要走的人那么多，以为这场附加赛肯定是打不成了。

有人过来和两队队员说话，并给他们送来食物和酒水，还有人给受伤者涂抹药物。

队员们有点莫名其妙，但还是接受了这份善意。

就在这时，主持人当场宣布：“附加赛即将开始，请各位尊贵的客人现在开始下注。比赛两队为留下队和想走队，诸位贵客可以下注哪支队伍可以获得最后胜利，以及押注谁会是最后一个活着的参赛者。”

两队队员顿觉不对，当即就要反抗。

可刚刚入场的工作人员突然全都离场。

那名主持人也跳上看台。

看台一圈出现了全副武装的打手，这些打手每个人手里都拿着长柄武器。

留在比赛场中的两队队员越发不安和惊慌，大声询问这是怎么回事。
chunks.englishText:
"Those 'others' include employees from your entertainment house, slaves discarded by the nobility, gambling addicts drowning in debt, the families of those gamblers, and people who have offended your boss..."

The manager’s expression changed drastically. He almost blurted out, "Who are you?", but managed to swallow the words just in time, changing them to: "I don't know what you're talking about, honored guest. The boat is about to leave. Are you still going to the arena or not?"

"Of course I'm going to the arena," Aruis Shang said, revealing an indifferent yet cruel smile. "But I don't like the look of you. What do you suggest I should do?"

The manager took a step back.

Aruis Shang hoisted his bone staff. "Did I ever tell you that when I'm bored, I also like to kill people for fun? You just said you wanted to make me feel right at home, didn't you? Then I'm sure you can fulfill this wish of mine, right?"

The manager’s expression froze, and he turned and ran.

*Splish.*

A sharp sword tip protruded from the manager's chest.

Aruis Shang gently pulled out the razor-sharp longsword, watching the blood slide off the blade without a single drop remaining behind, before sliding it back into the bone staff.

The manager’s corpse collapsed to the ground.

The hooded boatman stood quietly on the boat, looking as though he had either been scared out of his wits or remained utterly indifferent.

Aruis Shang leaped onto the boat and asked impatiently, "Who else are we waiting for?"

The boatman immediately used his pole to push the small craft into the water channel.

As the small boat drifted away, people finally emerged to clean up the manager’s corpse.

"Magin was completely suppressed. He didn't even have time to use his innate ability."

"It's not that he didn't have time; he had no opportunity to use it at all. That arrogant young master drew his sword incredibly fast—I didn't even see when he unsheathed it."

"No wonder he dares to run around alone. He's nothing like as weak as he looks."

"Damn it! This guy's a complete lunatic. He kills the moment he says he will."

"Do you think that arrogant young master figured out that Magin was going to send him off as a sacrificial lamb..."

"Impossible. If he figured it out, why would he get on the boat?"

"Because he was... bored? Looking for a thrill?"

Another orc came running over. "Orders from above: do nothing! Just treat him like an ordinary distinguished guest."

The orc who was dealing with the corpse immediately transformed into a black bat and flew off.

On the boat, Aruis Shang sensed something. He looked up and saw a bat darting across the top of the tunnel.

An estate in the outskirts.

Guest after guest was led into the viewing arena through different tunnels.

Without exception, every single guest wore an exquisite mask.

The boatman who had brought Aruis Shang remained utterly silent and obedient throughout the entire journey. Once he delivered his passenger, he quietly waited in place.

On the shore, other attendants were responsible for reception and guidance.

Though he had come through a drainage channel, the place he stepped ashore was a small lake within the estate.

The guests were first ushered into a beast-drawn carriage.

Inside the carriage were numerous masks, left for the guests to choose from at will.

Aruis Shang casually selected an eye-mask style.

The vehicle came to a stop—they were already deep inside the estate.

However, rather than entering any of the estate's buildings, they were led into an open-air arena resembling a beast-taming pit.

By the time Aruis Shang arrived, seven or eight out of ten seats in the stands were already filled.

He was guided to the VIP section, which drew a few extra glances from nearby guests.

Ten minutes later, two teams entered the competition grounds—twelve members per team, twenty-four in total.

At first, the match seemed relatively normal, merely two teams of orcs fighting over a leather ball.

The format was somewhat like rugby, but these orcs wore no protective gear. As long as they could get the ball into the opponent's goal, it didn't matter whether they used their heads, feet, or threw it with their hands.

This ball game, known as "Beastball," was immensely popular among terrestrial orcs, boasting formal leagues.

However, the match they were watching now was clearly not an official one, for there were no fouls in this game. You could use any means necessary to injure or even kill your opponents.

Aruis Shang could see that while the participants from both teams were playing with all their might, they did not harbor any intent to inflict a fatal blow on the members of the opposing team.

As long as an adversary was injured to the point of being unable to get back up, the attacking side would halt their assault and focus entirely on driving the ball toward the opponent's goal.

Let us temporarily refer to the two teams as the Red Team and the Blue Team.

After a thirty-minute match, the final result was a loss for the Red Team.

The host announced the Blue Team as the victors, granting them a reward of five hundred gold daeduns. All Blue Team members who could still move erupted into cheers.

Aruis Shang had assumed the match would end here. Before it started, he had casually bet on the Red Team to win, and with the final result, he lost ten gold daeduns.

"Do you think this match was boring and ordinary? That there was no need to make it so mysterious?" A guest suddenly tilted his head and spoke to Aruis Shang.

Aruis Shang gave a light hum.

"Don't be disappointed. What comes next is the essence of this match; right now is merely a little warm-up." The guest chuckled softly.

Sure enough, just as the Blue Team members were preparing to leave, the host suddenly asked if they would be willing to play an extra match against the Red Team.

As long as the Blue Team could win again, they would receive an additional one thousand gold daeduns.

Similarly, if the Red Team could pull off a comeback, they would also receive that thousand gold daeduns.

The breathing of members from both teams grew heavy.

Five hundred gold daeduns was already a generous enough prize. Divided among everyone on the team, while it might not ensure every member a life of absolute ease forever, it was more than enough to guarantee a high-quality lifestyle for the next ten or twenty years.

If they could secure another thousand gold daeduns on top of that, it would mean each person would get an additional 125 gold daeduns.

Based on the purchasing power of gold daeduns, they could buy a detached house in a non-central district of the royal capital and even run a small business. If they lived in another city, they could buy an even larger house and enjoy an even better quality of life.

It was no exaggeration to say that their lives and the lives of their families would be fundamentally altered.

The winning Blue Team members were in a better position since they already had five hundred gold daeduns as a baseline. But the losing Red Team... even though their odds of winning were slim, they still wanted to take a gamble on the chance.

That was a thousand gold daeduns!

Some members of the Blue Team were tempted, while others just wanted to quit while they were ahead, grab their newly won prize money, and leave immediately.

The same went for the Red Team. Many of them were heavily injured and believed that even if they played another match, their chances of winning were minimal, and it would likely lead to severe, untreatable injuries. If luck wasn't on their side, they might even lose their lives. Half of the Red Team wanted to walk away rather than play an extra match.

The host smiled and announced, "Those who wish to leave, please stand to the left. Those who wish to stay and play, please stand to the right."

The team members looked at each other in dismay. A sense of unease gnawed at their hearts, and the more sensitive ones felt their heart rates spike.

Yet, at this moment, they had no choice but to make a decision.

Some moved. Supported by their teammates, they limped over to the left side—these were the heavily injured who wanted no part in continuing the competition.

Others walked to the right, determined to keep fighting.

The two teams split once more into two groups.

There were seventeen people who wanted to leave. One person had already stepped into the left-hand group, hesitated, and then walked back to the right-hand group.

A total of seven people wanted to stay.

Seeing so many people wanting to leave, the team members assumed this extra match would surely be called off.

People approached the team members, bringing them food and drinks, while others applied medicine to the wounded.

The members found it a bit inexplicable, but they accepted this goodwill nonetheless.

Right at that moment, the host announced on the spot: "The extra match is about to begin. Will all honored guests please place your bets now. The two teams for this match are the 'Staying Team' and the 'Leaving Team.' My esteemed guests, you may wager on which team will achieve final victory, as well as bet on who will be the last surviving participant."

The team members instantly sensed something was amiss and moved to resist on the spot.

Yet the staff who had just entered the arena suddenly all retreated.

The host leaped up into the stands as well.

A ring of fully armed thugs appeared around the perimeter of the stands, every single one of them wielding a long-handled weapon.

The seven team members left in the arena grew increasingly uneasy and panicked, shouting loudly to demand an explanation for what was happening.

chunks.chineseText:
主持人：“最精彩的比赛即将来临，这是生与死的搏斗，是兽人与异变怪物的战争。诸位贵客不用担心，你们的安全会受到本娱乐场的最佳保护。”

“哦，快看！那些想走的兽人正在转变。”

就在所有观众的瞩目下，十七名想要离开的兽人忽然一个接一个倒下，他们神情痛苦，死得非常快。

阿瑞斯商：艹！

他是真没想到这个娱乐场竟然敢搞这一套。

这可是众目睽睽下的杀人，而且是用虫毒杀人！

可看台上的看客们发出惊呼后，不但没有人离开，很多人都睁大了眼睛，满眼期待和好奇地等待那些倒下的兽人尸体产生变化。

主持人骄傲又得意：“诸位贵客，大家都听过不少关于虫毒感染者、异变者的传说，但真正亲眼看到过虫毒发作，以及虫毒感染者开始异变的人又有几个？”

“你们今天看到的就是现场！是最真实的怪物异变过程！”

“等到这些怪物异变完成，接下来就是留下队七人和这些怪物的战斗。”

“想要知道是兽人的战斗力更强，还是异变怪物的战斗力更强？现在就开始下注吧！”

“比赛最后，本娱乐场还会现场抽取三位贵客手刃怪物的机会，请千万不要错过！”

七名兽人眼睁睁地看着自己的同伴死亡并发生异变，他们发出痛苦和愤怒的哀嚎。

有人想要冲上看台进行报复，但看台一圈的打手把他们集体打了下去。

主持人冲着这七名兽人大喊：“你们想要活命，想要获得奖金，只有杀死这些异变怪物。否则你们所有人只有死！”

“一千金达盾，只要你能活到最后，你一个人就能获得整整一千金达盾！不，是一千五百金达盾！”

“拼命吧！为自己杀出一条活路！只要你能活到最后，只要你能杀死所有怪物，你就能成为人人羡慕的富豪和英雄！”

主持人的声音充满蛊惑。

七名参赛兽人没有人想要和异变怪物拼命。

他们反应很快，当即团结起来，打算逮着一个突破口突破。

可看台上出现了三尊炼金大炮，炮口正对准他们。

主持人还炫耀：“看，这就是我们娱乐场为贵客们准备的安全措施。有这三尊炼金炮在，这些怪物一个都别想靠近看台。”

七名兽人无奈，蓝队队长深吸气：“只能拼命了！”

“无聊。”贵宾席中，一名衣饰华贵的年轻雄性兽人忽然发出嗤笑声。

戴着面具的宾客们正激动，那年轻兽人忽然从贵宾席跃入赛场。

“啊啊啊！”有宾客惊叫。

年轻兽人跳下去的时候，还顺脚把主持人也给踹了下去。

“你干什么！”主持人大惊。

宾客们也瞪大了眼睛。

年轻雄性兽人脸上带着懒懒的略显残忍的笑，衣服松垮垮，穿着颜色和样式完全不同的两只靴子，面对正在转变的十七个怪物，慢慢从骨杖里拔-出一支骨剑。

主持人悄悄后退，想跑。

七名兽人当即就有人想要抓住他。

可主持人却变身成鸟，飞了起来。

刷！

一只鸟翅膀落到地上。

主持人发出惨叫，不得不又变回人身。

鸟少了一支翅膀基本完蛋，但人少了一支胳膊好歹还能继续战斗一会儿。

年轻兽人一脚把主持人踹入正在变异的怪物群中。

主持人连滚打爬想要逃跑，可一只异变的爪子抓住了他。

十七只怪物的异变速度非常快，它们全都睁开了眼睛，闻到活人的味就杀了过来。

主持人几乎连像样的抵抗都没几下，就被刚刚苏醒正极度渴望血腥的怪物们撕碎。

主持人临死前的惨叫响遍全场。

看台上，所有看客都站了起来，但直到此时竟然都没有人离去，他们就像在看什么特别刺激的节目一样，对着赛场中的活人大喊大叫，为他们鼓舞加油。

那个主持人的死，就像是一道恰到好处的开胃菜，没有人在乎他的死亡。

就连那些打手和娱乐场的工作人员，在看到他被踹进赛场时也没有一个人下去救他。

年轻兽人挥舞骨剑，貌似在围着那些怪物转圈圈。

他的姿态敏捷又随意，就跟跳舞一样。

七名兽人也鼓起勇气迎战这些变异怪物。

可此刻，怪物们就像是被什么吸引一样全都涌向那名年轻人。

年轻人不再转圈，手持骨剑开始大杀特杀，那些让参赛者惧怕不已的怪物们在这个年轻人的剑下就跟泥捏的一样。

宾客们纷纷惊叫，还有人鼓掌和吹口哨。

有些宾客一脸跃跃欲试，似乎也很想跳下去和怪物们战斗。

在他们看来，那个只手持一支长剑，连变身都没有变身的年轻兽人都能把怪物们杀得头都抬不起来，那他们也能。

关金娱乐场的管事只能赶紧出来劝阻。

庄园主人也露面让大家不要太激动。

年轻兽人眼神冷漠，出手狠辣。

他无力去救这些感染者。

夏冰是特例，因为他觉醒了有抗毒能力的血脉天赋，让他没有被虫毒彻底杀死，他的身体虽然被虫毒改变，但他的生命力还在，他还没有真正死亡。

所以他拔除夏冰体内的虫毒后，夏冰还能恢复正常，还能继续生活。

可这些感染者，它们都已经先被虫毒毒死，之后身体才被虫毒改造。

他没办法救它们，只有让它们彻底安息。

受到虫毒感染变异的怪物们在面对其他活人时凶悍异常，但在面对吸收了虫母九分之二心脏的年轻兽人面前，受到了天然的强烈威压。

它们在面对年轻兽人时几乎没有多少战斗力。

“至高伟大的存在，诅咒之神科尼泽厄斯，请听您信徒的呼唤。这些可怜的虫毒感染者全都献祭给您，请您诅咒现场所有亲手谋害过无辜兽人的人都被烈火焚身！”

当晚，城郊一栋庄园突发大火，烧毁了庄园内大半建筑，更烧死了不少人。

这些人有身份尊贵者，有庄园主人，有关金娱乐场的工作人员，也有奴隶……

剩下的活人不是逃跑，就是到处找人求救。

就在负责这一带的治安官带着大量警卫和救火员赶来此处时。

有人正慢悠悠地走在空荡荡的马路上。

这条马路不知是在郊外的缘故，还是其他原因，原本该点燃的路灯全都没有点燃。

黑漆漆的道路，没有星月的夜晚，天空开始下起冰冷的小雨。

阿瑞斯商提着骨杖似乎正在享受这种清冷孤寂，又像是在与黑夜做着什么秘密交流。

他放走了所有参赛的无辜兽人，还把他们赢得的金达盾平分给他们。

客人和工作人员中也有没沾染过无辜者血的人，他们没有享受到诅咒之神的宠爱，他也没有管这些人，任由这些人逃跑。

有人想要救那些突然自-焚的兽人，用水浇、用土灭，都没有用，那是诅咒之炎，岂是普通灭火办法就能熄灭？

阿瑞斯商趁着混乱在那个庄园中转了一圈。
chunks.englishText:
Host: "The most magnificent match is about to arrive. This is a battle of life and death, a war between orcs and mutated monsters. Esteemed guests, do not worry; your safety will be guaranteed to the absolute utmost by this entertainment house."

"Oh, look! Those orcs who wanted to leave are transforming."

Before the gaze of every spectator, the seventeen orcs who had wished to leave suddenly collapsed one by one. Their expressions were filled with agony, and they died with terrifying swiftness.

Aruis Shang: *Damn it!*

He genuinely hadn't expected this entertainment house to dare pull such a stunt.

This was murder in broad daylight, and what's more, they were using insect venom to kill!

Yet, after gasping in shock, not a single guest in the stands left. Instead, many of them widened their eyes, watching with breathless anticipation and curiosity as the corpses of those fallen orcs began to undergo mutation.

The host sounded proud and smug. "My esteemed guests, all of you have heard many legends about insect venom infected victims and mutants, but how many of you have actually witnessed with your own eyes the onset of insect venom and the beginning of a victim's mutation?"

"What you are seeing today is live! It is the most authentic monster mutation process!"

"Once these monsters complete their mutation, the next part will be the battle between the seven members of the Staying Team and these monsters."

"Want to know whether the orcs' combat prowess is stronger, or the mutated monsters' combat prowess is stronger? Place your bets now!"

"At the end of the match, this entertainment house will also randomly draw three esteemed guests on-site and grant them the opportunity to slay the monsters with their own hands. Please make sure not to miss out!"

The seven orcs watched with their own eyes as their companions died and mutated, letting out wails of grief and rage.

Some tried to charge up into the stands to retaliate, but the thugs ringing the perimeter beat them all back down together.

The host shouted at the seven orcs: "If you want to stay alive, if you want to win the prize money, your only choice is to kill these mutated monsters! Otherwise, every single one of you will die!"

"One thousand gold daeduns! As long as you survive to the end, you alone will receive a full thousand gold daeduns! No, fifteen hundred gold daeduns!"

"Fight for your lives! Carve out a path to survival for yourselves! As long as you survive to the end, as long as you kill all the monsters, you can become wealthy men and heroes the envy of everyone!"

The host's voice was dripping with seduction.

Not a single one of the seven participating orcs wanted to risk their lives fighting the mutated monsters.

Reacting quickly, they immediately banded together, intending to find a breakthrough point and punch through.

However, three alchemical cannons appeared in the stands, their barrels aimed straight at them.

The host even showed off. "Look, these are the safety measures our entertainment house has prepared for our honored guests. With these three alchemical cannons here, not a single one of these monsters will be able to approach the stands."

Left with no other choice, the seven orcs gritted their teeth as the Blue Team captain took a deep breath. "We have no choice but to fight for our lives!"

"Boring." In the VIP section, a young male orc dressed in lavish attire suddenly let out a sneering laugh.

While the masked guests were in a state of high agitation, the young orc suddenly leaped from the VIP section directly down into the arena.

"Ahhh!" a few guests screamed in fright.

As the young orc jumped down, he casually kicked the host down with him on his way.

"What are you doing?!" the host cried out in alarm.

The guests also widened their eyes.

With a lazy, slightly cruel smile on his face, wearing loose-fitting clothes and a pair of boots completely different in color and style, the young male orc faced the seventeen monsters in the midst of transformation and slowly drew a bone sword from his bone staff.

The host crept backward, wanting to run.

Immediately, some of the orcs tried to grab him.

Yet the host transformed into a bird and took flight.

*Slash!*

A bird's wing dropped to the ground.

The host let out a miserable scream and was forced to revert to human form.

A bird losing a wing was essentially finished, but a human losing an arm could at least keep fighting for a little longer.

The young orc kicked the host squarely into the pack of mutating monsters.

The host scrambled and crawled, desperate to escape, but a mutated claw grabbed hold of him.

The mutation speed of the seventeen monsters was terrifyingly fast. They all snapped their eyes open, and catching the scent of living flesh, they lunged forward.

The host barely put up any semblance of resistance before he was torn to shreds by the newly awakened monsters, who were suffering from a rabid craving for blood.

The host's dying screams echoed across the entire arena.

Up in the stands, all the spectators stood up, yet up until this moment, not a single person left. Acting as though they were watching some intensely thrilling show, they hollered and screamed at the living beings down in the arena, cheering them on.

The host's death was like a perfectly timed appetizer; nobody cared about his demise.

Even the thugs and the entertainment house staff didn't send a single person down to rescue him when they saw him kicked into the arena.

The young orc brandished his bone sword, seemingly circling leisurely around the monsters.

His posture was agile and casual, reminiscent of a dance.

The seven orcs also mustered their courage to meet the mutated monsters in battle.

Yet at that moment, as if drawn by some invisible magnetic pull, all the monsters swarmed toward the young man.

Stopping his circles, the young man gripped his bone sword and began a vicious slaughter. Those monsters, which had struck terror into the hearts of the participants, were like clay figures under this young man's blade.

The guests gasped in shock one after another, and some began to applaud and whistle.

A few guests wore eager expressions, as if they desperately wanted to jump down and fight the monsters themselves.

From their perspective, since this young orc—who only held a single longsword and hadn't even transformed—was able to beat the monsters down so thoroughly that they couldn't even raise their heads, they could do it too.

The manager of Guanjin Entertainment House hurried out to urge calm.

The owner of the estate also showed his face, telling everyone not to get too excited.

The young orc's gaze was ice-cold, his strikes ruthlessly lethal.

He lacked the power to save these infected individuals.

Xia Bing had been a special case because he had awakened a bloodline talent with anti-toxin properties, preventing the insect venom from completely killing him. Though his body had been altered by the insect venom, his life force remained; he had not truly died.

Therefore, after the venom was purged from Xia Bing's body, he could return to normal and continue living his life.

These infected victims, however, had already been poisoned to death by the insect venom first, their bodies reshaped by it afterward.

He could not save them; the only mercy he could grant was to let them rest in peace.

The monsters mutated by the insect venom were ferocious and tyrannical when facing other living humans, but in front of this young orc—who had absorbed two-ninths of the Insect Mother's heart—they were suppressed by an innate, overwhelming pressure.

They possessed practically no combat effectiveness whatsoever when facing the young orc.

"O supreme and mighty existence, Conizeus, God of Curses, please hearken to the call of your devout follower. All these pitiful insect venom-infected victims are sacrificed to you. I beg you to curse everyone present who has personally murdered innocent orcs, that they may be consumed by raging flames!"

That very night, a massive fire broke out in the suburban estate, reducing over half of its structures to ashes and burning numerous people to death.

Among them were nobles of high status, the estate owner, employees of Guanjin Entertainment House, and slaves alike...

The remaining survivors either fled or scurried everywhere begging for help.

By the time the local sheriff arrived with a massive contingent of guards and firefighters, someone was strolling leisurely down the empty street.

Whether due to being in the suburbs or for some other reason, the streetlights that should have been lit were all dark.

Along the pitch-black road, on a starless and moonless night, a cold, fine drizzle began to fall from the sky.

Aruis Shang carried his bone staff, seemingly enjoying this desolate solitude, or perhaps engaging in some secret communion with the night.

He had let all the innocent participating orcs go, and even split the gold daeduns they had won evenly among them.

Among the guests and staff, there were also those who had never stained their hands with the blood of the innocent. Having not enjoyed the favor of the God of Curses, he left them alone, letting them run for their lives.

Some tried to rescue the orcs who had suddenly burst into spontaneous combustion, dousing them with water or smothering them with dirt, but it was all in vain. That was the Flame of Curses—how could ordinary firefighting methods ever extinguish it?

Taking advantage of the chaos, Aruis Shang took a stroll through the estate.

chunks.chineseText:
他理所当然地收走了那三尊炼金炮，并把庄园密室中的财富席卷一空。

今晚的消耗全部回来了，还有得赚。

有人悄悄跟在他身后，不止一个。

阿瑞斯商就像不知道一样，大摇大摆地在途中招了辆车，就这么径直回去了双灯旅馆。

旅馆管家看到这位进入房间就没有出来的纨绔少爷竟然从旅馆大门外进来，嘴巴微微张开。

然后这位眼尖的管家还看到这位贵客的衣服和靴子上似乎都沾染了一点血迹？

旅馆大厅中也有不少人在看着阿瑞斯商。大多兽人都对战斗气息很敏感，他们能感觉出来这名年轻兽人身上还未消散的肃杀之气。

阿瑞斯商丝毫没把那些打量的目光放入眼里，乘坐升降机上了顶楼，在中年女仆无奈的眼神中，回到卧室，倒头就睡。
chunks.englishText:
He quite naturally cleared out those three alchemical cannons and looted the wealth stored in the estate's secret chamber clean.

Everything spent tonight had been fully recovered, with a handsome profit on top.

Someone was tailing him quietly—more than one person, in fact.

Acting as if he were completely oblivious, Aruis Shang swaggered out, flagged down a carriage along the way, and headed straight back to the Double Lantern Hotel just like that.

When the hotel manager saw the arrogant young master—who hadn't stepped foot out of his room since entering—walking in from the hotel's front entrance, his mouth fell slightly agape.

Then, the sharp-eyed manager noticed that this distinguished guest's clothes and boots seemed to be stained with a few specks of blood?

Inside the hotel lobby, quite a few people were also watching Aruis Shang. Most orcs were sensitive to the aura of battle, and they could sense the lingering, murderous intent that had yet to dissipate from this young orc.

Aruis Shang paid those probing gazes not an ounce of heed. He boarded the elevator to the top floor, ignored the middle-aged maid's helpless look, returned to his bedroom, and fell fast asleep the moment his head hit the pillow.

chunks.chineseText:
第125章 一夜扬名

黑森林城，不帅揉了揉眼睛。

他刚才眼皮有点跳。

也不知道是他这边要出事，还是商非凡在王城“玩”得太野。

虎王看到他的动作，亲切地说：“时间不早，你有两天没睡了吧？先去休息，明天上午十点，我们进地下城。”

他们下午赶路，入夜时抵达黑森林城。

虎王虽然想要尽快进入地下图书馆，见到那位老祖宗，但黑森林城还有很多事等待他处理。

如果他没有亲自前来也就算了，他既然亲自来了，肯定要在各处露面。

首先就是慰问血骨军团，和团长蒙川见面了解最新情况。

其次就是连夜面见黑森林城城民，慰问伤者，表达自己对丹顿侯爵失职的愤怒，明言表示会把这件事查个清清楚楚，不会放过任何有罪之人。

关于岩浆爆发一事则模糊带过，只说王城已经派出最好的地质研究者和相关天赋者正对此事进行探查。允诺到时候不管情况如何，只要查清就会告知民众。

第三就是去南城码头见黑水河水军统领巴特将军，接手黑森林城水军。

虎王并没有上来就掳夺巴特的将军职位，而是以一种和缓的方式给巴特安排了两名副手。

而明显已经收到王后消息的巴特表现得很安宁。

这让虎王越发忌惮丹顿家族暗中养的那支私军，但他除了安排人手盯住巴特将军今后的行踪以外，其他的事情他都暂时无能为力——连那支军队藏在哪里都不知道，打都不知道朝哪里打。

这些事情全部做完，虎王才能安下心去地下城图书馆。

但等这些事办完，已经半夜。

虎王再急，也得给自己和给手下休息的时间，尤其不帅连续两天王城和黑森林城来回跑，几乎就没怎么休息。

不帅跟着虎王从头跑到尾，累倒是不累，就是老是被人暗中打量或被眼刀。

自从他是虎王私生子的秘密暴露后，他就经常收到这些夹杂好奇、鄙视、同情、羡慕妒忌和带有某些目的的打量目光，离开王城一年多，也离开这些目光一年多，他差点就要不习惯了。

“谢陛下。”不帅很干脆地行礼退下。

他并不想站在虎王身前身后充当近臣，但虎王不让他走，他也不好擅自离开，只能跟着。

搞得虎王带着的几个真正近臣和近卫们看他的目光都有点不对劲。

一个已经被赶出王城的私生子，突然又回到虎王身边，虎王对其还非常亲切温厚，是个人都会怀疑吧？

不帅贴着狰爷裹着外衣直接躺下的时候，王城多处地方灯火通明。

一场“娱乐性质”的竞赛，事前还做好了万全防护，类似性质的竞赛，关金娱乐场进行过不止一次，每次都能顺利结束并迎来好评。

可这次却出了事，而且不出事则已，一出就是大事。

关金娱乐场死掉多少工作人员，包括参赛人员全部死光，都不是问题。问题是死亡名单中还有宾客，而且是大把的宾客。

这些宾客中有富豪，有官员，也有贵族。

可以说哪怕只是死掉一个，也会让关金娱乐场头疼不已。

而这次死掉的宾客足足有三十多人！

还是被烧死，尸体烧得跟焦炭一样。

关金娱乐场在事发后立刻竭尽所能地封锁消息。

但庄园发生了大火，老远就有人看到，在关金娱乐场想要封锁消息时，该区治安官已经带着救火队赶往现场。

更糟糕的是逃出的宾客和参赛队员把事情全都宣扬了出去。

宾客们不会说太多，尤其是与他们不利的事情。

但参赛队员可管不了这么多，再说当时帮他们杀死变异者、分他们金达盾的贵族少爷可是跟他们说了，要想不被灭口，最好的做法就是尽自己所能把当晚的事情传出去，知道的人越多，他们越安全。

至于担心事后报复？

这场娱乐死了那么多权贵，关金娱乐场自身都难保，哪还有精力来追杀当时的参赛者。

正好他们手头有了这么多金达盾，传完消息就可以带着家人连夜离开王城，关金娱乐场现在根本顾及不了他们。

所以事发不到半个小时，事情就传开了。

随着富豪、官员、贵族家里跑来现场找人，消息再也控制不住。

特别调查局也被惊动，因为事情涉及到虫毒感染。

现场也不再只有一两个治安官，治安局派出了大量人手赶赴现场查案。

事发后一个小时，城卫军包围了整个关金娱乐场，治安总局局长亲自出面搜捕关金老板。

但整个关金娱乐场的上层几乎全部消失，只剩中下层管理人员和普通工作人员，这些人被抓捕审问时都不知道发生了什么事情。

“当时到底发生了什么事情？有谁知道详情？”治安局局长怒问手下。

“我们找到了三名宾客，还有几名工作人员，他们吓得很厉害。根据他们告诉我们的情况……”手下尽可能详细叙述。

“所以当时解决那些虫毒异变者的是一名贵族少爷？”

“对。”

“他是谁？”

“暂且还不知道他的身份，宾客们都戴了面具，我们正在打听。不过他的打扮非常有特色，他当时手持一支锋利的骨剑，骨剑藏在骨杖中。另外他穿着两只颜色和样式都不一样的靴子。”

“庄园失火，现场宾客和工作人员身上突然起火又是怎么回事？”

“呃，这件事也正在查，原因暂时不明。”不等局长骂人，该名治安官就赶紧说道：“因为这些人身上的火难以扑灭，他们跑到哪里，哪里就会被点燃。那座庄园之所以大半被烧毁，就是因为这点。”

局长：“查这些死者的关联，看他们是不是共同吃喝了什么，或者共同佩戴了什么东西，抑或共同参与了某件事。”

“是。”治安官脸上露出迟疑之色。

治安局长皱眉：“你是不是还有什么没说？”

治安官：“我们听到一些传言，说那些宾客和工作人员身上会起火，很可能和邪神祭祀有关。您知道，虫毒感染者出现在哪里，哪里必然会有邪神信徒。当晚关金娱乐场故意用虫毒感染部分参赛者，很可能也是祭祀仪式的一部分。”

治安局长深吸气，打算找特别调查局局长好好谈谈，这事太大，他们治安局已经扛不住。

“无论如何都要把关金老板和他们的高层给我抓回来！”

“是。”

“确定客人自-焚和那个跳入赛场杀怪的贵族少爷无关？”治安局长突然问。

治安官毫不犹豫地摇头：“应该是无关，被我们询问的多名目击者都肯定很多人身上突然起火时，那名贵族少爷还在和虫毒感染怪物打斗。”

“那贵族少爷为什么会跳进赛场？”

“有人说他是找刺激，也有人说他看不过眼……”

“尽快找到这个人！就说有问题请教他。”

“是。”

类似的对话在多处地方发生。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 125: Famous Overnight (Part 1)

In Black Forest City, Bu Shuai rubbed his eyes.

His eyelid had been twitching slightly just a moment ago.

He wasn't sure if something was about to go wrong on his end, or if Shang Feifan was running completely wild "playing around" in the Royal City.

Seeing his gesture, the Tiger King said affectionately, "It's getting late. You haven't slept in two days, have you? Go get some rest first. Tomorrow morning at ten, we'll enter the dungeon."

They had traveled through the afternoon and arrived at Black Forest City as night fell.

Although the Tiger King was eager to enter the underground library as soon as possible to see that legendary ancestor, there were still many matters in Black Forest City awaiting his personal attention.

It would have been one thing had he not come in person, but since he had made the trip himself, he naturally had to show his face in various places.

First was to pay his respects to the Blood Bone Legion, meeting with Commander Meng Chuan to receive a briefing on the latest situation.

Second was to hold a nocturnal audience with the citizens of Black Forest City, comforting the injured, expressing his profound anger over Marquis Danton's dereliction of duty, and explicitly stating that he would thoroughly investigate the matter and spare no guilty party.

As for the magma eruption, it was glossed over with vague rhetoric, claiming only that the Royal City had already dispatched the finest geological researchers and talented awakened ones to investigate the phenomenon. He promised that whatever the circumstances, the public would be informed once the truth was uncovered.

Third was to visit the South City Wharf to meet General Bart, commander of the Black Water River naval forces, and take over command of the Black Forest City navy.

Instead of abruptly stripping General Bart of his rank, the Tiger King adopted a more temperate approach, assigning two deputy commanders to Bart's side.

Bart, who had clearly already received a message from the Queen, behaved with absolute composure.

This only made the Tiger King even more wary of the private army secretly maintained by the Danton family. However, apart from assigning personnel to monitor General Bart's future movements, there was nothing else he could do for the time being—he didn't even know where that army was hidden, let or alone where to strike.

Only after all these tasks were completed could the Tiger King finally set his mind at ease and head to the underground library.

By the time these affairs were settled, it was already the middle of the night.

No matter how anxious the Tiger King was, he had to give himself and his subordinates time to rest, especially since Bu Shuai had been running back and forth between the Royal City and Black Forest City for two consecutive days with virtually no sleep.

Following the Tiger King through every step of the journey, Bu Shuai wasn't particularly tired; it was just that people kept sizing him up in secret or casting sharp, dagger-like glances his way.

Ever since the secret of him being the Tiger King's illegitimate son was exposed, he had constantly received these probing gazes mixed with curiosity, contempt, sympathy, envy, jealousy, and hidden agendas. Having left the Royal City for over a year—and thus escaping these looks for just as long—he had almost fallen out of the habit.

"Thank you, Your Majesty." Bu Shuai offered a crisp salute and withdrew.

He had no desire to linger in front of or behind the Tiger King acting as a close minister, but since the Tiger King hadn't dismissed him, it wouldn't do to leave without authorization, leaving him no choice but to tag along.

This resulted in the Tiger King's actual close ministers and bodyguards casting rather peculiar looks in his direction.

An illegitimate son who had once been banished from the Royal City suddenly returned to the Tiger King's side, and the Tiger King treated him with extreme warmth and affection—anyone would harbor suspicions, wouldn't they?

The moment Bu Shuai wrapped himself in his outer garment and lay down beside ferocious beast Zeng Ye, multiple locations across the Royal City were still brightly lit.

It was supposed to be an "entertainment-style" competition, complete with thorough security precautions beforehand. Similar events had been held at the Guanjin Entertainment Arena more than once, each time concluding smoothly and earning rave reviews.

Yet an accident had occurred this time—and if disaster was going to strike, it had to strike in a catastrophic way.

The exact number of Guanjin Entertainment Arena staff killed, or the fact that all the participating contestants had perished, wasn't the real issue. The crux of the matter was that the casualty list included guests, and a large number of them at that.

Among these guests were wealthy tycoons, government officials, and high-ranking nobles.

It was safe to say that even if just a single one of them had died, it would have given the Guanjin Entertainment Arena an excruciating headache.

Yet this time, over thirty guests had died!

And they had been burned to death, their corpses charred to the consistency of charcoal.

Immediately following the incident, the Guanjin Entertainment Arena tried every possible means to suppress and seal off the news.

However, the manor had suffered a massive blaze visible from afar. Just as the arena attempted a cover-up, the local magistrate had already led a firefighting squad rushing toward the scene.

What was even worse was that the guests and contestants who managed to escape broadcasted everything far and wide.

The guests wouldn't say too much, especially about matters detrimental to themselves.

The contestants, however, couldn't care less. Besides, that aristocratic young master who had helped them slay the mutated beasts and distributed Golden Dars to them had given them a piece of advice: if they wanted to avoid being silenced, the best course of action was to spread the events of that night as far as possible. The more people who knew, the safer they would be.

As for fearing post-incident retaliation?

With so many powerful elites dead in this entertainment massacre, the Guanjin Entertainment Arena was struggling just to save its own skin; they hardly had the energy to hunt down the surviving contestants.

And since they now had so many Golden Dars on hand, they could simply pack up their families and flee the Royal City overnight once the news was spread. The arena simply couldn't look after them now.

Consequently, less than half an hour after the incident, the news broke wide open.

As the families of wealthy tycoons, officials, and nobles rushed to the scene to search for their missing relatives, the situation spiraled completely out of control.

Even the Special Investigation Bureau was alarmed, as the case involved parasite venom infection.

The scene was no longer populated by just a couple of magistrates; the Public Security Bureau dispatched a massive force to rush to the location and investigate the case.

One hour after the incident, the City Guard surrounded the entire Guanjin Entertainment Arena, and the Chief of the Public Security Bureau personally stepped forward to hunt down and arrest the owner of Guanjin.

However, the upper management of the entire Guanjin Entertainment Arena had practically vanished, leaving behind only middle and lower-level management and ordinary staff. When these people were captured and interrogated, they had no idea what had actually transpired.

"What on earth happened back there? Does anyone know the details?" the Chief of Public Security demanded angrily of his subordinates.

"We managed to find three guests and a few staff members, and they were terrified out of their wits. According to what they told us..." The subordinate detailed the account as thoroughly as possible.

"So the ones who dealt with those parasite-mutated monstrosities at the time were an aristocratic young master?"

"Yes."

"Who is he?"

"His identity remains unknown for now. The guests were all wearing masks, and we are currently making inquiries. However, his attire was extremely distinctive: he carried a sharp bone sword concealed inside a walking staff. Moreover, he wore a pair of boots that differed in both color and style."

"What about the manor catching fire? How did the sudden ignition of the guests and staff at the scene happen?"

"Uh, that matter is also under investigation, and the cause is temporarily unknown." Before the Chief could curse, the magistrate quickly added, "Because the fire on these individuals was extremely difficult to extinguish, wherever they fled, that place would catch fire as well. That's the main reason why a large portion of the manor was burned to the ground."

The Chief ordered: "Investigate the connections among these victims. See if they shared a common meal, wore a common item, or jointly participated in any specific event."

"Yes." A look of hesitation flickered across the magistrate's face.

The Chief frowned: "Is there something else you haven't told me?"

The magistrate replied: "We've heard some rumors suggesting that the sudden ignition of the guests and staff is very likely related to an evil god sacrifice. As you know, wherever parasite-infected individuals appear, worshippers of evil gods are bound to follow. The fact that the Guanjin Entertainment Arena deliberately infected some contestants with parasite venom that night was likely part of the sacrificial ritual."

The Chief took a deep breath, intending to have a serious talk with the Director of the Special Investigation Bureau; this matter was simply too colossal for the Public Security Bureau to shoulder alone.

"Bring the owner of Guanjin and their higher-ups back to me, no matter what!"

"Yes."

"Are you certain that the self-immolation of the guests is unrelated to that aristocratic young master who leaped into the arena to slaughter the monsters?" the Chief suddenly asked.

Without a shred of hesitation, the magistrate shook his head. "It should be unrelated. Multiple eyewitnesses we questioned confirmed that when those people suddenly burst into flames, that aristocratic young master was still actively fighting the parasite-infected monsters."

"Then why did that aristocratic young master leap into the arena?"

"Some say he was looking for a thrill, while others say he simply couldn't stand by and watch..."

"Track this person down as quickly as possible! Tell him we have some questions we'd like his guidance on."

"Yes."

Similar conversations were taking place in numerous locations across the city.
