By the time a squad of bailiffs stormed into the small building rented by the tabloid, impounded everything inside, and attempted to arrest the tabloid's editor-in-chief and editors, the situation escalated into an even bigger uproar.

Had those two beastmen from the tabloid—who claimed to be the editor-in-chief and editor—simply surrendered and meekly left with the bailiffs, the matter might have quietly faded into obscurity.

However, possessed by some unknown madness, the moment the bailiffs arrived to make arrests, the two of them grabbed a pair of massive megaphones, leaped onto the rooftop, and shouted at the surrounding crowd of onlookers:

"Freedom of the press, or death!"

"The masses demand the truth! For you to ban the newspaper agency is to ban the truth!"

"The privileged should not ride roughshod above the law! The law grants people the right to speak and to know the truth!"

"The Queen is dispatching people to arrest newspaper staff on trumped-up charges—this is a blatant, naked violation of the citizenry!"

"To safeguard the public's right to know, and for the freedom of journalistic reporting, we are willing to offer our lives!"

The leading bailiff flew into a rage, pointing at the two beastmen holding forth on the roof and roaring, "Pull them down here for me!"

Ding Gou, who had self-proclaimed himself as editor-in-chief, suddenly pulled out a long saber and shouted, "It matters not if our heads are severed, so long as our convictions remain true! Kill me, Ding Gou, and others will follow in my footsteps! For the sake of freedom of the press—!"

*Swish!*

The long saber swept across Ding Gou's throat, and blood sprayed outward.

The surrounding beastmen stared wide-eyed, letting out gasps of shock.

The bailiff down below was also dumbfounded: *Mother of Insects, how come he actually killed himself?!*

Peidan, who had self-proclaimed himself as editor, burst into tearful sobs, crying out, "Brother Ding, go on ahead! This brother of yours is coming right along to keep you company!"

Peidan suddenly produced an oil-belly worm lamp, opened it, and poured the lamp oil inside straight over his head.

"Stop him! Quickly stop him!" the leading bailiff roared. He couldn't even wait for his subordinates to scramble onto the roof; he rushed up there himself.

Peidan flicked his hand, flames flickering from his fingertip, while loudly proclaiming: "Our heads may roll and our blood may flow, but the truth of the news can never be extinguished! Today I offer my body to my ideals, asking only for freedom of the press! Ah-ah-ah!"

*Boom!* Peidan's entire body ignited, instantly turning into a human torch.

More and more beastmen gathered around the vicinity. Seeing the two beastmen on the rooftop—one slitting his throat in suicide, the other setting himself ablaze—they were all utterly stunned.

Suddenly, a sorrowful cry rang out from the crowd: "Big brother! No, big brother don't die! Why drive my big brother to his death? How are my one-year-old sister and I supposed to survive?!"

"Waaah, Daddy, Daddy, why did you die?"

"The Queen is driving people to their deaths!"

"This is outrageous! The Tiger Kingdom's royal family flew into a blind rage and ruthlessly drove two living souls to their deaths!"

"Aaaaaah, I'll fight you bastards to the death! Give me back my brother's life!"

"Daddy, Daddy, you died such a tragic death!"

"Kill those running dogs! Kill those villains who oppress the common folk! Kill them!"

Chaos erupted on the scene. A dozen or so beastmen rushed out from the crowd of onlookers, charging toward the bailiffs who had been arresting people and smashing things up.

Upon seeing a situation that should have been straightforward explode into public fury, the leading bailiff panicked for a moment. Yet faced with the charging beastmen, he couldn't just stand there doing nothing.

He immediately roared at the top of his lungs: "We are bailiffs! This is a crime scene! Everyone stand back, or else you will all be arrested on charges of disturbing the peace!"

"You lackeys of the Queen! Driving two people to their deaths wasn't enough, and now you want to drive even more to their graves? Come on then, you think I'm scared of you? Brothers and sisters, charge! Taking down one of them is breaking even, taking down two is a profit!"

A chaotic brawl broke out right then and there.

*Boom!* Something on the scene emitted a loud bang, billowing with smoke.

Someone curiously peered toward a shelf nearby and spotted a beastman squeezed inside a crate, wearing a piece of cloth on his head and holding a strange lighting fixture, as if engaging in some shady business.

The bailiffs blew their whistles frantically, calling for reinforcements from the City Guard.

Nearby patrol squads heard the whistle blows and sprinted toward the location at top speed.

By the time the riot was completely quelled, several corpses had been left behind at the scene, with dozens more injured. Yet among the dead, not a single one was a bailiff or a city guard; every single casualty was a common citizen.

chunks.chineseText:
城卫军虽然在努力驱赶围观的兽人，但天空、屋顶、街道上围观的兽人太多了。

很多兽人天性桀骜不驯，只要没有特别强硬的理由和实力，根本没办法驱赶他们离开。

“这是怎么回事？你们竟然打死了这么多人？谁动的手？”城卫军南营营长赶来，吃惊地看向地上躺着的尸体。

眼看周围的兽人全都带着愤怒的目光瞪向他们。

领头的治安官冷汗唰地流下来：完了，事情闹大了。

城卫军南营营长深吸气，一挥手：“只要是当事人，全都给我带走！”

最后，原本来抓人的十来名治安员连同地上的尸体一起，都被城卫军带走了。

玩家论坛。

“卧槽！好爽！原来跟官方势力对抗是这种感觉，哎呀，当时我的心脏都要跳出喉咙。”

“这也就是游戏，要是现实，臣妾真的不敢。”

“快快快！之前抹脖子和自-焚的丁勾皮蛋两位大侠快出来献身说法，把自己杀死是什么一个感觉？爽不爽？”

“爽你个鬼啊！不过……我承认我当时自己把自己说得热血沸腾了，艹，真没想到老子有一天抹脖子能抹得那么豪爽！”

“亲身经历者奉劝诸位一句，要自杀千万别自-焚。虽然游戏降低了痛感，但那种窒息和恐惧……，当你发现自己无论如何都不能呼吸，那种一点点等待死亡降临的恐惧就会将你淹没。先不说现实中火烧自己有多疼，光是窒息的痛苦就会让你后悔。真的，我应该换种方式。幸亏这是游戏，能模糊死亡感受，否则我非得留下心理阴影不可。”

“哈哈哈，楼上煞笔不解释！”

“虫日的狗蛋给我滚！听说现场有人喊我爸爸，儿子，快出来！”

“去泥马！那是舞台效应懂吗？”

“兄弟姐妹们，准备好啊。我们三天不能上了，你们可千万别让报社倒了！”

“孩砸，放心的去吧。报社我们接手了。”

“留影哥已经做出初级照相机和胶卷。下一份八卦报，等着震撼三重奏吧！”

“什么？照相机都做出来了，这是什么神人啊？”

“太好了，以后我们是不是能看到游戏世界里的NPC和风景都是什么样了。”

“我要看俺们谷主的盛世美颜，不要写生画，要真实照片！”

“我想看二王子和谷主一起的，最好是两人都躺在床上的。”

“王室照会有的，床照也会有的，我们八卦报一定会努力满足大家的要求。”

“只是初级复古款，等我做出可便携的现代入门款，大家再来夸赞啊。”

“滚！炫耀鬼都去死！”

玩家们开开心心，热热闹闹。

虎国王城某权贵的家里，聚集在一起的七八个人则是愁眉苦脸。

“我说你的那个手下是怎么办事的？这么点小事都办不好，竟然把人逼到要自杀的程度？”

“谁知道那蠢货都干了什么！”

“逼死两个人也就算了，竟然还跟围观的民众打斗，这是想要激起民愤吗？”

“当时情况太乱了，我总觉得事情没那么简单，就像是有人在故意挑事。”

“好了，不管是不是有人挑事，目前已经死了好几个人，又有那么多人看见。王后不担心这些，但如果虎王震怒，我们怎么办？”

“这可是材料展销会和传承分享大会举办前期，城里到处都是外来的商人和各国名流，这事如果爆开……”

“不能掩盖吗？”

“当时围观的人那么多，要怎么掩盖？”

“不管怎么样，这事不能瞒着王后，先报上去吧。”

“报给王后？你去报？”

“……那家报社还封吗？”

“封泥马麻痹封！先把那些死者家属都搞定，别让他们闹腾起来。这事闹大，我们都没好果子吃！”

几个人商讨后，一致决定先瞒着王后，他们先处理此事首尾，直到瞒不下去再说。

原本要被封的八卦报社大门敞开，好些兽人在大门进进出出。

城卫军特别派了巡逻队在这里平均一个小时巡逻一次，防止再闹出事情。

“那家八卦报怎么忽然多了那么多人？”

“不知道啊。是不是有人看不下眼，在为那家报社打抱不平？”

“也许是那几个惨死兽人的家人和朋友。”

“总觉得要发生大事了。”

“王后心眼也太小了，不就是曝光当年她夺宝害死自家亲戚，结果被亲侄女儿小三的事吗？她如果没做这事，人家也不会曝光出来。”

“看王后怒成这样，还不惜逼死人，看来那八卦报上说的也是真的了。”

“我也觉得像是真的。”

“但也有人说是污蔑，是有人故意给王后泼黑水。”

“已经有人去找报上提到的那个林格莱特家族，王后当年有没有逼迫他们家把安妮塔和她妹妹嫁给老兽人，找他们问一问就知道。”

“哎呀，我现在就想知道安妮塔夫人给我们陛下生下的儿子拉斐尔郎沐知不知道其母亲与王后之间的仇恨根源，如果原来不知道，现在知道了，他会是什么反应？”

不帅什么反应都没有，他还在忙着提炼魔晶，顺便指导商非凡如何给自己的魔法进行奠基。

魔法师必须要有魔法天赋，用比较形象的话来说就是要拥有一枚魔法种子。

但有了种子不代表就能让它生根发芽，你得培育它、激活它，再想办法促使它生根发芽。

魔法奠基就相当于是给魔法种子准备适合的土壤和肥料，还要浇上一点水。根据魔法种子的不同，土壤配比、肥料种类、浇水多少，甚至是温度见光向阴等都得考虑到。

适合的土壤，才能让种子茁壮成长，否则种子就算发芽，也会长得瘦弱和歪曲，大大影响到将来。

特调局总局长眼看上门找拉斐尔“谈心”的人越来越多，直接在大门上挂了一个“拉斐尔郎沐出差中”，自己也遁了。

比起不帅这边的忙碌，雷米尔就坐不住了，他去偷偷见了伊娃。

伊娃看他又不请自来，皱眉：“不是跟你说，少到这里来吗？”

雷米尔抿了抿嘴唇：“最近王宫里有些不利于我的传言，有人提起我和内蒂有来往，还说内蒂是为了保护我才杀死五公主。”

伊娃意外：“你和内蒂不是秘密来往吗？怎么会泄露？”

雷米尔神色阴沉：“我不知道。也许内蒂和别人提起过。”

“都是谁在传？”

“宫里的侍女和仆人。有和我交好的侍卫提醒我。他的未婚妻就是一名宫廷侍女。”

伊娃想了想，不在意地说：“只是一点传言，只要对方手头没有铁板的证据，你就当做不知道。就算知道了也没什么，少年慕艾，你长得这么好，在虎王身边的地位也不低，有个侍女会喜欢上你不是很正常的事情吗？”

雷米尔的脸色变好了一些：“我想着我常来见一见多丽丝，让人以为我是多丽丝的入幕之宾，就不会认为我和内蒂有什么关系。”

“幼稚。”伊娃嗤笑，“你是想打造风流人设吗？”

雷米尔低头。
chunks.englishText:
Even though the City Guard were doing their utmost to drive away the onlookers among the beastmen, the sheer number of spectators filling the skies, rooftops, and streets was overwhelming.

Many beastmen were naturally untamed and rebellious; unless there was an exceptionally forceful justification and overwhelming might, it was virtually impossible to drive them off.

"What is going on here? How on earth did you people beat so many to death? Who struck the blows?" The commander of the City Guard's Southern Camp arrived, staring in astonishment at the corpses lying upon the ground.

With all the surrounding beastmen glaring at them with furious gazes, cold sweat instantly poured down the lead bailiff’s back: *It’s over. The situation has blown up.*

The Southern Camp commander took a deep breath and waved a hand. "Take all the involved parties into custody!"

In the end, the dozen or so bailiffs who had originally come to make arrests, along with the corpses on the ground, were all hauled away by the City Guard.

The Players' Forum.

"Holy shit! So satisfying! So this is what it feels like to go up against official factions. Ah, my heart was about to leap right out of my throat!"

"This is just a game, though. If it were in real life, this concubine genuinely wouldn't dare."

"Quick, quick, quick! Those two heroes, *Ding Gou Pi Dan*, who previously slit their throats and self-immolated, come out and share your firsthand accounts! What does it feel like to kill yourself? Is it awesome?"

"Awesome my ass! But... I admit, at the time I actually got myself so worked up I was boiling with passion. Fuck, I never truly expected that one day I could slice my own throat with such heroic flair!"

"As someone who experienced it personally, let me offer everyone a piece of advice: if you're going to commit suicide, absolutely do not choose self-immolation. Even though the game lowers the pain threshold, that sensation of suffocation and terror... When you discover that you cannot breathe no matter what, the sheer dread of slowly waiting for death to arrive will completely engulf you. Leaving aside how painful burning oneself is in reality, just the agony of suffocation alone will make you regret it. Seriously, I should've picked a different method. Thank goodness this is a game that blurs sensory feedback upon death; otherwise, I’d definitely be left with psychological trauma."

"Hahaha, what an absolute dumbass upstairs, no explanation needed!"

"Get lost, you insect-day dog-egg! I heard someone at the scene shouting 'Daddy'! Son, get your ass out here!"

"My foot! That was just stage effect, understand?"

"Brothers and sisters, get ready. We won't be able to log in for three days—you guys better make sure the tabloid doesn't go under!"

"Little ones, go forth with peace of mind. We've taken over the tabloid."

"Brother Photography has already whipped up a primary camera and film rolls. Get ready for the triple-whammy shock in the next gossip edition!"

"What? They've even made a camera? What kind of freakish prodigies are these people?!"

"Fantastic! From now on, will we finally get to see what the NPCs and scenery in the game world actually look like?"

"I want to see the peerless beauty of our Valley Master! No sketches, I want real photographs!"

"I wanna see the Second Prince and the Valley Master together. Ideally, both of them lying in bed."

"Royal photos will be had, and bed photos will be had as well! Our Gossip Tabloid will definitely strive to satisfy everyone's demands."

"This is just a rudimentary retro model, though. Wait until I craft a portable modern entry-level model before you guys start showering me with praise."

"Piss off! All you show-offs can drop dead!"

The players were merry and lively.

Inside the residence of a certain high-ranking noble in the Tiger Kingdom's royal capital, seven or eight individuals were gathered together, all wearing gloomy, distressed expressions.

"I ask you, how did your subordinate handle things? Such a minor affair couldn't even be managed properly, actually driving people to the point of suicide?"

"Who the hell knows what that idiot was up to!"

"Driving two people to their deaths is one thing, but he actually started brawling with the onlookers. Was he trying to incite public outrage?"

"The situation at the scene was way too chaotic. I keep feeling like things aren't that simple, as if someone was deliberately stirring up trouble."

"Alright, whether someone was stirring trouble or not, several people have already died, and so many witnessed it. Her Majesty the Queen might not care about such trifles, but if the Tiger King flies into a rage, what do we do?"

"And right before the material exhibition and inheritance sharing convention, too! The city is packed with visiting merchants and international luminaries everywhere you look. If this scandal blows wide open..."

"Can't it be covered up?"

"With so many people watching at the scene, how are we supposed to cover it up?"

"No matter what, we can't keep this from the Queen. Let's report it upward first."

"Report it to the Queen? You gonna go do the reporting?"

"...Then that tabloid—do we still seal it up?"

"Seal your mother's rotting asshole! Go fix things with the dead victims' families first, and stop them from making a ruckus. If this gets blown out of proportion, none of us will have a good end!"

After conferring, the group unanimously decided to keep it from the Queen for now, handling the loose ends themselves until it could no longer be concealed.

The doors of the Gossip Tabloid, which was originally slated for sealing, stood wide open, with quite a few beastmen stepping in and out.

The City Guard had specifically dispatched a patrol squad to circle the premises once every hour on average to prevent any further incidents.

"How come that gossip tabloid suddenly has so many people around it?"

"No idea. Could it be that some folks couldn't stand by and are fighting to uphold justice for that tabloid?"

"Perhaps it's the family and friends of those tragically murdered beastmen."

"I have a bad feeling something major is about to happen."

"The Queen really is petty. Isn't it just about her seizing a treasure back then, accidentally causing the death of her own relative, and then her own niece turning out to be the other woman? If she hadn't done those things in the first place, people wouldn't have exposed her."

"Seeing the Queen get this furious, to the extent of driving people to suicide, it looks like what was written in that gossip rag was probably true after all."

"I'm leaning toward it being true, too."

"But some people are saying it's pure slander, that someone is deliberately splashing dirty water on the Queen."

"Some people have already gone to look for the Lingelate family mentioned in the article. Whether the Queen pressured their family into marrying off Anita and her younger sister to an old beastman back then—we'll know as soon as we ask them."

"Aiyaya, right now I just want to know if Raphael Langmu—the son our majesty bore with Madam Anita—knows about the deep-seated grudge between his mother and the Queen. If he didn't know before, but knows now, how is he going to react?"

Handsome wasn't reacting in any particular way; he was still busy refining magic crystals while casually instructing Shang Feifan on how to lay the foundation for his own magic.

A magician must possess innate magical talent. To use a more vivid analogy, they must harbor a seed of magic.

Yet possessing a seed doesn't mean you can instantly make it take root and sprout; you have to nurture it, activate it, and find ways to coax it into germination.

Laying the foundation of magic is equivalent to preparing suitable soil and fertilizer for the magic seed, and then watering it slightly. Depending on the specific variety of the magic seed, everything from the soil composition and fertilizer type to the volume of water, and even environmental factors like temperature, sunlight, and shade must be meticulously considered.

Only suitable soil allows a seed to thrive; otherwise, even if the seed sprouts, it will grow stunted and warped, severely crippling its future potential.

Seeing more and more people coming to "have a heart-to-heart" with Raphael, the Chief Director of the Special Investigation Bureau simply hung a sign on the front door reading: *Raphael Langmu is currently away on official business,* and promptly slipped away.

Compared to the bustling activity over at Handsome's side, Remier could no longer sit still. He snuck out to meet Eva in secret.

Seeing him arrive uninvited once more, Eva furrowed her brows. "Didn't I tell you to come here less often?"

Remier pressed his lips together. "Lately, there have been some unfavorable rumors about me within the royal palace. Someone brought up my associations with Neti, and even claimed that Neti killed the Fifth Princess merely to protect me."

Eva looked surprised. "Weren't your dealings with Neti kept secret? How could they leak?"

Remier's expression turned gloomy. "I don't know. Perhaps Neti mentioned it to someone else."

"Who's spreading it?"

"Court maids and servants. A guard who is on good terms with me gave me a warning. His fiancée happens to be a palace maid."

Eva pondered for a moment and said dismissively, "It's just idle gossip. As long as they don't have concrete, ironclad evidence in their hands, you just play dumb and pretend you don't know. Even if it's out in the open, so what? A young man's heart turns to romance; you're exceptionally handsome, and your standing by the Tiger King's side is hardly low. Isn't it perfectly normal for a maid to harbor a crush on you?"

Remier's complexion improved slightly. "I figured that if I frequently come to visit Doris, people will assume I'm Doris's intimate companion, and they won't suspect that there's anything between Neti and me."

"Naive," Eva scoffed. "Are you trying to cultivate a playboy persona?"

Remier lowered his head.

chunks.chineseText:
伊娃轻叹：“我这里你不要常来，这对你不好。一个贵族稍微风流点，别人只会羡慕。但你身份不一样，你将来……是要做大事的人，保护好你的名声对你非常重要。否则你想让别人提起来，就是一个沉醉在女兽人裙下的前虎王侍卫？”

雷米尔腾地抬头：“当然不是！”

伊娃伸手抚摸他的后脑勺。

雷米尔微微偏头。

伊娃收回手，心里想着孩子大了不好管了。

“你也听到那个八卦报上说的内容了吧？”伊娃改换话题。

雷米尔总算想起来自己是来干什么的，问：“那是你让人放出去的吗？”

伊娃摇头：“不是我。”

那报道内容八成为真，但关于她怎么找到石耳的内容都是胡编乱造。

“那是谁？对方怎么会知道得这么清楚？”

“我也想知道，可惜报社的那两个兽人全都自杀，现在想要跟他们询问是谁给他们提供的情报，也无法知道。”

“那家报社好像还在。”

“在就对了。”伊娃唇角勾出一丝微笑。

从目前的两期报道来看，那家报社的报道内容显然对她有利，也不知道是不是另一个仇恨王后的人。

伊娃甚至怀疑透露相关情报给那家报社的人就是虎王。

“如果那家报社继续经营下去，也许后面会有更不利王后的消息传出。”雷米尔略微有点兴奋：“只逼死那两个报社工作人员，还有打死好几个民众这件事，传出去必然会让王后在民间的威望大大下跌。”

“是啊，等着……谁？！”伊娃突然挥手。

一支骨刺从她手指尖弹出，直直射入靠墙的衣柜中。

咚，衣柜内发出声响。

雷米尔迅速跳起，手持武器，小心接近衣柜，猛地拉开衣柜门。

一个瘦小的兽人从衣柜里滚出来。

伊娃的准头非常好。

那支骨刺正正射入兽人心脏。

雷米尔检查尸体，确定对方确实死亡，又检查对方的种族特征。

“奇怪，这好像是个天残。不知道是谁派来的。”

伊娃脸色难看，“不管是谁派来的。没有我的联系，你后面暂时都不要过来我这边了。”

雷米尔也知道事情重大，严肃点头：“我知道了。”

伊娃通过密道送走雷米尔，当即就把尸体处理了。

这是被她发现的第一个窃-听者。

现在她只希望这也是不明势力派出来的第一个人。

好在这个人躲了没多久就被她发现，就算在她这里听到什么也无法传递回去。

玩家百里风箭死了，但他一下线就把消息传给了同伴。

同伴那边看到百里风箭传回来的内容，激动得跳起来：这个死值得！他们似乎挖到大消息了。

该玩家眼珠一转，向他们委托任务的女管家只让他们潜入伊娃的房间调查她和雷米尔来往的证据，可没说不让他们把消息再转卖给其他人。

次日，王城八卦报第三期没再遵循三日一发的间隔，火速推出。

这次的头版头条果然和那两名报社员工被逼死有关，而且这次不但有文字内容，还有更直击兽人眼球的图画！

那图画看起来栩栩如生，都不像是画的。

“这是相片！我知道。以前大繁华纪就有过类似的炼金工具。我记得某一年某国拍卖会上就有人拿出一个从遗迹里挖出来的相机，就是能即时拍下真实场景。”

“这家八卦报不简单啊，竟然能弄到相机。”

“也许这家八卦报后面有人支持？”

“嘿嘿，刚开始也许没有，但现在就说不定了。”

“是啊，治安官派人去查封都没能查封掉……咳！”

“听说已经贴了封条，还砸了一台印刷机，但治安官走后，就有人把封条撕了，那台印刷机好像也被修好游-行。”

不知道是不是为了暂避锋芒，这期报道并没有提到王后或任何一名王室，只把重点放在了治安官和报社工作人员的冲突上，并大力宣扬民众需要真相这一宗旨。

也不知道是不是这期内容图文并茂特别刺激人眼，还是写的人特别善于煽情，报道出来的下午就有兽人开始组织游-行，满大街的举着牌子高呼：“我们需要新闻自由！我们需要知道真相！权贵的特权不应该超过国家法律！”

刚开始游-行的兽人还不多，只有个位数，但随着时间过去，加入的兽人越来越多，等游-行队伍走到王宫附近时，规模已经达到数百人。

而这还只是开始！

王后没有收到手下的及时汇报，但她从王宫仆人口中得知了外面的示威游-行内容。

王后脸色非常黑。

她总感觉那示威游-行就是冲着她来的。

但她现在就算再恨，也不可能派人冲出去把那些游-行的兽人全都抓起来。

她要真这么做了，就是在给虎王递刀子，杀她的刀！

虎王听到克莱门特的汇报，头疼地按住额头。

该死的王后，净给他找事！

也不看看现在都是什么时候。

如果王后真的能把那报社悄无声息地封掉，把里面的人都解决，那也是她的本事。

可看看她现在做的好事！

不但没能把报社顺利封掉，还把人给逼死了，更把无关的人也牵扯进来，导致无关民众也被打死好几个。

现在好了，都闹出游-行示威了！

“那家王城八卦报……”克莱门特迟疑。

“不能封！”虎王毫不犹豫地说。

现在真的封了这家报社才是要命。

他的虎国养的可不全都是羊族兔族那样的老实兽人，更多的是虎豹豺狼这些凶兽族啊！
chunks.englishText:
Eva sighed softly. "You shouldn't come to my place too often; it's not good for you. For an ordinary noble to be slightly romantic, others will only look on with envy. But your status is different. In the future... you are someone destined to accomplish great things. Protecting your reputation is paramount to you. Otherwise, when people mention you in days to come, do you want them to think of you merely as a former Tiger King's guard wallowing in female beastmen's skirts?"

Remier jerked his head up. "Of course not!"

Eva reached out and stroked the back of his head.

Remier tilted his head slightly away.

Eva withdrew her hand, thinking to herself that children were becoming harder to manage the older they got.

"You've also heard the contents of that gossip tabloid, haven't you?" Eva changed the subject.

Remier finally remembered why he had come in the first place and asked, "Was that something you had people leak?"

Eva shook her head. "It wasn't me."

The core content of that report was eighty percent true, but the parts detailing how she managed to find the Stone Ear were entirely fabricated out of whole cloth.

"Then who was it? How could the other party know the details so clearly?"

"I'd love to know as well, but unfortunately, those two beastmen from the tabloid both committed suicide. Now, if we want to ask them who provided the intelligence, there's no way to find out."

"That tabloid still seems to be running."

"Right that it's running." A trace of a smile tugged at the corners of Eva's lips.

Judging by the first two reports, the content published by that tabloid was clearly beneficial to her. She wondered if it was someone else harboring a deep hatred for the Queen.

Eva even suspected that the person who leaked the relevant intelligence to the tabloid might be the Tiger King himself.

"If that tabloid continues to operate, perhaps even more unfavorable news about the Queen will come out later." Remier sounded slightly excited. "Just driving those two tabloid staffers to suicide, coupled with beating several citizens to death—once that gets out, it will inevitably cause the Queen's prestige among the common folk to plummet drastically."

"Indeed. Just wait and see—who?!" Eva suddenly lashed out with her hand.

A bone spur shot straight out from the tip of her finger, piercing directly into the wardrobe against the wall.

*Thud.* A muffled sound came from inside the wardrobe.

Remier leaped up instantly, weapon in hand, and cautiously approached the wardrobe before violently yanking the door open.

A scrawny beastman rolled out from inside the wardrobe.

Eva’s aim had been immaculate.

That bone spur had driven squarely into the beastman's heart.

Remier inspected the corpse, confirming the individual was indeed dead, and then checked the target's racial characteristics.

"Strange, this looks like someone with a congenital disability. Who on earth could have sent him?"

Eva's expression turned ugly. "Whoever sent him... until I contact you, you are not to come over to my side for the time being."

Knowing the gravity of the situation, Remier nodded solemnly. "I understand."

Eva escorted Remier away through the secret passage and immediately disposed of the corpse.

This was the first eavesdropper she had managed to uncover.

Right now, she could only hope this was also the first person sent by unknown factions.

Fortunately, this fellow hadn't hidden for long before she discovered him; even if he had overheard anything at her place, he had no way of passing it back.

The player *Baili Fengjian* had died, but the moment he went offline, he relayed the news straight to his companions.

Upon seeing the details sent back by Baili Fengjian, his comrades leaped up in excitement: this death was totally worth it! It seemed they had just struck a massive vein of news.

The player's eyes rolled as a thought struck him: the female butler who commissioned their quest had only instructed them to sneak into Eva's room to investigate evidence of her interactions with Remier; she hadn't said they couldn't turn around and resell the intelligence to someone else.

The next day, instead of adhering to the previous three-day interval, the fourth edition of the Royal Capital Gossip Tabloid was rushed out in blazing speed.

True to form, this issue's front-page headline was related to the two tabloid employees driven to suicide, and this time it didn't just feature text—it included illustrations that struck even harder at the beastmen's eyes!

The artwork looked remarkably lifelike, hardly resembling drawings at all.

"These are photographs! I know them. Back during the Great Prosperous Era, there were similar alchemical tools. I remember at some nation's auction years ago, someone brought out a camera excavated from ancient ruins that could instantly capture real scenes."

"This gossip tabloid is no simple operation; to think they actually managed to get their hands on a camera."

"Maybe there's someone backing this tabloid from the shadows?"

"Heh, maybe not at the start, but right now? Hard to say."

"Yeah, I heard the bailiffs sent men to seal the place up, and even smashed a printing press, but right after the bailiffs left, someone tore down the seals and that printing press seemed to have been fixed and paraded around."

Whether to steer clear of the limelight or for other reasons, this issue's report made no mention of the Queen or any member of royalty, focusing entirely on the conflict between the bailiffs and the tabloid staff while vigorously championing the principle that the citizenry deserved the truth.

Perhaps because this edition's text-and-image combination was particularly eye-catching, or because the author possessed an extraordinary talent for agitating emotions, by the afternoon after publication, beastmen began organizing a parade. Marching down the streets, they hoisted placards high and chanted in unison: "We need freedom of the press! We need to know the truth! The privileges of the nobility must not supersede the laws of the nation!"

At first, the parading beastmen numbered only in the single digits, but as time ticked by, more and more joined the ranks. By the time the procession reached the vicinity of the royal palace, its scale had swelled to several hundred people.

And this was merely the beginning!

The Queen hadn't received timely reports from her subordinates, but she learned of the external demonstrations straight from the mouths of the palace servants.

The Queen's complexion was pitch black.

She had an overwhelming premonition that the protest march was directed squarely at her.

Yet no matter how furious she felt right now, she couldn't possibly dispatch troops to charge outside and arrest every single parading beastman.

If she truly did that, she would simply be handing the Tiger King a blade—a blade to execute her with!

Hearing Clement's report, the Tiger King rubbed his temples with a throbbing headache.

That damned Queen was nothing but a constant source of trouble!

Didn't she even look at what time it was?

If the Queen had genuinely been capable of sealing that tabloid away without a whisper and quietly disposing of everyone inside, that would have been her own competence.

But look at the fine mess she’d made now!

Not only had she failed to successfully seal the press, but she'd driven people to suicide, dragged unrelated parties into the fray, and resulted in several innocent citizens being beaten to death.

And now look at it—they'd gone and stirred up a protest parade!

"That Royal Capital Gossip Tabloid..." Clement hesitated.

"It cannot be sealed!" the Tiger King stated without a moment's hesitation.

To actually shut down that tabloid right now would be absolute suicide.

The Tiger Kingdom he governed wasn't entirely populated by docile beastmen like the Sheep or Rabbit tribes; the majority consisted of fierce predatory clans like Tigers, Leopards, Jackals, and Wolves!

chunks.chineseText:
第157章 踩到雷米尔

八卦报第四期紧跟在第三期的次日就推出，一副要把八卦报搞成日报的势头。

同时一银一份的价格也降低到了十个铜达铢就能购买一份。

还是只有一张纸，正面是报道的内容，背面就全是广告。

前三期，都只有油墨供应商的广告。但这一期广告一下增多了十来个，占面积有大有小。

因为是花钱买的报纸，绝大多数人在看完正面的报道内容后，都会把反面的广告也全都看一遍。

这些广告也很绝，他们不止在宣扬自己的产品，同时也是打折优惠券，表示只要剪下相应的广告内容，带到店里就能获得很大优惠。

这下买报的人都觉得这份报纸买得比较划算，就算他们自己不想要广告上的优惠券，也可以剪下来送给有需要的人。

何况其中好几个优惠券真的很优惠，也很实用。

实用的报纸，加上价格一下降到十分之一，全王城购买八卦报的人一下多了许多。

路上叫卖报纸的人也不再只有几个成年兽人，而是变成了大量幼崽。

幼崽年龄不一，从五六岁到十来岁都有，背着一个报袋满大街叫卖。

八卦报说了，只要卖掉一份，他们就能拿到一铜的提成，只要干得好，他们一天赚的铜达铢说不定比他们父母都高。

在金钱奖励的刺激下，这些小幼崽卖报卖得特别卖力，他们脸皮还厚，敢于钻入任何店铺商家，敢于向任何人兜售，而成年兽人对于幼崽总是比较宽容的，只要不是特别缺钱，也不介意花十铜买上一份。

实际上，王城很多人也正在等待第四期的八卦报，有人满心期待会看到什么样的劲爆消息，有人则是惴惴不安地担心自己或和自己有关的人成为头条主角……

雷米尔早上来到城卫军东营报道，一进营地大门就感觉到怪怪的。

一路上他碰到不少城卫军，有人认识他，就跟他打招呼问好，有人不认识他也会盯着他看。

而不管认识他还是不认识他的，看他的眼神都有点古怪。

“长官，日安！”一名士兵向他行礼。

“日安。等等，是不是发生了什么事，和我有关？”雷米尔一把抓住士兵。

他认识对方，这名士兵还跟他出过几次任务。

士兵尴尬地挠头，他看到雷米尔行礼后就想离开，没想到被对方一把抓住。

“长官，没什么。”

“说！”

士兵无奈，小声说：“今天的八卦报出来了，您看到就知道是怎么回事。”

说完，这名士兵使了个巧劲，挣脱雷米尔的手，撒腿就溜。

雷米尔也无意死抓住这名士兵不放，得到答案就大踏步走向办公室。

办公室内，几名尉官正聚在一起，有人拿着报纸正念着上面的内容。

“哇！”

“哦！没想到啊。”

“真看不出来，雷米尔中尉会玩得这么花。”

“你们说五公主的死真的是因为……”

一只手突然伸进几人当中，一把抢过一名尉官手中报纸。

该尉官大怒，正要骂人，就看清了抢报纸人的脸。

咳，有人干咳。

几名尉官迅速散开：“工作了，工作了。”

“啊，我这边要出去巡逻，先走了。”

“我这边也有点事，我去材料市场。”

能找到理由的尉官都跑了，剩下几个面面相觑，走也不是，留也不是。

雷米尔快速浏览八卦报头条内容，他的脸色正不自知地变得越来越黑。

【五公主之死，惊天内-幕！

由内部不知名人士透露消息，五公主之死含有惊天内-幕，这位小公主并不是病死，而是死于情杀！王宫所有知情人士都被封口，而被封口的原因只因为他！

本报记者得到消息后冒死对各知情人士进行暗访和调查，终于查出五公主死亡始末的真正原因。原来五公主和王后身边大侍女内某一起喜欢上一名宫廷侍卫。

这名宫廷侍卫乃是虎王近卫，是虎王这几年最为欣赏和信任的近卫之一，年少英俊，家世不凡，且具有王室血脉。

据传，五公主想要独占这名英俊的年轻侍卫，但该侍卫却并不喜欢骄横跋扈的五公主，他便以独爱侍女内某为借口拒绝了五公主。

五公主大怒，把侍女内某叫至王宫一处偏僻花园，对内某进行了各种人格和外貌以及身世上的羞辱，并宣称她一定会得到那名英俊侍卫。

内某担心爱人真的落到五公主手中，为了避免爱人名声和心灵受损，也因为被羞辱得怒上心头，激动之下竟杀死了五公主！

虎王和王后惊闻小公主被人谋害，万分伤心，勒令侍卫统领克莱门特快速破案。

侍卫统领克莱门特能力卓绝，很快就从少许线索中锁定嫌疑人，并抓捕了真正凶手侍女内某。

在审问内某为何要杀害公主的过程中，内某为保护那名侍卫，不愿让人知道那名侍卫才是五公主死亡的要因，就先一步揽下所有罪名，并在当天就在狱中自杀身亡。

侍女内某却不知道，因为她身上少有的天然香水味道，侍卫统领克莱门特已经知晓她的情人是谁。

虎王从克莱门特口中知道了那名侍卫的名字，虽然知道这名侍卫就是五公主死亡的导-火索，但可能是考虑到五公主并不是真正死在该侍卫手中，也可能是出于惜才和对该侍卫父母的愧疚心理，虎王一力隐瞒了此事，并没有把该侍卫的名字让王后知晓。

事后，有人去询问那名侍卫是否认识侍女内某并和她关系密切，该侍卫矢口否认。

可怜侍女内某为保护情人献身，却不知道她心爱的情人并不止她一个女人。该侍卫经常前往王城最有名的销金窟，和王城最有名的交际花多丽丝王妃打得火热，惹得多丽丝芳心暗许，每次接待该侍卫竟不收一铜！

就问多丽丝免费接待那名侍卫，为何旖梦楼老板没有任何反应？

原来这名侍卫竟然和旖梦楼老板伊娃也有密切关系，且两人言谈中所图甚大，两人提起虎王和王后丝毫没有尊敬之意，更对王后带有深刻仇恨，巴不得王后出丑。

为了隐瞒两人的密切关系，伊娃不惜杀死窃-听者。

看到这里，可能诸君都会好奇，那名虎王近卫到底是谁？

据可靠消息，这名英俊的年轻侍卫已经在近期从侍卫营转到城卫军，不过刚满二十一岁就成为了一名中尉，真正前途远大。

而家世如此优越的他为什么会周旋在多个女人之间，为什么会对王后有敌意，他和旖梦楼老板伊娃又是什么样的密切关系？

欲知后事，请等待本报记者的持续调查结果。】

雷米尔手指捏紧报纸，用力到手指发白。

这条新闻虽然没有指名道姓，但那详细的内容和说出他的名字又有什么区别？

只要对他稍微熟悉一点的人，就能从新闻中的内容中分析出那名英俊的年轻侍卫就是他！
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 157: Stepping on Remier

The fourth edition of the Gossip Tabloid was released the very next day following the third, showing clear momentum to turn the gossip sheet into a daily paper.

Simultaneously, the price per copy was dropped from one silver coin down to just ten copper Dazhu.

It was still a single sheet of paper, with the front page dedicated to news reports while the entire reverse side was packed with advertisements.

The first three issues had carried only advertisements from ink suppliers. However, this issue saw the number of ads suddenly expand by a dozen or so, varying in size.

Because people had actually paid money for the paper, the vast majority of readers read through all the advertisements on the back after finishing the front-page reports.

These ads were also quite ingenious; they didn't merely promote products—they doubled as discount coupons. Readers were told that simply clipping out the corresponding advertisement and bringing it to the store would net them substantial savings.

This made buyers feel the newspaper was exceptionally cost-effective; even if they didn't want the coupons on the ads themselves, they could clip them out and give them to anyone who did.

Moreover, several of those coupons offered genuinely deep discounts and were immensely practical.

Combined with the practical utility of the paper and a price slashed to a tenth of its original cost, the number of people purchasing the Gossip Tabloid across the royal capital skyrocketed instantly.

The peddlers hawking papers on the streets were no longer just a few adult beastmen, but had been replaced by a massive horde of urchins.

These children ranged in age from five or six all the way to their early teens, slinging canvas newspaper bags over their shoulders as they cried out their wares up and down every street.

The Gossip Tabloid had made it clear: for every single copy sold, they would pocket a commission of one copper coin. As long as they worked hard, the copper Dazhu these little kids could rake in in a single day might well surpass what their parents made.

Spurred by monetary rewards, these young urchins peddled newspapers with extraordinary diligence. Being thick-skinned by nature, they dared to squeeze into any shop or storefront and pitch to literally anyone. Adult beastmen, meanwhile, were generally tolerant toward children; unless they were desperately short on cash, they didn't mind spending ten coppers to buy a copy.

In truth, a large portion of the royal capital was eagerly awaiting the fourth issue of the Gossip Tabloid. Some were filled with anticipation for whatever explosive gossip might be inside, while others squirmed in anxious dread, terrified that they—or someone connected to them—might become the protagonist of the front-page headline.

When Remier arrived at the City Guard's Eastern Camp for duty that morning, the moment he stepped through the camp gates, he felt something was off.

Along the way, he encountered numerous City Guard soldiers. Those who recognized him offered greetings and bows, while those who didn't still stared fixedly at him.

Regardless of whether they knew him or not, every single gaze directed his way carried a hint of weirdness.

"Good day, sir!" a soldier saluted him.

"Good day. Wait, has something happened—something involving me?" Remier grabbed the soldier by the arm.

He recognized the fellow; this soldier had accompanied him on several missions previously.

The soldier gave an awkward scratch of his head. He had intended to slip away immediately after executing his salute, never expecting to be snagged by the officer.

"Sir, nothing is going on."

"Spit it out!"

Helpless, the soldier lowered his voice. "Today's Gossip Tabloid is out. You'll understand everything once you read it."

With that, the soldier executed a clever maneuver, wrenched his arm free from Remier's grip, and bolted away at a run.

Remier had no intention of forcibly detaining the soldier anyway; having obtained his answer, he strode onward toward his office.

Inside the office, several junior officers were clustered together, one of them holding a newspaper and reading its contents aloud.

"Whoa!"

"Oh! I never would've guessed."

"Hard to imagine Lieutenant Remier plays things so wild."

"You guys reckon the Fifth Princess's death was really because..."

A hand suddenly shot into their midst, snatching the newspaper right out of an officer's grip.

The officer flew into a rage, about to unleash a torrent of curses, before he caught sight of the face of the person who had snatched it.

*Ahem,* someone coughed drily.

The junior officers scattered in an instant. "Time to work, back to work."

"Ah, I've got a patrol scheduled outside, I'm heading out first."

"I've got matters to attend to as well, heading to the material market."

Those who could conjure up an excuse all vanished, leaving behind a few who exchanged awkward glances, not knowing whether to leave or stay.

Remier rapidly scanned the headline of the Gossip Tabloid, his complexion unconsciously growing darker and darker.

【The Shocking Inner Truth Behind the Fifth Princess's Death!

According to insider information leaked by an anonymous source, the death of the Fifth Princess contains earth-shattering secrets. The young princess did not die of illness, but was instead the victim of a crime of passion! Every single person in the royal palace who knew the truth was silenced, and the reason they were silenced was entirely because of *him*!

After obtaining this intelligence, our reporters risked death to conduct covert interviews and investigations among those in the know, finally unearthing the true origins of the Fifth Princess's demise. It turns out the Fifth Princess and a senior maid named 'N' by the Queen's side had simultaneously fallen in love with the same palace guard.

This palace guard is a personal guardsman of the Tiger King, ranking among the most admired and trusted elite guards of recent years. He is young, handsome, possesses an extraordinary family background, and even carries royal blood.

Rumor has it that the Fifth Princess desired to monopolize this handsome young guard exclusively. However, the guard held no affection for the arrogant and overbearing Fifth Princess, using his deep devotion to the maid 'N' as an excuse to rebuff her.

Furious, the Fifth Princess summoned the maid 'N' to a secluded garden within the royal palace, subjecting her to all manner of insults regarding her character, appearance, and background, while declaring that she would undoubtedly obtain the handsome guard in the end.

Terrified that her beloved would truly fall into the Fifth Princess's clutches—both to protect her lover's reputation and psyche, and driven to a frenzy by the humiliating insults—the maid 'N' was so overwrought that she unexpectedly murdered the Fifth Princess!

Upon discovering that the little princess had been murdered, a grief-stricken Tiger King and Queen ordered Guard Commander Clement to solve the case with all haste.

Possessing exceptional capability, Guard Commander Clement quickly locked onto a suspect from meager clues and arrested the true culprit, the maid 'N'.

During the interrogation regarding why she murdered the princess, in order to protect the guard and prevent anyone from discovering that he was the underlying catalyst for the Fifth Princess's death, the maid 'N' took the blame entirely upon herself. That very day, she committed suicide in her prison cell.

Little did the maid 'N' know that due to a rare natural perfume scent lingering on her person, Guard Commander Clement had already figured out the identity of her lover.

Though the Tiger King learned the guard's name from Clement and knew the young man was the fuse that triggered the tragedy, perhaps out of consideration that the princess wasn't actually killed by the guard's own hand, or perhaps out of a惜才 [cherishing talent] mentality and guilt toward the guard's parents, the Tiger King forcefully covered up the matter, keeping the guard's identity concealed from the Queen.

Afterward, when someone inquired whether the guard knew the maid 'N' and maintained an intimate relationship with her, the guard flatly denied it.

Pitiable was the maid 'N', who sacrificed herself to protect her lover, completely unaware that her beloved was hardly faithful to her alone. This same guard frequently visited the royal capital's most infamous den of debauchery, growing wildly intimate with the capital's premier courtesan, Consort Doris. So deep was Doris's infamously fickle heart captured that she refused to accept a single copper coin whenever she hosted him!

One might ask: why did the owner of the Dream-Weaving Tower raise no objection when Doris received that guard free of charge?

As it turns out, this very guard maintained an exceedingly close relationship with Eva, the proprietress of the Dream-Weaving Tower as well. In their private conversations, the two showed not a shred of respect for the Tiger King and Queen, harboring a profound hatred for the Queen and longing for nothing more than to see her publicly disgraced.

To conceal their close ties, Eva went so far as to murder an eavesdropper.

Reading this far, all honored readers are likely curious: exactly who is this personal guardsman of the Tiger King?

According to reliable intelligence, this handsome young guardsman was recently transferred from the Guard Camp to the City Guard. Having just turned twenty-one, he has already attained the rank of lieutenant, with a truly boundless future ahead of him.

Why would someone with such a privileged background weave through multiple women? Why does he harbor such intense hostility toward the Queen? And what kind of intimate relationship does he share with Dream-Weaving Tower's proprietress, Eva?

To discover what happens next, please await our reporters' continued investigative findings.】

Remier’s fingers clamped down on the newspaper, gripping it with such force that his knuckles turned completely white.

Although the news report refrained from naming names, what difference did those meticulous details make from shouting his identity aloud?

Anyone even slightly familiar with him could instantly deduce from the article's descriptions that the handsome young guard in question was none of other than him!

chunks.chineseText:
而且这篇新闻从头到尾、字里行间都对他充满了恶意。明明五公主之死和他毫无关系，却写得他像是蓝颜祸水且花心滥情，随便玩弄女兽人。

但最让雷米尔恐惧也最让他不可思议的是，这篇新闻竟然暴露出他和伊娃的关系！

更可怕的是，伊娃明明已经杀死那个窃-听者，可他们的说话内容貌似还是传了出去，更在今天被公开在八卦报上。

会不会已经有人知道他和伊娃的真实关系？

雷米尔慌乱了。

他心里确实非常想把自己的身世曝光出去，想让世人都知道他才是虎王的亲生子，他才是真正的王室直系血脉！

但同时他又心知肚明，这时并不是他曝光身份的最佳时机，王后还没有死，郎侦老伯爵还活着，一旦他的身份曝光，他现在得到的所有好处都将消失，而曾经拉斐尔郎沐经历过的所有痛苦和悲惨，都会在他身上重演一遍，也许更糟糕！

“雷米尔少爷！”门口突然传来喊声。

雷米尔倏然转身，看到外公家里的老仆。

老仆先对他行礼，然后神色凝重地对他说：“雷米尔少爷，老爷请您立刻回去一趟。”

雷米尔皱眉，他本能猜到郎侦老伯爵叫他回去是什么事，他心里抗拒，当即找借口：“我还有工作，等我下班后……”

老仆叹了口气，眼睛扫过雷米尔捏在手里的报纸：“您也看到八卦报的内容了。老爷说有些事越快解决越好，您不注重自己的名声，也要考虑伯爵府和您死去的父母。”

雷米尔倏地捏紧双拳，心头怒意上涌：“我知道了，等会儿我会找时间过去。”

他确实不想过去见老伯爵，但他也知道，这种丑闻需要尽快解决，他这时不可能找伊娃帮他，而此时有能力帮他也愿意帮他的人只有他这个名义上的外公了。

雷米尔刚离开城卫军东营不久，就又有人来找他。

这次来的是虎王身边近侍，说虎王召雷米尔速速进宫。

办公室内的其他尉官跟近侍说了雷米尔已经先被他外公叫走的事。

近侍点头表示知道，当即回去复命。

王宫内，虎王听到近侍回复，挥挥手，让所有侍候的人全部离开，又命人把克莱门特叫来。

克莱门特踏入书房。

“把门关上。”虎王沉声命令。

克莱门特反身关上书房大门。

一声叹息在身后不远处响起。

克莱门特转身，就看到虎王神色疲累地靠在宽大的椅子上，一只手捏着眉心。

过了好一会儿，克莱门特才听到虎王说：“去查查那个伊娃。”

“是。”克莱门特正要退下。

虎王再次开口：“王后有找你问话吗？”

克莱门特一顿：“在您召唤我之前，王后那边的侍女已经来找我。”

“你去了吗？”

“还没有。”

“去吧。要怎么说，你心里有数。”

“明白。”

克莱门特等了一会儿，见虎王再没有其他吩咐，这才离开书房，前往王后宫殿。

克莱门特刚进门，就看到几名仆人拿着打扫工具，抬着一堆被打碎的物品走出。

看来王后心情不太好啊。

克莱门特让侍女去禀报王后，就在宫殿外等待传唤。

很快，侍女就过来请克莱门特进去。

王后在外殿见了克莱门特，她脸上有明显重新上妆的痕迹，外衣似乎也换过了。

“我不想听谎话。”王后神色严厉，上来就开门见山：“内蒂喜欢的那个侍卫是不是就是郎雷米尔？”

克莱门特：“是。”

这事也隐瞒不住，八卦报就差没指名道姓。

“为什么要瞒着我？是虎王让你瞒着我的吗！”

“……陛下认为这件事和雷米尔侍卫无关，不想把更多无辜者牵扯进来。”

“无辜者？”王后冷笑：“只要和我女儿死亡一事有关，谁也不是无辜者！既然茜娜这么喜欢那个雷米尔，内蒂还为了雷米尔杀了茜娜，那就让雷米尔去陪她们两人好了。”

克莱门特神色淡定：“雷米尔不是普通侍卫，他外公是郎侦老伯爵，他母亲是前侍卫统领，他父母都是为国牺牲的英雄，没有叛国以上的大罪，就是陛下也不能随意处置他。”

王后抬起手掌，似乎想要发作，但看到克莱门特那张宠辱不惊的脸，想到这人的身份和身后家世，到底还是忍了下去。

“叛国大罪？那报纸上不是说他在和那个妓-院老板娘伊娃密谋什么吗，你可以去好好查查，看他们到底想干什么！”王后阴沉沉地说道。

克莱门特顺势点头：“是。”

郎侦老伯爵府。

雷米尔已经在老伯爵对面干坐了好一会儿。

但到现在老伯爵一言不发，就那么坐在那里看着他。

“外婆呢？”雷米尔尽量神色自然地询问。

老伯爵听雷米尔询问老伴，这才终于开口：“她身体不太舒服，正在卧床休息。”

“我去看看外婆。”雷米尔作势起身。

“坐下！”老伯爵一声爆喝。

雷米尔身体一抖，没敢站起来。

老伯爵闭了闭眼睛：“我郎家没有敢做不敢当的人。我就问你，你和那个侍女内蒂舒密尔是不是一对？”

雷米尔皱眉，“外公，你不要相信八卦报上那些胡说八道。我只是认识她，我在王宫里做事，内蒂舒密尔又是王后身边的大侍女，自然会经常看到她。但我和她也就是点头之交。”

“哦，是吗？这么说你没有睡过她。”

“外公！”

老伯爵眼神复杂，声色不再那么严厉：“如果你真的和她是情人关系，承认也没什么。五公主的死亡是她咎由自取，和你毫无关系。如果两位陛下因此要找你麻烦，我自会保你。

而陛下只要脑子没糊涂，就不可能让你给五公主的死亡负责。也许王后那边会比较难说话，但他们顶多也就是让你远离王宫，把你派到比较冷清的职位上。但你现在还年轻，与其留在权力中心，还不如……”

“外公！”雷米尔打断老伯爵，“我和内蒂舒密尔真的什么都没有。”

老伯爵眼中闪过失望，过了一会儿，点点头：“好，你说没有那就没有吧。”

老伯爵不仅失望，他还感到一丝心冷。

按照克莱门特查到的线索以及知情人士的口供，雷米尔和内蒂关系非常亲密，两人就是妥妥的情人关系。

可内蒂死了，甚至可以说是为保护雷米尔而死，可雷米尔不但不见半点伤心，反而想尽办法想要割离与内蒂的关系。

连对正打得火热的情人都如此绝情，那已经知道自己身世的雷米尔又会对他和老太婆有多少祖孙情？

如果雷米尔真的对他有感情、相信他，今天就不会在他面前连番否认。

老伯爵其实在等待这个外孙跟他求助，跟他述说自己的困境。

他知道这个外孙是假的没错，但好歹也是从小养到大的孩子，要说没感情又怎么可能？
chunks.englishText:
Furthermore, from beginning to end, between every single line, the news article was filled with malice toward him. Clearly, the Fifth Princess's death had nothing to do with him, yet it painted him as a seductive, fickle playboy who casually toyed with female beastmen.

However, what terrified and bewildered Remiel the most was that this news report actually exposed his relationship with Eva!

What was even more frightening was that despite Eva having already eliminated that eavesdropper, their conversation had apparently still leaked, and it was now being published in a gossip tabloid for all to see.

Could someone already know the true relationship between him and Eva?

Panic gripped Remiel.

Deep down, he desperately wanted to expose his heritage, to let the whole world know that he was the Tiger King's biological son, the true and direct royal bloodline!

Yet, at the same time, he knew all too well that this was not the optimal time to reveal his identity. The Queen was still alive, and Elder Count Langzhen was still breathing. Once his identity was exposed, all the privileges he currently enjoyed would vanish, and all the agony and tragedy that Raphael Langmu had once suffered would be repeated upon him—perhaps even worse!

"Young Master Remiel!" a voice suddenly called out from the doorway.

Remiel snapped around to see an elderly servant from his maternal grandfather's household.

The old servant first bowed to him, then said with a grave expression, "Young Master Remiel, the Master asks that you return immediately."

Remiel frowned. Instinctively guessing why Elder Count Langzhen had summoned him back, he felt a wave of internal resistance and immediately made an excuse: "I still have work. After my shift ends..."

The old servant sighed, his eyes sweeping over the newspaper clutched in Remiel's hand. "You've seen the contents of the gossip tabloid as well. The Master says some matters are best resolved as quickly as possible. Even if you don't care about your own reputation, you must consider the Count's Estate and your deceased parents."

Remiel abruptly clenched his fists, a surge of anger rising in his chest. "I understand. I'll find time to go over shortly."

He truly did not want to go see the old count, but he also knew that such a scandal needed to be settled swiftly. It was impossible to ask Eva for help at a time like this, and the only person capable of helping him—and willing to do so—was this grandfather in name only.

Shortly after Remiel left the East Camp of the City Guard, another visitor came looking for him.

This time, it was a close attendant of the Tiger King, stating that the Tiger King summoned Remiel to enter the palace with all haste.

The other lieutenants in the office informed the attendant that Remiel had already been summoned away first by his grandfather.

The attendant nodded in acknowledgment and immediately returned to report back.

Inside the royal palace, upon hearing the attendant's report, the Tiger King waved his hand, dismissing all attending servants, and ordered someone to summon Clement.

Clement stepped into the study.

"Close the door," the Tiger King commanded in a deep voice.

Clement turned and shut the study doors.

A sigh sounded not far behind him.

Clement turned around to see the Tiger King leaning wearily against a broad chair, one hand pinching the bridge of his nose.

After a long while, Clement finally heard the Tiger King say, "Go investigate that Eva."

"Understood." Clement was about to withdraw.

The Tiger King spoke again: "Has the Queen called upon you?"

Clement paused. "Before you summoned me, the Queen's maid had already come looking for me."

"Did you go?"

"Not yet."

"Go. You know how to handle what should be said."

"Understood."

Clement waited for a moment, and seeing that the Tiger King had no further instructions, he left the study and headed toward the Queen's palace.

The moment Clement stepped inside, he saw several servants holding cleaning tools, carrying out a pile of shattered items.

It seemed the Queen was in a rather foul mood.

Clement had a maid announce his arrival to the Queen and waited outside the palace for summons.

Soon, the maid came to invite Clement in.

The Queen received Clement in the outer hall. There were obvious traces of fresh makeup on her face, and she seemed to have changed her outer robe as well.

"I do not wish to hear lies," the Queen said with a stern expression, cutting straight to the point. "Is the guard Netti liked none other than Lang Remiel?"

Clement replied, "Yes."

This matter could no longer be concealed; the gossip tabloid had practically named him outright.

"Why keep it from me? Was it the Tiger King who ordered you to hide this from me?!"

"...His Majesty believed this matter had no bearing on Guard Remiel and did not wish to drag more innocents into it."

"Innocents?" The Queen let out a cold laugh. "As long as it involves my daughter's death, no one is innocent! Since Xina was so fond of that Remiel, and Netti even killed Xina for his sake, then let Remiel go keep the two of them company."

Clement maintained a calm demeanor. "Remiel is no ordinary guard. His grandfather is Elder Count Langzhen, his mother was the former Guard Commander, and both his parents were heroes who sacrificed themselves for the country. Short of an act of high treason, even His Majesty cannot dispose of her—or him—at will."

The Queen raised her palm, appearing ready to fly into a rage, but upon seeing Clement's unflappable face and remembering his identity and powerful family background, she ultimately reined it in.

"High treason? Doesn't that newspaper claim he was conspiring with that brothel madam, Eva? You can go investigate thoroughly and see what on earth they are up to!" the Queen said darkly.

Clement nodded smoothly. "Understood."

At the Estate of Elder Count Langzhen.

Remiel had been sitting in stiff silence opposite the old count for quite a while.

Yet, up until now, the old count had not uttered a single word, merely sitting there and staring at him.

"Where is Grandmother?" Remiel asked, trying to sound as natural as possible.

Hearing Remiel inquire about his wife, the old count finally spoke. "She isn't feeling well and is resting in bed."

"I'll go check on Grandmother," Remiel said, making a motion to stand.

"Sit down!" the old count barked in a thunderous roar.

Remiel's body jerked, and he dared not rise.

The old count closed his eyes for a moment. "My Lang family produces no cowards who dare not own up to their actions. I'll ask you this: are you and that maid Netti Schumil a couple?"

Remiel frowned. "Grandfather, do not listen to those wild fabrications in the gossip tabloid. I merely know her. I work in the royal palace, and Netti Schumil was a senior maid at the Queen's side, so naturally I would see her frequently. But she and I are nothing more than acquaintances who nod in passing."

"Oh, is that so? Then you're saying you never slept with her."

"Grandfather!"

A complex look crossed the old count's eyes, and his tone lost some of its harshness. "If you truly were lovers, there is no shame in admitting it. The Fifth Princess's death was brought upon herself and has nothing to do with you. If Their Majesties attempt to trouble you over this, I will naturally protect you.

Furthermore, as long as the Sovereign hasn't lost his mind, he could not possibly hold you accountable for the Fifth Princess's death. The Queen's side might be more difficult to deal with, but at most, they would just remove you from the royal palace and post you to some quiet, obscure position. But you are still young; rather than remaining at the center of power, it would be better to—"

"Grandfather!" Remiel interrupted the old count. "Netti Schumil and I truly had nothing between us."

Disappointment flashed in the old count's eyes. After a moment, he nodded. "Very well. If you say there was nothing, then there was nothing."

The old count was not only disappointed; a chill had seeped into his heart.

According to the clues uncovered by Clement and the testimonies of those in the know, Remiel and Netti's relationship had been exceptionally close—they were a bona fide couple.

Yet Netti was dead, arguably having died to protect Remiel, and not only did Remiel show not a shred of grief, he was instead trying every possible means to sever any connection with her.

If he could be so ruthless even to a lover he had been passionately involved with, then how much familial affection could Remiel, who already knew his true heritage, possibly harbor for him and the old woman?

If Remiel genuinely had affection for him and trusted him, he would not have repeatedly denied it in front of him today.

In truth, the old count had been waiting for this grandson to seek his help and pour out his difficulties.

He knew this grandson was a fake, yes, but the boy was still a child he had raised since childhood. How could there be no affection between them?

chunks.chineseText:
他也不指望这个孩子在知道身世后会对他们一家有多少依恋，他只希望这个孩子是个有情有义的人，有自己的原则，做事不说堂堂正正，至少能对得起自己的良心。

他从没有想过要报复这个孩子，不管这孩子身世如何，那都是上代人做的孽，和他无关。

可雷米尔的表现却让老伯爵的心一点点变得冰冷。

也许是他们家的教育出了问题，也许是雷米尔根子就坏掉，也许是他那个母亲故意把他养歪……

“你变成现在这样，也有我的责任。我就不应该让你十六岁就搬出去一个人住。”老伯爵忽然道。

雷米尔皱眉，不快：“我变成怎样了？让您如此不满？”

老伯爵似乎对雷米尔的冲撞语气并不在乎：“跟着老虎学勇猛跟着猫儿学爬树，一个人的少年时期非常重要，在你年满十六岁以后，我只给你指派家庭教师，却没有亲自教导你，这是我的失职。”

“外公？”雷米尔非常不喜欢老伯爵现在的语气。

老伯爵看着雷米尔的眼睛，问：“你和那个伊娃是什么关系？”

雷米尔瞬间警惕起来，他最担心的就是老伯爵询问他和伊娃的关系。

“我和她能有什么关系？我就是去过几次旖梦楼，见到过她而已。”

“哦？你们没有密谋商量什么？”

“当然没有！”

老伯爵紧紧盯着雷米尔，此时的他看起来就像是一头盯上猎物的猛兽，眼神异常凶狠。

“我再给你最后一次机会，说出你和伊娃的真正关系。我既然是你的外公，不管你有什么改变、不管你遇到什么事，只要你自己想要脱离出来，我都会尽心尽力地帮助你，哪怕失去这个伯爵头衔！”

雷米尔咬紧牙关，不让自己避开老人的眼睛：“外公，我真没有说谎，我和伊娃没有任何关系，我也没有和她密谋什么事情。那就是那个八卦报为了哗宠取宠在胡说八道。”

老伯爵看了他好一会儿，最终点点头，像是相信了。

雷米尔刚松了一口气。

就听老伯爵用一种不容拒绝的语调和他说：“从现在开始，你不用去城卫军了。我会把你送到南方的复兴联盟，我年轻时曾经游历过那里，在那里买了一个能种植的庄园。原本我把那里当做我们家的退路，现在……我把那个庄园送给你。你到那里去经营这个庄园，以后都不要回来虎国，更不要再去见那个伊娃。除非伊娃愿意跟你到复兴联盟生活。”

雷米尔心惊：老头这是什么意思？他知道了什么？

不，他太紧张了，老头说的肯定不是他想的那个意思。也许老头只以为他喜欢上了风尘女，同时担心他被王后仇视，就想把他送到国外避风头。

“谢谢外公。但是我在城卫军做得好好的，我不想现在就离开。何况陛下对我十分信任，他说过让我到城卫军只是历练，他以后还有更重要的工作要交付给我。”雷米尔用自以为委婉的口吻婉拒。

老伯爵看他的眼神似乎闪过一丝伤痛，但很快就被老人掩饰过去。

雷米尔以为自己看错。

老伯爵沉默良久，最后劝了一次：“以你的能力和学识，你到南方联盟也能闯出一片天。何必留在王城跟着某些人瞎搅和？”

雷米尔假装听不懂，“外公，我觉得留在王城挺好的。”

老伯爵忽然露出疲累之色，“好吧，你想留在王城就留在王城吧。终归是那人的种，你想要争一争，我也能理解。不过，别把伯爵府扯下水。你外婆已经老了，我们只想过安稳平静的生活。”

雷米尔心惊，差点跳起来，好不容易才维持好脸上表情。

“外公，你、你在说什么？”

老人安静地看着他，不带任何感情地说道：“你知道我在说什么。如果你还有一点良心，那就别把我和你外婆扯进你和你母亲的阴谋中。”

哐当！

雷米尔惊得站起，身体撞倒木椅。

“你知道了！你是不是知道了？！”雷米尔已经不知道自己在说什么。

老人端起桌上的茶杯，抿了一口，淡淡回复：“我知道什么？你以为我知道了什么？”

雷米尔转头就冲出了老伯爵府，他的心乱了。

他要去找伊娃，他要去把这个重大消息告诉伊娃！

老伯爵夫人从屋内走出，走到老伴身边，扶起被撞倒的椅子，坐上去，叹了口气。

“你怎么突然说出来了？”

老伯爵面对老伴，什么面子里子都不要了，郁闷地说：“我给了他选择，他不肯要，非要蹚浑水。这好歹也是我们养出来的崽子，总不能眼睁睁看他去送死！”

“人各有志。他很可能被他母亲灌输了很多不应该有的念头。”

“安妮塔……”老伯爵对这个女兽人的看法也很复杂，既同情她曾经的遭遇，又痛恨她把其他无辜者扯进她的复仇计划的心狠手辣。

“你小心。雷米尔肯定去找他母亲了。一旦让安妮塔知道我们知道了雷米尔的身世，恐怕她会有所行动。”老夫人担心地说。

“杀了我们灭口吗？”老伯爵冷笑：“我就坐在这里等着她！”

“阿瑞斯商是不是知道你的计划？”老夫人忽然问。

老伯爵轻哼一声。

老夫人忽然就放心了。

要说安妮塔心狠手辣筹谋日久，那个阿瑞斯商就更不是什么好东西，一肚子坏水，更阴险狡诈！

如果阿瑞斯商站在他们的对面，是他们的敌人，老夫人能愁得睡不着觉。

但现在那个满肚子坏水的阿瑞斯商是他们这边的人，且眼里心里只有他们家拉斐尔，老夫人就淡定了。

就让那对凶兽互咬去吧。

阿瑞斯商要是输了，她和老头子就带着拉斐尔离开虎国去其他地方生活，远远离开这些是是非非和这群心脏脏的牲口们！
chunks.englishText:
He did not expect this child to be overly attached to their family after learning his true heritage; he only hoped the child was a person of sentiment and righteousness, possessing his own principles. Even if his actions weren't entirely upright, he should at least be able to live up to his own conscience.

He had never thought of retaliating against this child. No matter what the child's background was, that was the sin of the older generation and had nothing to do with him.

Yet Remiel's attitude caused the old count's heart to grow cold, bit by bit.

Perhaps something had gone wrong with their family's education; perhaps Remiel's very foundation was rotten; or perhaps that mother of his had deliberately warped him...

"You turning out like this is also partly my responsibility. I should never have let you move out to live alone at sixteen," the old count suddenly said.

Remiel frowned, displeased. "How have I turned out? To make you so dissatisfied?"

The old count seemed indifferent to Remiel's confrontational tone. "Just as following a tiger teaches bravery and following a cat teaches tree-climbing, a person's youth is of paramount importance. After you turned sixteen, I merely assigned you private tutors instead of personally guiding you—that was my dereliction of duty."

"Grandfather?" Remiel intensely disliked the old count's current tone.

Staring straight into Remiel's eyes, the old count asked, "What is your relationship with that Eva?"

Instant vigilance flared within Remiel. What he feared most was the old count inquiring about his relationship with Eva.

"What relationship could I possibly have with her? I've simply been to the Dream Pavilion a few times and caught sight of her, that's all."

"Oh? You haven't been plotting or discussing anything together?"

"Of course not!"

The old count stared fixedly at Remiel. At this moment, he looked like a fierce beast locking onto its prey, his gaze exceptionally savage.

"I will give you one last chance: state the true nature of your relationship with Eva. Since I am your grandfather, no matter what changes you've undergone or what troubles you encounter, as long as you wish to extricate yourself, I will do my utmost to help you—even if it means losing this title of count!"

Remiel clenched his teeth, forcing himself not to avert his eyes from the old man's gaze. "Grandfather, I really am not lying. I have no relationship with Eva whatsoever, nor have I plotted any matters with her. That gossip tabloid is simply spinning wild falsehoods for the sake of catching attention."

The old count studied him for a long moment before finally nodding, as if he believed him.

Remiel let out an internal breath of relief.

Then he heard the old count say in an uncompromising tone, "From now on, you need not go to the City Guard. I will send you to the Restoration Alliance in the south. I traveled extensively there in my youth and purchased a cultivable estate. Originally, I reserved that place as our family's fallback, but now... I give that manor to you. Go there and manage it, and never return to the Tiger Kingdom again. Furthermore, do not go to see that Eva ever again—unless she is willing to follow you and live in the Restoration Alliance."

Remiel was shaken to the core: What on earth did the old man mean by this? Did he know something?

No, he was just being overly nervous; the old man certainly didn't mean what he suspected. Perhaps the old man merely thought he had taken a fancy to a courtesan and, worried that he might incur the Queen's wrath, wanted to send him abroad to weather the storm.

"Thank you, Grandfather. But I am doing well in the City Guard, and I don't wish to leave right now. Besides, His Majesty places great trust in me; he told me that my stint in the City Guard is merely to temper myself, and he has even more important work to entrust to me in the future." Remiel declined with what he thought was a tactful tone.

A flash of what seemed like sorrow crossed the old count's eyes as he looked at him, though the old man masked it away instantly.

Remiel thought he must have seen wrong.

After a long silence, the old count made one final attempt at persuasion: "With your capability and knowledge, you could carve out a brilliant future in the Southern Alliance. Why insist on remaining in the Royal City to meddle in muddy waters?"

Feigning ignorance, Remiel replied, "Grandfather, I think staying in the Royal City is quite good."

The old count suddenly looked fatigued. "Very well. If you wish to stay in the Royal City, then stay. After all, you are that person's seed; I can understand your desire to contend for things. However, do not drag the Count's Estate down with you. Your grandmother is already old, and we only wish to live out our days in peace and quiet."

Remiel was startled, nearly leaping to his feet, and it took a supreme effort to maintain his facial expression.

"Grandfather, what—what are you talking about?"

The old man quietly looked at him, speaking without a trace of emotion: "You know what I'm talking about. If you still have an ounce of conscience, do not drag your grandmother and me into the conspiracy between you and your mother."

Clatter!

Startled, Remiel sprang up, his body knocking over the wooden chair.

"You know! Do you know?!" Remiel no longer knew what he was shouting.

The old man picked up the teacup on the table, took a sip, and replied indifferently, "Know what? What do you think I know?"

Remiel spun around and bolted out of the Count's Estate, his mind in complete disarray.

He had to find Eva! He had to convey this momentous piece of news to her!

The Countess emerged from the inner rooms, walked over to her companion, righted the toppled chair, sat down, and sighed.

"Why did you suddenly blurt it out?"

Facing his wife, the old count cast aside all pride and face, saying gloomily, "I gave him a choice, but he refused it, insisting on wading into these murky waters. He is still a cub we raised after all—how could I just stand by and watch him march to his death!"

"Everyone has their own aspirations. He was likely instilled with a great many improper notions by his mother."

"Anita..." The old count's view of this female beastman was deeply conflicted; he both pitied her past sufferings and loathed the ruthlessness with which she dragged other innocents into her plot for revenge.

"Be careful. Remiel will surely go looking for his mother. Once Anita realizes we know Remiel's heritage, she'll likely make a move," the old lady worriedly said.

"Will she murder us to keep us quiet?" The old count sneered. "I'll just sit right here and wait for her!"

"Doesn't the merchant Ares know of your plan?" the old lady suddenly asked.

The old count let out a soft huff.

Suddenly, the old lady felt completely at ease.

If Anita was ruthless and meticulous in her long-laid plans, that merchant Ares was even less of a saint—he was brimming with bad intentions and was infinitely more cunning and sinister!

If the merchant Ares stood opposed to them as their enemy, the old lady would be so worried she wouldn't be able to sleep.

But now, that scheming merchant Ares was on their side, and his eyes and heart held nothing save for their family's Raphael, so the old lady felt entirely at peace.

Let those two ferocious beasts tear into each other.

If Ares lost, she and the old man would simply take Raphael and leave the Tiger Kingdom to live elsewhere, far, far away from all these rights and wrongs and this herd of dark-hearted beasts!

chunks.chineseText:
第158章 施法

雷米尔没能见到伊娃，他刚进旖梦楼就被多丽丝拉了过去。

多丽丝暗中告诉他，伊娃让他这段时间不要再来旖梦楼，更不要找她，如果有事，她会主动联系他。

雷米尔心急如焚，他非常需要马上见到伊娃，把老伯爵很可能已经知道他真正身世的事告诉对方。

但多丽丝只摇头说，伊娃看到八卦报上的内容后就把楼里的事情都交给她，人已经离开，现在人在哪里，她也不知道。

因为身世的事事关重大，雷米尔也不敢让多丽丝转告，只能留下口信，告诉多丽丝他有非常紧急且重要的事要告诉伊娃，让伊娃一定要尽快联系他。

雷米尔从旖梦楼出来，深吸几口气，整理了下衣着，叫来一辆兽车，前往城卫军东营。

他告诉自己，必须镇定，要做出什么事都没有的样子，他这时千万不能慌。

到了东营，又收到口信，说是王宫有侍从过来，让他一收到讯息就去王宫面见陛下。

雷米尔头疼无比，他用膝盖想都能猜出虎王这时找他过去必然是要问伊娃的事，他得想个好的借口，至少不能让虎王知道他知道伊娃的真实身份。

好在伊娃早就设想过她身份如果暴露后的应对方法，也教了他一套说辞。

“……她曾经被郎飞统领救下，也是在郎飞统领的关照下才能在王城里落脚开店。后来郎飞统领牺牲，她就很关注我，不过因为她的身份问题，她一直没有接触我，直到我偶尔去旖梦楼放松，她才和我接触。我们在一起时，大多聊的都是郎飞统领生前的一些事情。”

雷米尔垂着眼眸，语气平稳地说完。

“原来是这样。”坐在上首的虎王手里把玩着王印，嘴角似乎还含着笑，似乎让雷米尔过来只是拉拉家常。

“这么说那八卦报上说的后半段内容都是假的了？”

雷米尔语气微冷：“我已经说了实话，如果您不相信，我也没办法。”

虎王见雷米尔如此，到底是自己儿子，也不想真的伤了他的心，就语气缓和地说：“那个伊娃是否真的被郎飞救过，这事还需要求证。可如果对方有意设计，想要骗你入坑，那么肯定会做好相关方面的布置。

在别人眼中，你年龄小却身份高贵，且即将继承一个偌大的伯爵府，本身也很有能力，还是我身边近臣，打你主意的人肯定不会少。

那个伊娃，在我查明她的底细之前，你就暂时不要和她接触了。那个旖梦楼也别再去了。”

雷米尔见虎王语气缓和，他的神情也跟着放软，语气中带着委屈说：“知道了，我以后不会去了。”

虎王又试探地问：“你对王后……”

雷米尔眼神倔强，“她害死我母亲，我还不能骂她两句吗？”

虎王叹息，“王后那边你没事别招惹她，那报上说破茜娜的死和你也有一点关系，王后可能会迁怒你。如果她找你麻烦，你先避着点。有你外公在，她也不敢明着对你做什么，顶多就是让你难受、让你没脸。”

雷米尔忽然抬起头，眼神痛苦又悲愤：“难道我要永远躲着她让着她，就连她要迁怒我，我都只能忍耐吗？等我以后真正身世暴露，她让我死，我是不是也只能去死？”

“胡说什么！”虎王微怒，看到雷米尔没有掩盖住的悲伤神情，心里也很不是滋味，但他也不能明说他的计划，只能说：“有我在，谁敢让你死？王后那边……以后你就会知道，现在你的忍耐，将来自会补偿你。”

雷米尔几次要把老伯爵很可能知道他真正身世的事告诉虎王，但话到嘴边又咽了回去。

看老伯爵那个意思，应该是不打算把这件事说出去，而且对方那说话的神情和态度也不像是知道拉斐尔才是他亲外孙的样子……也许还在寻找证据？也许是有其他顾忌？

既然老伯爵打算帮他隐瞒，他又何必多此一举，如果让虎王从老伯爵那里得知安妮塔还活着的事，那还不如暂时什么都不跟他说。

“那个八卦报持续胡说八道，破坏他人名声，污蔑权贵，更对王室不敬。难道陛下要任由这家报社就这么经营下去？”雷米尔恨声说。

他现在恨死这家八卦报了。

虎王：“我已经让人盯住这家报社，看它背后有谁在操控。不过现在并不是关停这家报社的好时机，这家报社刚闹出多条人命，又已经在王城闹出偌大名气，王城民众现在都在等着新一期八卦报的发行，如果在此时关停它，很可能会激起不必要的民愤。”

虎王说的都是实话，只不过隐瞒了部分更深层的心思。

他想挖掘出这家报社背后的情报提供者，只看这报社发行的前四期内容，就知道这家报社背后有一个多么厉害的情报提供队伍。

首先，他要只知道这支队伍由谁掌控，是否是虎国的对立方。

其次，如果对方身后势力不大，他也许可以把这支队伍收到自己旗下。

还有更说不出口的第三点理由，目前那八卦报上提到的头条新闻虽然大部分都和王室有关，但对方的目标似乎隐隐指向王后。

他一直想着要如何平稳地把王后拉下王后的宝座，又不会波及到她所生的王子和公主。八卦报现在做的事可以说很符合他的利益，比起封禁这家报社，还不如把这家报社“不惧强权、敢于报道真实”的名气彻底培养起来，哪怕这会让王室损伤一点面子。

可今后他拿下这家报社，让其成为他的口舌，那这家报社的价值可就大了。到时候他让八卦报真真假假掺杂一些消息，想抹黑一些人、挑拨某些人、打击某些人等就会容易得多。

这些涉及肮脏政治手段的话，虎王自然不可能跟雷米尔全部交代出来，且雷米尔也不是他看中的继承人。

“我这里有一份重要邀请函，要送给一个避世的大部落，那个大部落实力雄厚，但少于外人接触，我怀疑对方听到传承大会的消息也不会主动过来。你跑一趟，最迟明天就出发，把这份邀请函送给对方，一定要请到那大部落的头领过来。”

虎王拿出一份精美的请柬。

雷米尔眼睛有点发红：“您也想让我离开王城？”

虎王猜测老伯爵可能也跟雷米尔说过类似的话，让他先离开王城一段时间。

“这段时间王城有点乱，你又被王后盯上，不如暂时离开。”

雷米尔上前接过请柬，眼睑下垂遮盖住真正想法，只说：“我知道了。”

虎王看着雷米尔离开的背影，深深叹息。他在保护这孩子，这孩子怎么就不明白呢？

不帅那边也看到了八卦报第四期的头条内容。

他很惊讶地问商非凡：“你这么快就让报社提到伊娃，就不怕她跑路？”

商非凡接过报纸迅速看完，挑眉：“这可不是我让他们报道的内容，这应该是他们内部自己自作主张。”

“玩家怎么会知道伊娃和雷米尔私会的事？还提到他们密谋？”
