"What I want to discuss with you this time, brother, Ah Dai has probably already mentioned to you." The village chief of Heaven-Defect Village sighed before he even began speaking.

Just as Shang Feifan was about to recall what Ah Dai had mentioned to him about the village, Ah Dai whispered from the side: "I told you, there's something fishy about those village cubs being taken away."

Shang Feifan pinched Ah Dai's mouth, gesturing for the village chief to explain in detail.

The village chief gave a bitter smile. "Ah Dai is right. The matter of those children we couldn't afford to raise being taken away does indeed have issues, but we had no choice *but* to do it."

Present this time were not only the village chief, but also three very elderly-looking old orcs.

One of the elderly male orcs, while twisting a straw rope, said to Shang Feifan: "Don't blame the village chief for this; it was a decision made by our entire village. Don't judge us just yet—listen to the beginning and end of this matter first."

With his patience wearing thin, Shang Feifan nodded. "Please speak."

When the village chief sent Ah Dai to invite Shang Feifan over, he had already made up his mind to spill everything.

He and the village elders had discussed it: they simply couldn't find anyone else who could help them. If Shang Feifan were merely an ordinary, wealthy merchant-artisan, they wouldn't even bring it up. But they... had witnessed with their own eyes a massive number of Undead Corpses attacking that strange orc-gathered encampment outside Heaven-Defect Valley. Coupled with Shang Feifan's prior warning to them, didn't this plainly indicate that the person who attacked that camp and castle had a connection to Shang Feifan?

Heaven-Defect Village lived in seclusion, and interpersonal exchanges were exceedingly barren. The capable figures they knew were few and far between, let alone a big shot who was capable, powerful, and wealthy.

Now that they had finally discovered an extraordinary figure who also shared a sliver of friendship with them, the hearts of the village chief and elders became active.

As for the possibility that the other party might manipulate Undead Corpses and not walk the path of normal innate bloodlines—was that point important?

What mattered was that Ah Dai trusted him.

Ah Dai had been a rather special child back in the village. Despite his young age, he was quite perceptive of people; he seemed to naturally know who could be trusted and who shouldn't be approached.

The fact that he managed to evade "adoption"—that a tiny cub, without the deliberate care of elders, managed to stumble and grow up to that size, waiting all the while until Shang Feifan arrived—was enough to prove his survival instincts were far stronger than those of other cubs.

The fact that Ah Dai could bring this person back and show him off indicated that this person possessed absolute integrity.

Above all, that matter had been like a thorn stuck in their hearts. Knowing full well there was a problem yet lacking the ability to deal with it left them unable to sleep peacefully even at night.

They simply wanted to give it a try.

Fortunately, Shang Feifan displayed a willingness to listen.

This was an extremely good start. Regardless of whether Shang ultimately agreed to their request, at least they could share this secret with someone else; should anything happen to Heaven-Defect Village, the secret wouldn't simply be buried with them.

Following that, the village chief recounted the difficult circumstances and predicaments of their village to Shang Feifan.

Because Heaven-Defect Village had limited capacity and insufficient self-recovery capabilities, it was fundamentally incapable of raising too many children.

Coupled with the discrimination from nearby orcs, they were barred from expanding their gathering and hunting territories, and arable farmland was something they couldn't possibly compete for.

Under such circumstances, outsiders kept throwing defective infants into Heaven-Defect Valley—sometimes a dozen or so in a year, and up to twenty or thirty during worse years.

Heaven-Defect Village truly couldn't raise so many infants, yet they couldn't just turn a blind eye to them either, leaving them with no choice but to tighten their belts to get by.

However, as days turned into months and years into decades, the orcs in the village married and bore children of their own. Naturally, everyone cherished their own offspring more. When the village forcibly demanded that everyone squeeze out food and living resources to feed abandoned, unfamiliar infants, causing their own children to cry out in hunger as a result, the villagers finally exploded.

The villagers could understand why the village chief and elders were willing to accept those abandoned defective infants—they themselves had been raised the exact same way. But everything must have its limits; when you and your own children were on the verge of starvation, and people still expected you to show universal benevolence, that wasn't making things difficult—that was driving people to their deaths.

The village chief and elders also knew things couldn't go on like this. They wanted to earn more food and living resources, but suffered from the surrounding barrenness; even if they wanted to do hard labor, no one would hire them.

Just as they found themselves in an extreme dilemma, an adventurer squad appeared.

"The members of this squad were both very powerful and very wealthy. When they accidentally discovered our village and learned of our plight, they offered to help us. The way they helped us wasn't by providing living supplies and food, nor by hiring us as laborers, but by offering to adopt the children our village couldn't afford to raise."

"At first, we hesitated, fearing those children might meet a bad end if taken away. But that squad promised us that we could regularly visit the children who were taken away. If we felt those children weren't living well, or if the children themselves wanted to come with us, we could take them back."

"We really had it too hard back then, and it coincided with the winter when food was most scarce. If we hadn't agreed, quite a few cubs in the village might have starved to death. Afterwards, the village discussed it collectively and ultimately agreed to let that adventurer squad take away the infants our village couldn't raise."

"However, that adventurer squad didn't take all the infants; they would go through a certain selection process. We didn't know what their selection criteria were—anyway, some relatively robust children were chosen, and sickly ones were chosen as well."

The village chief suddenly added: "When they took the infants away, they originally intended to give our village a sum of upbringing fees, but our village refused it. We only hoped those children could survive. If the village hadn't been in such dire straits, unable to support so many children, we wouldn't have let outsiders take away those abandoned infants."

Hearing this, Shang Feifan interrupted to ask: "That group of people comes to pick infants every year?"

"Yes. Almost every year, and always in the winter." The village chief paused. "Judging by past timing, they should be coming over quite soon."

Shang Feifan nodded: "Then have you guys regularly visited the children who were taken away?"

"Of course!" the village chief replied swiftly. "Every year when they come to select people, we tag along with them to their territory to check on how the taken-away infants are doing."

Shang Feifan understood: "You saw with your own eyes that those taken-away infants seemed to be doing all right, but you still sensed that something was amiss, is that right?"

The village chief once again wore a bitter smile: "Yes."

"The village chief went once and came back to tell me the situation, and I went along twice." This time, the speaker was another relatively strapping old man whose voice was quite hoarse, as if he hadn't spoken for a long time.

"Just as you said, on the surface, it appeared those children were all doing quite well. They had warm, sturdy housing—though a dozen children slept in a single room, every child had their own bed, along with warm, clean bedding. The clothes they wore were clean and undamaged, of a reasonably suitable size, even if they were uniform garments."

"The food they ate wasn't too bad either. Although it was all some sort of mush whose raw ingredients were unknown, at least they could eat their fill."

"They even attended classes, with people teaching them knowledge and hunting techniques."

At this point, the old man paused: "Orcs must learn how to hunt, but hunting techniques are often skills used to slaughter others. Those children were trained like soldiers—obeying orders strictly, showing not the slightest fear of pain or injury. I suspect that even their fear of death has been suppressed to the absolute minimum."

The village chief licked his lips and said bitterly: "Though our village is poor and can't afford to raise many children, the kids in our village were genuine youngsters back then, each with their own personality, and most of them were quite mischievous—unless they were so hungry they couldn't move. But those children were all cut from the exact same mold; in their eyes... there was no light, only numbness and obedience."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第237章 天残村长的委托 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
“那些人其实有做掩饰，但可能听令已经深入那些幼崽的骨子里，导致他们的一举一动都能看出痕迹。而且那些孩子明显害怕那些成年兽人。可当我悄悄问他们，他们过得怎么样，想不想和我回村里时，那些孩子都说他们过得很好，不想回村。”

村长捂住脸，这个心理包袱对他太沉重。

可村里条件就那样，他顾得了一头，就顾不了另一头。

老兽人：“我们又质问对方为什么要把孩子们训练成这样。他们说这是为了幼崽们好，让他们从小就学会一定生存和战斗技能。他们还说他们对幼崽们采取军队类管理，也是为了打磨小崽子们爱玩爱闹的不良性子，同时也方便他们管理。”

“我说这样养育幼崽不对，他们就笑着说‘难不成我们花费大量资源和粮食就是为了做好事？你们其实也心知肚明，我们养育这么多孩子，肯定是要用他们的。这是我们冒险团培养团队成员的方式，如果你们看不顺眼，以后可以不把那些被弃养的天残幼崽交给我们’。”

“随后他们中像是管事的人又出来打圆场说，这些幼崽交给我们村，我们村也养不好，甚至养不活。把幼崽们送来他们团，至少能保证这些幼崽可以活下去。说听令和遵守纪律只是一种团队要求，并不是虐待孩子。”

“之后他们就带我们参观了孩子的住宿楼、训练场、食堂这些地方，还让几个幼崽和我们说话。”

商非凡抬手，打断村长和老兽人：“你们检查过孩子身体没有？有没有发现明显伤痕？比如被惩罚的痕迹。”

村长和老兽人都摇头：“我们有偷偷检查，但我们只接触到几个那些人让我们接触的孩子，那几个孩子身上除了训练的摔打伤，并没有其他严重伤痕。其他孩子我们都只能远远看到，就算近距离接触，也没机会看他们衣服下面有没有受伤。”

商非凡笑了笑：“这个冒险团队也没说错，他们又不是专门做慈善的，领走那些幼崽肯定是想把他们训练培育成能用的工具，采取军事化管理也是理所当然。所以你们到底想要跟我说什么？或者明白说，你们想要我做什么？”

村长和三位村老互看。

唯一的老妇人开口了：“如果只是把孩子们培养成冒险团队成员，甚至是炮灰类成员，我们虽然难过，但也不会责怪那个冒险团队。毕竟那些孩子至少能长大，至于能不能在任务中活下来则得看他们自己的个人本事。可是……”

“那个所谓的冒险团队至今为止已经带走不下五百个孩子，时间跨度长达二十三年。可这么多年，我们没有看到一个成年孩子。”

“问他们，他们就说长大的孩子已经转移培训地点，跟着团队出去做任务。”

“我们希望见到成年的孩子，但他们说成年的幼崽愿不愿意回天残村是他们的自由，他们无法强求。”

老妇人深吸气：“我们最终会产生怀疑，并不想再把幼崽交给他们带走，是因为有个半大的幼崽逃了回来，但他刚逃到谷口那片树林的边界处就……死了。巨虫通知我们，我们查看那半大孩子的尸体，发现他身上伤痕累累，更发现他后脖颈的位置有个圆形伤口。”

另一名老兽人：“那个圆形伤口不是新伤口，一看就是反复受伤，我懂一点医术，那明显就是有什么器具长期插-入后脑那个位置。”

商非凡下意识想到了他“复活”的场景，他可是从后脑亲手拔-出了一根管子。

难道那些被带走的天残幼崽也与洛伦米尔顿有关？

“你们有抬着尸体去找那支冒险团队质问吗？”商非凡问。

村长狠狠揉脸，用力说：“没有！我当时是想带着村人和那孩子的尸体要去找他们质问，但……”

“我阻止了大家。”老妇人打断村长，冷静说：“一来，抬着尸体过去质问会打草惊蛇，让剩下的孩子日子更不好过。至少我们没办法把那些孩子给讨回来。如果惹怒那些人，把幼崽们杀了灭口怎么办？”

“二来，就算我们把尸体抬过去，他们也可以不承认。理由太多了，比如说这个半大幼崽受不住训练的苦，早就自己跑掉，他在外面受到什么伤害，自然和他们冒险团队没有任何干系。”

老妇人握紧双手：“我们没有证据。那孩子身上什么都没有留下来，死前也没有留下任何只言片语。”

“这是什么时候发生的事情？”商非凡问。

村长回答：“四年前。”

商非凡心里想，怪不得阿呆躲着那群人，不肯参与挑选，村民们也没有逼迫他，后来阿呆要跟他走，村民们也没有阻拦，原来根子在这里。

“那这四年来，你们还是假装什么都不知道，依然让那些人来挑选幼崽？”

“三年，今年还没到时间。”村长痛苦道：“我们也不想，但我们投鼠忌器。他们来人试探过我们，给我们隐瞒过去了。我们害怕拒绝那些人，那些人会直接带着还在培训中的幼崽消失，更怕他们干脆直接攻打我们村、抢夺我们村的幼崽。”

村长看向阿呆，“所以如果有幼崽不想被那些人挑中，我们也不会强求，还会帮忙把他们藏起来。那些人觉得幼崽数量少，我们就说孩子调皮，自己跑出去玩，我们一时半会儿找不到。”

阿呆做农民揣，窝在他商爸怀里，一脸呆样，就像是不知道大人们在讨论什么。

他感觉到村长和村老的目光，也明白他们想要他帮忙说说话，但他全当没看到没看懂。

村长在心里叹气，也没为难这个小家伙。

“他们有要求带走你们村自己村民生的孩子吗？”商非凡问。

“他们没有主动提。”村长脸色有点难看：“一开始有傻的村民还想让自己的孩子冒充孤儿，去那冒险团队占便宜，等孩子长大了，再让孩子回村。但是这样做的村民都没能等到自己的孩子回来。之后又发现那个逃回却重伤死去的半大崽儿，大家就更打消了这个心思。”

“那你们村有失踪的村民孩子吗？”商非凡又问。

这下村长的脸色更难看了：“有……”

老兽人在一边解释：“我们也不确定失踪的幼崽是不是那个冒险团队带走了，因为以往每几年都会失踪一两个孩童，有的是自己跑出去玩遇到危险回不来，有的是不想待在村里想去找自己的亲人，所以……”

商非凡听到这里已经明白全部始末，捏了捏阿呆的小爪子，问：“你们想让我去查看那个冒险团队是不是真的在培养团队成员，以及查看他们到底对带走的幼崽做了什么，对么？”

村长和三位村老齐齐点头。

老妇人叹息，“我们知道这事委托你是我们厚颜，但我们也找不到更适合更有能力的人了。如果你拒绝，我们也能理解。但如果有可能还是希望你能帮帮我们、帮帮这些年被带走的那么多幼崽。当然，我们也不会让你白忙一趟，我们村曾经在后山挖掘出一些东西……”
chunks.englishText:
"Those people actually tried to cover it up, but perhaps obedience has already been deeply ingrained into the bones of those cubs, causing traces of it to show in their every movement. Moreover, those children were clearly afraid of the adult orcs. Yet when I quietly asked them how they were doing and if they wanted to return to the village with me, all the children said they were doing very well and didn't want to go back."

The village chief covered his face; this psychological burden was far too heavy for him.

However, the village's conditions were just like that—if he took care of one end, he couldn't take care of the other.

The old orc said, "We questioned the other party again as to why they trained the children into such a state. They said it was for the cubs' own good, allowing them to learn certain survival and combat skills from a young age. They also said that adopting a military-style management over the cubs was meant to grind away their bad habits of playing and making a fuss, while also making it convenient for them to manage."

"When I said this way of raising cubs was wrong, they just smiled and said, 'Could it be that we spend a massive amount of resources and food just to do good deeds? You actually know in your hearts that since we raise so many children, we are definitely going to use them. This is the way our adventure group trains team members. If you find it an eyesore, you don't have to hand over the abandoned Defective cubs to us in the future.'"

"Then, someone among them who seemed to be in charge came out to smooth things over, saying that if these cubs were handed over to our village, our village wouldn't be able to raise them well, or even keep them alive. Sending the cubs to their group could at least guarantee that these cubs would survive. They claimed that listening to commands and observing discipline was merely a team requirement, not child abuse."

"Afterward, they took us to tour the children's dormitory, training grounds, cafeteria, and other places, and even let a few cubs speak with us."

Shang Feifan raised a hand, interrupting the village chief and the old orc: "Did you check the children's bodies? Did you find any obvious scars? For example, traces of punishment?"

The village chief and the old orc both shook their heads: "We secretly checked, but we only came into contact with a few children whom those people allowed us to approach. Aside from the bruises and scrapes from training, there were no other serious scars on those few children. We could only see the other children from afar, and even during close contact, we had no opportunity to check if there were injuries under their clothes."

Shang Feifan smiled. "This adventure group didn't say anything wrong; they aren't running a charity. Taking those cubs away definitely means training and cultivating them into usable tools, and implementing militarized management is only a matter of course. So what on earth do you want to tell me? Or to put it bluntly, what do you want me to do?"

The village chief and the three village elders looked at each other.

The only old woman spoke: "If they were merely training the children to be members of an adventure group, or even cannon-fodder members, although we would feel sad, we wouldn't blame that adventure group. After all, those children could at least grow up, and as for whether they could survive missions, that would depend on their own personal abilities. However..."

"That so-called adventure group has taken away no fewer than five hundred children so far, spanning a period of twenty-three years. Yet throughout all these years, we haven't seen a single grown child."

"When we asked them, they said the children who have grown up have already been transferred to another training location and went out on missions with the group."

"We hope to see the grown children, but they said it is the freedom of the grown cubs whether they want to return to Defective Village or not, and they cannot force it."

The old woman took a deep breath: "The reason we ultimately grew suspicious and no longer wanted to hand the cubs over to them to take away is because a half-grown cub escaped back, but the moment he fled to the boundary of the woods at the valley entrance, he... died. The giant insects notified us, and when we examined the half-grown child's corpse, we found that his body was covered in wounds, and even more so, there was a circular wound on the back of his neck."

Another old orc chimed in: "That circular wound was not a fresh wound; one could tell at a glance that it was injured repeatedly. I know a bit of medicine, and that was clearly caused by some apparatus being inserted into the back of the head for a long time."

Shang Feifan instinctively thought of the scene where he was "resurrected"—he had pulled a tube out from the back of his head with his own hands.

Could those Defective cubs who had been taken away also be related to Loren Milton?

"Did you carry the corpse to confront that adventure group?" Shang Feifan asked.

The village chief rubbed his face fiercely and said with force, "No! At the time, I wanted to lead the villagers and the child's corpse to find them and demand an explanation, but..."

"I stopped everyone," the old woman interrupted the village chief, saying calmly: "Firstly, carrying the corpse over for a confrontation would alert the enemy and make the lives of the remaining children even worse. At the very least, we wouldn't be able to get those children back. What if it angered those people and they killed the cubs to eliminate witnesses?"

"Secondly, even if we carried the corpse over, they could simply deny it. There are too many excuses, such as this half-grown cub being unable to endure the hardship of training and running away on his own long ago, and whatever injuries he suffered outside naturally having nothing to do with their adventure group."

The old woman clenched her hands: "We have no evidence. Nothing was left on the child's body, and he didn't leave a single word before dying."

"When did this happen?" Shang Feifan asked.

The village chief replied, "Four years ago."

Shang Feifan thought to himself: No wonder A-Dai hid from that group of people and refused to participate in the selection, and the villagers didn't force him. Later, when A-Dai wanted to leave with him, the villagers didn't stop him either. The root of the matter was right here.

"Then for these past four years, you still pretended not to know anything and continued to let those people come and select cubs?"

"Three years. This year's time hasn't arrived yet," the village chief said in anguish. "We didn't want to, but we were constrained by fear. They sent people to test us, and we managed to muddle through it. We are afraid that if we refuse them, those people will directly disappear with the cubs still in training, and we are even more afraid that they will simply attack our village directly and snatch our cubs away."

The village chief looked at A-Dai. "Therefore, if any cub does not want to be chosen by those people, we won't force them and will even help hide them. When those people feel the number of cubs is too small, we say the children were mischievous, ran out to play by themselves, and we couldn't find them for a while."

A-Dai held his hands inside his sleeves, nestled in his Shang-dad's arms, looking completely blank, as if he didn't know what the adults were discussing.

Sensing the gazes of the village chief and the elders, he understood they wanted him to help put in a good word, but he pretended not to see or understand at all.

The village chief sighed inwardly, but didn't make things difficult for this little fellow.

"Did they demand to take away children born to your own villagers?" Shang Feifan asked.

"They didn't proactively bring it up." The village chief's face looked a bit ugly: "In the beginning, some foolish villagers wanted to let their own children pretend to be orphans to take advantage of that adventure group, waiting until the children grew up before letting them return to the village. But the villagers who did this never waited for their children to return. Afterward, when they discovered that half-grown cub who had escaped back only to die heavily wounded, everyone completely dispelled this notion."

"Then are there any missing children from your village?" Shang Feifan asked again.

At this, the village chief's face turned even uglier: "There are..."

The old orc explained from the side: "We aren't certain whether the missing cubs were taken away by that adventure group, because in the past, every few years one or two children would go missing. Some ran out to play on their own and encountered danger unable to return, while others didn't want to stay in the village and wanted to find their own relatives, so..."

Hearing this, Shang Feifan already understood the whole story. He pinched A-Dai's little claw and asked, "You want me to check whether that adventure group is truly training team members, and to see what on earth they did to the cubs they took away, right?"

The village chief and the three village elders nodded in unison.

The old woman sighed, "We know it is shameless of us to entrust this matter to you, but we can't find anyone more suitable or capable. If you refuse, we can understand. But if possible, we still hope you can help us—help the so many cubs who have been taken away over the years. Of course, we won't let you work in vain; our village once dug up some things in the back mountain..."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第237章 天残村长的委托 (Part 3)
chunks.chineseText:
村长立刻起身，从后面干草堆里掏出一口箱子，提了过来。

老妇人用下巴指了指那口箱子：“里面的东西我们用不上，也不知道要找谁换粮食换物资。就凭我们这些被人鄙视的天残乡巴佬，东西拿出去也只有被抢被骗的份。”

村长打开箱子，亮出里面存放的物品。

商非凡眼睛扫过去，中级鉴定术发挥作用，他的脑子里直接给出了这些物品的名字、来历和作用。

现在商非凡已经明白他在兽人大陆学到的技能与知识绝大多数都是游戏系统直接灌输给他，包括鉴定术需要的丰富知识。很可能他的鉴定术连接了游戏系统的数据库，达到什么级别就能鉴定出那个级别内的所有物品。

光球点赞：你猜得太对了。鉴定术需要的知识太庞大，没办法全部塞给你，只能采取连接主脑数据库的方式，只要你不和我断开，你的鉴定术就一直能使用。

商非凡发现箱子里的东西看着陈旧，但都还算整齐干净，不像是坏掉的样子。

村长讪笑：“这都是从后山墓地里挖出来的。我们没特意去挖，只是有一年地动，一些地下墓穴被翻了上来，里面的尸骨和陪葬品见了天光，我们就给那些尸骨重新掩埋了，陪葬品就捡了一些还算完好地回来。”

商非凡感兴趣地：“后山墓地里埋的都是普通尸体？不是不死尸？”

村长脸黑了：“如果埋的都是不死尸，我们哪里还敢住在这里。”

商非凡心想，那就不一定了。你可是亲口说过这一大片闹过不死尸，要不是有祭司献祭自己的小儿子，那些不死尸也不会消失。而且那个人渣用的玩家身体原材料九成九就是不死尸，说不定那些不死尸并不是消失，而是跟彭石城那边的不死尸一样，都只是找了个地方躲了起来。

这么一想，商非凡就心动了。

他之前觉得不死尸数量太多不好处理太讨厌，可发现不死尸听令肯干活还不要工资的诸多美好优点后，他就有一点想要多多益善。

如果他能把这片地界藏着的不死尸也找出来……

而这对他并不是什么难事。

商非凡对于找寻不死尸一事可要比去找那什么冒险团队有兴趣多了。

【这里面有一个外戴式大脑辅助处理计算器，也叫外置脑芯片，可以辅助使用者进行思考、计算、存储和搜索，相当于让使用者多出几个异能，例如过目不忘、数据库搜索、强力计算等。】

商非凡原本很是看不上那箱子里的东西，虽然都是大繁华纪的东西，但功能上地星基本都有，他看着真的没什么稀奇，还有些珠宝首饰之类对他更没吸引力，顶多就是当做古董卖给兽人大陆的拍卖行。

可一听光球提醒里面竟然还有脑芯片这个好东西，他的兴趣顿时就来了。

“外戴式脑芯片？”

【因为当时的人们恐惧芯片内置，就研发了外置式，有入耳式，也有贴头皮式。也有人说这是光脑的最初原形机，可惜兽人的科技文明没有能发展到光脑那一步就被战争摧毁了。】

“你不就是光脑？”

光球拒绝回应这个问题。

商非凡也没纠结这点，他把那个外戴式脑芯片拿了出来。

这玩意的造型还很有童心，看起来就像是一个小猫外形的发夹。

这东西如果能拿到地星那边，应该会有用吧？

而且技术上应该也不会有太大的断层，又没有多少炼金痕迹，纯科技物品，正正好。

“这个活我接了，但我不保证结果。只能说查到什么就是什么。”商非凡不是很负责地说。

村长和三位村老却同时露出笑容：“能查就行。”

村长紧接着说：“那就麻烦诺曼兄弟在我们村再待几天，那个冒险团队的人应该在这几天就会到。到时候你可以不和他们碰面，暗中跟上去。”

阿呆仰头看他商爸，眼里有担忧，神情小复杂。但他嘴巴从始至终都闭得紧紧，不想去影响他商爸。

商非凡笑，心想要是阿沐在这里，不用报酬都会接下这个任务。当即揉了揉阿呆的方脑袋，把小猫发夹往他头毛上一别：“那这事就这么说定。这个权当做定金。”

村长和三位村老自然没有二话，他们还觉得商非凡拿的定金太少，还想多塞点。

商非凡摆摆手，表示定金不用那么多，反正最后都会是他的。

“如果我发现那个冒险团队确实有问题，你们送出去的那些幼崽确实都在受罪，你们打算怎么做？”商非凡出门前，转头问。

村长毫不犹豫：“我们村会出人想方设法把成年和没成年的幼崽都接回来。如果他们还敢找来，我们就和他们拼了！”

商非凡刚想问村人的武力值比起那冒险团队如何。

村长又腆着脸搓手说：“如果我们村去救人时，恰好有一大群不死尸也游荡到那个冒险团队的老巢那里，还追着那些冒险团队的人咬，且不咬我们，那就更好了。”

商非凡：“……”原来你们打着这个主意。

几个老兽人加一个壮年的村长全都用期盼的星星眼看他。

商非凡眼睛疼，嗯道：“诅咒你们此时心想事成。”

这次轮到村长和村老们无语。就不能祝福吗？为什么非要诅咒？
chunks.englishText:
Citing this, the village chief immediately stood up, pulled out a chest from the pile of dry hay in the back, and brought it over.

The old woman pointed her chin at the chest: "We have no use for the things inside, nor do we know who to find to trade them for food and supplies. With just us Defective bumpkins who are looked down upon, taking these things out would only result in us being robbed or cheated."

The village chief opened the chest, revealing the items stored inside.

Shang Feifan swept his gaze across them, and his Intermediate Appraisal Skill took effect, directly giving him the names, origins, and functions of these items in his mind.

By now, Shang Feifan already understood that the vast majority of the skills and knowledge he learned on the Orc Continent were directly instilled into him by the game system, including the rich knowledge required by the Appraisal Skill. It was very likely that his Appraisal Skill was connected to the game system's database; as long as a certain level was reached, all items within that level could be appraised.

The Orbling gave a thumbs-up: *You guessed right on the mark. The knowledge required for the Appraisal Skill is too vast to cram into you all at once, so we can only adopt the method of connecting to the mainframe database. As long as you don't disconnect from me, your Appraisal Skill will always be usable.*

Shang Feifan found that the items in the chest looked old, but they were still quite neat and clean, not looking damaged at all.

The village chief chuckled awkwardly: "These were all dug up from the graveyard in the back mountain. We didn't intentionally go digging; it's just that one year there was an earthquake, and some underground tombs were overturned. The skeletons and funerary objects within were exposed to the light of day, so we re-buried those skeletons and picked back some of the funerary objects that were still relatively intact."

Shang Feifan asked with interest, "Are the things buried in the back mountain graveyard all ordinary corpses? Not Undead?"

The village chief's face turned dark: "If they were all buried with Undead, we wouldn't dare live here."

Shang Feifan thought to himself: That might not necessarily be true. You were the very one who said this large area used to be plagued by Undead, and if it weren't for a priest sacrificing his youngest son, those Undead wouldn't have disappeared. Moreover, ninety-nine percent of the player body raw materials used by that scum were Undead. Who knows? Perhaps those Undead didn't disappear at all, but just like the Undead over at Pengshi City, they simply found a place to hide.

Thinking of this, Shang Feifan felt tempted.

Previously, he felt that the Undead were too numerous to handle and quite annoying, but after discovering the many wonderful advantages of the Undead—such as obeying orders, being willing to work hard, and not demanding wages—he had developed a slight "the more the better" mentality.

If he could also find out the Undead hidden in this region...

And this wasn't particularly difficult for him.

Shang Feifan was far more interested in searching for Undead than in going after some adventure group.

*[There is a wearable auxiliary brain-processing calculator in here, also called an external brain chip. It can assist the user in thinking, calculating, storing, and searching, which is equivalent to giving the user a few extra supernatural abilities, such as a photographic memory, database searching, powerful calculation, and so on.]*

Shang Feifan had originally looked down upon the items in that chest. Although they were all items from the Great Prosperous Era, Earth basically had equivalents for all their functions. He really didn't find them marvelous, and there were also some jewelry and ornaments that held even less attraction for him, at best only useful to sell as antiques to auction houses on the Orc Continent.

Yet upon hearing the Orbling's reminder that there was actually such a good thing as a brain chip inside, his interest was instantly piqued.

"A wearable brain chip?"

*[Because people at that time feared built-in chips, they developed external ones; some are in-ear types, and some are scalp-attached types. Some people say this is the initial prototype of an optical brain, but unfortunately, the technological civilization of the orcs was destroyed by war before it could develop to that step.]*

"Aren't you an optical brain?"

The Orbling refused to answer this question.

Shang Feifan didn't dwell on it either; he took out that wearable brain chip.

The design of this gadget was quite childlike, looking just like a cat-shaped hairpin.

If this thing could be taken back to Earth, it should be useful, right?

Moreover, the technology shouldn't have too large a gap, and it lacked any heavy alchemical traces—it was a pure technological item, which fit just right.

"I've taken this job, but I don't guarantee the results. I can only say whatever I find out is what I'll find out," Shang Feifan said rather irresponsibly.

The village chief and the three village elders simultaneously broke into smiles: "As long as you can investigate, that's enough!"

The village chief immediately followed up: "Then we'll have to trouble Brother Norman to stay in our village for a few more days. The people from that adventure group should arrive within these couple of days. By then, you don't have to meet them face-to-face; you can just follow them in secret."

A-Dai looked up at his Shang-dad, worry in his eyes and a slightly complicated expression. But his mouth remained tightly shut from beginning to end, not wanting to affect his Shang-dad.

Shang Feifan smiled, thinking that if A-Mu were here, he would accept this task without any reward. He immediately rubbed A-Dai's square head and tucked the little cat hairpin into his hair: "Then it's settled. Consider this as the deposit."

Naturally, the village chief and the three village elders had no objections. In fact, they felt Shang Feifan had taken too little as a deposit and even wanted to stuff more into his hands.

Shang Feifan waved his hand, indicating that the deposit didn't need to be that much since everything would end up his anyway.

"If I find that that adventure group really does have problems, and the cubs you sent out are indeed suffering, what do you plan to do?" Shang Feifan asked, turning around just before heading out the door.

The village chief didn't hesitate: "Our village will send out people to find a way to bring back both the grown and underage cubs! If they still dare to come looking for trouble, we'll fight them to the death!"

Shang Feifan was just about to ask how the villagers' combat strength compared to that adventure group.

The village chief rubbed his hands with a ingratiating smile and said, "If, when our village goes to rescue people, a large swarm of Undead happens to wander into that adventure group's lair and chases those adventure group members around biting them while leaving us alone—that would be even better."

Shang Feifan: "..." So this was what you were plotting all along.

The few old orcs plus the stalwart village chief all looked at him with expectant, starry eyes.

Shang Feifan's eyes ached. He let out an "en" and said, "I curse you all to have your wishes fulfilled right this instant."

This time, it was the village chief and the elders who were left speechless. Couldn't you offer a blessing? Why did you have to curse?

第238章 来挑选幼崽

等那些人过来还需要几天时间，商非凡不想待在天残村，就靠着儿砸的瞬移能力回去了一趟莫约镇。

郎沐不在镇子里，他出去勘察地况了。

商非凡和郎沐之间有同心契约联系，又有相关炼金道具辅助，很容易就找到了郎沐。

一家三口在一起腻歪了两天，商非凡把他这几天做的事和他的打算都一五一十告诉郎沐。

“天残村的事如果你有时间有能力，能管还是管一管好。如果他们村的孩子真的无法养活也愿意送出来，那我们这边的基地建成后，可以让他们把孩子送到我们这边来。”

郎沐如果不是手头上有重要的事情做，他一定会和商非凡一起去查查那个冒险团。

商非凡摸下巴：“我的直觉告诉我，那个冒险团不是和洛人渣有关，就是和邪神信徒有关。”

郎沐没有妄加猜测，只说：“你要小心行事，如果发现情况不对，先别急着消灭他们，以防他们报复。”

商非凡了解郎沐的担心和顾忌，摆摆手：“大不了我把整个天残村都带回来。”

郎沐嘴唇弯了弯。老商并没有说大话，他们现在也算是有能力，更有财力和足够的粮食能养活这么多人。

只要黑水荒原没有岩浆爆发的威胁，凭借他的自然亲和力和自然类魔法，他明年就能让黑水荒原多出大片能耕种的土地。

到时候别说养万把口人，就是几十万也不是问题。

商非凡把来争宠的阿呆拨到一边，自己往郎沐大腿上一躺，霸占了位子。

郎沐笑，手指插-入雄兽的头发顺了顺，随口说：“另外，洛伦米尔顿吃了那么一个大亏，不可能就这么算了，他现在不出来，肯定是在谋划对他更有利的事情。”

商非凡不喜欢郎沐对洛人渣那颇为了解的口吻，揣着满肚子的酸味说：“那你觉得他是在谋划什么事情？召唤更多玩家？搞强制召唤术？”

郎沐缓缓摇头，眼里闪过一丝自嘲：“我想那人应该会故技重施，再寻找另一个傻瓜。”

商非凡立刻反应过来：“你是说那个人渣打算再找一个气运之子？”

光球冒出来：【恭喜！】

商非凡一巴掌把光球撩旁边，又把光球捞回来：“你是想说我是兽人大陆的最新气运之子？”

光球：【是。不过洛伦米尔顿应该找不到你身上，因为你不是这个世界的土著，更不是兽人大陆的原生生命。】

“就算我现在用的身体是兽人大陆的材料？”

【那不一样，你的生命来源和孕育方式和正常兽人大陆的生命不一样。】

“那他会再次找到郎沐头上吗？”

【郎沐的气运值并没有恢复。】

商非凡放心了……还不能放心，他肯定不能让洛伦米尔顿再增加气运值，毕竟一个人再厉害也没办法和大势和幸运做斗争。

就是那种你费尽千辛万苦才达成某件事，甚至还不一定做得到，结果对方靠着好运就轻松做到了。

和这种人做对手，真的能把自己气死。

不过好在光球立马告知两人：【商非凡虽然不是兽人大陆的气运之子，但他受到了天河星意识的青睐，甚至是被委托。当我选中商非凡，就表示天河星意识也选中了他。】

商非凡若有所思：“所以接下来就是一场气运之争了对么？”

【对！你们必须抢在洛伦米尔顿给自己增加气运之前把他彻底消灭，不能给他丝毫喘息的可能性。】

“那你倒是把他的藏身地点标出来给我啊。”商非凡没好气地说。

光球转了几圈，似乎下了某个决定，给商非凡发布了一个新任务。

【接受天残村村长的委托，查清楚冒险团队带走幼崽训练和培养一事的真相。完成后奖励天眼系统的完全使用权。】

四天后，天残谷第一场初雪飘落。

就在洋洋洒洒的飞雪中，天残谷谷口有村人传信，那个冒险团队的人来了。

村民把三个冒险者带入村中。

三个身材不一的兽人有着统一的神情，那就是对这个天残村庄的不屑，眼神扫过天残村民时都带着一种掩饰都掩饰不了的高高在上。

为首的兽人有着食肉种族的锐利五官，自称“苍牙”。他的姿态看似温和，嘴角始终挂着恰到好处的微笑，但那双琥珀色的竖瞳看村民幼崽时却冰冷得像是蛇类在打量猎物。

另外两名两人从他们的耳朵上看不出他们的种族，只一胖一瘦像是哼哈二将一样站在苍牙身后，眼神时不时扫过村中建筑和村民，像是在盘算着什么。

村长迎上前来。

苍牙一挥手：“客气话就别多说了，今年的幼崽准备好了吗？”

村长听着这话特别不是味，这个冒险者说话的口气就不像是领养孩童，更像是在挑拣牲口。

但天残村是求着人的一方，他们只能假装没听懂，还要陪着笑脸说：“都准备好了。”

村长回头招招手。

几位村老抱着、牵着、领着十来个孩子走到三名冒险者面前。

苍牙皱眉：“今年人数怎么这么少？”

村长挤出笑容：“今年被扔到我们村的幼崽就不多。”

苍牙眼中闪过一丝不满，口中却温和地说：“那么你们村有村民想要把幼崽送给我们培养吗？我们冒险团这几年发展得很不错，需要很多人手。比起从外招成年兽人进团队，不如从小培养更忠心也更适合。我们团对自己培养出来的成员各种福利待遇也很优厚。如果你们村有幼崽想要报名参加，我们每年可以帮他们送薪酬回来，甚至可以把薪酬直接换成你们最需要的粮食和生活物资。”

村长心脏一颤，心想这帮家伙果然不满足于年年下降的幼崽数量，想要“强抢”了。

如果没有商非凡，他和村人还要忧愁一番要如何解决对方的“好意”。

如今有了商非凡，那他只管拖延时间就是。

于是，村长就一脸激动地说：“真的吗？还有这样的大好事？那真是太好了。不过这事重大，我还得和村老以及村民们商量。等明年……”

“也不用等明年。”苍牙打断村长，“你现在就去问问你们村民的意思，如果有意把幼崽送到我们冒险团进行培养的，我们不但不会收取他的培养费，还会给一笔安家费。”

苍牙对身边胖兽人使了个眼色。

那胖兽人立刻笑眯眯地拿出一个口袋，打开，亮给村长看：“这就是我们的安家费，虫粉。这批虫粉可不是陈货，而是今年才制成的新粉，味道可香，营养也丰富，摊饼做糊糊蒸着吃都可以。”

就隐身站在一边的商非凡还探头往袋子里看了看。

一袋子灰色粉末，看起来特别眼熟。这不是他曾经在那条深渊附近的强盗窝里发现的主要粮食之一吗？

去了王城后他很少再见到有人吃这种虫粉，差点忘了这种虫粉才是兽人大陆底层人士最常食用的粮食之一。

苍牙补充：“如果你们的幼崽被挑中，一人可以得二十斤虫粉的安家费。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 238: Coming to Select Cubs

It would still take a few days for those people to arrive. Not wanting to stay in Defective Village, Shang Feifan relied on his son's teleportation ability to make a trip back to Moyue Town.

Lang Mu wasn't in the town; he had gone out to survey the terrain.

Shang Feifan and Lang Mu were bound by a heartbeat pact and aided by related alchemical items, making it very easy to locate Lang Mu.

The family of three acted all affectionate and clingy together for two days, during which Shang Feifan told Lang Mu everything about what he had been doing over the past few days and his plans.

"If you have the time and ability regarding the matter in Defective Village, it's best to manage it if you can. If the children in their village truly cannot be raised and they are willing to send them out, once our base here is built, we can have them send the children over to our side."

If Lang Mu didn't have important matters on his hands, he definitely would have gone with Shang Feifan to check out that adventure group.

Shang Feifan rubbed his chin: "My intuition tells me that adventure group is either related to Loren the Scum or to the Cult of the Evil God."

Lang Mu didn't make wild guesses and merely said, "You must act with caution. If you find the situation is amiss, don't rush to eliminate them, just in case they retaliate."

Understanding Lang Mu's worries and misgivings, Shang Feifan waved a hand: "At worst, I'll just bring the entire Defective Village back."

The corners of Lang Mu's lips curved upward. Old Shang wasn't boasting; they currently had the ability, as well as the financial resources and sufficient food to support so many people.

As long as the Black Water Wasteland wasn't threatened by volcanic eruptions, relying on his natural affinity and nature-type magic, he could make large tracts of land in the Black Water Wasteland arable by next year.

When that time came, to say nothing of supporting ten thousand people, even several hundred thousand wouldn't be a problem.

Shang Feifan pushed aside A-Dai, who had come over to vie for favor, stretched out, and lay down right across Lang Mu's thighs, usurping the spot.

Lang Mu smiled, threaded his fingers through the male orc's hair to smooth it down, and said casually, "Besides, after taking such a huge loss, it's impossible for Loren Milton to just let it go. Since he isn't showing himself now, he must be plotting something even more advantageous to himself."

Shang Feifan disliked the rather knowledgeable tone Lang Mu used when speaking of Loren the Scum, and filled with a belly full of sour jealousy, he muttered, "Then what do you think he's plotting? Summoning more players? Performing some kind of forced summoning spell?"

Lang Mu slowly shook his head, a trace of self-mockery flashing in his eyes: "I imagine that fellow will probably use the same old trick and go search for another fool."

Shang Feifan instantly reacted: "You're meaning that scum plans to find another Child of Fate?"

The Orbling popped out: *[Congratulations!]*

Shang Feifan swatted the Orbling aside with a slap, then fished it back: "Are you trying to say I'm the newest Child of Fate of the Orc Continent?"

The Orbling: *[Yes. However, Loren Milton shouldn't be able to trace it to you, because you aren't a native of this world, let even an indigenous lifeform of the Orc Continent.]*

"Even though the body I'm using right now is made of materials from the Orc Continent?"

*[That's different. Your life origin and method of conception are unlike normal lifeforms of the Orc Continent.]*

"Then will he find Lang Mu's head again?"

*[Lang Mu's Fate Value has not recovered.]*

Shang Feifan felt relieved... though he couldn't completely relax yet. He definitely couldn't let Loren Milton increase his Fate Value again; after all, no matter how formidable a person was, they could never fight against the general trend and sheer luck.

It was that infuriating feeling where you exhausted every ounce of hardship to accomplish something—or perhaps couldn't even manage it—while the other party easily achieved it purely by relying on good luck.

Being opponents with such a person could genuinely make one die of anger.

Fortunately, the Orbling immediately informed the two of them: *[Although Shang Feifan is not the Child of Fate of the Orc Continent, he has been favored by the consciousness of the River of Heaven, and even entrusted by it. The moment I chose Shang Feifan, it meant the consciousness of the River of Heaven chose him as well.]*

Shang Feifan thought deeply: "So what comes next is a battle of fate, right?"

*[Correct! You must completely eliminate Loren Milton before he can increase his fate for himself, without giving him the slightest possibility of a breathing space.]*

"Then you might as well mark out his hiding spot for me," Shang Feifan said ungraciously.

The Orbling spun around a few times, seemingly making some sort of decision, and issued a new quest to Shang Feifan.

*[Accept the commission of the Defective Village chief and investigate the truth behind the adventure group taking away cubs for training and cultivation. Upon completion, reward full usage rights of the Heavenly Eye System.]*

Four days later, the first early snow of Defective Valley drifted down.

Amidst the swirling, scattered snowflakes, a villager sent word from the valley entrance: the people from that adventure group had arrived.

The villagers brought the three adventurers into the village.

The three orcs of varying builds shared a unified expression: utter disdain for this Defective village. Whenever their gazes swept over the Defective villagers, they all carried an unmaskable sense of condescension.

The leading orc possessed the sharp facial features of a carnivorous race and called himself "Cang Ya". His posture seemed gentle, and an appropriate smile hung at the corners of his mouth the entire time, yet those amber slit-pupils looked upon the village cubs with the icy gaze of a serpent sizing up its prey.

As for the other two, their race couldn't be determined from their ears; one fat and one thin, they stood behind Cang Ya like guardian deities, their eyes sweeping over the village's buildings and villagers from time to time as if calculating something.

The village chief hurried forward to welcome them.

Cang Ya waved a hand: "Let's dispense with the polite pleasantries. Are this year's cubs ready?"

Hearing this phrasing, the village chief found it particularly grating; the tone with which this adventurer spoke did not sound like someone adopting children, but rather like someone picking out livestock.

However, Defective Village was the party begging for favors, so they could only pretend not to understand and force a smile. "They're all ready."

The village chief turned back and beckoned.

Several village elders carried, pulled, and led a dozen or so children over to the three adventurers.

Cang Ya frowned: "Why is the number of people so small this year?"

The village chief squeezed out a smile: "There weren't many cubs abandoned and thrown to our village this year."

A trace of dissatisfaction flashed in Cang Ya's eyes, but his voice remained gentle as he said, "Then do any villagers in your village want to send their cubs to us for cultivation? Our adventure group has developed quite well these past few years and needs a lot of manpower. Cultivating them from a young age makes them more loyal and suitable compared to recruiting adult orcs from outside. Our group also offers generous welfare and benefits for the members we cultivate ourselves. If any cubs in your village want to sign up and participate, we can help send their salary back every year, and can even convert the salary directly into the food and living supplies you need most."

The village chief's heart gave a jolt, thinking to himself that these fellows were indeed unsatisfied with the year-by-year declining number of cubs and intended to resort to "forced seizure."

If not for Shang Feifan, he and the villagers would have had to worry about how to resolve the other party's "kind intentions."

Now that they had Shang Feifan, all he needed to do was stall for time.

Thus, the village chief said with an excited expression: "Is that true? Such a great and wonderful thing? That's truly wonderful. However, this is a major matter, and I still need to discuss it with the village elders and the villagers. We can wait until next year..."

"There's no need to wait until next year either," Cang Ya interrupted the village chief. "Go ask your villagers for their opinions right now. If anyone intends to send their cubs to our adventure group for training, not only will we waive the training fee, but we'll also give a settlement allowance."

Cang Ya gave a look to the fat orc beside him.

The fat orc immediately smiled, took out a pouch, opened it, and showed it to the village chief: "This is our settlement allowance—insect powder. This batch of insect powder isn't old stock; it's newly made powder from this year. It smells exceptionally fragrant and is rich in nutrients. You can make pancakes, porridge, or steam it to eat."

Shang Feifan, who was standing invisible right beside them, even poked his head over to take a look inside the bag.

A bag of gray powder, looking particularly familiar. Wasn't this one of the primary food staples he had once discovered in that bandit lair near the abyss?

After going to the royal city, he rarely saw anyone eating this kind of insect powder anymore, almost forgetting that this insect powder was one of the most frequently consumed foods for the people at the bottom of the Orc Continent.

Cang Ya added: "If your cubs are chosen, each person can get twenty catties of insect powder as a settlement allowance."

chunks.chineseText:
胖兽人：“我们的车子就在谷外，不用担心我们带的虫粉不够。我们可不止巡回你们这一个村子。”

言下之意，他们可以挑拣的幼崽很多，不差你们村这几个。

一般苦于冬季粮食不够的贫穷村落人听到这话，心里下意识就会焦急起来，原本有所犹豫的也会断然下决定。

但天残村的村民已经怀疑这个冒险团队，自然不会为了一点粮食就把自家孩子送去受苦受罪。

可就这么拒绝也不好，毕竟他们村是这么穷，就因为没有足够粮食才养不活这么多被抛弃的外来幼崽，如果他们这时不动心，一定会让这三兽人怀疑。

村长一狠心，当即就高兴说：“我去找人，三位贵客还请稍等。”

村长转头去找人了。

村民们不喜欢这种场合，以前还会看看热闹，后来感觉这个冒险团队不对劲，他们就没有看热闹的热情了，每次来看，总觉得像是在亲手送那些孤儿幼崽去受罪乃至送死。

三位村老和几个成年村民守着十几个幼崽站在那里等待。

苍牙三人也不耐烦光站在那里，就开始在十几个幼崽中挑选起来。

主要挑选的人就是苍牙，另外两人只负责掠阵。

十几个衣衫破旧的天残孤儿排成一列，他们瘦弱的身体在飞雪中冻得微微发抖，眼里却闪烁着渴望的光。

这些幼崽有一半都无法变身，维持着纯兽的状态。纯兽的幼崽身上没有衣服，只有他们的皮毛鳞甲，他们虽然是纯兽状态，但有几个也能看出明显的残缺。

另外一半能变成人形的也是身体上各有残缺。有两个还维持着半兽半人的模样，一个长着鼠头和鼠类四肢，躯干却是人形。另外一个上肢是鱼鳍，露出来的肌肤和脸部全是鳞片，像是两栖生物。

这些幼崽年龄不一，最小的还在襁褓中，最大的也不过七八岁。

七八岁的幼崽有的是前面挑选后剩下来的，有的是最近一年才被扔到谷口附近。

之所以七八岁还会被遗弃，不过是家里想要看看变身的可能性，等了七八年也没等到，觉得幼崽不可能再变身成兽人，留着也只会慢慢变成野兽，就扔了。

通常两岁以后还被遗弃的幼崽绝大多数都是纯兽状态。

如果能被选上，是不是就能吃饱饭了？一个鹿族的小男孩攥紧了衣角，他的左腿比右腿短了一截，鹿角也没有发育，眼睛却亮得惊人。

他想离开这里，他是今年刚被扔来的，他知道自己不是这个村子的孩子，也无法融入这个村庄，他想要离开，哪怕吃点苦，只要能吃饱肚子，能让他平安长大，他愿意去接受所谓的训练和培养。

虽然村里老人在这之前就跟他们所有幼崽都说过，那些被带走的孤儿，再也没回来过，他们也不知道那些离开村子被带走的幼崽过得到底怎么样。

旁边的兔耳少女浑身发抖，她的右眼蒙着白翳，左耳只剩半截，嘴巴还是三瓣唇。

“不要选我……不要选我……”她在心里默念，可当其中一名兽人扫视过来时，她又下意识挺直了腰，生怕显得不够精神。

另一个半蛇少女偷偷抬头看向苍牙。就见那高大兽人的手指正轻柔地抬起一个孩子的下巴，像是在检查什么。

苍牙的动作很温柔，可她却莫名打了个寒颤。

真的能离开这里吗？这个冒险团队真的愿意要他们，还愿意给他们吃饱？我这样的，他们是不是不会要？一个没有胳膊只长了两个小翅膀的男孩攥紧拳头，光着的脚趾蜷曲，尖锐的趾甲扎入已经覆盖了薄薄一层雪的硬土中。

他不想再饿肚子，不想再被其他村子的小孩嘲笑没胳膊没手。可他又害怕出去后的遭遇更惨——他是在村里长大的，有个老兽人收-养了他，但今年对方身体不行了，家里分到的粮食也不多，他是主动自己走出来的，他想把剩下的粮食都留给老兽人。

商非凡就在旁边看着苍牙跟挑拣牲口一样挑拣那些孤儿。

从对方选出来的人员来看，似乎并不看中幼崽是否健康、是否可爱美丽、以及残缺度更少之类。

几个被挑选出来的幼崽又紧张又兴奋。

苍牙还选了一个才出生不到三个多月的奶崽和一个走路还不稳的五岁纯兽幼崽。

不说那个才三个多月的奶崽，那个五岁的纯兽幼崽一看就是骨骼有问题，很可能有软骨症之类的先天病症。

这种病症很难治疗，至少对于普通兽人来说。

商非凡在游戏商城里搜索了一下，发现了可以治疗软骨病的药剂。

该药剂需要两百个贡献点。这笔贡献点对于现在的他来说不算贵，但想到除了主线任务和奇遇任务，他做其他任务极少有能一次性拿到上百的贡献点数，就可以知道这种药剂如果放到兽人市场上得卖多贵。

所以这个冒险团队为什么要选一个患有软骨症的幼崽，还挑选了还在喝奶中的奶崽？

他们挑选预备队员的标准到底是什么？

商非凡仔细打量苍牙。

苍牙似乎有所感知，转头看了看。没发现什么异样，又继续伸手拍拍摸摸那些任他挑选的幼崽。

商非凡的目光落到了苍牙的右手上。

苍牙的右手中指戴着一枚戒指，戒面比较长，呈长方形。

商非凡注意到，每当苍牙的手碰触到幼崽，那枚戒指的戒面就会微微变色。

哦，不是变色，是戒面里面有液体一样的东西，像气温柱里的水银一样会上升和降落。

苍牙选择幼崽就是根据戒面的液体柱反应。

只要测试那个幼崽时液体柱超过中段，苍牙就会给幼崽打上合格的标签，让该幼崽站到另一边。

大约今年可供挑选的人数太少，有一个勉强液体柱达到戒面中间位置的幼崽最后也被苍牙挑拣出来。

“只有四个？”胖兽人眉头紧皱，小声跟同伴说：“这也太少了。”

“等会儿再去其他村子看看，如果能凑到十个最好。”瘦兽人也小声说。

苍牙转头，胖瘦两个兽人立刻闭嘴。

苍牙心情显然不太好。

他们确实还有其他村落可以去，但那些村子的兽人对自己的幼崽都非常看重，不是实在过不下去，绝不会把自己的幼崽交出去。

实际上兽人大陆从古至今都十分重视幼崽，也只有天残幼崽才会被弃养。

其实新生纪以来，就算是天残幼崽，能狠心抛弃的也不多了。

就算是完全不能变身的纯兽，家里人也宁愿养着，直到对方彻底失去人性才会驱赶到荒野。

天残村已经是他们幼崽来源最多也最安全的地方。

他们也可以满大陆的抢夺、盗窃和拐带幼崽，他们也确实在这么做。但因为满大陆兽人对幼崽的极度重视，他们成功的几率并不高，风险和代价还特别大。

这也是上面特别看重各地天残村落的缘故。

反正上面也不是看重幼崽的身体条件，而是另有一套选拔标准。
chunks.englishText:
"Our carts are right outside the valley, so you don't need to worry about us lacking insect powder. We aren't just touring your village alone."

The subtext was clear: they had plenty of other children to choose from, and they weren't desperate for the few kids in this village.

Normally, impoverished villagers plagued by winter food shortages would instantly panic upon hearing this. Even those who had hesitations would make a resolute decision on the spot.

However, the villagers of the Village of the Flawed were already suspicious of this adventuring party. Naturally, they wouldn't send their own children off to suffer and endure hardship just for a little bit of food.

Yet, outright refusal wouldn't do either. After all, their village was extremely poor, and it was precisely because of insufficient food that they couldn't feed so many abandoned foreign children. If they showed no interest at all, it would definitely arouse suspicion among the three beastmen.

Steeling his heart, the village chief immediately beamed and said, "I'll go find some people. Please wait a moment, three esteemed guests."

The village chief turned and went to round up the children.

The villagers disliked such occasions. In the past, they might have come out to watch the excitement, but ever since they sensed that something was amiss with this adventuring party, they had lost all enthusiasm for watching. Every time they came to watch, it always felt like they were personally sending those orphaned children off to suffer or even face death.

The three village elders and several adult villagers stood guard by a dozen or so children, waiting.

Cang Ya and his two companions were too impatient to just stand there, so they began picking through the dozen-plus youngsters.

Cang Ya was the one doing the main selecting, while the other two merely stood guard and observed.

The dozen-odd ragged orphans of the flawed lineage stood in a row, their emaciated bodies trembling slightly in the drifting snow, though their eyes flickered with a desperate yearning.

Half of these children were unable to transform, remaining trapped in their pure-beast states. The pure-beast cubs wore no clothes, only their fur, pelts, or scales. Even in their pure-beast forms, several of them bore obvious deformities.

The other half, who could transform into human shapes, likewise suffered from various physical impairments. Two of them still maintained a half-beast, half-human appearance: one had a rat's head and rat-like limbs, but a human torso; another had upper limbs shaped like fish fins, with exposed skin and a face entirely covered in scales, resembling an amphibian.

These children varied in age; the youngest was still in swaddling clothes, while the oldest was no more than seven or eight years old.

Some of the seven- or eight-year-old children were leftovers from previous selections, while others had been dumped near the valley entrance within the past year.

The only reason children of seven or eight were still abandoned was that their families had wanted to test the possibility of transformation. After waiting seven or eight years with no results, believing that the children would never be able to transform into beastmen and would only slowly degenerate into wild beasts if kept, they threw them away.

As a rule, the overwhelming majority of children abandoned after the age of two were stuck in their pure-beast states.

*If I get chosen, will I finally get to eat my fill?* A young Deer-clan boy clenched the hem of his ragged garment. His left leg was a notch shorter than his right, and his antlers had failed to develop, yet his eyes burned with an astonishing brilliance.

He wanted to leave this place. He had only been dumped here this year. He knew he wasn't a child of this village and could never integrate into it. He wanted to leave; even if he had to suffer a little bit, as long as he could fill his belly and grow up safely, he was willing to accept whatever training and nurturing they spoke of.

Although the village elders had warned all the children beforehand that those orphans who were taken away had never returned once, and nobody knew what kind of life those departed children were living outside...

Beside him, a rabbit-eared girl was trembling all over. Her right eye was clouded with a cataract, her left ear was missing the top half, and her mouth retained a hare-lip.

*Don't pick me... Don't pick me...* she chanted inwardly. Yet when one of the beastmen swept a glance her way, she instinctively straightened her back, terrified of looking insufficiently spirited.

Another half-snake girl secretly raised her gaze to look at Cang Ya. She saw the tall beastman's fingers gently lifting a child's chin, as if inspecting something.

Cang Ya's movements were very gentle, yet for some reason, she shivered.

*Can we really leave this place? Does this adventuring party really want us, and are they really willing to feed us? Won't they want someone like me?* A boy lacking arms and possessing only a pair of tiny wings clenched his fists, his bare toes curling, sharp talons digging into the hard soil which was already covered by a thin layer of snow.

He didn't want to starve anymore, nor did he want to be mocked by the children of other villages for lacking arms and hands. Yet he was also terrified that what awaited him outside would be even more brutal—he had grown up in the village; an old beastman had adopted him, but this year the old man's health had failed, and the household's grain allocation was meager. He had walked out of his own accord, wanting to leave all the remaining food for the old man.

Shang Feifan watched from the side as Cang Ya picked through the orphans just as one would inspect livestock.

Judging from the individuals the man selected, it seemed he didn't place much value on whether the children were healthy, cute, beautiful, or possessed fewer physical deformities.

The few picked-out children were both nervous and excited.

Cang Ya even selected a nursing infant less than three months old and a five-year-old pure-beast toddler who was unsteady on his feet.

Putting aside the three-month-old nursing baby, that five-year-old pure-beast toddler clearly had skeletal issues, very likely a congenital disease like rickets.

Such a condition was extremely difficult to treat, at least for ordinary beastmen.

Shang Feifan searched the in-game mall and discovered a potion capable of curing rickets.

The potion cost two hundred contribution points. This amount of contribution points wasn't too expensive for him right now, but considering that aside from main quests and encounter quests, he rarely earned hundreds of contribution points at once from other tasks, it was easy to deduce just how exorbitantly expensive such a potion would be if sold on the beastman market.

So why would this adventuring party choose a child afflicted with rickets, and even pick a nursing baby?

What on earth was their standard for selecting reserve members?

Shang Feifan carefully sized up Cang Ya.

Cang Ya seemed to sense something, turning his head to look around. Finding nothing out of the ordinary, he continued reaching out to pat and touch the children left to his picking.

Shang Feifan's gaze landed on Cang Ya's right hand.

On Cang Ya's right middle finger was a ring. The gemstone bezel was quite long and rectangular.

Shang Feifan noticed that every time Cang Ya's hand touched a child, the surface of the ring's bezel would subtly change color.

Ah, it wasn't changing color; rather, there was a liquid-like substance inside the bezel, which rose and fell just like the mercury in a thermometer.

Cang Ya's selection of the children was based on the reaction of this liquid column inside the bezel.

Whenever a child was tested and the liquid column surpassed the halfway mark, Cang Ya would slap a passing grade label on that child and instruct them to step to the other side.

Perhaps because the number of available candidates this year was too small, one child whose liquid column barely reached the middle of the bezel was ultimately picked out by Cang Ya as well.

"Only four?" The fat beastman frowned deeply, whispering to his companion, "This is way too few."

"We'll check out the other villages later. If we can scrape together ten, that'd be best," the thin beastman also muttered softly.

Cang Ya turned his head, and the fat and thin beastmen instantly clamped their mouths shut.

Cang Ya's mood was clearly less than stellar.

It was true that they still had other villages to visit, but the beastmen in those villages held their own offspring in extremely high regard; unless they were truly at death's door, they would never hand over their children.

In fact, since ancient times, the Beastman Continent had attached immense importance to their young. Only flawed-lineage children would ever be abandoned.

Even since the dawning of the New Era, there weren't many left who could harden their hearts to abandon even flawed children.

Even for pure beasts who couldn't transform at all, their families would rather raise them until the day they completely lost their humanity before driving them out into the wilderness.

The Village of the Flawed was already the place with the largest and safest source of children for them.

Of course, they could also pillage, steal, and abduct children from all over the continent, and indeed they were doing precisely that. But due to the extreme importance the continent's beastmen placed on their young, their success rate was not high, and the risks and costs were exceptionally steep.

This was precisely why the higher-ups placed such special importance on the flawed-lineage villages scattered everywhere.

Anyway, the higher-ups weren't looking at the children's physical conditions anyway; they had a completely different set of selection criteria.

chunks.chineseText:
苍牙作为选拔人，到如今都还没有摸清这个选拔标准是什么，只能凭借戴着的戒指来判断。

他也不敢多问。他可不想和那些带回去的幼崽一样，哪天就莫名消失了。

周围有少数村民围观，眼神复杂。

几个年长的雌性兽人交头接耳，目光时不时瞥向那些孩子，又迅速移开，像是不忍，又像是羞愧。

年轻的雄性们站在外围，表情阴晴不定——他们知道村里养不起太多孩子，可看着这些孩子被带走，还是前途未知的那种，他们又觉得特别打脸。

如果他们能再强大一些，如果他们能更有本事，是不是就能养活更多孩子？

甚至能让全天下的天残幼崽都能在他们天残谷吃饱穿暖幸福开心的生活？

这些年轻的雄性兽人想到了那些古怪兽人跟他们说的话，他们说他们就是为了改变天残兽人的处境而来，想要团结全天下所有天残兽人的力量。

其实那些兽人虽然说话怪了点、举动诡异了一点，但大多数人都还……挺好的。

那么大一个营地就在他们村落附近，要说村民完全和玩家们没有往来，那就不可能。

不少年轻兽人和幼崽其实都暗中和玩家们有了来往，不少幼崽还无师自通学会了去玩家营地卖萌讨食。

如果不是村老和村长再三警告他们，让他们不要和那些古怪兽人多来往多接触，可能不少年轻村民已经和玩家们打成一片。

村长回来了，他带来了三个孩子。

村老和村民看到三个幼崽的面容，不少人都变了颜色，有些不会掩饰的直接就长大了嘴巴。

村长带了他的次子和幼子，以及阿呆。

村长妻子跟了出来，脸色凄苦。

她一点都不想自己的孩子跟那些冒险团成员走，哪怕只是暂时。

做母亲的都害怕自家孩子会出事，更何况是这么冒险的卧底行为。

但村长回去把情况和村民们一说明，阿呆第一个跳了出来，还说就他一个就可以，带上其他人都是累赘。

村长的长子已经接近成年，没办法再跟冒险团成员走——他们不喜欢大孩子，最喜欢十二三岁以下的，越小越好。

村长的另外两个孩子被阿呆一刺激，主动跳出来跟父母说，他们愿意去冒险。

村长原本就无意让其他村民的孩子跟着冒险，他回来前就已经决定让自己的次子跟着跑一趟。

没想到他家老三也要去，还吵着闹着要去。

其他幼崽一看村里幼崽老大们都主动去了，也闹腾起来，一个个胆子大的像是能捅破天。

这些不知轻重的幼崽都被自家父母爷奶给揍了。

最终村长拍板决定，就带他的两个孩子和阿呆去充数。

三个自愿去参加培养的，已经不少了。

阿呆看看自己油光水滑的皮毛，再看看村里幼崽，当即跳到水桶里沾上水，又跳出来在地上来回打了几个滚，还往草堆里钻了一通，等再出来，就变成一个脏兮兮满身泥和野草的小野崽子。

村长竖起大拇指。这小阿呆果然不呆！

苍牙三人果然对村长只送来三个幼崽没有表达任何不满，还夸奖了村长做的对、有前瞻性。

苍牙给村长两个孩子以及阿呆都测了测。

村长两个孩子都没能让液体柱超过戒面中间位置，但苍牙决定还是把这两个小崽子带上。

当苍牙测到阿呆时，那戒面中的液体柱唰地一下都快顶到满格。

苍牙睁大眼睛，狂喜。

多少年了！他还是第一次遇到接近满格的幼崽！

上次另外一支队伍的领头人带回来一个液体柱达到三分之二的，都获得了极为丰厚的奖励。

那他这个快要满格的，岂不是能让他狠狠发一笔大财？也许直接就能提拔他跃一个大级别。

苍牙激动无比，脸上血色都多了不少。

为了不让村长等人看出异样，苍牙暗中连续深呼吸几次，终于把兴奋之情给勉强压下。

“你叫什么名字？”苍牙特别和蔼可亲地问阿呆。

阿呆呆头呆脑地仰头看着苍牙，“啊？”

村长连忙在一边解释：“阁下莫怪，这孩子有点呆，反应比较慢，但不是真的傻子，他名字就叫阿呆。”

苍牙笑起来：呆子才好啊，呆子才会乖乖听话，不会瞎折腾。

苍牙弯腰想要把阿呆抱起来。

阿呆一个蹦跶，躲到一边。

村长又帮忙解释：“阿呆这孩子比较认生，不怎么喜欢接触人。不过您有什么事情跟他说，他能听懂。”

苍牙心里其实也嫌弃阿呆身上脏兮兮的，见小幼崽不肯被抱，他还乐得不用弄脏衣服，就只是对阿呆和几个被选中的幼崽说：“跟我们走吧。你们以后就会过上好日子，再也不用担心吃不饱。”

村长和村老把苍牙一行人和被选中的幼崽一直送到谷口外。

商非凡一路跟随。

他发现当苍牙他们经过谷口出的林子时，林子里的生物像是全都消失了，那一只只性格各异的巨虫全都不见了踪影。

苍牙几个也没察觉半点异样，走到谷口，看到他们留在谷口外的人手，转身就对村长等人告辞。

“你们这次也要跟我们去看看吗？如果想去，那就等我们回来时接你们。到时会给你们发信号。”胖兽人说。

村长赔笑：“那就麻烦诸位了。”

苍牙忽然问：“之前我们过来时经过一座废墟，看到一座塌掉的城堡，还有一些房屋和帐篷。那里原本不是有很多人吗？现在这些人都去了哪里？那里发生了什么事？”

村长露出恐惧又茫然的神色，喏喏说：“我们也不知道那个小城池发生了什么事，就好像一夜之间，里面的人都消失了。那天晚上，我们都听到了轰轰的炮响声，但我们不敢出来查看，等第二天天亮再过来，就发现那里已经空了。”

村老也一脸后怕地说：“大概是被强盗偷袭了吧。这一片的强盗很厉害，我早就跟他们说过，他们那一带没有地险可守，用来做城池太危险了。可那些人也不听我们这些老头老太的。”

苍牙连续问了几个问题，可村长和村老全都一问三不知。

苍牙也不觉得这穷得养不活多余孩子的天残村能知道什么紧要事，用答应的六十斤虫粉就把他们打发了。

六十斤虫粉都不够一麻袋的，村长单手提起来就回村了。

商非凡则跳上了苍牙一行人的车辆。
chunks.englishText:
As the person in charge of selection, Cang Ya still hadn't figured out what these selection criteria actually were, and could only judge by the ring on his finger.

He didn't dare ask too many questions either. He had no wish to end up like those children brought back, who mysteriously vanished one fine day.

A small number of villagers watched from the sidelines with complex gazes.

A few elderly female beastmen whispered among themselves, their gazes occasionally darting toward those children before swiftly shifting away, looking as though they felt both unbearable pity and profound shame.

The young males stood on the outer perimeter, their expressions shifting between light and shadow—they knew the village couldn't afford to raise too many children, yet seeing these kids taken away—and to an unknown fate at that—still felt like a heavy slap to their faces.

If they could be a bit stronger, if they could have more capability, would they be able to raise more children?

Could they even let all the flawed-lineage children across the entire world live full, warm, happy, and joyful lives right here in their Valley of the Flawed?

These young male beastmen thought of what those eccentric beastmen had said to them. They said they had come precisely to change the plight of the flawed beastmen, and wanted to unite the strength of all flawed beastmen under heaven.

Actually, even though those beastmen spoke a bit strangely and behaved rather bizarrely, most of them were... pretty good.

With such a massive camp located right near their village, it was impossible for the villagers to have no interaction with the players whatsoever.

Quite a few young beastmen and children had actually established secret contacts with the players, and many youngsters had even figured out on their own how to go to the player camp to act cute and beg for food.

Had it not been for the repeated warnings of the village elders and the chief, telling them not to overly mingle or contact those eccentric beastmen, many young villagers would likely have already become fast friends with the players.

The village chief returned, bringing three children with him.

When the village elders and villagers saw the faces of the three children, the expressions of many changed dramatically. Some who were poor at hiding their feelings dropped their jaws wide open.

The village chief had brought his second son, his youngest son, and Ah Dai.

The village chief's wife followed behind them, her face filled with bitter sorrow.

She didn't want her children to go off with those members of the adventuring party at all, even if it was only temporary.

Any mother would fear for her children's safety, let alone in such a risky undercover operation.

Yet when the village chief went back and explained the situation to the villagers, Ah Dai was the first to jump up, declaring that he alone was enough and that bringing anyone else would just be dead weight.

The village chief's eldest son was approaching adulthood and couldn't go along with the adventuring party—they disliked older children and preferred those under twelve or thirteen, the younger the better.

Stung by Ah Dai's provocation, the village chief's other two children proactively stepped forward and told their parents that they were willing to go on the adventure.

The village chief had never intended to let other villagers' children follow this dangerous venture in the first place; before coming back, he had already decided to let his second son make the trip.

He hadn't expected his third son to want to go as well, making a great fuss and clamoring to join.

When the other children saw that the village's top kids had all volunteered, they started kicking up a fuss too, acting so daring it seemed as though they could pierce the vault of heaven.

These uncomprehending youngsters were promptly thrashed by their respective parents and grandparents.

In the end, the village chief pounded his fist to finalize the decision: he would take his two children and Ah Dai to make up the numbers.

Three volunteers participating in the training was already quite a few.

Ah Dai looked at his own slick, glossy fur, then looked at the village kids. He immediately jumped into a water bucket to get wet, hopped out, rolled back and forth in the dirt several times, and even burrowed through a pile of hay. When he emerged again, he had transformed into a filthy little wild beast caked in mud and weeds.

The village chief gave him a thumbs-up. This little Ah Dai really wasn't dumb at all!

True to form, Cang Ya and his two companions expressed zero dissatisfaction over the village chief bringing only three children, even praising the village chief for doing the right thing and showing great foresight.

Cang Ya tested the village chief's two children as well as Ah Dai.

Neither of the village chief's children managed to make the liquid column surpass the middle of the bezel, but Cang Ya decided to bring these two little ones along anyway.

When Cang Ya tested Ah Dai, the liquid column inside the bezel surged up in a flash, nearly hitting the absolute top.

Cang Ya's eyes widened in wild, ecstatic joy.

How many years had it been?! This was his very first time encountering a child close to maxing out the gauge!

Last time, the leader of another team brought back a child whose liquid column reached two-thirds, and they had received extraordinarily generous rewards.

With this one nearly hitting the top, wouldn't that allow him to rake in a massive fortune? Perhaps it would even directly promote him by a major rank!

Cang Ya was violently excited, the color in his face surging richly.

To avoid letting the village chief and the others notice anything amiss, Cang Ya secretly took several continuous, deep breaths, finally managing to forcefully suppress his excitement.

"What's your name?" Cang Ya asked Ah Dai with exceptional amiability.

Ah Dai blankly raised his head to look at Cang Ya. "Huh?"

The village chief hurriedly explained from the side, "Please don't take offense, esteemed guest; this child is a bit slow-witted and has sluggish reactions, but he's not actually an idiot. His name is literally Ah Dai (Dullhead)."

Cang Ya chuckled: *An idiot is even better. Only an idiot will obediently follow orders without kicking up random trouble.*

Cang Ya bent down, intending to pick Ah Dai up.

Ah Dai gave a little hop and dodged to the side.

The village chief again helped explain, "Ah Dai here is rather unaccustomed to strangers and doesn't like physical contact. But if you have anything to say to him, he can understand."

In truth, Cang Ya was secretly disgusted by how filthy Ah Dai looked. Seeing that the little beastman refused to be held, he was more than happy to spare his clothes from getting dirtied. He simply said to Ah Dai and the other selected children: "Come with us. From now on, you'll live a good life and never have to worry about going hungry again."

The village chief and the village elders escorted Cang Ya's group and the selected children all the way outside the valley entrance.

Shang Feifan tailed them the entire way.

He discovered that as Cang Ya and his group passed through the forest at the valley entrance, the creatures inside seemed to have completely vanished; those giant insects, each with their own distinct temperaments, had all disappeared without a trace.

Cang Ya and his companions didn't sense the slightest anomaly. Reaching the valley entrance and seeing the manpower they had left behind outside, they turned around and bid farewell to the village chief and the others.

"Are you folks coming with us to take a look this time? If you want to come, just wait for us to pick you up when we return. We'll send out a signal then," said the fat beastman.

The village chief forced a smile. "Then I'll have to trouble you all."

Cang Ya suddenly asked, "Earlier when we came by, we passed through some ruins and saw a collapsed castle, along with some houses and tents. Weren't there quite a few people living there originally? Where did those people go now? What happened over there?"

The village chief wore an expression of terror mingled with bewilderment, stammering, "We... we don't know what happened to that small settlement either. It was as if overnight, everyone inside just vanished. That night, we all heard the booming sounds of cannons, but we didn't dare come out to check. When dawn broke the next day and we came over, we found the place was already empty."

The village elder also chimed in with lingering fear, "They probably got ambushed by bandits. The bandits around here are vicious. I told them long ago that their area lacked any natural terrain defenses to hold, making it far too dangerous to use as a city. But those people wouldn't listen to us old folks."

Cang Ya asked several questions in a row, but the village chief and village elder remained completely oblivious to everything.

Cang Ya didn't think a poverty-stricken Village of the Flawed—one that couldn't even afford to feed its extra kids—could possibly know any vital matters, so he brushed them off with the promised sixty catties of insect powder.

Sixty catties of insect powder didn't even fill a single burlap sack; the village chief hoisted it up with one hand and headed back to the village.

As for Shang Feifan, he leapt aboard the carts of Cang Ya's party.

第239章 空中之城

商非凡跟着车队跑了一圈，发现这个所谓的冒险团队大概在天残谷附近已经经营了很长一段时间。

他们和这里的村落都有接触，很多村落都生活在犄角旮旯非常偏僻的地方，但他们都知道，还很熟悉。

相反，遇到凡是稍微大一点的镇子，只要人口超过三五千以上的，他们顶多就是停留打尖，绝口不提招募孩童作为预备队员培训的事。

这样的“招募”没有鬼才怪。

商非凡心知肚明。

苍牙一行人会专门去钻偏僻贫穷的小村落，就因为那种村落会有人养不活孩子，某些人甚至眼皮子浅到能为几袋粮食就把孩子卖掉，更因为那种村落的村民就算后悔也没有能力去寻找孩子。

而不选择大一点的镇子，一来人口众多的村镇大多生活还算过得去，不至于卖儿卖女，不想养的天残也大多会丢到天残谷，他们没必要再询问一遍。二来这种聚集地的兽人们见识也比较多，很难被他们忽悠住。三来一旦这些中型以上聚集地的兽人后悔或者想要调查冒险团，他们冒险团就有暴露和被找麻烦的危险。

这么一大圈跑下来，除去在天残村的“收获”，苍牙一行人只弄到了两个幼崽。

这两个幼崽还不是因为身体残缺被家里人弃养，而是家里实在养不活他们——半大小子吃穷老子，别看这两个小兽人都只有五六岁大，却特别能吃。偏生这两家人还特别能生。

有时候就是这么奇怪，越是贫穷的人家越是能生孩子，某些富裕的人家却连求一个孩子都不能得。

听苍牙说能把孩子带去学本事，将来还能拿薪酬回来，这次还能得到二十斤的虫粉做安家费，这两家人几乎是忙不迭地把自家十五岁以下的孩子全都推了出来。

要不是苍牙选人有要求，两家人恨不得冒险团把他们还不能做事捕猎的孩子都带走。

除了这两家人，也有少数动心的，但他们推出来的孩子都不合格，液体柱距离中间位置还远着呢。

胖兽人一路叨咕说今年选中的幼崽太少，回去怕不是会被上面念叨。

但苍牙却满心喜悦，今年人数不多，但质量好啊，只一个接近满格的阿呆就能顶得上上百只达到合格线的幼崽，也许还不止。

苍牙等人开始返程，他们把所有幼崽集中在一辆车中。

这时他们对幼崽还算和颜悦色，一天按照两顿给食水，虽然吃的只是虫粉，但能让幼崽们敞开了吃。

商非凡见了，总有种猪贩子把小猪仔带到市集上贩卖，先给它们塞一肚子食物增加重量的错觉。

其实更像是断头饭。商非凡凉凉地想。

阿呆混在八个幼崽中毫无违和感，难吃的冲泡虫粉和生水，他也照样吃得美美的，虽然吃的不多。

村长的两个孩子知道阿呆能随手拿出很多好吃好喝好玩的，但这两个孩子年龄都已经超过十岁，是这九个幼崽中年龄最大的两个，尤其是老二康康，已经十三岁，很懂事了。

村长给家里三个孩子分别取名壮壮、康康、饱饱，特别朴实地表达了他的衷心愿望。老三饱饱还是个女娃娃，但饱饱还小又调皮，长相也比较像她爹，不特意收拾的话看起来就和男娃娃一样。

两个孩子都没有嘴馋地让阿呆偷偷拿出更好吃的食物，康康自认自己是哥哥，还暗中护着老三和这个小阿呆。虽然他以前也欺负过阿呆，但一码归一码嘛。

以前是因为整个村子都穷，他爸他妈还要拿出家里不多的食物给其他没爹妈的孩子吃，他们兄弟妹吃不饱，自然讨厌会来家里分他们食物的阿呆。

现在阿呆不会抢占他们的食物，还愿意给他们村子帮忙，那他们自然也要讲义气。

康康其实也不知道阿呆具体要给村子帮什么忙，只是听爸爸说要让幼崽跟着那些冒险团的人去探查情况，查清楚往年他们天残村送去那个冒险团的幼崽们到底过得怎么样，而阿呆第一个踊跃报名，让康康很是佩服。

康康觉得他作为村长的孩子怎么能把村里的事情交给一个已经离开村子的幼崽去办，就也站出来了。

当他和老三都被选中，康康其实有点后悔还有点害怕，但看阿呆一点都不怂的样子，他就也挺起了胸膛。

康康不知道阿呆不怂是因为他知道他商爸暗中跟着他们，会时刻保护他这个崽儿，当然半点不害怕。

康康还暗中交代村中其他几个被选中的幼崽，让他们不要把阿呆的事情跟冒险团的人说，并答应他们只要他们闭紧嘴巴就会罩着他们。

几个幼崽心思各异，但表面上都答应了。

阿呆回村炫耀他爸可没半点遮掩，就差敲锣打鼓，四个幼崽除了那个还在襁褓中的奶崽，其他三个自然都知道阿呆有了一个富有还待他好的爸爸的事。

所以当他们看到阿呆也跟着来了，还弄得自己脏兮兮，几个小幼崽心里都挺奇怪的。

但还没等有小幼崽问出来，就被那个没有手臂只有一对小翅膀的男孩给阻止了——就一脚踹在想要问话的软骨症小幼崽屁股上。

翅膀男孩叫江旭，是养他的老兽人给他取的名字。

江旭已经十一岁，可能是营养不够充足的缘故，他外形看起来就跟八岁九岁的男孩差不多大。

但江旭在村里孩童中却相当有名，这家伙相当能打，别看他没有手，小翅膀也只能扇两下无法飞起来，但他能跳起来用尖锐的脚趾甲抓人，还能让嘴巴变成弯钩去叨人，性子也特别凶。

村里比他小的幼崽都有点怕他。就是比他大的小少年们也只敢用嘴巴骂骂他，不敢和他真刀实枪地打。

所以江旭踹软骨症小幼崽，那小幼崽也敢怒不敢言。还好不是很痛，就是把他想要问出口的话给踹没了。

软骨症幼崽年龄小、胆子也小，他也不知道自己为什么会被看中，只知道以后可以不用饿肚子。至于阿呆的事，他就是当时好奇想要问一问，也没有非要告密的意思——向大人告密的崽都不是好崽！

另一个被选中的幼崽，左腿比右腿短了一截的鹿族男孩和村里人不亲，和村里的幼崽自然也玩不到一起，他在外面长大，又一直被外面的兄弟姐妹歧视，最后还被家里人抛弃，心性就有点左了。

他没有立刻和冒险团的人说出阿呆的事，不是他惧怕江旭和村长次子，而是他感觉到了一丝阴谋的气息。

阿呆也好，村长的次子和幼子也好，都不像是会跟着冒险团走的。可他们却主动跟来了，为什么？

鹿族男孩想要看看能不能借此事谋取更大的好处，就暂时也闭紧了嘴巴。

商非凡没去管价格小崽子的弯弯绕绕，他也不担心阿呆的事被冒险团的人知道，他相信阿呆，那小家伙绝对能编出一个适合的借口。

而且只看苍牙对阿呆的满意程度，哪怕他知道阿呆有问题，恐怕也会铁了心带阿呆回去。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 239: City in the Sky (Part 1)

Following the convoy around for a tour, Shang Feifan discovered that this so-called adventure team had likely been operating around the Heaven-Crippled Valley for quite a long time.

They had contact with the villages here. Many of these settlements were tucked away in extremely remote, secluded corners, yet the team knew of them and was very familiar with their locations.

Conversely, whenever they encountered slightly larger towns—any place with a population exceeding three to five thousand—they would at most stop for a quick meal, never once mentioning the recruitment of children as trainee members.

There had to be something fishy about this kind of "recruitment."

Shang Feifan knew it like the back of his hand.

Cang Ya and his party specifically sought out remote and impoverished small villages precisely because in such places, families might struggle to feed their children. Some people were so short-sighted that they would sell their flesh and blood for a few bags of grain; moreover, if the villagers of such places later regretted it, they lacked the capability to search for their children.

As for why they avoided larger towns: Firstly, villages and towns with dense populations generally managed to get by well enough that they didn't need to sell their sons and daughters. Any disabled children they didn't want to raise were mostly thrown into the Heaven-Crippled Valley anyway, so there was no need for the team to ask around again. Secondly, the beastmen in such settlements were more worldly and hard to hoodwink. Thirdly, once the beastmen in these medium-sized or larger settlements regretted their actions or tried to investigate the adventure team, the team would face the risk of exposure and trouble.

After running such a large circuit, aside from their "harvest" in Heaven-Crippled Village, Cang Ya and his group had only managed to secure two cubs.

These two cubs weren't abandoned by their families due to physical disabilities, but simply because their families literally could not afford to feed them—a growing boy could eat his parents out of house and home. Even though these two little beastmen were only five or six years old, they had monstrous appetites. To make matters worse, these two families were exceptionally prolific.

Sometimes it was just so strange: the poorer a family was, the more children they could produce, while some wealthy families couldn't get a single child no matter how hard they prayed.

Hearing Cang Ya say that the children could be taken away to learn skills, earn a salary in the future, and even receive twenty catties of insect powder right now as a settling-in allowance, the two families practically scrambled to push forward every single child under fifteen years of age.

If Cang Ya hadn't set strict requirements for his selections, the two families would have wished the adventure team could take away all their children who were still too young to work or hunt.

Aside from these two families, there were a few others who felt tempted, but the children they pushed forward failed to make the cut—the liquid column in the test tube was still far from the middle mark.

The fat beastman muttered all the way that the cubs selected this year were far too few, and he feared he would catch an earful from the higher-ups upon returning.

Yet Cang Ya was brimming with joy. The headcount was low this year, but the quality was exceptional! A single Ah Dai, whose test result was close to the maximum mark, was worth hundreds of cubs who merely met the passing threshold—perhaps even more.

Cang Ya and his men began their return journey, gathering all the cubs into a single carriage.

For now, they treated the cubs quite affably, providing food and water twice a day. Although they only ate insect powder, the cubs were allowed to eat their fill.

Seeing this, Shang Feifan always had the surreal illusion of a pig dealer leading piglets to market for sale, stuffing their bellies with food beforehand to artificially increase their weight.

In fact, it felt more like a condemned prisoner's final meal, Shang Feifan thought coldly.

Ah Dai blended seamlessly among the eight other cubs, eating the foul-tasting, rehydrated insect powder and raw water with evident relish, even though he didn't eat much.

The village chief's two children knew that Ah Dai could casually produce all kinds of delicious food, drinks, and toys, but both of them were already over ten years old, making them the oldest among the nine cubs. Especially the second child, Kangkang, who was thirteen and very sensible.

The village chief had named his three children Zhuangzhuang, Kangkang, and Baobao, expressing his earnest and utterly down-to-earth wishes. The third child, Baobao, was still a little girl, but she was young, mischievous, and took after her father in appearance; without special grooming, she looked just like a boy.

Neither of the two children greedily pestered Ah Dai to secretly pull out better food. Kangkang considered himself an elder brother and covertly protected both his younger sister and little Ah Dai. Although he used to bully Ah Dai in the past, business was business.

In the past, the whole village was poor, and his parents had to scrape together the family's meager food to give to other orphans, leaving his own family hungry. Naturally, they resented Ah Dai, who came to their house to take a share of their food.

Now that Ah Dai wouldn't be hogging their food and was even willing to help out their village, they naturally had to show solidarity.

Kangkang didn't actually know what specific help Ah Dai was going to give the village; he had only heard his father say that the cubs were going to follow the adventure team people to scout the situation and find out how the children sent by Heaven-Crippled Village in previous years were actually doing. Ah Dai had been the first to enthusiastically volunteer, which deeply impressed Kangkang.

Kangkang felt that as the village chief's son, how could he leave village business to a child who had already left the village? So he had stepped forward as well.

When both he and his younger sister were selected, Kangkang felt a brief pang of regret and fear, but seeing how completely unfazed Ah Dai looked, he puffed out his chest too.

Kangkang had no idea that Ah Dai was fearless simply because he knew his Shang Daddy was secretly following them and would protect his cub at all times. Naturally, there was not a shred of fear.

Kangkang also covertly instructed the other selected cubs in the village, telling them not to mention Ah Dai's situation to the adventure team members, and promised that as long as they kept their mouths shut, he would cover for them.

The several cubs harbored different thoughts, but all agreed on the surface.

Ah Dai had made no secret of showing off his father when he returned to the village—he was practically beating drums and gongs. Aside from the baby still in swaddling clothes, the other three cubs naturally all knew that Ah Dai had acquired a wealthy father who treated him well.

Therefore, when they saw Ah Dai tagging along and looking all dusty, the other little cubs felt quite puzzled.

Before any of the little cubs could ask, however, they were stopped by the armless boy with only a pair of tiny wings—he delivered a swift kick to the backside of the rickets-afflicted little cub who was about to speak.

The winged boy was named Jiang旭 (Jiang Xu), a name given to him by the old beastman who raised him.

Jiang Xu was already eleven years old, but perhaps due to a lack of proper nutrition, his physical stature looked no bigger than an ordinary eight- or nine-year-old boy.

Yet Jiang Xu was quite famous among the village children. This fellow was a fierce fighter; despite having no arms and tiny wings that could only flap twice without achieving flight, he could leap up and scratch people with his sharp toenails, or transform his mouth into a hooked beak to peck at them. His temper was also exceptionally vicious.

The younger cubs in the village were somewhat afraid of him, and even the older youths only dared to curse him with words, not daring to truly trade blows with him.

Thus, when Jiang Xu kicked the rickets-afflicted cub, that little cub didn't dare to show his anger. Fortunately, it didn't hurt much; it simply kicked the words he wanted to ask right back into his stomach.

The rickets-afflicted cub was young and timid, and he had no idea why he had been chosen, knowing only that he wouldn't have to starve in the future. As for Ah Dai's matters, he had only been curious and wanted to ask; he hadn't meant to snitch at all—cubs who snitched to adults were bad cubs!

Another selected cub, a Deer-tribe boy whose left leg was noticeably shorter than his right, wasn't close to the villagers and naturally couldn't mingle with the village cubs. Having grown up outside and constantly faced discrimination from his external siblings before finally being abandoned by his family, his temperament had become somewhat twisted.

He didn't immediately spill the beans about Ah Dai to the adventure team, not out of fear of Jiang Xu or the village chief's second son, but because he sensed a whiff of conspiracy.

Neither Ah Dai nor the village chief's second son and younger child seemed like the type to follow the adventure team willingly. Yet they had voluntarily come along—why?

The Deer-tribe boy wanted to see if he could leverage this situation to extract greater benefits, so he temporarily kept his mouth shut as well.

Shang Feifan didn't bother meddling in the petty schemes of these little brats, nor was he worried about the adventure team finding out about Ah Dai. He trusted Ah Dai; that little fellow could definitely fabricate a suitable excuse.

Moreover, judging by how satisfied Cang Ya was with Ah Dai, even if he realized something was amiss with the boy, he would likely be dead-set on taking Ah Dai back with him.

chunks.chineseText:
