chunks.chapterTitle: 第245章 回程安排和日常 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第245章 回程安排和日常

商非凡把偌大的浮空之城送入雕像广场，也幸好这座城是无根之物，否则他想收取一座连带大片土地的城市哪可能这么容易。

商非凡注意到雕像广场的空间大小似乎没有任何变化，被收进去的浮空之城则像是变小了许多，就贴在广场边缘地带，像是广场边沿多了一块农田。

收取浮空之城后，商非凡浮在半空看向不远处被群山包围的盆地。

那里的地形非常像是第二座天空之城，和天空之城就像是镜像存在。

目前为止，那边的邪神信徒似乎还没有发现天空之城出事。

天空之城有自己的遮掩方法，从下方看根本看不到天空中浮着一座城。

也有可能天空之城的地位比较高，下方那个基地还没有资格知道天空之城的事。

当然更有可能是天空之城发生变故太快，那位蛰离吞噬一座城人口的速度也超过邪神信徒们的想象，让他们根本没有时间把消息传递出去。

商非凡心想，如果他不带走天空之城，等到真神教的人上来查看，就会发现一座诡异的空城。

就像是地星那边一些古老遗迹一样，人们留下了明显的生活痕迹，饭菜都还在饭桌上，衣物行李没有收拾，家畜和坐骑都还在栅栏里，可所有人全都消失了。

出于一丝好奇和警戒心，商非凡隐身跑过去查看那座地面基地。

但等他赶到那里，看到的却是又一座空城。

只不过这座空城能看出来明显收拾过的痕迹，属于公共库房里的物品已经全都转移走。像是个人的居所内部不少都显露出匆忙的收拾痕迹，很多人连打开的抽屉和柜门都没来得及关上。

应该是知道上面的天空之城出事了？

这是觉得无法应对，就干脆躲开？

这样匆忙离开，让这座城留下了不少东西，更能从留下的痕迹看出这座城里生活的人平时都在干些什么。

如果说上面的天空之城更像是一座综合了农业和科研的大型基地，那么这座地面之城就是一座妥妥的军营。

商非凡还在这座军营里发现了一个金属加工厂。

走的人把能带走的器械都带走了，只留下了带不走的炼钢炉和相关附加设施，但后来人也讨不了好，因为这些设施都已被炸毁。

商非凡在这座军营中溜溜达达转了一圈，没发现什么好东西。

零碎的东西很多，他看到有用的——以后他和阿沐要养许多人，这些零零碎碎的别看单买不值钱，但买的多了，那也是一笔庞大支出，就随手丢进雕像广场，原本以为并没有多少东西，结果回头一看，他竟然在广场一角丢出了一个巨大的“垃圾堆”。

其中最多的就是家具和日用品。

商非凡还通过能量感知，摸到了地下。

地下部分分成了几个大功能区。

在这里，商非凡发现了类似生物研究的区域。

同样，能被带走的重要东西都被带走，商非凡最后也只是收取了一些家具、工具和消耗品之类的东西。

“爸爸……”阿呆在雕像广场里醒了过来。

商非凡感知到，把阿呆捞出来：“醒了，准备回家。”

阿呆错过了最精彩的部分，圆溜溜的眼睛透出一丝迷茫：“那个老爷爷解决了吗？”

“暂时解决。”商非凡简单回答。

他没有进入知识之神的异度空间，自然不知道路德维希是被串在了那根绳子上，还是已经被蛰离消化掉。

但按照路德维希的实力推断——他应该和洛人渣的实力相差不大，既然连洛人渣都只能靠损失一具分-身才能逃出知识之神的异度空间，那么路德维希应该也差不多。

不过就是不知道路德维希有没有分-身或者替命术之类的保命术法。

不管路德维希能不能逃出来，至少他暂时是没办法跑到他面前给他找麻烦了。

就算对方真的逃出来并直面他，商非凡也自信能和对方周转一二，而不是像之前只能靠臭果来祸水东引。

吸收融合了那枚虫母心脏碎片，又无意间吸收消化了那枚用黑暗之神神格碎片炼制的戒指，再加上和厄穆克拉索逃逸出的一丝力量战斗了一番，他现在的实力何止提升一倍？

商非凡有种强烈感觉，只要给他一段时间把刚才强行容纳的那些庞大能量好好消化，他的实力还会再来一次突飞猛进，说不定就能冲击已经很久没有人能冲击的法神境界。

不过商非凡强行压制了这股冲动。

他的提升太快了。

他的身体和精神都需要去适应这份刚刚得到的庞大力量。

比起一个劲地利用这些能量去冲击更高等级，他更愿意稳打稳扎地把这些庞大能量全都吸收消化得干干净净，真正成为自己的东西，并打磨好身体，再去冲击更高层次。

阿呆看看左右，搞不清楚这里是哪里，但他没有过多询问，只要他两个爸爸在，他就无所畏惧，在哪里都不怕！

有阿呆在，接下来的行动就可以加速。

阿呆带着他商爸瞬移回天残村。

老商特意避开天残村其他村民眼睛，暗中把天残村长的两个幼崽送到村长家中，并告知村长和悄悄赶来的村老们，其他救出的幼崽已经不适合回到天残村生活，他会另外安排。

村长和村老们听说这次送去的幼崽全都安然无恙，就都松了口气。

他们对商非凡能否救出前面那些年送出的幼崽并不抱希望，而听商非凡的意思，他把那个佣兵团队基地中能找到的幼崽都救出了。

这对他们就已经足够安慰。

至于说商非凡要把幼崽们带走另外安排，这对他们更是大好事。

他们就算有心想要安顿那些幼崽也无力，还不如交给商非凡。想来这位应该会给那些孩子一条活路？

“以后如果有人来问你们，你们就当什么都不知道，管好你们村幼崽的嘴巴。”商非凡提醒。

村长心感不妙，立刻追问：“那佣兵团队到底是个什么底细？”

商非凡淡淡回答：“邪神信徒。”

“哦，原来是邪……什么？！”村长和村老们全都惊地站了起来。

村长看向自家两个孩子。

饱饱还有点懵懂，更大一些的康康就说：“我们刚去那儿，那个佣兵团的人带我们去吃饭，但吃饭前要我们先赞颂一位神灵，叫厄穆克拉索。”

康康毫不打颤地报出这个有点拗口的名字。

饱饱听到也在一边抱怨：“那些人可凶可凶，要我们必须背出这位神-的-名字，背不出来就不准吃饭。”

“我问这位神灵是什么神。他们说是我们这个世界乃至整个宇宙的至高神和唯一神。”康康补充。

村长差点呸出来，但他不敢，只小声说：“祂不是我们的神，祂是外来的邪神。以后你们务必忘掉那个名字，再也不能去想那个名字，更不能呼唤！”

康康已经明白什么是邪神。

但饱饱还不太懂，扯了扯哥哥的胳膊。

康康就跟妹妹说：“就是坏的会害人的恶神。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 245: Return Arrangements and Daily Life (Part 1)

Shang Feifan sent the massive floating city into the Statue Square. Fortunately, this city was a rootless object; otherwise, collecting a city attached to a vast tract of land wouldn't have been so easy.

Shang Feifan noticed that the spatial dimensions of the Statue Square didn't seem to change at all. The floating city that had been taken inside seemed to have shrunk significantly, clinging to the edge of the square like an extra patch of farmland.

After collecting the floating city, Shang Feifan hovered in midair, looking toward the basin surrounded by mountains not far away.

The terrain there looked very much like a second Sky City, existing almost as a mirror image of the one in the sky.

So far, the evil god's cultists over there didn't seem to have discovered that something had happened to Sky City.

Sky City had its own methods of concealment; looking up from below, one couldn't see a city floating in the sky at all.

It was also possible that Sky City held a higher status, and the base below wasn't qualified to know about its existence.

Of course, it was even more likely that the incident in Sky City had happened too quickly. The speed at which that Zhe Li devoured the population of an entire city exceeded the cultists' wildest imaginations, leaving them no time to send word out.

Shang Feifan thought to himself that if he hadn't taken Sky City away, when the members of the True God Cult came up to investigate, they would have found a bizarre, empty city.

Just like some ancient ruins back on Earth, where people left behind obvious traces of life—meals still on the dining tables, clothes and luggage unpacked, livestock and mounts still in their pens, yet every single person had vanished.

Out of a touch of curiosity and vigilance, Shang Feifan concealed his figure and flew over to inspect the ground base.

But when he arrived, what he saw was yet another empty city.

However, this empty city showed clear signs of having been packed up. The items in the public warehouses had all been transferred away. Inside many personal residences, there were signs of hurried packing; many people hadn't even had time to close the drawers and cabinet doors they had opened.

They must have known that something had happened to Sky City above?

Did they feel unable to handle it and simply choose to flee?

Leaving in such a rush meant many things were left behind in the city, and the traces left behind made it even clearer what the people living here usually did.

If the Sky City above was more like a large-scale base combining agriculture and scientific research, then this ground city was a proper military camp.

Shang Feifan also discovered a metal processing plant in this military camp.

Those who left had taken all the equipment they could carry, leaving behind only the immovable steel-smelting furnaces and related auxiliary facilities. However, any latecomers wouldn't benefit either, as these facilities had all been blown up.

Shang Feifan strolled around the military camp but didn't find anything of great value.

There were many odds and ends. Seeing things that might be useful—since he and A'Mu would have to support many people in the future, and though these miscellaneous items might not seem worth much individually, buying them in bulk would be a massive expense—he casually tossed them into the Statue Square. He originally thought it wasn't much, but when he looked back, he had actually piled up a massive "garbage heap" in a corner of the square.

Most of it consisted of furniture and daily necessities.

Through energy perception, Shang Feifan also made his way underground.

The underground section was divided into several large functional zones.

Here, Shang Feifan discovered an area resembling a biological research facility.

Similarly, any important things that could be taken had been removed. In the end, Shang Feifan only collected some furniture, tools, and consumables.

"Daddy..." Ah Dai woke up inside the Statue Square.

Sensing this, Shang Feifan scooped Ah Dai out. "You're awake. Get ready to go home."

Ah Dai had missed the most exciting part. His round eyes held a trace of confusion. "Is that old grandpa dealt with?"

"Dealt with for now," Shang Feifan replied simply.

He hadn't entered the God of Knowledge's alternate dimension, so he naturally didn't know whether Ludwig had been strung up on that rope or already digested by Zhe Li.

But judging by Ludwig's strength—he shouldn't be too far off from that scumbag Luo. Since even that scumbag Luo could only escape the God of Knowledge's alternate dimension by sacrificing a clone, Ludwig should be in a similar boat.

However, it was unknown whether Ludwig had any life-saving techniques like clones or substitute arts.

Regardless of whether Ludwig could escape, at least he wouldn't be able to run over and cause trouble for him anytime soon.

Even if the other party did escape and confront him directly, Shang Feifan was confident he could hold his own and maneuver around him, rather than having to rely on stinky fruits to divert the disaster like before.

Having absorbed and fused that fragment of the Broodmother's heart, unintentionally absorbed and digested the ring crafted from a fragment of the God of Darkness's divinity, and fought against a sliver of escaped power from Emukraso, his current strength had more than doubled.

Shang Feifan had a strong feeling that as long as he was given some time to properly digest the massive energy he had just forcibly accommodated, his strength would leap forward once again. He might even be able to charge toward the realm of the Dharma God, a realm no one had been able to reach for a very long time.

However, Shang Feifan forcibly suppressed this urge.

His advancement was too rapid.

Both his body and mind needed to adapt to this newly acquired, immense power.

Rather than blindly using this energy to charge toward a higher level, he preferred to take steady, solid steps to completely absorb and digest all of this massive energy, making it truly his own, and temper his body before aiming for a higher realm.

Ah Dai looked left and right, unable to figure out where they were, but he didn't ask too many questions. As long as his two daddies were around, he was fearless. He wasn't afraid of being anywhere!

With Ah Dai around, their subsequent movements could be accelerated.

Ah Dai teleported his Daddy Shang back to Tiancan Village.

Old Shang deliberately avoided the eyes of the other villagers of Tiancan Village. He secretly delivered the village chief's two cubs to the chief's home and informed the chief and the village elders who had quietly gathered that the other rescued cubs were no longer suited to return to Tiancan Village to live, and that he would make other arrangements for them.

Hearing that the cubs sent away this time were all safe and sound, the village chief and the elders all breathed a sigh of relief.

They hadn't held much hope that Shang Feifan could rescue the cubs sent out in previous years. But from what Shang Feifan meant, he had rescued all the cubs that could be found in that mercenary group's base.

This was comfort enough for them.

As for Shang Feifan taking the cubs away to make other arrangements, this was an even greater boon for them.

Even if they had the heart to settle those cubs, they lacked the ability. It was better to hand them over to Shang Feifan. Surely, this master would give those children a path to survival?

"If anyone comes to ask you in the future, just pretend you know nothing. Keep a tight lid on the mouths of your village's cubs," Shang Feifan warned.

Sensing that something was wrong, the village chief immediately pressed, "What on earth is the background of that mercenary group?"

Shang Feifan replied flatly, "Cultists of an evil god."

"Oh, so they're e... what?!" The village chief and the elders all stood up in shock.

The village chief looked at his two children.

Baobao was still a bit oblivious, but the older Kangkang said, "When we first got there, the people from the mercenary group took us to eat. But before eating, they wanted us to praise a deity named Emukraso."

Kangkang recited this somewhat tongue-twisting name without a single stutter.

Hearing this, Baobao also complained from the side, "Those people were super, super fierce. They made us memorize the name of this god. If we couldn't recite it, they wouldn't let us eat."

"I asked what kind of god this deity was. They said He is the supreme and only god of our world, and even the entire universe," Kangkang added.

The village chief almost spat in disgust, but he didn't dare. He only whispered, "He is not our god; He is an invading evil god. From now on, you must forget that name. You must never think of it again, let alone call upon it!"

Kangkang already understood what an evil god was.

But Baobao didn't quite understand yet and tugged at her brother's arm.

Kangkang told his sister, "It's a bad, wicked god that harms people."

chunks.chapterTitle: 第245章 回程安排和日常 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
饱饱害怕了。捂住嘴巴，害怕自己念过那么多次恶神-的-名字会引来厄运。

村长和村老们眼神互相交流，没多一会儿，村长就下了决定：“阁下，我有一个不情之请。”

村长想要把自家两个孩子交给商非凡一起带走。

他心痛，更不舍。

但邪神信徒已经知道他们这个点，如果他们发现他们的一个基地没有了，肯定会过来查问。

他可以保证村里的成年人不会乱说，但他没办法保证能管住小孩子们的嘴巴。

当时可是很多人都看到他把康康和饱饱交给苍牙他们带走，现在两个孩子回来，说他们毫不知情，他们相信，邪神信徒们可不会相信。

如果那些邪神信徒对孩子们使用一些操纵精神的邪法，孩子们很可能会说出一些不该说出来的事情。

不管是为了两个孩子好，还是为了他们整个村子，村长能想到的最好方法就是假装两个孩子没回来。

村长的这个请求并没有出乎商非凡预料。

如果是刚来这个世界的他，他肯定懒得管这个闲事——他是来这个游戏世界休闲放松的，可不是来给自己找事干。

但这不是遇到他家阿沐，他来到这个世界的意义已经彻底改变了嘛。

郎沐的领地需要人手发展，而且他都已经带上那么多小崽子，再加上两个根本不是事。

“丑话还是需要说在前头的。两个孩子我可以带走，但需要他们自己愿意，另外我不保证他们一定会生活顺心，也不保证他们的绝对安全，只能说他们会和其他幼崽一样，会让他们上课，也会让他们做一些力所能及的事情，吃饱穿暖应该还是没问题的。而你们也能随时去探望。”

商非凡骄傲地说：“我爱人是黑水荒原大区的新领主，我们打算在那里建造一座城，会在城里办学校，带过去的幼崽会都安排在那里上课学习。等有了确切地点，我会安排人给你们送信，如果找不到确切地点，你们可以先找到莫约镇，从那里打听。”

商非凡没提学费和生活费，他就当资助贫困生了。到时候就和两个崽儿签个毕业后需要为黑水荒原大区工作多少年的合约，其他资助生一样。

村长当然不指望他家两个孩子能像阿呆一样好运并得到阿呆一样的待遇，他只求两个孩子能有口饭吃、能平平安安地长大。

这时听说两个孩子还能上课，他们大人还能随时去探望，村长心里喜悦，忙不迭地说：“谢谢，谢谢！这样就很好。放心，康康他们已经不小了，在家里时就能做很多事。您带过去绝对不会给您添很多麻烦。”

商非凡无所谓道：“你们一家子想好就行。我给你们十五分钟告别时间。想要带东西的话，带上小孩心爱的物品就可，其他衣服食物之类的日常生活用品就不用带了，到时候我们那边统一安排。”

年老的女兽人忽然开口：“那座学校是天残幼崽和正常幼崽在一起上课吗？”

商非凡：“当然。”

村长愣住，老兽人们面露愁容。

商非凡哂笑：“你们都在担心什么？怕非天残的幼崽歧视和欺负天残幼崽？”

村长和村老们没说话，但他们的表情已经说明一切。

商非凡摇摇头：“你们想太多了。小孩子对别人的态度都是教出来的，在我们黑水荒原、在我和郎沐管辖下的学校，无论是什么样外表的孩子都一样，我们黑水荒原就没有天残和非天残之分。”

村长失语。他很想相信商的话，但他又很难相信。

商非凡也懒得解释太多，兽人们对天残天生低人一头的根深蒂固认知岂是三言两语就能拔除？

就连天残兽人们也都自认自己无论是地位还是能力都不如正常兽人。

只听他们称呼其他兽人为“正常”兽人，就知道他们已经在潜意识中把自己划分为“不正常”之列。

但这种根深蒂固并不是不能动摇，相反只要有适当的管理和教育方式，从上往下，天残甚至能变成人们口中的天幸，成为人人羡慕的对象。

人的意识转变有时候真的就看上位者的喜好。

“我也是天残。”商非凡还是给村长他们吃了一颗定心丸。

村长和村老们大吃一惊：“阁下你怎么可能是天残？”

完全看不出来！

“我和阿呆在某方面一样，我的兽形一直都是幼年体。”商非凡笑，想起自己变成小脑斧滚在阿沐怀里的幸福感，眼里藏了一丝丝他自己也不知道的温柔：“但你们觉得我的人形很弱吗？”

阿呆抬起头看他商爸，也很吃惊，又很惊喜：原来商爸跟他一样哎。真棒！

村长和村老们听商非凡如此“自曝其短”，虽然有些不好意思，但心里是真的放心下来了。

岂是他们心里也清楚，商非凡这么说九成是在安慰他们。人家兽形是幼崽状态，说不定只是长得慢，人形又没问题。

据他们所知，就有一些特殊种兽人就是兽形长得极慢，那是他们幼年期本来就漫长，但如果让他们长成了，那是巨兽也无法比拟的厉害！

康康和饱饱在同父母深谈过后——其实刚才大人们的对话已经让两个孩子有点了解他们留在村里不安全这点，并没有怎么闹腾，就同意和商非凡一起离开。

村长的长子壮壮听到父母和弟妹的谈话，当即做了一个决定，他也要跟着弟妹一起去那座还没有盖起来的黑水荒原城。

村长了解长子在想什么，无非就是想要保护弟妹，另外也是到了对外界好奇的年纪，想要出去看看。

天残村的生活一眼就能看到底。

以往村里的孩子长大后也因为对外界（对天残鄙视和排斥）的畏惧，而不敢离开村子发展。

能走出去的刚成年孩子极少。

加上荒野危险，就算想要离开村子到外面走走，也苦于不敢一个人或少数人上路，而只能等待商队，然后看商队愿不愿意带着他们。

但不是每个商队都是好人，走出去再也没有回来的村民，谁也不知道他们身上到底发生了什么事。

现在这位修理师至少赢得了天残村民们的信赖，他还愿意负担起和他无关的幼崽们的生活和教育，而且还有大本事！

对于村长长子来说，这就是一个走出去的绝好机会。

更别说这次出去，他还能照顾自己的弟妹和村里其他幼崽。

一只羊也是赶，三只羊……反正都是塞到广场里让他们睡觉，商非凡完全不介意再多带一个。

相反有了壮壮这个接近成年的大崽子，还能帮他带带其他幼崽，挺好。

商非凡走前，对村长和村老们微微一笑：“还有一件事，我需要对你们做一个精神暗示，倒不是怕你们说出我的事情，而是避免你们被牵连。放心，对你们不会有任何损伤，还能保护你们不被他人精神力伤害。只要对方的精神力没有强过我。”

村长夫妻和村老们毫不犹豫，一口答应。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 245: Return Arrangements and Daily Life (Part 2)

Baobao grew scared. She covered her mouth, terrified that having uttered the wicked god's name so many times would bring misfortune upon her.

The village chief and the elders exchanged looks. Before long, the village chief made a decision: "Your Excellency, I have an audacious request."

The village chief wanted to hand his two children over to Shang Feifan to be taken away together.

His heart ached, and he was deeply reluctant.

But the evil god's cultists already knew about their village. If they discovered that one of their bases was gone, they would definitely come to investigate.

He could guarantee that the adults in the village wouldn't talk, but he had no way to guarantee he could control the children's mouths.

Back then, many people had seen him hand Kangkang and Baobao over to Cang Ya and the others. Now that the two children were back, even if they claimed they knew nothing, the villagers might believe them, but the cultists certainly wouldn't.

If those cultists used some wicked mind-control spells on the children, the children would very likely speak of things they shouldn't.

Whether for the sake of the two children or the entire village, the best method the village chief could think of was to pretend the two children had never returned.

This request from the village chief did not catch Shang Feifan by surprise.

If it were the him who had just arrived in this world, he would definitely have been too lazy to meddle in this business—he had come to this game world to relax and leisure, not to find trouble for himself.

But hadn't he met his beloved A'Mu? The meaning of his arrival in this world had completely changed.

Lang Mu's territory needed manpower to develop, and since he was already bringing along so many little cubs, adding two more was no trouble at all.

"I must lay down the ugly truths first. I can take the two children, but they must be willing. Furthermore, I cannot guarantee their lives will always be smooth sailing, nor can I guarantee their absolute safety. I can only say that, like the other cubs, they will attend classes and be given tasks within their capabilities. Having enough food and warm clothes shouldn't be an issue. And you can visit them at any time."

Shang Feifan said proudly, "My partner is the new lord of the Blackwater Wasteland region. We plan to build a city there and set up a school in it. The cubs we bring over will all be arranged to study there. Once we have a precise location, I will arrange for someone to send you a letter. If you can't find the exact location, you can first find Moyue Town and ask around there."

Shang Feifan didn't mention tuition or living expenses; he would treat it as sponsoring underprivileged students. When the time came, he would have the two cubs sign a contract agreeing to work for the Blackwater Wasteland region for a certain number of years after graduation, just like the other sponsored students.

The village chief, of course, didn't expect his two children to be as lucky as Ah Dai or receive the same treatment. He only begged for them to have food to eat and grow up safely.

Hearing now that the two children could even attend classes and that the adults could visit them at any time, the village chief was overjoyed. He said hurriedly, "Thank you, thank you! This is wonderful. Don't worry, Kangkang and the other are no longer small; they could already do many chores at home. Taking them along will definitely not cause you much trouble."

Shang Feifan said indifferently, "As long as your family has thought it through. I'll give you fifteen minutes to say goodbye. If you want to bring things, just bring the children's favorite belongings. There's no need to bring other daily necessities like clothes and food; we will arrange everything uniformly over there."

An elderly female beastman suddenly spoke up, "Will that school have Tiancan cubs and normal cubs attending classes together?"

Shang Feifan: "Of course."

The village chief froze, and the elderly beastmen showed worried expressions.

Shang Feifan sneered, "What are you all worried about? Afraid that the non-Tiancan cubs will discriminate against and bully the Tiancan cubs?"

The village chief and the elders remained silent, but their expressions said it all.

Shang Feifan shook his head. "You're overthinking. Children's attitudes toward others are taught. In our Blackwater Wasteland, in the schools under the jurisdiction of Lang Mu and myself, children of any appearance are equal. In our Blackwater Wasteland, there is no distinction between Tiancan and non-Tiancan."

The village chief was speechless. He desperately wanted to believe Shang's words, but it was hard to believe.

Shang Feifan was too lazy to explain further. How could the beastmen's deep-rooted perception that the Tiancan were naturally inferior be uprooted with just a few words?

Even the Tiancan beastmen themselves believed they were inferior to normal beastmen in both status and ability.

Just hearing them refer to other beastmen as "normal" beastmen showed that they had subconsciously categorized themselves as "abnormal."

But this deep-rooted belief was not unshakable. On the contrary, with proper management and education, from the top down, "Tiancan" (Heavenly Crippled) could even become what people called "Tianxing" (Heavenly Blessed), becoming objects of envy for everyone.

A change in people's consciousness sometimes truly depended on the preferences of those in power.

"I am also a Tiancan," Shang Feifan said, offering the village chief and the others a reassuring pill.

The village chief and the elders were greatly shocked. "How could Your Excellency be a Tiancan?"

It was completely unnoticeable!

"In a certain aspect, Ah Dai and I are the same. My beast form has always remained in its juvenile state." Shang Feifan smiled, recalling the happiness of turning into a little tiger and rolling around in A'Mu's arms. A trace of tenderness, of which he himself was unaware, hid in his eyes. "But do you think my human form is weak?"

Ah Dai looked up at his Daddy Shang, also very surprised and pleasantly shocked: *So Daddy Shang is just like me. Awesome!*

Hearing Shang Feifan "expose his own shortcoming" like this, the village chief and the elders felt a bit embarrassed, but their hearts truly set at ease.

In truth, they also knew in their hearts that Shang Feifan saying this was ninety percent just to comfort them. His beast form being in a cub state might just mean he grew slowly, while his human form had no issues whatsoever.

As far as they knew, there were indeed some special beastman species whose beast forms grew extremely slowly because their childhood was naturally long. But once they fully matured, they would be so powerful that even giant beasts couldn't compare!

After a deep conversation with their parents—in fact, the adults' conversation just now had already made the two children understand somewhat that staying in the village was unsafe—Kangkang and Baobao didn't make a fuss and agreed to leave with Shang Feifan.

Hearing the conversation between his parents and his younger siblings, the village chief's eldest son, Zhuangzhuang, made a decision on the spot: he also wanted to follow his siblings to that Blackwater Wasteland city that hadn't even been built yet.

The village chief understood what his eldest son was thinking. It was nothing more than wanting to protect his younger siblings, and also reaching the age of curiosity about the outside world, wanting to go out and see.

Life in Tiancan Village could be seen through to the end in a single glance.

In the past, when the children in the village grew up, they didn't dare to leave the village to develop due to their fear of the outside world (its contempt and rejection of the Tiancan).

Very few newly matured children ever walked out.

Coupled with the dangers of the wilderness, even if they wanted to leave the village to travel, they suffered from not daring to set out alone or in small numbers. They could only wait for caravans and see if the caravans were willing to take them.

But not every caravan was good. For those villagers who walked out and never returned, no one knew what had actually happened to them.

Now, this repairman had at least won the trust of the Tiancan villagers. He was even willing to take on the living and educational expenses of cubs unrelated to him, and he possessed great abilities!

For the village chief's eldest son, this was an excellent opportunity to step out.

Not to mention that by going out this time, he could also take care of his younger siblings and the other cubs from the village.

Whether herding one sheep or three... since they were all going to be stuffed into the square to sleep anyway, Shang Feifan didn't mind bringing one more at all.

On the contrary, having Zhuangzhuang, a near-adult big cub, who could help him look after the other cubs, was actually quite good.

Before leaving, Shang Feifan smiled slightly at the village chief and the elders. "One more thing. I need to place a mental suggestion on you. It's not because I'm afraid you'll speak of my affairs, but to prevent you from being implicated. Don't worry, it won't cause you any harm, and it can even protect you from being harmed by others' mental energy—as long as the other party's mental energy is not stronger than mine."

The village chief, his wife, and the elders agreed without the slightest hesitation.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第245章 回程安排和日常 (Part 3)
chunks.chineseText:
次日，天残村民并不知道商非凡又回来过的事情，倒是发现村长家的长子也不见了。

村长就一脸担忧加哀伤，苦笑着对村民们说：壮壮担心他的弟妹，硬是跑出去找他们了。

村民们纷纷安慰村长，心中则都在骂村长长子不懂事，怎么能就这么偷跑出去，也不怕在外面出事。

天残村这边还是和往日一样，过着日出而作日入而息的平淡贫瘠生活。

之后没几天，果然有人到村里询问情况。

村民对于苍牙带走幼崽们的情况倒是交代得清清楚楚，但对于其他事情就全都一问三不知。

那些人中也果然有人对村民实施了精神控制之类的天赋技能，问出了阿呆这个奇怪幼崽。

但村民们也只知道阿呆被一个外地人领养，不知为何又主动跟苍牙他们走了。

按照村民们的想法，那就是阿呆也只是表面光，他害怕再次被抛弃，就选择先一步主动离开了那个外地人，宁可跟着苍牙他们去学本事当佣兵。

那些人反复询问村民那个阿呆的养父长什么样、做什么事、从哪里来。

他们询问最多的就是村长。

村长在被控制下，把他知道的事情都说了出来。

那些人见村长知道的并不比村民多，还反反复复都只是担心自家三个孩子，最终就放过了村长。

另一头，商非凡和阿呆瞬移回了莫约镇。

那里，郎沐早已在等着他们。

阿呆刚抬起小爪子。

他老爹就把他随手一丢，人就冲了过去。

“阿沐！”商非凡一眼看到站在镇口的郎沐，冲上去一把抱住。

“你怎么知道我今天现在回来？”老商无比欣喜。

郎沐轻笑，摸摸爱人的短发：“感觉到的。说说吧，你这几天都干了什么？”

简直让他提心吊胆。

另外，他能明显感觉到商非凡实力提升了一大截。

商非凡一拉他的手：“走，我慢慢跟你说。这次收获不小。哦，对了，系统那边还没给我任务完成的奖励，等我来催催。”

寒冷的冬风吹过阿呆的头毛，被落在镇口的阿呆：……爸爸们啊，你们是不是忘了什么？

“噗嗤！”每天都会到镇口散步的郎老夫人快步走过来，抄起可怜兮兮的小阿呆：“我的小宝贝哦，被爸爸们忘记了呀，奶奶等下帮你打他们啊。”

那两只大的不仅忘了儿子，也忘了她这个姥姥和镇子上的其他人，两人一见面眼中就只有彼此，其他人都成了背景。

“曾奶奶~~”阿呆委屈坏了，一脑袋扎入老夫人的怀中。连老人的称呼又差辈这点都忘记纠正了。

但不到一会儿，小家伙就兴奋起来，用他特有的呆萌神情说：“曾奶奶，我跟你说我这几天的历险记呀，特别特别惊险哦！”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 245: Return Arrangements and Daily Life (Part 3)

The next day, the villagers of Tiancan Village had no idea that Shang Feifan had returned. However, they did notice that the village chief's eldest son was also missing.

With a face full of worry and grief, the village chief said to the villagers with a bitter smile, "Zhuangzhuang was worried about his younger brother and sister, so he insisted on running out to find them."

The villagers comforted the village chief one after another, while in their hearts, they all scolded the chief's eldest son for being thoughtless. How could he just sneak out like that? Was he not afraid of running into trouble outside?

Tiancan Village went on as usual, living a plain and impoverished life of working at sunrise and resting at sunset.

A few days later, as expected, people came to the village to inquire about the situation.

The villagers explained the situation of Cang Ya taking the cubs away very clearly, but they knew absolutely nothing about anything else.

Among those people, someone indeed used an innate skill like mind control on the villagers and asked about the strange cub, Ah Dai.

But the villagers only knew that Ah Dai had been adopted by an outsider, and for some reason, had actively chosen to leave with Cang Ya and the others.

In the villagers' minds, Ah Dai's adoption was just for show. Fearing being abandoned again, he had chosen to proactively leave that outsider first, preferring to follow Cang Ya and the others to learn skills and become a mercenary.

Those people repeatedly questioned the villagers about what Ah Dai's adoptive father looked like, what he did, and where he came from.

The one they questioned the most was the village chief.

Under control, the village chief spoke of everything he knew.

Seeing that the village chief knew no more than the other villagers and was repeatedly just worrying about his own three children, those people finally let him go.

On the other side, Shang Feifan and Ah Dai teleported back to Moyue Town.

There, Lang Mu had already been waiting for them.

Ah Dai had just raised his little paw.

His daddy casually tossed him aside and rushed forward.

"A'Mu!" Shang Feifan spotted Lang Mu standing at the entrance of the town at first glance, rushing up to pull him into a tight embrace.

"How did you know I would be back at this exact time today?" Old Shang was incredibly delighted.

Lang Mu chuckled softly, stroking his lover's short hair. "I felt it. Tell me, what have you been up to these past few days?"

It had kept him on tenterhooks.

In addition, he could clearly sense that Shang Feifan's strength had increased by a massive margin.

Shang Feifan pulled his hand. "Come, I'll tell you slowly. The harvest this time is quite substantial. Oh, right, the system hasn't given me the reward for completing the mission yet. I'll have to urge it later."

The cold winter wind blew through Ah Dai's hair. Left behind at the town entrance, Ah Dai: *...Daddies, did you forget something?*

"Pfft!" Old Madam Lang, who took a walk to the town entrance every day, walked over quickly and scooped up the pitiful little Ah Dai. "Oh, my little baby, you were forgotten by your daddies. Grandma will help you beat them up later."

Those two big ones had not only forgotten their son, but also her, the grandmother, and everyone else in the town. The moment they met, there was only each other in their eyes, and everyone else became background noise.

"Great-grandma~~" Ah Dai was incredibly aggrieved, burying his head into the old lady's embrace. He even forgot to correct the fact that the old lady's form of address was off by a generation again.

But in no time, the little fellow grew excited again, saying with his uniquely adorable, dazed expression, "Great-grandma, let me tell you about my adventures over the past few days. It was super, super thrilling!"

chunks.chapterTitle: 第246章 路德维希之死 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第246章 路德维希之死

路德维希再次恢复意识，就发现自己被串在一根绳子上，被驱赶着进入一座诡异的城池。

驱赶他、看管他们这些俘虏的人是模样怪异的巨齿兽人，一个个看起来凶神恶煞，而且极为警惕。

当发现有人恢复神智，好几个巨齿兽人一起涌上前来，拿着手中长矛就戳他。

如果不是他身上的魔法袍靠谱，这些巨齿兽人能在他身上戳出几个窟窿！

不疼，可羞辱性极大。

巨齿兽人一边戳，还一边骂骂咧咧：“又来一个！这次可不会让你们给跑了！”

“这老家伙似乎不怕我们的矛尖！”

“抽他！抽到他不能动为止！”

几根长矛不再戳刺他，改成用力抽打，而且尽朝着路德维希的头脸抽。

路德维希要气疯了。

他想使用魔法，却发现自己四肢无力，魔力更像是被封禁一样。

没有魔力，他就是一个肉身不算强大的孱弱老人，现在全靠身上的魔法袍和其他炼金饰品保护他。

巨齿兽人们抽打一会，发现路德维希脸上连个印子都没有留下，顿时脸色大变。

“坏了！这个老家伙很可能跟前面逃过两次的那个年轻兽人一样，小心他弄坏绳子逃跑！”

路德维希正死命搜刮自己的力量，想要动用储物戒指，从里面取出可以解决他目前困境的宝贝。

可那些巨齿兽人忽然冲上来，揪住他的头发就对他一顿拳打脚踢，在虐打中，更是抢走他身上所有炼金饰品。

更过分的是，那些巨齿兽人竟然还在强行脱他的魔法袍和脚上的魔法靴。

路德维希从没有受到这样的侮辱，忍不住发出怒斥。

可这些巨齿兽人不但没有因此停下他们的过分行为，反而大声呼喝、彼此提醒：“这老家伙果然神智清醒，揍他，把他揍成烂泥，只要留口气就行！千万不能让人跑了！”

魔法袍和魔法靴以及其他所有能保护他的物品全都被剥离，路德维希顿时成了真正的孱弱老人，空有一身魔力却无法施展。

巨齿兽人带着对连续两次从他们手中逃脱的年轻兽人的恨，全都发泄到了路德维希身上。

没有保护的老法圣被几个巨齿兽人暴揍得奄奄一息。

巨齿兽人害怕他逃跑，不但打肿了他的头脸、打落了他满口牙齿，更打断了他的胳膊和双腿，肋骨更是断了好几根。

路德维希现在除了一根脊椎和头骨还算完好，身上的骨头就没几根完整的。

这样的路德维希无法走路，完全就是被绳索上串连的其他俘虏硬拖着走。

路德维希疼到想大声惨叫，但他端了那么多年，直到现在也无法拉下脸面，只强行忍耐发出痛苦的抽气声。

巨齿兽人见他如此“顽强”，更是害怕他在城门口逃脱，揍他的手越发重。

路德维希眼眶崩裂，口中呕出一口口发黑的鲜血，只觉得自己内脏都烂成一团。

这些巨齿兽人是真的就只给他留了一口气。

他堂堂一代法圣，眼看就要摸到法神的境界，怎么就落到这种境地？

那个无法用言语描述的可怕存在到底是怎么冒出来的，又为什么会针对他和天空之城？

路德维希心中有猜测，怀疑那可怕存在就是这个世界的古神力量残留。

他现在站在外来神灵那一边，这个世界的古神自然会针对他。

只是他以为古神的力量都已经被厄穆克拉索牵制住……他知道厄穆克拉索被众神力量封印住，但也因此造成众神也没有办法腾出手来。

而以他的实力，不说能在没有神灵的兽人大陆横行，至少自保没有问题。

而且他已经足够小心，来到兽人大陆这么多年，他一直在想法提升实力，哪怕成为真神教教主，也没有大肆发展或暴露自己的身份。

他只是让跟着他一起来还活着的魔法师们帮他调-教那些真神教教徒，把一个草台班子给拉扯成了一个能与祭司宫抗衡的庞然大物。

他也亲自拟定了对虎国高层的渗透计划。

原本一切都发展得很顺利，按照他的设想，很快他们就能把整个虎国收到手中，让虎国成为真神教的发展大基盘。

但也不知道哪里出了差错，虎国高层尤其那个虎王忽然就变得精明起来，竟然接二连三挖掘出他们深埋在虎国内部的钉子，还一一拔除。

他们更对真神教内部非常了解一样，抓捕他们教徒几乎一抓一个准，无论教徒怎么躲避都没用。

还有他们安排在虎国王城的种种措施，从让厄穆克拉索的神力降临到用不死尸祸害整个王城乃至虎国，再由真神教出面收拾烂摊子……等一系列计划全都莫名其妙败北！

有能力做到这点还让他摸不着真正敌人在哪的人不多。

他的手下给他报过几个名字，说就是这几个人在王城出现后，他们真神教才开始变得特别不顺利。

其中有三个人的名字让他最为在意，天残谷主、拉斐尔郎沐，以及一个叫阿瑞斯商的炼金师。

阿瑞斯商听说还能炼制空间道具，对于这样一个技术型人才，听说还是一个纨绔性子的年轻人，路德维希并没有怎么放在心上。

倒是那个拉斐尔郎沐，据说还是特调局的特别调查官，专门负责抓捕和调查真神教信徒。另外听说此人还是虎王的私生子，虽然是个假的。

这个拉斐尔郎沐也曾是他们真神教谋夺虎国计划中的一颗棋子。

但这颗棋子不知道怎么回事就脱离了他们的控制。

路德维希已经下令让手下重点调查这个人，并盯梢他的一举一动。

但如果说到他最怀疑的人，则是最后一人，天残谷主！

路德维希知道天残谷主就是洛伦米尔顿。

他还知道洛伦米尔顿比他更早和厄穆克拉索接触，并更早地加入真神教。

但可能洛伦的成神之路和厄穆克拉索的指引不同，也可能是因为洛伦米尔顿的野心更大。

当然更可能是他路德维希带着一众魔法师出现后，洛伦米尔顿自感势单力薄——他也有少数魔法师跟随他，但总体人数比他这边少得多，无法和他们竞争，就自觉退出了刚开始经营的真神教，转而去经营独属于自己的新组织。

他们并没有撕破脸，也算是友好分手。

他一直关注着洛伦米尔顿，他虽然看不上这家伙使出的种种卑劣手段，也不得不承认，对方就是靠着这些手段才能顺利走到现在，而他……一个老牌法圣最后也不得不选择和对方同样的路子来延续自己的未来。

所以现在天空之城出事，他第一个怀疑的就是洛伦米尔顿。

他怀疑对方的势力已经发展到可以吞并真神教的程度，洛伦米尔顿想要更多资源，想要更大的地盘，而想要养活更多信众，就需要大片能耕种的土地，那有着大量农田的天空之城自然会让对方垂涎。

说来，洛伦米尔顿搞出来的那个天残谷势力，里面的天残兽人似乎都有些古怪。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 246: The Death of Ludwig (Part 1)

When Ludwig regained consciousness, he found himself strung along a rope, being herded toward a bizarre, eerie city.

The guards driving and monitoring them were strange-looking, grotesque-faced Orcs with jagged teeth. Every single one of them looked ferocious, murderous, and extremely vigilant.

Noticing that someone had regained consciousness, several of the jagged-toothed Orcs swarmed over, jabbing at him with the long spears in their hands.

Had it not been for the reliable defense of his magic robe, these jagged-toothed Orcs could easily have poked several holes right through his body!

It didn't hurt much, but the humiliation was absolute.

As they poked him, the jagged-toothed Orcs cursed incessantly: "Another one! We won't let you escape this time!"

"This old bastard doesn't seem to fear our spearheads!"

"Lash him! Beat him until he can't move!"

The long spears ceased their jabbing, replaced by heavy, vicious lashes—aimed squarely at Ludwig's head and face.

Ludwig was driven to the verge of madness.

He tried to channel his magic, only to find his limbs heavy and powerless, his magical energy seemingly sealed away entirely.

Without magic, he was nothing more than a frail old man with an ordinary physique. Right now, he was relying entirely on his magic robe and other alchemical accessories for protection.

After thrashing him for a moment, the jagged-toothed Orcs noticed that not even a single mark had been left on Ludwig's face, and their expressions altered drastically.

"Dammit! This old bastard is likely the same as that young Orc who escaped twice earlier! Be careful he doesn't break the rope and get away!"

Ludwig was frantically searching through his inner strength, desperately trying to access his spatial ring to retrieve a treasure capable of resolving his current predicament.

Suddenly, however, the jagged-toothed Orcs rushed forward, grabbing him by the hair and raining a flurry of punches and kicks upon him. Amidst the abuse, they stripped away all the alchemical accessories adorning his body.

To make matters worse, these jagged-toothed Orcs proceeded to forcefully rip off his magic robe and the magical boots on his feet.

Never in his life had Ludwig suffered such degradation. A furious roar escaped his lips.

Yet, far from halting their outrageous behavior, the jagged-toothed Orcs only shouted louder, reminding one another: "This old bastard really is conscious! Beat him! Beat him into a pulp as long as you leave him breathing! Whatever you do, don't let him get away!"

Stripped of his magic robe, magic boots, and every other item capable of shielding him, Ludwig was instantly reduced to a truly feeble old man, possessing vast reservoirs of magic yet utterly unable to unleash them.

Channeling all their bitter resentment toward the young Orc who had slipped through their fingers twice consecutively, the jagged-toothed Orcs vented every ounce of their fury upon Ludwig.

Left completely unprotected, the aged Saint-tier Mage was beaten by several jagged-toothed Orcs to within an inch of his life.

Terrified that he might escape, the Orcs not only battered his head and face until they swelled horribly and knocked out every last one of his teeth, but they also fractured his arms and legs, snapping several of his ribs into the bargain.

Aside from his spine and skull, which remained relatively intact, virtually every bone in Ludwig's body had been shattered.

In this state, Ludwig could no longer walk; he was simply dragged along the ground, hauled mercilessly by the other captives tied to the same rope.

The pain was so agonizing that Ludwig wanted to shriek at the top of his lungs. Yet, having maintained his lofty dignity for so many years, he could not bring himself to lower his pride even now. He could only clench his teeth in forced endurance, letting out miserable, ragged gasges.

Seeing how "resilient" he was, and terrified that he might somehow slip away at the city gates, the jagged-toothed Orcs rained blows down upon him with even greater ferocity.

Ludwig's eye sockets ruptured, and he vomited dark, congealed blood, feeling as though his internal organs had all liquefied into a wretched mash.

These jagged-toothed Orcs were truly leaving him with nothing more than a single breath of life.

How had he—a towering Saint-tier Mage on the very threshold of the Divine Mage realm—fallen to such a wretched pass?

Where on earth had that indescribable, terrifying entity sprung from, and why was it targeting him and the Sky City?

A suspicion gnawed at Ludwig's heart: he suspected that terrifying entity was the residual power of the ancient gods of this realm.

Now that he stood firmly on the side of the foreign deities, it was only natural for the ancient gods of this world to target him.

He had simply assumed that the power of the ancient gods was entirely held in check by Eumuklaso... He knew that Eumuklaso had been sealed away by the power of the pantheon, but he had believed that this stalemate meant the gods themselves were utterly powerless to spare any attention.

Given his own strength—let alone running rampant across the Orc Continent where true gods were absent—he had figured self-preservation would pose no problem at all.

Moreover, he had been exceedingly cautious. In all his years on the Orc Continent, he had constantly sought ways to elevate his strength. Even after becoming the Hierarch of the True God Cult, he had never recklessly expanded or exposed his true identity.

Instead, he had simply allowed the surviving mages who accompanied him to whip the True God Cult's devotees into shape, turning a ragtag mob into a behemoth capable of contending with the Priest Palace.

He had even personally drafted the infiltration plan targeting the upper echelons of the Tiger Kingdom.

Originally, everything had been progressing smoothly. According to his blueprints, it wouldn't be long before they seized complete control of the Tiger Kingdom, turning it into a massive foundation for the True God Cult's expansion.

Yet somewhere, something had gone terribly wrong. The higher-ups of the Tiger Kingdom—particularly the Tiger King himself—had suddenly grown shrewd, unearthing the sleeper agents they had buried deep within the kingdom one after another, thoroughly uprooting them.

They seemed to possess an intimate, frighteningly detailed understanding of the True God Cult's inner workings. Whenever they hunted down cultists, their arrests were unerringly precise; no matter how the cultists hid, it was all in vain.

Furthermore, all the various measures they had deployed within the Tiger King City—from plunging Eumuklaso's divine power into the realm to plaguing the entire royal city and the Tiger Kingdom with undead scourges, only for the True God Cult to step in and clean up the mess... one after another, this entire series of elaborate plans had inexplicably collapsed into failure!

Few people possessed the capability to pull this off while keeping the true enemy shrouded in shadow.

His subordinates had reported several names to him, claiming that it was only after these individuals appeared in the royal city that the True God Cult's operations began to encounter such bizarre and frustrating obstacles.

Among them, three names concerned him the most: the Master of the Heaven-Severing Valley, Raphael Langmu, and an alchemist named Ares Shang.

Ares Shang was rumored to possess the ability to forge spatial artifacts. As for such a technically skilled talent who was reportedly a dissolute young wastrel, Ludwig had never truly taken him seriously.

As for Raphael Langmu, he was rumored to be a Special Investigation Officer of the Special Investigation Bureau, specifically tasked with hunting down and investigating True God Cultists. In addition, rumor had it that this man was the illegitimate son of the Tiger King—though that claim was ultimately a fabrication.

This Raphael Langmu had once been a chess piece in their grand design to usurp the Tiger Kingdom.

Yet somehow, this chess piece had broken free of their control.

Ludwig had already ordered his subordinates to prioritize investigating this individual and keep a close eye on his every move.

However, if there was one person he suspected above all others, it was the final name: the Master of the Heaven-Severing Valley!

Ludwig knew very well that the Master of the Heaven-Severing Valley was none other than Loren Milton.

He also knew that Loren Milton had made contact with Eumuklaso earlier than he had, joining the True God Cult at an even earlier date.

Perhaps Loren's path to divinity diverged from Eumuklaso's guidance, or perhaps Loren Milton simply possessed even greater ambitions.

Then again, it was far more likely that when he, Ludwig, arrived with a retinue of mages, Loren Milton had felt hopelessly outmatched—though Loren had a small faction of mages following him, their overall numbers paled in comparison to Ludwig's, making direct competition impossible. Consequently, Loren had wisely withdrawn from the True God Cult he had initially helped cultivate, turning instead to forge an exclusive new organization entirely of his own.

They had never had a falling out; it could be considered an amicable parting of ways.

Ludwig had always kept a close eye on Loren Milton. While he held the man's various despicable and underhanded methods in utter contempt, he had to admit that it was precisely by relying on such tactics that his opponent had managed to reach this point. And he... an old, venerable Saint-tier Mage, had ultimately been forced down that very same path to prolong his own future.

Thus, now that disaster had struck the Sky City, his very first suspect was Loren Milton.

He suspected that the man's faction had grown powerful enough to swallow the True God Cult whole. Loren Milton wanted more resources, a larger territory, and sustaining a greater populace of followers required vast tracts of arable land. Naturally, the Sky City, with its immense expanses of fertile fields, would make the man drool with greed.

Come to think of it, those Heaven-Severing Orcs belonging to the Heaven-Severing Valley faction that Loren Milton had conjured up all seemed somewhat peculiar.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第246章 路德维希之死 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
不但人人都能觉醒血脉天赋能力，而且他们的人数也在以一种不合理的速度增长。

几万兽人看起来不多，但一个封闭的小村落怎么可能在短短数年内就培养出几万青壮兽人？

他又不是不知道那个天残村的情况。

总之，他一直在警惕洛伦米尔顿。

但他以为洛伦米尔顿不会蠢到一开始就对上他们真神教，就像他清楚洛伦米尔顿的底细一样，洛伦米尔顿也了解他们的能力。

为此，他们之间还有不少合作。

现在他们两方对上，那就是彼此消耗，对彼此都没有任何好处，只会让别人得渔翁之利。

可如果不是洛伦米尔顿，又会是谁？

谁有这样的力量能操纵那样的可怕存在来对付他？

还有这里到底是哪里？

路德维希不断想着这些问题。

他只能让这些问题来分离他对痛苦的感知，他必须让自己大脑忙碌起来。

为此，他甚至没有去想失去那个气运值几乎满格的小幼崽对他的损失——想起来就让他心痛到极点，还是不想了！

如果他能更早一点得到那个方脑袋小幼崽，如果他能更早一点掠夺对方的气运，也许他现在已经一脚踏入法神境界。

也不至于在面对那个可怕存在时，连还手之力都没有！

路德维希还抱着希望。

希望那个可怕存在没有发现他那间实验室的秘密，希望对方没有破坏整座天空之城。

只要那个气运人偶还在，他也许还有机会能从这个绝境中逃脱。

看，他没有死在那个可怕存在手下，这不就表明他的运气还不是太糟糕。

这样想的路德维希没有看到一股庞大的怨气冲入他的身体，怨气中还夹杂着一缕诡异的黑光。

如果是没有失去魔力的他，他也许能察觉这些。

但现在他的眼睛、他的感知、他的精神力……全都弱到和普通兽人差不多，身体素质还不如普通兽人。

就算此时他身体因为那些怨气和诅咒有所反应，他也只以为是被那些巨齿兽人暴揍导致的痛苦。

忍住！他一定要挺过这关！

只要能让他有使用魔力的机会，他就一定能解决目前的困境。

这些可恶的卑贱的巨齿兽人，他一个都不会放过，他会让他们都付出应有的代价！

还有躲在背后操纵这一切的阴谋者，他也一定会找出来！

路德维希在心中暗暗发誓，肿胀着两只眼睛，眼睁睁地看着自己被拖入那诡异的城池中。

这是一座不该存在的城。

仔细看，它的墙砖竟然全都是由巨大的书籍堆叠而成，城墙歪曲出怪异的弧度。

书本上刻满看不懂的远古文字，也许是神文。那些文字并非静止，它们如同蛆虫般缓缓蠕动，时而重组，时而扭曲，仿佛在无声尖叫。

城门是由无数文字组成。

这些文字不断变化，有时是赞美诗，有时是诅咒文，更多时候是毫无逻辑的字符组合。偶尔某个词句会突然渗出暗红色的液体，顺着墙壁蜿蜒而下，在城门口汇聚成小小的血洼。

城楼上挂着巨大的牌匾，上面的文字时而清晰，时而模糊。

“知识之城？”路德维希在心中呢喃出这座城的名字。

他仿佛听到有谁在他耳边说：“欢迎来到知识的殿堂……或者地狱。”

进入城中，能听到锁链拖地的哗啦声，让人闻之恐惧。

脚下的石板并非固定——它们是由浮动文字铺成的路，每一步都会让字符扭曲变形，仿佛踩在活物上。

街道两侧的建筑并非普通房屋，而是高耸的书架，每一层都塞满了像是活着的书籍。

那些书本的封面长着溃烂的眼睛，书页边缘探出细长的黑色触须，每当有人经过，它们便会发出沙沙的低语：“读我……读我……”

空气中弥漫着认知污染，哪怕只是轻轻吸入一口，脑海中就会浮现出不属于自己的记忆碎片——某个兽人战士的濒死惨叫，一位学者的疯狂呓语，甚至是一些根本无法理解的、不知从哪里来的禁忌知识。

路德维希身体一震，勉强抬起头直直地看向知识之城的最中央。

那里，十二座扭曲的象牙白高塔刺破铅灰色的天空，塔身布满眼睛形状的镂空雕花。

这些眼睛正散发出宛如鬼火版的光芒，数不清的眼睛以不同频率眨动，投射出变幻莫测的几何图形和各种记号，将整座城市笼罩在癫狂的光影之中。

无数声音涌入耳中，像是有无数人在不断重复着支离破碎的知识片段。

鲜血从路德维希和其他无意识的兽人耳中流出。

路德维希发出了惨叫。

那些声音太多太吵，无数多的知识强行塞入他的大脑。

砰！路德维希的脑袋爆炸开来。

就真物理性质的爆炸。

但路德维希这样都没有死。

进入这座城的人，在他们的知识没有被挖掘干净前，他们就不会死去。

路德维希没有看到，那些进入城中的无意识者身体表面的皮肉蠕动着化作一个个文字。

而他的身体情况更糟糕。

那些无意识者感受不到自己被吸干、被剥夺一切，转化为单纯知识的痛苦。

这也许是知识之神最后的善意？

可路德维希神智清醒，他也因此彻骨感受到自己被挖空的全部过程！

他要逃！

他要逃出去！

他不甘心就这么死去！

只可惜知识之神已经陨落，如今统治这座城的，仅仅是祂神格碎片形成的一缕混乱意识。它没有形体，没有理智，只剩下对知识的扭曲渴望——它吞噬灵魂，不是因为饥饿，而是因为它需要维持自己的存在。

每个踏入这座城的活物，都会成为它的养分。

路德维希作为一个老牌法圣，他拥有的知识是足以让他骄傲的。

原本就算如此，路德维希也无法引起这座知识之城的主人，混乱意识的注意。

但他身携庞大的怨气，还有来自诅咒之神的诅咒。

混乱意识感知到同为神灵的力量，就下意识向路德维希投注了一丝关注。

真是……好久没有看到知识储备量如此丰富的养料。

等等！这养料竟然携带了让它讨厌的诅咒之神的力量？

就算是知识之神也不想得罪诅咒之神。混乱意识别看意识混乱，可它对诅咒之神的忌惮简直深植于意识最深处。

既然是诅咒之神看中的小玩具，那就先让诅咒之神玩个愉快吧。

混乱意识轻轻一弹，就把已经变成一团烂肉的路德维希给弹入了“知识抽取池”。

路德维希最后看到的场景是无数巨大的齿轮，他躺在齿轮上，被传送、被一次次碾压。

看不见的光线钻入他的身体，每当他被“榨取”一次，就从他身上抽取出一条墨水般的丝线。

路德维希不住哀嚎，他开始哀求。

他以为自己用了很大的声音在乞求，实际上他的声音只有他自己能听到。

咔嚓，咔嚓，齿轮不断滚动。

路德维希反复不断地感受到自己被碾压、被榨取、被抽魂……

Chapter 246: The Death of Ludwig (Part 2)

Not only could every single one of them awaken innate bloodline talents, but their numbers were also swelling at an absurd, unreasonable rate.

Tens of thousands of Orcs might not sound like much on paper, but how could an isolated little village foster tens of thousands of able-bodied Orc warriors in the span of just a few short years?

It wasn't as if he was ignorant of the situation in that Heaven-Severing Village.

In short, he had always remained on high alert against Loren Milton.

However, he had assumed Loren Milton wouldn't be foolish enough to openly lock horns with the True God Cult from the very beginning. Just as he knew Loren Milton's bottom line inside and out, Loren Milton likewise understood their capabilities.

Because of this, they had engaged in quite a few collaborations.

If their two factions were to clash now, it would only result in mutual exhaustion—benefiting neither side and leaving a third party to reap the fisherman's spoils.

Yet, if it wasn't Loren Milton, who else could it be?

Who possessed such terrifying might to manipulate that monstrous entity against him?

And where on earth was this place?

Ludwig's mind raced as he wrestled with these questions.

He forced his mind to chew on these mysteries simply to distract himself from the agonizing waves of pain; he had to keep his brain occupied.

To that end, he didn't even dare dwell on the loss of that little cub whose destiny value was practically maxed out—the mere thought of it filled his heart with a stabbing, excruciating grief, so he quickly forced it out of his mind!

If only he had captured that square-headed little cub a bit sooner, if only he had plundered the other's destiny sooner, perhaps he would already have stepped foot into the Divine Mage realm by now.

He wouldn't have been left utterly defenseless when facing that terrifying entity!

Ludwig still harbored a shred of hope.

He hoped that terrifying entity hadn't discovered the secrets hidden within his laboratory, hoped it hadn't destroyed the entirety of the Sky City.

As long as that destiny puppet remained intact, perhaps he still had a chance to claw his way out of this desperate dead end.

Look—he hadn't died under the hands of that monstrous entity, which surely proved his luck wasn't entirely exhausted yet.

Lost in these thoughts, Ludwig failed to notice a massive surge of resentment pouring directly into his body, mixed inextricably with a wisp of eerie black light.

Had he still possessed his magic, he might have sensed it.

But right now, his eyesight, his perception, his spiritual force... everything had withered away until it was roughly on par with an ordinary Orc, his physical constitution even inferior to theirs.

Even when his body reacted to those malefic怨气 (resentments) and curses, he simply assumed the torment was the lingering agony inflicted by the brutal beating of the jagged-toothed Orcs.

Endure! He had to push through this trial!

The moment he regained the opportunity to channel his magic, he would undoubtedly resolve this current predicament.

These damned, lowly jagged-toothed Orcs—he wouldn't spare a single one of them! He would make every last one of them pay the price they deserved!

And that mastermind lurking in the shadows pulling the strings, he would track them down as well!

Ludwig silently swore a blood oath in his heart, his swollen eyes glaring blankly as he was dragged further into that bizarre, nightmarish city.

This was a city that had no right to exist.

Upon closer inspection, its ramparts were constructed entirely out of colossal, tightly stacked tomes, the city walls twisting into unnatural, grotesque angles.

The books were covered in incomprehensible ancient scripts, perhaps divine runes. These characters were not static; they wriggled and squirmed slowly like maggots, constantly reforming and distorting as if silently shrieking.

The city gates were composed of countless characters in perpetual flux. At times they formed hymns of praise, at times curses, and more often than not, illogical combinations of glyphs. Every so often, a certain phrase or word would suddenly ooze dark red liquid, winding its way down the walls to pool in tiny puddles of blood right at the threshold.

A massive plaque hung from the gate tower, the characters upon it flickering between clarity and blur.

"City of Knowledge?" Ludwig murmured the city's name in his heart.

He seemed to hear someone whispering right beside his ear: "Welcome to the halls of knowledge... or perhaps, hell."

Entering the city, one could hear the chilling, ominous clatter of heavy chains dragging across the ground, striking terror into the marrow of anyone who heard it.

The cobblestones beneath their feet were not fixed in place—they were pathways paved from shifting, floating text. Every single step caused the glyphs to warp and distort, as though one were treading upon living flesh.

The structures lining both sides of the street were not ordinary houses, but towering bookshelves, every single tier crammed with books that appeared disturbingly alive.

The covers of those tomes bore rotting, festering eyes, while slender black tentacles poked out from the edges of their pages. Whenever anyone passed by, they would hiss in raspy whispers: "Read me... Read me..."

The air was thick with cognitive pollution. Even a single shallow inhalation was enough to flood the mind with fragments of memories that didn't belong to one—the dying shrieks of an Orc warrior, the frantic, raving nonsense of a scholar, or even forbidden knowledge of unknown origin that defied all mortal comprehension.

Ludwig shuddered violently, forcing his head up to stare directly at the absolute center of the City of Knowledge.

There, twelve twisted, ivory-white spires pierced the lead-grey sky, their surfaces riddled with hollowed-out, eye-shaped carvings.

Those eyes emitted a spectral, ghost-fire glow. Countless eyes blinked at erratic, desynchronized frequencies, casting shifting geometric patterns and arcane symbols that plunged the entire metropolis into a frenzy of chaotic light and shadow.

A cacophony of countless voices flooded his ears, as though millions of people were endlessly repeating fragmented, shattered shards of knowledge.

Blood streamed from the ears of Ludwig and the other unconscious Orcs.

A piercing shriek tore from Ludwig's throat.

The voices were overwhelmingly loud and chaotic, a vast, crushing ocean of knowledge forcibly crammed into his brain.

*Bang!* Ludwig's head exploded.

Literally, physically exploded.

Yet even in this state, Ludwig did not die.

Those who entered this city would not find the release of death until every last scrap of knowledge within them had been thoroughly mined and hollowed out.

Ludwig could not see how the flesh on the bodies of those unconscious wretches writhed and morphed into words.

His own physical state, however, was far more wretched.

Those unconscious souls could not feel the torment of being sucked dry, stripped of everything they were, and converted into pure knowledge.

Perhaps this was the final, twisted mercy of the God of Knowledge?

Yet Ludwig was completely conscious, and because of this, he felt every agonizing second of his being hollowed out to the bone with crystal-clear clarity!

He had to escape!

He had to get out of here!

He refused to reconcile himself to dying like this!

Alas, the God of Knowledge had already fallen. What ruled this city now was merely a scrap of chaotic consciousness born from its shattered divine spark. It possessed no form, no reason, only a twisted, insatiable craving for knowledge. It devoured souls not out of hunger, but because it needed them to sustain its own pathetic existence.

Every living thing that crossed into this city became its nutrient.

As a veteran Saint-tier Mage, Ludwig possessed a wealth of knowledge great enough to fill him with pride.

Normally, even with such a hoard, Ludwig wouldn't have caught the attention of the City of Knowledge's master—that chaotic consciousness.

However, he carried a monumental mountain of *怨气* (resentment), compounded by a curse bestowed by the God of Curses.

Sensing a power akin to that of a deity, the chaotic consciousness instinctively cast a sliver of attention toward Ludwig.

My, my... It had been so long since it had laid eyes on a nutrient with such a rich reserve of knowledge.

Wait! This nutrient actually carried the power of the God of Curses, which it loathed?

Even the God of Knowledge had no wish to cross paths with the God of Curses. Fragmented and chaotic though its awareness might be, a deep-seated dread of the God of Curses was etched into the very deepest recesses of its being.

Since this was a little plaything favored by the God of Curses, it might as well let the God of Curses have its fun first.

With a gentle flick of its chaotic will, Ludwig—now reduced to a mere lump of mangled flesh—was tossed straight into the "Knowledge Extraction Pool."

The final scene Ludwig beheld was an expanse of countless massive gears. He lay across the cogs, being conveyed forward, crushed and ground down over and over again.

Invisible rays of light bored into his body. Every single time he was "extracted," a thread as dark as ink was forcefully pulled from his form.

Ludwig wailed incessantly, reduced to begging for mercy.

He believed he was crying out at the top of his lungs, but in reality, his desperate pleas could only be heard by himself.

*Clack, clack, clack*—the gears ground on without end.

Over and over, Ludwig experienced the cyclical torment of being crushed, squeezed dry, and having his soul ripped away...

chunks.chapterTitle: 第246章 路德维希之死 (Part 3)
chunks.chineseText:
痛苦已经成了他剩下人生的唯一旋律。

最后的最后，路德维希想：如果有地狱，这里一定就是地狱。

他恨！恨到不知道该找谁报复。

他不甘心就这么死去，还是不知道仇人是谁的死去。

他要报复，他一定要做些什么！

洛伦米尔顿！肯定是你。一定是你也想抢夺那个气运值几乎满格的幼崽，才会暗中偷袭他，把他害到这种地步。

路德维希痛苦地凝聚自己最后的灵魂之力和所有怨恨，用最恶毒的咒语诅咒卑鄙无耻的洛伦米尔顿。

那凝聚了路德维希所有恨意和不甘的恶毒诅咒化作一支黑箭，直直射向远方。

噗呲！路德维希仅剩下的烂肉彻底被磨成了黑色的墨汁，从齿轮间一点点滴落。

混乱意识察觉了那支凝聚了无尽仇恨和诅咒的黑箭，但它没管。

远在莫约镇的商非凡忽然抬起头，看向通透高远的天空。

就在刚刚的一刹那，他似乎感知到一股无法言喻的欢愉传递到他的灵魂中。

就像是一只只小幼崽的小嫩爪爪，在亲昵地碰触他，在向他道谢和告别……

郎沐通过同心契约也感知到了那无比的舒畅和快乐。

他跟商非凡一样，抬头看向天空。

“那些幼崽的灵魂被解放了，他们已经回归天地本源。”商非凡下意识说出。

郎沐抓住他的胳膊，轻轻：“嗯！”

“路德维希？”郎沐听商非凡提起他很可能遇到了法圣路德维希，也是一阵后怕。

商非凡低下头看爱人：“刚才……应该和他有关。”

“你觉得对方现在是生还是死？”郎沐又问。

商非凡很理解郎沐的担心，对于一名八级的老牌法圣，再怎么小心也不为过。

“我没办法感知到知识之神那边的情况，但我有个强烈预感，他就算没死，情况也会糟糕万分。”

气运反噬可不是开玩笑的，更何况还有诅咒之神亲自“赐予”的诅咒。

“既然那些幼崽的灵魂得到解放，至少路德维希现在已经衰弱到无法再困住他们。”

“路德维希不是问题，如果他冒头，那我们再想法解决他就是。”商非凡眼看自己也一路冲击到八级顶阶，自然敢说出这样的大话。

“好！”郎沐也跟着安心。

法圣又如何，他们连邪神都对上了，还在乎一个法圣吗？

“我们得专心解决黑水荒原的岩浆爆发问题了，经过我这几日的勘察，地底岩浆已经越来越活跃，必须赶紧泄流。”

“泄洪渠道规划出来了吗？”

“已经拟定的差不多，现在就等你这个施工大队长指挥不死尸大军开挖渠道。”

商非凡笑起来，“好，接下来就交给我。”

郎沐迟疑片刻，到底还是说出：“彭石城地形特殊，又距离岩浆爆发点很近，那里非常适合作为一个巨大的泄洪湖。当然，位于半山腰的彭石城不会有事。可如果我们想要让岩浆集中到那里，地底压力很可能会导致彭石城所在的山变成一座火山……”

Chapter 246: The Death of Ludwig (Part 3)

Pain had become the sole melody remaining in his existence.

In the end, as his consciousness faded into the abyss, Ludwig thought: If there is a hell, this must be it.

He hated! Hated with a fury so profound he didn't even know whom to seek vengeance against.

He refused to die like this—to perish without even knowing the identity of his enemy.

He wanted revenge! He had to do something!

Loren Milton! It must have been you. It had to be you, greedy for that cub whose destiny value was practically full, who launched a sneak attack from the shadows and drove him to this wretched end.

With agonizing effort, Ludwig gathered the final remnants of his soul force and all his accumulated malice, casting the most venomous curse imaginable upon that despicable, shameless Loren Milton.

That malevolent curse, condensing every ounce of Ludwig's hatred and unwillingness, transformed into a black arrow that shot straight off into the distance.

*Puchi!* The pathetic shred of flesh Ludwig had left was ground completely into black ink, dripping down drop by drop from between the rotating cogs.

The chaotic consciousness perceived that black arrow, condensed from endless hatred and curses, but it paid it no mind.

Far away in Moyue Town, Shang Fanfan suddenly lifted his head, gazing up at the vast, crystalline expanse of the sky.

At that exact, fleeting moment, he seemed to sense a wave of ineffable joy washing into his soul.

It felt as though countless tiny, tender paws of little cubs were affectionately brushing against him, murmuring words of gratitude and bidding him farewell...

Through the Sympathetic Heart Pact, Langmu likewise perceived that peerless sense of comfort and euphoria.

Like Shang Fanfan, he raised his gaze to the heavens.

"The souls of those cubs have been liberated; they have returned to the origin of heaven and earth," Shang Fanfan murmured instinctively.

Langmu caught him by the arm, offering a soft, "Mn!"

"Ludwig?" Hearing Shang Fanfan mention that he likely encountered the Saint-tier Mage Ludwig, Langmu felt a lingering wave of dread.

Shang Fanfan lowered his gaze to look at his beloved: "Just now... it must have had something to do with him."

"Do you think he's dead or alive right now?" Langmu asked again.

Shang Fanfan fully understood Langmu's anxieties. When dealing with a veteran Rank 8 Saint-tier Mage, no amount of caution could ever be considered excessive.

"I have no way to perceive what's happening over at the God of Knowledge's domain, but I have a strong premonition—even if he isn't dead, his situation will be unimaginably dire."

Destiny backlash was no laughing matter, to say nothing of the personal curse "bestowed" upon him by the God of Curses.

"Since the souls of those cubs have found their release, at the very least, Ludwig has been weakened to the point where he can no longer trap them."

"Ludwig isn't a problem. If he dares to stick his head out, we'll just figure out a way to deal with him," Shang Fanfan declared boldly, confident now that he had pushed all the way to the peak of Rank 8.

"Alright!" Langmu felt his heart settle at those words.

So what if he was a Saint-tier Mage? They had already gone toe-to-toe with an Evil God; why would they care about a mere mage?

"We need to focus on resolving the magma eruption issue in the Blackwater Wasteland. Based on my surveys over the past few days, the subterranean magma is growing increasingly active; we have to vent it right away."

"Have the flood relief channels been mapped out?"

"Pretty much finalized. Now I'm just waiting for you, our chief engineering commander, to lead the undead army out to start digging."

Shang Fanfan chuckled. "Alright, leave the rest to me."

After a brief moment of hesitation, Langmu finally voiced his concern: "The terrain of Pengshi City is unique, and it's located very close to the epicenter of the magma eruption. It would make an ideal location for a massive flood-relief lake. Of course, Pengshi City itself sits halfway up the mountain and will be safe. But if we want to funnel all that magma converge there, the subterranean pressure might just turn the mountain holding Pengshi City into a volcano..."

第247章 临时托儿所

镇长狼守嘴巴大张地看着商非凡和郎沐身后。

附近的镇民也惊讶异常，全都围了过来。

小镇唯一的小广场上站着数量巨多……按照商非凡告诉他的，有三千多个兽人幼崽。

这些幼崽最小的才几个月大，被年长的幼崽抱在怀里，拱来拱去地到处找奶。

稍大些的三五岁幼崽茫然地牵着同伴的衣角，尾巴紧张地蜷着。

更大一些的小少年和亚成年则绷着脸站在外围，眼神警惕又无措。

这些幼崽们大多维持着兽形，也有一部分维持着人形，人形都穿着统一制式的“校服”。

在这些幼崽现在的认知里——

他们要么就是天生为天残，家中养不活或不想养，被一个邪恶组织带走。

要么就是被那个邪恶组织强行抢去。

至于那些真神教教徒的孩子则是认定自己从小被抛弃，被一个邪恶组织弄去培养，以极为残忍的教育方式想要把他们培养成邪恶存在，将来好为那邪恶组织所用。幸好商非凡去救他的孩子和其他幼崽，发现他们，把他们都给救了出来。

而这个邪恶组织就是真神教。

商非凡篡改了这些幼崽的记忆，但没有全盘抹消，小的还好糊弄，但亚成年们说不定好奇之下会去寻找自己的记忆，搞不好就埋下一些隐患。

与其如此，还不如把事实真相留给他们，只是在认知上稍微做一点修改和灌输。

对于那些接受了真神教多年洗脑教育的幼崽，商非凡都给他们下了极深的精神暗示，让他们知道真神教的邪恶，让他们明白真神教教导的那些都是错误。并给这些幼崽灌输“我知道这些教育内容不好，我只是为了活下去才假装接受，其实我心里知道这都是不对”的强烈认知。

实际上有不少幼崽确实心里这么想。

而那些被教导的不知道什么是对错的幼崽，有了商非凡的强行划分和灌输，他们也会学会对比和思考。

商非凡并不指望这些幼崽将来长大都会成为品性优良的好孩子，歹竹里面能出好笋，良好的教育环境一样能养出畜生，一个人将来会变成什么样，除了看教育和成长环境，也看他自身。

商非凡只要做到问心无愧，给这些幼崽提供他能提供的良好教育和成长环境，并尽量把隐患降到最低，之后这些孩子会长成什么样，就全看他们自己。

以往这样的麻烦事，他可都是交给背后的组织去做，他只要把人带到，之后就什么都不用他烦。

背后有个优秀且庞大的后勤组织真的很爽。

现在嘛，他貌似从尖刀变成了手握尖刀的人……好在他还有一个能干的姨父和看似柔弱其实后勤能力超一流的姥姥！

郎老夫人之前因为家事不幸，心情拖累身体，搞得病歪歪，做什么事都无力。

但自从认回郎沐，搞清楚郎家的不幸根源在哪里，又狠狠报复了仇人后，郎老夫人的精神气就回来了。

然后阿呆的出现，彻底让郎老夫人振作——郎沐和商非凡不要她烦，但阿呆还小，两个大只的明显是要去做大事的，没空教养阿呆，她这个做曾奶奶的自然要给家里第四代创造一个更好的生活和教育环境！

郎老爷子在外面查勘哪里适合做基地，郎老夫人就在莫约镇这边做好后勤工作。

不知不觉间，郎老夫人就把后方的事情料理得顺顺当当，还和莫约镇民从上到下都处得非常好。

莫约镇镇长就更不用说了，这位就是个特别重视感情、特别注重家人的义气汉子！

他认郎沐这个亲人，而郎沐也愿意继续认他这个姨父，他就真心把郎沐和郎家人全都当做自己人看。

如今面对商非凡带来的“巨大-麻烦”，他也只是震惊幼崽数量之多，却没有半点推托之意。

镇长一巴掌拍在商非凡肩上：“你小子！你这是把哪里的育幼院搬空了？”

“暂时寄养。”商非凡着重说明这点，“等我和郎沐解决了岩浆爆发的问题，就带他们去新城。最长三个月。”

莫约镇也确实没办法长期抚养这么多幼崽，不说没这么大地方安置这么多幼崽，光是给幼崽们吃的食物就是个大问题。镇长是个实在人，没强行应承自己做不到的事。

“你们已经把新城地点决定下来了？”镇长顺口问。

“差不多了。老爷子已经赶过去那边查勘，等确定适合就会传消息回来。”

“岩浆爆发的问题，只靠你和郎沐两个，你们能解决？”镇长眼中带着忧虑。他更想问，他们莫约镇是不是在岩浆爆发的范围内，要不要搬迁。

商非凡正要回答。

就听围观的镇民们从震惊中清醒，纷纷嚷嚷开：

“这么多崽？！”

“天啊，那个小猫崽才多大啊，连奶牙都没长齐……”

“你看那个狼族小子，眼神凶的嘞，怕是已经能打架了。”

“哎呀，我看那个崽特别像我十年前不小心弄丢的崽儿，我去瞅瞅！”

“狗-屎！你这个老头子都不能生了，哪来的崽子？等等，我忽然觉得旁边那个很像我那没有见过面的闺女生的！”

好嘛，不但嚷嚷，他们还直接动手了。

镇上的老中年兽人们已经自发地围了上去，有的掏出随身带的零食分给幼崽，有的蹲下来检查他们身上的伤。

亚成年的崽儿下意识地后退，他们很多都不习惯来自成年人的关心和疼爱。

但更多的幼崽，尤其是那些年纪小的，已经开始往镇民怀里钻，嘴里还喊着爷爷奶奶爸爸妈妈，反正只要觉得味道对的，愿意抱自己的，就先拱了再说。

郎沐见到这一幕，按住额头。

行吧，他知道兽人们稀罕幼崽，莫约镇就有不少中老年兽人要么没成家，要么就是没孩子，看到这么多孩子，还有很多幼崽和自己种族相同，怎么可能不动心？

如果真有几个看对眼的，那也是好事。

总之，莫约镇民的热情和发自内心对幼崽们的关心，至少能让这些惶恐不安的幼崽们能稍微安心。

商非凡不想镇长难做，当着镇民的面，挥手就放出一堆物资。

物资分门别类，全都用箱子和袋子装的好好的，占据了小广场很大一块地方。

镇长和好奇的镇民们走过去看，就见那堆物资分为食物和日用品。

食物从常见的虫粉，到价值较高的麦粉、肉干、鲜肉、瓜果蔬菜……应有尽有，甚至还有几箱给奶崽喝的珍贵奶粉。

日用品则包括成批的布匹、毛皮，还有已经做好的衣裤鞋袜，以及铺盖被褥、锅碗瓢盆、牙刷肥皂等日常需要用到的物品。

镇民们还看到了不少玩具和训练器械。

商非凡单独把药品拿给镇长，都是一些常见药。

准备如此周全，而且这样大的量，别说给三千多幼崽在三个月内使用，就是再翻一倍也足够。

Chapter 247: Temporary Nursery

Town Chief Lang Shou stared with his mouth agape at Shang Feifan and Lang Mu behind him.

The nearby townsfolk were also exceptionally astonished, crowding around in a circle.

In the town’s only small plaza stood a massive number of… according to what Shang Feifan had told him, over three thousand beastmen cubs.

The youngest of these cubs were only a few months old, held in the arms of older cubs, wriggling and crawling around everywhere in search of milk.

The slightly older cubs, around three to five years old, held onto their companions' hems in a daze, their tails tightly curled in nervousness.

The even older pre-teens and sub-adults stood rigidly on the outer perimeter, their gazes vigilant yet helpless.

Most of these cubs still maintained their beast forms, while a portion maintained their human forms, all wearing uniform-style "school uniforms."

In the current cognition of these cubs—

Either they were born with congenital physical defects, unable to be raised or unwanted by their families, and were taken away by an evil organization.

Or they were forcibly snatched away by that evil organization.

As for the children of the True God Cult members, they were convinced that they had been abandoned since childhood and taken by an evil organization to be nurtured, subjected to extremely cruel educational methods to train them into evil entities so they could be used by that evil organization in the future. Fortunately, Shang Feifan went to rescue his child and the other cubs, discovered them, and saved them all.

And this evil organization was none other than the True God Cult.

Shang Feifan had tampered with these cubs' memories, but he hadn't completely erased them. The younger ones were easy enough to fool, but the sub-adults might go looking for their memories out of curiosity, which could potentially plant hidden dangers.

Rather than doing that, it was better to leave them with the actual truth, only making slight modifications and instilling changes in their cognition.

For those cubs who had been subjected to years of brainwashing education by the True God Cult, Shang Feifan had implanted deep mental suggestions into them, making them realize the evil nature of the True God Cult and understand that everything the cult taught was wrong. He instilled a strong cognitive awareness in these cubs: "I know this educational content is bad; I only pretended to accept it just to survive, but in my heart, I knew it was all wrong."

In reality, quite a few cubs actually thought this way.

As for those who had been taught without knowing right from wrong, with Shang Feifan’s forceful categorization and indoctrination, they would also learn to compare and think for themselves.

Shang Feifan didn't expect all these cubs to grow up to be upstanding children of exceptional character—after all, even bad bamboo can sprout good shoots, and a good educational environment can still raise beasts. How a person turns out in the future depends not only on their education and upbringing environment, but also on themselves.

Shang Feifan only needed to have a clear conscience, provide these cubs with the best education and growth environment he could offer, and minimize the hidden dangers as much as possible. After that, how these children would grow up depended entirely on them.

In the past, he would have handed such troublesome matters over to the organization behind him; all he had to do was bring the people back, and he wouldn't have to worry about anything else afterward.

Having an excellent and massive logistics organization behind you really felt fantastic.

Now, though, he seemed to have transformed from the sharp blade into the person wielding the sharp blade... Fortunately, he still had a capable uncle-in-law and a grandmother who looked delicate but possessed top-tier logistical capabilities!

Previously, due to family tragedies, Old Madam Lang’s mood had dragged down her health, leaving her sickly and powerless to do anything.

However, ever since she recognized Lang Mu, figured out where the root of the Lang family's misfortune lay, and ruthlessly retaliated against her enemies, Old Madam Lang’s vigor had returned.

Then, the appearance of A-Dai completely revitalized Old Madam Lang—Lang Mu and Shang Feifan didn't need her to worry about them, but A-Dai was still young, and the two big guys were obviously going to do great things with no time to raise A-Dai. As his great-grandmother, she naturally had to create a better living and educational environment for the fourth generation of the family!

Old Patriarch Lang was out surveying locations suitable for a base, while Old Madam Lang handled the logistical work right here in Moyue Town.

Before she knew it, Old Madam Lang had managed the affairs of the rear flawlessly and got along exceptionally well with the people of Moyue Town from top to bottom.

Not to mention the Town Chief of Moyue Town—this man was a righteous fellow who placed special emphasis on affection and family!

He recognized Lang Mu as family, and since Lang Mu was willing to continue acknowledging him as an uncle-in-law, he truly regarded Lang Mu and the entire Lang family as his own people.

Now, facing the "huge trouble" brought by Shang Feifan, he was only shocked by the sheer number of cubs, without a single thought of shirking responsibility.

The town chief slapped Shang Feifan on the shoulder: "You brat! Whose nursery did you empty out to bring all these here?"

"Temporarily fostering them," Shang Feifan emphasized this point. "Once Lang Mu and I resolve the magma eruption issue, we'll take them to the New City. Three months at most."

Moyue Town truly had no way of long-term fostering for so many cubs. Not to mention not having enough space to accommodate so many of them, simply providing food for the cubs was a major problem. The town chief was a practical man and didn't make reckless promises about things he couldn't do.

"You've already decided on the location for the New City?" the town chief asked casually.

"Pretty much. The old patriarch has already rushed over there to survey it. Once it's confirmed suitable, he'll send word back."

"As for the magma eruption issue, just relying on the two of you, can you handle it?" Worry flickered in the town chief's eyes. He wanted to ask whether Moyue Town was within the range of the magma eruption and whether they needed to relocate.

Shang Feifan was just about to answer.

When he heard the onlookers snap out of their shock and start shouting clamorously:

"So many pups?!"

"Good heavens, how old is that little cat cub? It hasn't even grown its milk teeth yet..."

"Look at that wolf tribe brat, his gaze is so fierce; I reckon he can already fight."

"Aiya, that pup looks just like the one I accidentally lost ten years ago, I'm going to take a look!"

"Bullshit! You old codger can't even reproduce anymore, where'd you get a pup? Wait, I suddenly feel like the one next to it looks remarkably like the daughter I've never met!"

Well, not only were they shouting, but they also took action directly.

The older and middle-aged beastmen of the town had spontaneously surrounded them. Some pulled out snacks they carried with them to share with the cubs, while others squatted down to check the injuries on their bodies.

The sub-adult pups instinctively backed away; many of them were unaccustomed to care and affection from adults.

But more of the cubs, especially the younger ones, had already begun burrowing into the townspeople's arms, calling out grandpas, grandmas, daddies, and mommies. In short, as long as the scent felt right and someone was willing to hold them, they would wriggle their way in first.

Seeing this scene, Lang Mu pressed a hand to his forehead.

Fine, he knew how much beastmen adored cubs, and Moyue Town had quite a few middle-aged and elderly beastmen who were either unmarried or childless. Seeing so many children, with many cubs belonging to their own races, how could they not be tempted?

If a few actually hit it off, that would be a good thing.

In any case, the enthusiasm of the Moyue Town people and their heartfelt care for the cubs would at least allow these terrified little ones to feel a bit more at ease.

Not wanting to make things difficult for the town chief, Shang Feifan waved his hand right in front of the townspeople and released a pile of supplies.

The supplies were sorted and categorized, all packed neatly in boxes and bags, taking up a large section of the small plaza.

The town chief and the curious townspeople walked over to take a look, seeing that the pile of supplies was divided into food and daily necessities.

The food ranged from common insect powder to higher-value wheat flour, jerky, fresh meat, melons, fruits, and vegetables—everything was available, and there were even several boxes of precious powdered milk for the nursing cubs.

The daily necessities included batches of fabric and furs, ready-made clothing, pants, shoes, and socks, as well as bedding, pots, pans, toothbrushes, soap, and other everyday essentials.

The townspeople also spotted plenty of toys and training equipment.

Shang Feifan handed the medicines to the town chief separately; they were all common remedies.

With such comprehensive preparation and in such massive quantities, let alone lasting over three thousand cubs for three months, even doubling that amount would be more than enough.

chunks.chineseText:
有些不愿意抚养这么多幼崽的镇民这时也没二话了，抚养物资完全不用他们镇子出，看这个量，说不定他们镇还能赚一点，何乐而不为？

不过就是要收拾一个地方出来给幼崽们住而已，正好风洞山那边那么多山洞还空着，暂时让幼崽们住进去也没事，只要安排好人手管理和照顾就行。

商非凡出手大方，除了这些给幼崽们的生活物资，他还额外送了一笔物资给莫约镇，作为照顾这些幼崽的费用。

这下镇民们就更没意见了，更有许多人踊跃报名愿意去照顾幼崽们。

现在可是冬季，正是最缺衣少食的时候。

虽然莫约镇的情况要比其他困难的村镇要好一些，但受制于耕地就那么大，他们也一直都过得紧巴巴，不至于饿死，但要说吃得有多好也不可能。

现在商非凡拿出这么多物资，很多家境一般的镇民就能靠照顾幼崽拿到额外的生存物资，过一个比较肥润的冬季。

郎老夫人在商非凡“带来”这么多幼崽后，就抱着阿呆在一边看着。

这时镇长狼守主动找到她，请她帮忙打理属于幼崽们的那份物资。

郎老夫人没有半分犹豫，一口答应。

毕竟幼崽们只是寄养，属于幼崽们的生活物资和给予莫约镇的酬劳物资，还是分开管理的比较好。

镇长找到郎老夫人，就是做给镇民和商非凡看，表明他们镇绝没有侵吞幼崽们物资的意思。

镇民们也觉得幼崽们的物资交给郎老夫人来管理更好，这样也不用担心幼崽们如果在物资上有什么缺乏，就找他们镇子算账。

镇长那边则把商非凡送给他们的那批物资，先拿出五分之一做公用，剩下的五分之四则说好当做照顾幼崽们的工资酬劳。

镇民们都觉得镇长这样分派没有问题，只是报名照顾幼崽的人更多——这些人倒也不全是为了酬劳，反正冬季也没什么事干，闲着也是闲着。

如何安排住处以及安排哪些人去照顾幼崽，如何安排他们上课和训练，这些都是镇长那边的职责。

郎老夫人则接手了临时校长一职，负责整体统筹以及幼崽们的具体生活事宜。

郎沐低声和老夫人说了一些事。

郎老夫人点点头，让孙子不用担心，说全部交给她。

老夫人特别麻利，当即就带着郎家的一部分人手，以及镇长那边调度来的人，先开始给幼崽们检查身体，看有没有生病和体弱的。

大一点的亚成年还好，那些还在吃奶的奶崽就需要多加小心，一个拉肚子都可能让他们病倒。

然后就是安排人给幼崽们按照不同年龄、种族、喜好来准备食物。

食物是最能让人安心的，只要吃饱了，幼崽们的不安也会少一些。

商非凡只管带出这些幼崽，以及给他们反洗脑，对这些幼崽的身体状况和心理状态倒真的没怎么注意。只能说……术业有专攻吧。

郎沐心细，但他也没能力把三千多幼崽都照顾到，只能找老夫人帮忙。

好在老夫人特别靠谱，又有莫约镇人的大力支持。

至此，幼崽安顿的事就算是暂时弄好。

商非凡从老夫人怀里把阿呆拎出来，“走了，跟你爹我去干活。”

老夫人刚想说阿呆这么小，你们带着他能干什么活。

就见阿呆兴奋地在他爹手上直蹦跶：“去去去，我要帮爸爸们干活，我很厉害！”

“对，全天下你第一厉害。”商非凡哈哈笑。

阿呆乐坏了，从他商爸的手臂中蹦到他郎沐爸爸的怀里，仰头，希望他郎沐爸爸也夸夸他。

郎沐笑，摸摸阿呆软软的头毛，夸奖：“我们阿呆最棒了！有你在，我和你商爸能省好多事。”

“嘿嘿~”阿呆笑得傻fufu。

镇长一直在关注商、郎二人的动向，看他们带着阿呆一副要赶着离开的模样，立刻找上他们。

“咳，我知道你们的事情很紧急。如果你们能稍微抽出几分钟……”镇长不知道该怎么继续说下去。

商非凡没开口，他看出来镇长主要是在跟郎沐请求。

郎沐听懂了，露出不好意思的神情：“姨父，是我不好，我应该一回来就去探望姨母，只是我……我不知道该怎么面对她，才会一直躲着她，都是我不好。”

“不不不！”镇长听到郎沐叫他姨父，脸上露出不自知的笑容。随即听到郎沐责怪自己，忙摆手：“跟你无关。你姨母那个性子……你也知道，她就是个别扭人，实际上她也特别关心你，但她也跟你同样，不知道该如何面对你，如果你愿意主动去看看她，她嘴上也许会说些难听话，但心里会很高兴。我……唉，抱歉！”

郎沐单手抓住镇长的手臂，“姨父，你们还肯认我，是我的幸运。我会去看她，等我把岩浆……”

话没说完，郎沐的嘴突然被商非凡捂住。

商非凡冷着脸说：“别说这种会立flag的话，想要去看姨母大人，那就现在去，有什么事现在就说清楚，也省得你们俩心里老是惦记这事。我们也不差这十几分钟半个小时。”

镇长用期盼的眼神看向郎沐。

郎沐一咬牙，“好，我们现在就去。”

迪莉娅夫人看到郎沐和商非凡出现，神情竟然很平静。

“你来了。”

“……抱歉，到现在才来探望您。”郎沐神情带着歉意说。

迪莉娅夫人轻哼一声：“怎么，连一声姨母都不肯叫了吗？我就知道我这个假姨母让你不爽，说不定还被你当仇人看。”

“哪里的话！”郎沐哭笑不得，“我这不是担心您这边对我有意见。”

迪莉娅夫人掠了掠头发，冷哼：“我能对你有什么意见？从头到尾都是我姐对不起你，是她害的你前面二十年生活凄苦，你再怎么怨恨她和与她有关的人都是应该的。”

这要郎沐怎么回？

事实确实如迪莉娅夫人所说，但长辈……他心里还是认镇长和迪莉娅夫人当长辈的，看在这两位的面子上，他也不会说安妮塔的坏话。

迪莉娅夫人看郎沐沉默，眼神软了软，这个孩子就是个心软的，安妮塔那样害他，他竟然还愿意相信他这个姨母，还把自己最亲的姥姥送到他们莫约镇来。

更不要说这段时间，郎沐又是给他们送宝贵的储物工具，又是送粮食和物资之类。

镇长说得没错，是她没脸见这个假外甥，见了也不知道该说什么。

让她为她姐道歉？

安妮塔配吗？

郎沐这孩子恐怕也不想要她这个假姨母替安妮塔道歉。

“安妮塔夫人和您……你们无关。”郎沐只能这么说。

迪莉娅夫人的眼神更加柔和，但嘴巴还是很硬。

“我们各算各的，我和安妮塔早就分开，你不是安妮塔的孩子，我反而更高兴。”迪莉娅说的是大实话。

郎沐的性子和为人，她一直看在眼中。

她丈夫也不是什么人都喜欢，郎沐自己不好的话，别说是她外甥，就是她亲儿子，狼守看不上还是看不上。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 247: Temporary Nursery (Part 2)

Those townsfolk who had been somewhat reluctant to foster so many cubs now had nothing more to say. The town wouldn't need to spend a single coin on the upbringing supplies; judging by the sheer quantity, their town might even turn a modest profit—why not?

They just needed to clear out a place for the cubs to live. Conveniently, Wind Cave Mountain still had plenty of empty caves where the cubs could stay temporarily, as long as they arranged personnel to manage and care for them.

Shang Feifan was exceptionally generous. In addition to these living supplies for the cubs, he sent an extra batch of provisions to Moyue Town as compensation for taking care of the little ones.

With that, the townspeople had even fewer objections, and many eagerly signed up to take care of the cubs.

It was winter right now, the exact season when food and clothing were in the shortest supply.

Although Moyue Town's situation was somewhat better than other struggling villages and towns, restricted by their limited arable land, they had always lived frugally. They wouldn't starve to death, but eating particularly well was out of the question.

Now that Shang Feifan had brought out so many supplies, many ordinary households in the town could rely on taking care of the cubs to earn extra survival supplies and get through a relatively well-fed winter.

After Shang Feifan "brought" so many cubs, Old Madam Lang held A-Dai and watched from the side.

At this moment, Town Chief Lang Shou proactively sought her out, asking her to help manage the share of supplies belonging to the cubs.

Old Madam Lang agreed without a moment's hesitation.

After all, the cubs were only being fostered; it was better to manage the cubs' living supplies and the remuneration given to Moyue Town separately.

The town chief sought out Old Madam Lang precisely to show the townspeople and Shang Feifan that their town had no intention whatsoever of swallowing up the cubs' supplies.

The townspeople also felt it was better to leave the cubs' supplies in Old Madam Lang's hands, as it eliminated any worry that if the cubs lacked anything in terms of provisions, someone would come knocking on their town's door to settle accounts.

As for the batch of supplies Shang Feifan gifted to them, the town chief took out one-fifth for public use, while the remaining four-fifths were designated as wages and compensation for taking care of the cubs.

The townsfolk agreed that the town chief's allocation was entirely fair; it was just that even more people signed up to care for the cubs—though these people weren't entirely doing it for the pay. Winter was uneventful anyway, so being idle meant they might as well do something.

How to arrange the living quarters, which personnel to assign to care for the cubs, and how to schedule their classes and training were the town chief's responsibilities.

Old Madam Lang took on the role of temporary principal, responsible for overall coordination and the specific daily affairs of the cubs.

Lang Mu spoke in a low voice to the old madam about several matters.

Old Madam Lang nodded, telling her grandson not to worry and that she would handle everything.

The old madam was exceptionally efficient. She immediately led a group of personnel from the Lang family, along with staff dispatched by the town chief, to begin health checks on the cubs to see if any were sick or frail.

The older sub-adults were fine, but those nursing babies required extra care; a simple bout of diarrhea could make them gravely ill.

Next came arranging for people to prepare food for the cubs according to their different ages, races, and preferences.

Food was the most reassuring thing; as long as their bellies were full, the cubs' anxiety would naturally subside.

Shang Feifan only bothered with bringing these cubs out and de-brainwashing them, paying very little attention to their physical and psychological states. You could only say... specialization was best left to the experts.

Lang Mu was meticulous, but he didn't have the capacity to personally care for over three thousand cubs, so he could only ask the old madam for help.

Fortunately, the old madam was remarkably reliable and had the strong support of the Moyue Town people.

With this, the arrangement for the cubs could be considered temporarily settled.

Shang Feifan scooped A-Dai out of the old madam's arms. "Let's go, time to go to work with your daddy."

The old madam was just about to say that A-Dai was so young, what work could they possibly bring him along for?

She saw A-Dai excitedly bouncing up and down in his daddy's hands: "Go, go, go! I want to help papas work, I'm super strong!"

"Right, you're the number one strongest in the entire world," Shang Feifan laughed heartily.

A-Dai was overjoyed, leaping from Shang-pa's arms right into Lang Mu-pa's embrace, tilting his head up in hopes that Lang Mu-pa would praise him too.

Lang Mu smiled, stroked A-Dai's soft hair, and praised: "Our A-Dai is the best! With you here, your Shang-pa and I can save so much trouble."

"Hehe~" A-Dai giggled foolishly.

The town chief had been keeping an eye on the movements of the two men. Seeing them about to leave with A-Dai in tow, he immediately approached them.

"Ahem, I know your matters are very urgent. If you could spare just a few minutes..." The town chief didn't know how to continue.

Shang Feifan didn't speak; he could tell the town chief was primarily appealing to Lang Mu.

Lang Mu understood, a trace of embarrassment on his face: "Uncle-in-law, it's my fault. I should have gone to visit Aunt as soon as I returned, but I... I didn't know how to face her, so I kept avoiding her. It's all my fault."

"No, no, no!" Upon hearing Lang Mu call him uncle-in-law, a smile surfaced uncontrollably on the town chief's face. Hearing Lang Mu blame himself immediately after, he hurriedly waved his hands: "It has nothing to do with you. Your aunt's temperament... you know how she is, she's just a stubborn person. In reality, she cares deeply about you too, but like you, she didn't know how to face you. If you're willing to go see her proactively, her mouth might say some harsh things, but in her heart, she'll be very happy. I... sigh, sorry!"
