Lang Mu grabbed the town chief's arm with one hand: "Uncle-in-law, it's my fortune that you're still willing to acknowledge me. I will go see her, once I finish dealing with the magma—"

Before he could finish, Lang Mu's mouth was suddenly covered by Shang Feifan's hand.

Shang Feifan said with a cold face: "Don't say those flag-raising things. If you want to go see Madam Aunt, then go right now. Whatever needs to be said, get it cleared up now, so you two don't keep lingering on this in your hearts. We're not pressed for these dozen minutes or half an hour."

The town chief looked at Lang Mu with expectant eyes.

Lang Mu gritted his teeth. "Alright, let's go right now."

When Madam Delia saw Lang Mu and Shang Feifan appear, her expression was surprisingly calm.

"You're here."

"…Sorry for only coming to visit you now," Lang Mu said with an apologetic expression.

Madam Delia let out a light snort: "What, won't even deign to call me aunt? I knew my fake aunt status displeased you, and you probably even view me as an enemy."

"What kind of talk is that!" Lang Mu was caught between laughter and tears. "I was just worried you might have grievances against me."

Madam Delia swept back a lock of her hair and coldly snorted: "What grievances could I possibly have against you? From start to finish, my sister was the one who wronged you. It was she who made the first twenty years of your life miserable. No matter how much you resent her and those related to her, it's only right."

How was Lang Mu supposed to respond to that?

The facts were indeed as Madam Delia stated, but as elders... in his heart, he still acknowledged the town chief and Madam Delia as his elders. For the sake of these two, he wouldn't speak ill of Anita.

Seeing Lang Mu fall silent, Madam Delia's gaze softened slightly. This child was soft-hearted; Anita harmed him so severely, yet he was still willing to trust her as his aunt and even sent his dearest grandmother to Moyue Town.

Not to mention that during this period, Lang Mu had gifted them precious storage tools, grain, and supplies.

The town chief was right; it was she who had no face to face this fake nephew, not knowing what to say upon meeting him.

Ask her to apologize for her sister?

Was Anita worthy?

Lang Mu probably didn't want her, this fake aunt, to apologize on Anita's behalf either.

"Madam Anita and you... you have nothing to do with each other." Lang Mu could only say this.

Madam Delia's gaze grew even softer, though her mouth remained hard.

"We each calculate our own accounts. Anita and I parted ways long ago. I'm actually happier that you aren't Anita's child," Delia spoke the unvarnished truth.

She had always observed Lang Mu's temperament and character.

Her husband wasn't someone who liked just anyone; if Lang Mu himself were lacking, let alone a nephew, even if he were his biological son, Lang Shou wouldn't look twice at him if he didn't approve.

chunks.chineseText:
能让他丈夫那么中意还愿意护着，郎沐就算和他们没有亲戚关系——原本郎沐就和狼守没有任何血缘关系，就说明她丈夫看中的就是郎沐这个人本人。

她也同样，她看中的也是郎沐这个人本人。

“叫我一声姨母。”迪莉娅强硬地要求。

郎沐却笑了，心甘情愿地张口：“姨母大人。”

郎沐还示意抱在怀里的阿呆：“阿呆，叫姨奶奶。”

阿呆抬起小爪子，呆呆地喊：“姨奶奶大人好。”

商非凡闷笑。

迪莉娅夫人脸黑了：“姨母就行了，那大人是什么意思？”

商非凡嘴贱地在一边说：“就是表示姨母你特别厉害的意思。”

“……滚！”迪莉娅夫人这个气啊。

两个人就带着崽儿顺势滚了。

郎沐走时还不忘调皮了一把：“那姨母大人还有姨父，我忙完事情再来看你们。”

迪莉娅夫人怒：“滚滚滚！谁要你们来看我！”

镇长无奈地看向妻子，就见妻子窝在长椅里很文明地骂骂咧咧。

镇长也笑了。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 247: Temporary Nursery (Part 3)

The fact that her husband liked him so much and was willing to protect him—even if Lang Mu had no blood relation to them (originally, Lang Mu had no blood ties to Lang Shou whatsoever)—meant that what her husband valued was Lang Mu himself as a person.

She felt the same way; what she valued was Lang Mu himself as a person.

"Call me aunt," Delia demanded forcefully.

Lang Mu smiled instead, opening his mouth willingly: "Aunt."

Lang Mu also signaled A-Dai, who was held in his arms: "A-Dai, call great-aunt."

A-Dai raised his little paw and called out blankly: "Hello, Great-Aunt Lord."

Shang Feifan snickered inwardly.

Madam Delia's face darkened: "Aunt is fine, what's with that 'Lord' business?"

Shang Feifan chimed in teasingly from the side: "It means auntie, you're extra awesome."

"…Get lost!" Madam Delia was hopping mad.

The two of them simply rolled away with the cub in tow.

Before leaving, Lang Mu didn't forget to be playful: "Then Madam Aunt and Uncle-in-law, we'll come visit you again once we're done with our work."

Madam Delia raged: "Get lost, get lost, get lost! Who wants you to come visit me!"

The town chief looked helplessly at his wife, only to see her curled up in the armchair, swearing in a very cultured manner.

The town chief chuckled as well.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第248章 彭石城主的噩梦 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第248章 彭石城主的噩梦

四周的烛火突然熄灭，只剩下幽蓝的冷光。

远处传来铁链拖地的声音，哗啦，哗啦……越来越近。

埃比尼泽猛地转头，看见自己的妻子石狲悦站在阴影中，她看起来仍旧如生时一般，只脸色青白，眼睛里流着血泪。

她怀里似乎抱着一个刚出生不久的幼崽，嘴里发出轻轻的哼唱声。

哼唱声突然停下，那双流着血泪的眼睛对向他，石狲悦轻声问他：“我们不在了，只独留你一个人，你能睡得好吗？”

埃比尼泽下意识想逃，却发现自己的双腿不知何时已被铁链锁住。

石狲悦缓缓走过来，抬起一只手，冰冷的手指掐住他的喉咙：

“我以我血、我魂诅咒你，诅咒你生时日日不得安生，死后时时不得安宁，你将被怨魂纠缠，将被所有人背叛，你无日不担心喝的水吃的食物中有毒，你……”

“你去死！去死——！”埃比尼泽猛然大吼。

他死去的妻子发出愉悦的笑声：“你杀不死我，杀不死我！哈哈哈，埃比尼泽，我要看着你死，我要你付出代价——！”

“我杀了你！”

埃比尼泽猛地睁眼，却发现自己并不在床上，而是站在一片漆黑的荒野中。

远处，一个披头散发的女兽人缓缓向他走来，她的脖子扭曲成诡异的角度，每一步都在地上留下血脚印。

“埃比尼泽，我心爱的人啊……”她的声音像刀刮在骨头上，“你为什么要害我？就是为了我家的血脉天赋吗？你这么想要，我给你啊。”

埃比尼泽想逃，但双腿像灌了铅。

每次都是这样，每次他都在该逃跑时无法挪动自己的双脚！

女兽人突然扑上来，尖锐的指甲刺进他的眼球！

埃比尼泽惨叫着惊醒，浑身冷汗淋漓。

醒来的他发现自己正站在彭石城的城墙上，低头望去，城民们的脸全都变成了腐烂的骷髅。他们仰着头，用空洞的眼窝注视着他，嘴里不停地重复着：“都是你的错……都是你的错……”

他还在噩梦中！

埃比尼泽心脏收缩，浑身冰冷。

他这样的情况已经维持很久，一开始他还会因为噩梦惊醒，真正的清醒。

但随着时间过去，他就进入了梦中梦状态，从噩梦醒来只会进入另一个噩梦。

当他以为两个噩梦是极限时，第三个噩梦、第四个噩梦……他就像是陷入了噩梦的套娃中，一个又一个，似无穷无尽。

最可怕的是这些梦境都异常真实！

他梦到自己被前城主活埋。棺材里的空气越来越少，他的指甲抓挠着木板，直到血肉模糊，直到泥土落下来覆盖他的口鼻。窒息感如此真实，以至于他惊醒时，喉咙里仍残留着泥土的腥味。

他梦见自己亲手掐死了最信任的心腹。可当他松开手时，心腹的脸竟然变成了他自己的——那张脸狞笑着，对他喊叫：“你终于疯了吗？”

他梦到自己被城中不满他作为的城民撕成碎片，梦到自己被审判被吊死被烧死，梦到那个失踪的幼崽回来找他报仇，挖出他的眼睛、挖出他的心脏、碾碎他每一根骨骼……

每一个噩梦都无比真实，他的灵魂也一次次被撕裂、被焚烧、被千刀万剐。每一次惊醒，冷汗都会浸湿他全身。

逐渐的，他甚至无法分辨他是真的清醒回到现实，还是仍旧在噩梦中。

起初，埃比尼泽还能勉强维持理智。他试图用最烈的酒麻痹自己，用熏香和安神药剂强迫自己入睡，甚至命令城里的祭司们日夜为他祈祷——这些祭司不属于祭司宫，只是彭石城自己培养的，就像一些村镇里的野祭司，并不被祭司宫承认。

所有作为都毫无用处。

那来自怨魂的诅咒——他认定这是被他害死的妻子和岳父留下的怨气在折磨他……就像附骨之疽，他的大脑成了噩梦的乐园，每一次闭眼，都像是主动跳入地狱。

渐渐地，他的眼眶凹陷下去，眼球布满血丝，面容枯槁如鬼。

他开始出现幻觉……

有时，他会看见他妻子的身影就站在议事厅的角落，冷冷注视着他，那么那么真实。可当他让手下人去确认时，却没有人能看见。

有时，他会听见自己的心跳声变成了诡异的低语，咒骂着他的愚蠢和失败——如果他好好地对待妻子，不去谋害岳父，他现在是不是有一个特别幸福的家庭？也不用日日夜夜受此折磨？而他除了城主之位，他最想得到的并没有得到。

最可怕的是，他甚至开始怀疑身边每一个人——他们会不会杀了我？会不会像石狲悦说的那样在他的日常饮食中下毒？会不会突然就冲出来给他一刀？会不会暗中背叛他，想要和城民一起审判他？

埃比尼泽开始召集驱魔师、诅咒师、死灵师……等所有与怨魂作孽相关的职业者。

他已经顾不得谣传，顾不得会不会变成丑闻。

他无比疯狂地想要彻底消灭妻子和岳父的怨魂。

他只想好好睡一觉。

为此，他可以不惜代价！

只可惜不管是哪个职业的天赋者，他们似乎都对石狲悦和前城主的怨魂毫无办法。

再厉害的驱魔师也只能看出他被浓重的怨气缠绕，但无法祛除。

他找来的诅咒师倒是看出他被人诅咒，但也找不到诅咒的根源在哪里，更无法消灭。

他用重宝请咒师无论如何都要帮帮他，对方出手了，却重伤败退，最后连重宝都没收，就像是怕被他牵连一样，看他的眼神就像是在看死人，最后还给他留下一句话，说是看在往日的交情上才会告诉他：“你完了，你被诅咒之神盯上了。赶紧想想你到底得罪了谁，竟然能请动神咒。”

神咒？埃比尼泽愕然，更颓丧万分。

他想不通他那已经死去的妻子怎么可能请动诅咒之神诅咒他。

难道这个家族还有他不知道的秘密？

对！一定是这样。

他和他们生活的时间还是太短了，他动手太早了，还没有来得及完全得知这个家族的秘密。

埃比尼泽悔恨无比！

他不后悔自己对石狲悦这个妻子动手，更不在乎一个岳父和一个流着石狲家族血液的幼崽，他后悔的是自己没有沉得住气，动手太早。

他想请动祭司宫的祭司为他消灭怨魂，他有认识的且关系比较好的祭司，但祭司宫的祭司们不知道怎么回事，竟然开始返回祭司宫，似乎祭司宫在召回所有祭司。

无奈下，他通过重重关系，找到了……真神教的一名主教。

都是神灵的力量，希望邪神的力量能在对付怨魂上有用。

如果有可能，埃比尼泽一点都不想接触邪神信徒，但他这不是没办法了吗？

为了能好好睡一觉，就是和恶魔合作他也在所不惜！

可那个看起来眼睛长在头顶上的主教连他请的咒师都不如，竟然和他一样做起了噩梦，还责怪他隐瞒，对他厉吼：“这不是怨魂的力量！这是更可怕的……来自昔日神灵的力量，你坑我！”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 248: Lord Ebenezer's Nightmare (Part 1)

The surrounding candlelight suddenly extinguished, leaving behind only an eerie, bluish-cold glow.

From the distance came the sound of iron chains dragging across the ground—clank, clank... growing closer and closer.

Ebenezer jerked his head around to see his wife, Shi Sunyue, standing in the shadows. She looked just as she had in life, except for her ashen complexion and the bloody tears streaming from her eyes.

She appeared to be cradling a newly born cub in her arms, humming a soft, gentle lullaby.

The humming abruptly stopped. Those eyes streaming bloody tears locked onto him, and Shi Sunyue asked him softly, "With us gone and only you left behind, can you sleep soundly?"

Ebenezer instinctively wanted to flee, only to find that his legs had somehow been bound by iron chains.

Shi Sunyue walked over slowly, raised a hand, and her ice-cold fingers clamped around his throat.

"I curse you with my blood and my soul—I curse you to never know peace in your waking days, nor rest in your death. You shall be haunted by vengeful spirits and betrayed by everyone. You will not pass a single day without the dread that the water you drink or the food you eat is poisoned. You..."

"Go to hell! Die—go die!" Ebenezer roared furiously.

His dead wife let out a gleeful laugh. "You can't kill me, you can't kill me! Hahaha, Ebenezer, I'm going to watch you die, I'm going to make you pay the price—!"

"I'll kill you!"

Ebenezer snapped his eyes open, only to find himself not in bed, but standing in a pitch-black wilderness.

In the distance, a disheveled female beastman was walking slowly toward him. Her neck was twisted at a grotesque angle, leaving a trail of bloody footprints with every step.

"Ebenezer, my beloved..." Her voice sounded like a knife scraping against bone. "Why did you harm me? Was it just for my family's bloodline talent? If you wanted it that badly, I would have given it to you."

Ebenezer wanted to run, but his legs felt as though they were filled with lead.

It was always like this. Every single time, he was unable to move his feet right when he needed to run!

The female beastman suddenly lunged forward, her sharp fingernails stabbing straight into his eyeballs!

Ebenezer shrieked and woke up with a start, drenched in a cold sweat.

Upon waking, he found himself standing atop the city walls of Pengshi City. Looking down, the faces of the townsfolk had all turned into rotting skulls. They tilted their heads upward, staring at him with hollow eye sockets, their mouths endlessly repeating, "It's all your fault... It's all your fault..."

He was still trapped in the nightmare!

Ebenezer's heart contracted, his entire body turning ice-cold.

This condition of his had persisted for a long time. At first, he would be startled awake by nightmares, achieving true consciousness.

But as time passed, he had entered a state of dreams within dreams; waking from one nightmare only led him straight into another.

When he thought two nightmares were the limit, a third nightmare, a fourth nightmare... He seemed caught in a matryoshka doll of horrors, one after another, as if endlessly recursive.

The most terrifying part was that these dreams were abnormally realistic!

He dreamed that he was buried alive by the former city lord. The air inside the coffin grew scarcer and scarcer; his fingernails clawed desperately at the wooden planks until his flesh was torn and bloody, until the soil fell down to cover his mouth and nose. The sensation of asphyxiation was so vivid that when he jolted awake, the fishy stench of earth still lingered in his throat.

He dreamed that he had choked his most trusted confidant to death with his own hands. Yet when he relaxed his grip, the confidant's face morphed into his own—that very face grinning hideously, screaming at him, "Have you finally gone mad?"

He dreamed that he was torn to shreds by townsfolk dissatisfied with his rule; dreamed that he was judged, hanged, and burned to death; dreamed that the missing cub returned to seek revenge, gouging out his eyes, ripping out his heart, and grinding every single bone in his body to dust...

Every single nightmare was unimaginably real, and his soul was repeatedly torn apart, incinerated, and subjected to a thousand cuts. Every time he snapped awake, cold sweat soaked his entire body.

Gradually, he could no longer tell whether he had truly awakened back to reality or was still trapped in a nightmare.

At first, Ebenezer could barely maintain his sanity. He tried to numb himself with the strongest liquor, forced himself to sleep using incense and calming potions, and even ordered the city's priests to pray for him day and night—though these priests didn't belong to the mainstream Temple of Priests, but were locally raised by Pengshi City itself, akin to wild priests in remote villages who lacked official recognition from the higher clergy.

All his efforts were utterly useless.

The curse stemming from the vengeful spirits—he was convinced this was the lingering resentment of his murdered wife and father-in-law tormenting him... Like a bone-deep gangrene, his brain had become a playground for nightmares. Every time he closed his eyes, it felt like willingly leaping into hell.

Slowly, his eye sockets sank inward, his eyeballs became bloodshot, and his features grew as withered as a ghost's.

He began to hallucinate...

Sometimes, he would see the figure of his wife standing quietly in the corner of the council chamber, gazing at him coldly—so very real. Yet when he sent his subordinates to check, no one else could see a thing.

Sometimes, he would hear his own heartbeat transform into a bizarre whisper, cursing his stupidity and failure—if he had only treated his wife properly and not murdered his father-in-law, wouldn't he have a wonderfully happy family right now? He wouldn't have to suffer this torment day and night. And yet, apart from the seat of the city lord, he hadn't even obtained what he desired most.

The most terrifying thing was that he began to suspect everyone around him—would they kill me? Would they poison my daily food and drink just as Shi Sunyue said? Would someone suddenly pounce out and stab me? Would they secretly betray me and plot to stand with the townsfolk in passing judgment on him?

Ebenezer began summoning exorcists, curse-masters, necromancers... and all manner of practitioners dealing with vengeful spirits and dark arts.

He no longer cared about rumors or whether it would spark a scandal.

With frenzied desperation, he wanted to completely eradicate the vengeful spirits of his wife and father-in-law.

He just wanted to get a decent night's sleep.

To that end, he would stop at nothing, no matter the cost!

It was a pity that, regardless of their specialization or talent, these practitioners seemed utterly helpless against the vengeful spirits of Shi Sunyue and the former city lord.

The most formidable exorcists could only discern that he was entangled by thick, oppressive resentment, but they were powerless to cleanse it.

The curse-master he hired managed to figure out that he had been cursed, yet could not trace the curse's origin, let alone eliminate it.

Using a priceless treasure, he begged the curse-master to help him no matter what. The expert made a move, only to be heavily injured and forced into retreat. In the end, the curse-master didn't even take his treasure, acting as though afraid of being implicated by association. The look in the curse-master's eyes was as if he were gazing at a dead man, and before leaving, he dropped a parting warning out of past courtesy: "You're finished. You've been targeted by a God's Curse. You better hurry up and figure out whose toes you stepped on to actually provoke a divine curse."

A divine curse? Ebenezer was dumbfounded, plunging into even deeper despair.

He couldn't fathom how his already-dead wife could possibly enlist a god of curses to place a curse upon him.

Could that family harbor secrets he knew nothing about?

Yes! That had to be it.

He simply hadn't lived with them long enough; he had made his move too hastily, before he could fully unearth the family's secrets.

Ebenezer was consumed by agonizing regret!

He didn't regret moving against his wife Shi Sunyue, nor did he care about a father-in-law or a cub carrying the bloodline of the Shi Sun family; what he regretted was lacking composure and striking far too early.

He had wanted to ask priests from the Temple of Priests to eradicate the vengeful spirits for him. He did know some priests with whom he shared relatively good relations, but for some unknown reason, the priests of the Temple of Priests had begun packing up and returning to the main temple, as if a general recall had been issued for all priests.

Left with no other choice, through countless connections, he managed to track down... a bishop of the True God Cult.

Since both relied on divine power, he hoped the power of an evil god might prove useful in dealing with vengeful spirits.

If he had any other choice, Ebenezer wouldn't have wanted to touch cultists of an evil god with a ten-foot pole, but wasn't he completely out of options?

For the sake of a good night's sleep, he would collaborate even with demons without a second thought!

Yet that bishop, whose eyes seemed permanently glued to the top of his head, turned out to be even more useless than the curse-master he had hired. The bishop ended up suffering from the exact same nightmares, and turning on him in fury, roared harshly: "This isn't the power of vengeful spirits! This is something far more terrifying... the power of an ancient deity! You set me up!"

chunks.chapterTitle: 第248章 彭石城主的噩梦 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
对方用最快速度逃离了彭石城，临走前还报复了他一把。

那个该死的真神教主教竟然用邪神雕像污染了彭石城的水源！

他听到了城中响起对邪神祭拜的诡异声音，命令手下找到了源头。

可看着那尊就被放在水源里的邪神雕像，他们全城人竟然没有一个敢把那雕像取出，更别说销毁。

所有接近雕像的人都会被邪神之力污染，变成邪神信徒。

为了处置这些突然冒出来的邪神信徒，他不得不大开杀戒。

埃比尼泽不会承认，他正好借用了邪神信徒这个借口在清除异己。

所有他觉得有可能背叛自己、在暗中说他这个城主的坏话、对他的命令阴奉阳违的人，他都趁机打成了邪神信徒，不听他们的辩驳，不听他们的喊冤，就这么把大量的城民和手下处死。

城主府中的死人越来越多。

一开始还只是仆役被责罚，后来责罚逐渐加重，等到城主“不小心”在愤怒下杀死了一个侍女，城主府中的死人就再也没有少过。

仆役、侍卫、管事、心腹手下……再到城中的富商、贵族、官员，乃至普通城民，越来越多的人因为莫须有罪名死在城主手中。

彭石城中，恐慌在蔓延。

“城主的命令变得越发极端了。”说话的人神色不安。

坐在他附近的一名官员也神色焦躁：“城主是疯了吗？他才下令征收‘安神税’，强迫城民上交能助眠的药材和炼金物品，没有就交钱，导致许多平民连最基本的粮食都快买不起了。”

“他还把所有拥有助眠天赋的城民都召入城主府，可……那些人没有一个回家，有人说他们因为无法帮助城主睡眠，已经被暴怒的城主杀死。”

另一名官员站起身，走来走去：“现在城主又要我们设立‘忠诚审查’，他怀疑城中有前城主势力残留，怀疑前城主势力正在暗中谋害他，要我们对任何对他流露出不满情绪的城民进行抓捕和严刑拷打，逼出他们身后的人。可是……我们都知道，哪来的前城主势力？那些人不是死了，就是早就逃走。”

“城主疯了。”最后一人闭上眼睛。

“为人不做亏心事半夜不怕鬼敲门，城主啊，他是……呵！”

“行了，这种事想想就好，管住自己的嘴，如果让城主听到，要是也被打成前城主势力，我们恐怕也活不了多久。”

“不能再让城主这么下去，否则大家都得玩完！”

“早知如此……”

“过去的事就别后悔了，当初我们已经做出选择。现在我们只需要再做出一次选择！”

“可是彭石城原城主血脉已经消失，我们到哪里再找来一个让王城承认的城主？”

“这么多年，城主还没有生下一个孩子，也是怪事。”

“嘘，他们都说这是来自那位的诅咒。”

“包括现在城主的情况也是？”

“你说呢？”

房间内年龄最长的老兽人站起来：“彭石城原城主一脉也还是有血脉留下来的。据我所知，当年那位生下一个孩子，怕被城主谋害，就让心腹冒死把那幼崽给送了出去。”

“哦？”众人精神振奋。

“那孩子在哪里？”众人忙问。

老兽人：“不知。”

“……”众人无语。不知道那个幼崽在哪里，要怎么推幼主上位。

老兽人却不慌不忙：“那就是一个石狲幼崽，只要我们找到一个年龄相当的幼崽，只要我们所有人都承认那个幼崽就是城主的独子，只要王城那边也愿意承认，那个被我们推出来的幼崽就会是下一个彭石城城主！”

房间内所有兽人沉默。

老兽人环视众人神色：“你们仔细想想吧，是留着现在的城主继续发疯的危险大，还是找一个幼崽来让王城承认他的继承权的危险大。”

不止是危险，背后还有巨大的收益。

只要想到下一个城主是一个由他们选出和推举上去的幼崽，他们可以控制这个幼崽做多少事情……

在场所有人都动心了。

“想要推举一位新城主好说，现在的问题是要如何解决现任的这位城主。”

类似的秘密聚会不止举行了一次，负责串联这些秘密聚会的人就是那个老兽人。

老兽人回家后，进入密室，看到里面一个正在学习传承秘技的石狲幼崽，不由走过去，慈祥地摸了摸他的头。

幼崽抬头，满眼孺慕地看向老兽人。

老兽人轻轻摩挲他的头顶软毛，轻声说：“我们家的未来就看你了。他埃比尼泽一个外人都能当城主，为什么我们真正的彭石城石狲一脉就不能坐上城主之位？”

幼崽眨眨眼，乖巧地说：“我都听爷爷的。”

老兽人欣慰地笑了。

万事俱备，只欠东风。

他只要等，等待城主孤注一掷找寻的那人送上门来。

城主不会知道他花了重金让人千辛万苦寻找来的救命人会是要他命的人。

隐身藏在暗中的商非凡已经跟着旁听了好几个秘密会议。

是的，他们早两日就到了，因为商非凡好奇城主现在的状况，就绕到城主府观察了一番，顺便就发现了这些彭石城贵族和官员的暗中打算。

这会儿听到老兽人跟孙子说的话，再瞅瞅那个比阿呆大了好多的石狲幼崽，商非凡伸手拍拍阿呆的脑袋。

“看，别人都给你把路铺好了。接下来你只要等待这些人把埃比尼泽那个人渣解决掉，你就能顺理成章地坐上城主之位。”

阿呆呆滞脸：拿到城主之位这么简单的吗？

这事在商非凡眼中真的就很简单。

不说他可以一力降十会，直接解决埃比尼泽，迫使彭石城所有人都同意阿呆上位。

就算走正常途径，他也能找大王子甚至是虎王，直接提交阿呆的身份。

阿呆就是前城主的直系血脉，他原本就比任何人都有资格接手彭石城城主之位。

但阿呆对当城主没多大兴趣，他还是要爸爸们哄的小宝宝呢，做什么苦逼的城主，窝在爸爸和曾奶奶的怀里喝奶不香吗？

商非凡见阿呆对城主之位丝毫不动心，就对郎沐叹息：“还是小崽子，不知道权力的美味。”

郎沐笑，竟然说：“一个小小的彭石城主之位算什么。我们阿呆将来可是要继承黑水荒原大领主之位的。”

商非凡心中一动，双眼发亮地看向阿呆。黑水荒原算什么，他和阿沐培养出来的崽子不说要统治整个天河星，怎么也得整个兽帝兽皇什么的才能有排面嘛。

阿呆身体一颤，一头钻入郎沐爸爸怀里。他总觉得他商爸好像在打什么坏主意，他将来说不定就要007了！

007这个说法还是商爸和郎沐爸爸开玩笑时说的，他可听懂了，那就是没日没夜都得工作的意思。

他、才、不、干！
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 248: Lord Ebenezer's Nightmare (Part 2)

The man fled Pengshi City at top speed, and before leaving, he exacted a petty revenge.

That damned bishop of the True God Cult had actually used an evil god statue to pollute Pengshi City's water supply!

Upon hearing eerie whispers worshiping the evil god echoing through the city, Ebenezer ordered his subordinates to trace the source.

Yet when they looked upon the evil god statue placed right inside the reservoir, not a single soul in the entire city dared to pull the statue out, let alone destroy it.

Anyone who came close to the statue would be corrupted by the evil god's power and transformed into a cultist.

To deal with these abruptly sprouting cultists of the evil god, he was forced to embark on a massive slaughter.

Ebenezer would never admit it, but he conveniently seized upon the excuse of evil god cultists to purge his political dissidents.

Everyone he suspected of potentially betraying him, whispering behind his back about his rule as city lord, or paying lip service to his commands while undermining them in secret, was branded as an evil god cultist. Refusing to listen to their arguments or pleas of innocence, he summarily executed a vast number of townsfolk and subordinates.

The bodies piling up inside the City Lord's Mansion grew steadily.

At first, it was merely servants being disciplined. Soon, the punishments escalated until, when the City Lord "accidentally" killed a maid in a fit of rage, the flow of corpses leaving the mansion never once slowed down.

Servants, guards, stewards, trusted confidants... and then the wealthy merchants, nobles, officials, and even ordinary townsfolk of the city—more and more people died at the city lord's hands on trumped-up charges.

Across Pengshi City, panic spread like wildfire.

"The City Lord's orders are becoming increasingly extreme." The speaker wore a deeply uneasy expression.

An official sitting nearby looked equally agitated and anxious: "Has the City Lord lost his mind? He just ordered the collection of a 'Mental Peace Tax,' forcing townsfolk to surrender medicinal herbs and alchemical items that aid sleep, or pay a hefty fine if they lacked them. It's gotten to the point where many commoners can barely afford basic food."

"He has also rounded up every townsfolk possessing sleep-inducing talents and dragged them into the City Lord's Mansion, but... not a single one of those people has returned home. Word is that because they couldn't help the City Lord sleep, they were executed by the enraged lord."

Another official stood up, pacing back and forth. "Now the City Lord wants us to establish a 'Loyalty Audit.' He suspects remnants of the former city lord's faction are lurking in the city, plotting against him in the dark. He’s ordered us to arrest and brutally torture any townsfolk who show the slightest sign of dissatisfaction, squeezing out the names of those behind them. But... we all know, where on earth are there any remnants of the former city lord? Those people were either dead or fled long ago."

"The City Lord is mad," the final official muttered, closing his eyes.

"He who does no evil sleeps without fear of ghosts knocking, but the City Lord... he's—heh!"

"Enough. Just keep thoughts like that to yourself and watch your tongue. If the City Lord catches wind of this and brands us as remnants of the old faction, none of us will live much longer."

"We can't let the City Lord go on like this, or we're all going to be ruined!"

"If we'd known..."

"No point regretting the past; we made our choice back then. Now we just need to make another choice!"

"But the bloodline of Pengshi City's former lord has vanished. Where are we supposed to find another lord recognized by the Royal City?"

"It's strange that after all these years, the current Lord hasn't managed to sire a single child."

"Hush. They all say it's a curse from *that* person."

"Including the City Lord's current condition?"

"What do you think?"

The oldest beastman in the room stood up. "A bloodline from the former city lord's lineage still exists. As far as I know, back then, that person gave birth to a child and, fearing the current lord would murder it, had a trusted confidant risk their life to smuggle the cub out."

"Oh?" The others perked up, their spirits lifting.

"Where is the child?" they asked eagerly.

The old beastman replied, "Unknown."

"..." Everyone fell silent. If they didn't know where the cub was, how were they supposed to push a young master to the throne?

Unfazed, the old beastman continued calmly, "It's just a Shi Sun cub. As long as we find a cub of roughly the right age, as long as all of us acknowledge that cub as the City Lord's sole legitimate son, and as long as the Royal City is willing to recognize it, the cub we push forward will become the next Lord of Pengshi City!"

Every beastman in the room fell silent.

The old beastman swept his gaze across their expressions. "Think about it carefully: is the danger greater if we let the current lord continue running amok, or if we find a cub and have the Royal City recognize his right of succession?"

Beyond mere safety, there were immense profits to be reaped behind the scenes.

Just the thought that the next city lord would be a child selected and hoisted into power by *them*—just how much could they manipulate through that puppet...

Every single person present was tempted.

"Pushing a new city lord is easy enough. The real problem right now is how to deal with the current one."

Such secret gatherings had been held more than once, and the person responsible for networking these clandestine meetings was none other than the old beastman.

Upon returning home, the old beastman entered his secret chamber and saw a young Shi Sun cub practicing secret ancestral techniques inside. He walked over and gently stroked the child's head.

The cub looked up at the old beastman with eyes full of filial devotion and yearning.

The old beastman softly stroked the soft fur on top of the child's head and whispered, "Our family's future rests on you. If an outsider like that Ebenezer could become city lord, why can't we, the true Shi Sun bloodline of Pengshi City, sit upon that throne?"

The cub blinked and said obediently, "I'll listen to Grandfather in everything."

The old beastman smiled with gratification.

Everything was ready; they only owed the eastern wind.

All he needed to do was wait—wait for the savior whom the City Lord was spending a fortune desperately searching for to deliver himself right to their doorstep.

The City Lord would never guess that the savior he had paid a king's ransom and endured untold hardships to find would ultimately be the one to take his life.

Hiding stealthily in invisibility, Shang Feifan had already tagged along and eavesdropped on several secret meetings.

Yes, they had arrived two days prior. Because Shang Feifan was curious about the City Lord's current state, he had detoured to observe the City Lord's Mansion and coincidentally uncovered these secret plots hatched by the aristocrats and officials of Pengshi City.

Hearing what the old beastman had just told his grandson, then glancing at the Shi Sun cub who was quite a bit older and bigger than A-Dai, Shang Feifan reached out and patted A-Dai on the head.

"Look, everyone's already paved the road for you. All you have to do next is wait for these people to take care of that piece of trash Ebenezer, and you can smoothly ascend to the position of city lord."

A-Dai wore a vacant expression: Is getting the position of city lord really this simple?

In Shang Feifan's eyes, it truly was that simple.

Leaving aside the fact that he could use brute force to crush all resistance, eliminate Ebenezer, and compel everyone in Pengshi City to approve A-Dai's ascension...

Even if they took the normal route, he could simply seek out the Eldest Prince or even the Tiger King to directly submit A-Dai's identity.

A-Dai was the direct bloodline of the former city lord; he was inherently more qualified than anyone else to take over as the Lord of Pengshi City.

Yet A-Dai had very little interest in being a city lord. He was still a little baby who needed his daddies to coax him! Why become some overworked, miserable city lord when drinking milk in the arms of his daddy and great-grandmother was so much better?

Seeing that A-Dai was completely unmoved by the prospect of the city lord's seat, Shang Feifan sighed to Lang Mu, "He's still just a little pup, completely ignorant of the sweet taste of power."

Lang Mu chuckled and remarked unexpectedly, "What is a tiny Pengshi City Lord position worth? Our A-Dai is destined to inherit the title of Great Lord of the Blackwater Wastelands in the future."

A thought stirred in Shang Feifan's heart, his eyes lighting up as he looked at A-Dai. What were the Blackwater Wastelands? The kid he and A-Mu raised wouldn't just rule the entire Tianhe Star; at the very least, he had to become some sort of Beast Emperor or Beast Sovereign to have any real prestige!

A-Dai trembled all over and dove headfirst into Daddy Lang Mu's arms. He always felt like Daddy Shang was plotting something evil, and that his future might just be filled with 007 work shifts!

The concept of "007" was something Daddy Shang and Daddy Lang Mu had joked about before, and he understood it loud and clear—it meant working day and night without a break.

He—was—not—doing—it!

chunks.chapterTitle: 第249章 王城派人至彭石城 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第249章 王城派人至彭石城

郎沐已经按照他的感知，在他认为适合的地点划出了一条又一条的线，最终汇聚到彭石城这个巨大的凹陷的盆地。

彭石城的地形已经是郎沐在短时间内勘探出来的最佳地形，岩石层多，天然凹陷，四周是群山和其他地方隔离，除了彭石城和少数村落，几乎看不到人烟，生命也极少。

如果没有彭石城，他们还可以引导地底压力，把压力集中到彭石城所在的山区，令岩浆在这里爆发，这样就会大大减轻地底压力，再加上刻意挖掘出来的泄洪渠道，那黑水荒原绝大部分的岩浆都会流往彭石城所在盆地。

“预计时间半个月。最好能在十二天内完成。”这是郎沐根据他的感知得出的数据。

“十二天……差不多够了。”商非凡颔首，手掌用力往下一劈：“开始吧。”

早已经等待命令的数万不死尸全都转身，只要能抓起工具的不死尸都提着一支被发下来的石镐。

这些石镐还是商非凡集中莫约镇和附近村镇人手，在短短三天中做出来的。

如果没有他之前在王城和天空之城收集到的大量金属，他恐怕就只能让不死尸用手去挖坚硬的石头。

除了石镐这个基本工具，商非凡还跟游戏商城兑换了不少特殊药剂，比如能软化岩石层的、能进行岩石爆破的、能暂时保持不死尸身体不会被高热烧毁的……

郎沐也不止是“画图”，他还会跟着不死尸的大队伍，在重要节点用魔法帮助这些“工人”。

叮叮当当的敲击声瞬间打破了黎明的寂静。石镐与岩石碰撞迸发出耀眼的火花，在昏暗的晨光中如同繁星坠落。

不死尸们不知疲倦地工作着，它们的皮肉和骨骼在高温下时时刻刻都在受损，却丝毫无感。

商非凡感叹，这些不死尸简直就像是这座大陆特地为他送来的工人，否则他还真的不知道要如何解决黑水荒原的岩浆爆发问题。

这可是大型自然-灾害，非人力可干涉。除非他的实力已经达到法神级别，可以移山倒海，直接疏导地底压力，避免大陆架震荡，或加固不稳的地形或直接把危险转移。

可现在他和郎沐距离法神境界都还差着一些，时间又不等人。

他和郎沐是想出了办法，但这个办法需要极多的人力和无数工具，这些人和工具还都要极为耐热，并且不怕受伤和牺牲。

可是这样怎么可能？

这世上不是没有心怀大义甘愿为他人牺牲自己的人，但想要在短时间内集中几万乃至十几万这样的人？

做梦呢！

可如果只是隐瞒或凭借暴-力压迫，把工人当奴隶使用，无视他们的生命，商非凡和郎沐也背负不起这样的巨孽，哪怕有大义之名。

所以这些从毒雾纪沉眠至今的不死尸最好了。

既能发挥它们不怕苦不怕累，更不怕热也不怕疼，还不怕死更不要工钱也不要吃饭的超级优良特质，更能借此解决这批势必会对兽人大陆全体生灵造成大害的群体。

简直不能更多全齐美。

如果没有不死尸，恐怕只有忽悠玩家来帮忙了……咳。

嗐，如果能把邪神信徒也弄来挖掘渠道就更好。

商非凡贪心不足地想。

不死尸挖掘速度远超普通工人，它们不需要休息，不会中暑，更不会因为恐惧而退缩。仅仅一个上午，三四千米长的泄洪渠已经初具雏形。

“照这个速度，三天就能完成通往彭石城深渊的主渠道。”郎沐站在商非凡身旁报告：“第一道工程，不死尸们先沿着你发现的那条通道开凿，将岩浆流引向彭石城外的那条深渊。你发现的那处岩浆池会是最先爆发的，也必须先解决。”

深不见底的裂谷，曾是远古时期神明大战留下的伤痕，如今却将成为吞噬灾难岩浆的巨口。

“之后就把不死尸分成五支大队，同时开工，挖出五条渠道，分别连通最不大稳定的五处喷发口，等渠道挖好，最后挖开喷发口附近，转移压力，让岩浆顺着我们挖好的渠道流淌，尽量不让岩浆流到地面上。”

“这里是一条远古地底河道，如今已经改路，可以利用，这样可以大大减少挖渠时间……”

郎沐最后总结：“目前来看不死尸损失率在预期范围内，备用尸源还算充足。”

随后一顿，“王城的人什么时候才会到？”

郎沐有点忧心。

商非凡拍拍爱人的肩膀：“放心，他们一定会来。”

大王子等人如果连他们送去的消息都不重视，那虎国也别玩了，直接洗洗睡吧，等他家阿呆长大后来接手好了。

王城那边接到商非凡和郎沐送去的消息，果然没人敢轻忽。

王城的议事大殿内，一封加急密报被呈上。

“这是拉斐尔郎沐传来的急信！信上说彭石城主埃比尼泽怨气缠身精神崩溃，虐杀臣民且肆意剥夺城民，已不适合继续治理彭石城。”

郎沐现在还是特别调查官，他原本就具有查看天下直传王者的权力。现在更被大王子从一级升到特级，他送来的信件都是直接送到大王子面前，不得有丝毫耽误。

大王子看完信件就召集了大臣：“彭石城主的事情是其次，更重要的是岩浆爆发的事！”

“信上说岩浆即将涌入彭石盆地，若不撤离，全城必毁。”

“另外，彭石城前城主一脉直系血脉尚存，被炼金大师阿瑞斯商偶尔所救。但彭石城一干人等似乎打算混淆城主血脉，可以请宫廷祭司前往验证身份，以免被宵小占据彭石城。”

“彭石城不重要，如果那里真的如信上所说，会成为一座火山。那彭石城今后还存不存在都难说了。”

“对！现在的重点是赶紧派人去通知当地子民，令他们立刻转移。”

“可那么多人要往哪里转移？附近有愿意接手这么多子民的领地吗？”

“你们是不是忘了郎沐现在就是黑水荒原的新领主，他说了，他即将建造的新城可以接收这些难民。”

“那就好！”

虽然也有人不想郎沐这个新领主这么快就拥有这么多领民，但……无论郎沐还是阿瑞斯商，可都是展露过他们獠牙的人，想和他们作对的，想暗中给他们找事的，也得掂量掂量自己的份量。

再说接受难民可不只是占便宜，相反，前期要付出的物资太多。

有些见不得郎沐好的人，巴不得他们因为这批难民而变得物资短缺。

“别做梦了，郎沐缺什么都不会缺钱，你们别忘了他身后站着的人是谁！”有人冷笑。

众人恍然：是啊，有个能炼制空间储物工具的炼金大师在，郎沐怎么可能缺钱缺物资，只要阿瑞斯商表示他要拍卖几个储物工具，不知多少人会主动送钱送物资过去。

大王子特别淡定地等所有人吵完，最后拍板：“有谁愿意前往彭石城传信？我会调遣王族骑兵团前往支援。”

“我！”伊曼切斯特站起身。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 249: Royal Envoys Sent to Pengshi City (Part 1)

Following his perception, Lang Mu had marked out line after line across the terrain he deemed suitable, ultimately converging on Pengshi City—a massive, naturally depressed basin.

The topography of Pengshi City was already the optimal terrain Lang Mu could survey within a short timeframe. It featured dense rock strata and a natural depression, isolated from other regions by surrounding mountains. Aside from Pengshi City and a few scattered settlements, human habitation was virtually nonexistent, and wildlife was extremely scarce.

Without Pengshi City, they could alternatively guide the subterranean pressure, focusing it toward the mountainous region where Pengshi City lay to trigger a volcanic eruption. This would drastically alleviate the underground pressure. Coupled with deliberately excavated flood-relief channels, the vast majority of the Black Water Wasteland's magma would flow directly into the basin where Pengshi City stood.

"The estimated time is half a month. It would be best to complete it within twelve days." This was the data Lang Mu derived from his perception.

"Twelve days... That should be just about enough." Shang Feifan nodded, chopping his palm down forcefully: "Begin."

The tens of thousands of Undead corpses, having awaited the command for some time, all turned around. Every Undead capable of gripping a tool hoisted a newly distributed stone pickaxe.

These pickaxes were handcrafted by the workforce Shang Feifan had gathered from Moyue Town and nearby villages in a mere three days.

Had it not been for the massive quantities of metal he had previously collected in the Royal City and the City in the Sky, he likely would have had to force the Undead to dig through the hard rock with their bare hands.

Aside from basic tools like pickaxes, Shang Feifan had also redeemed numerous special potions from the game mall—potions capable of softening rock strata, executing rock blasts, and temporarily preventing the Undead's bodies from being incinerated by extreme heat...

Lang Mu did more than just "draw maps"; he accompanied the massive host of Undead, using magic at critical nodes to assist these "workers."

The rhythmic clanging of pickaxes instantly shattered the tranquility of dawn. The collision of stone pickaxes with the bedrock sparked dazzling fireworks, falling like shooting stars through the dim morning light.

The Undead worked tirelessly. Though their flesh and bones suffered constant damage under the high heat, they felt no pain whatsoever.

Shang Feifan sighed. These Undead were practically laborers specially delivered to him by the continent itself; otherwise, he truly wouldn't have known how to resolve the magma eruption crisis in the Black Water Wasteland.

This was, after all, a large-scale natural disaster, something beyond mortal intervention. Unless his strength had already reached the Divine Mage realm, allowing him to move mountains and drain seas, directly channel subterranean pressure, prevent tectonic plate tremors, stabilize unstable terrain, or directly transfer the danger elsewhere.

Yet, both he and Lang Mu were still some distance away from the Divine Mage realm, and time waited for no one.

Though he and Lang Mu had devised a plan, it required immense manpower and countless tools—and both the personnel and the tools had to be extraordinarily heat-resistant, fearless of injury, and ready for sacrifice.

How could such a thing be possible under normal circumstances?

It wasn't that the world lacked righteous individuals willing to sacrifice themselves for others, but wanting to gather tens or even hundreds of thousands of such people within a short timeframe?

Keep dreaming!

Furthermore, if they relied on deception or violent oppression to treat workers as slaves and disregard their lives, neither Shang Feifan nor Lang Mu could shoulder such monstrous karma, not even under the banner of righteousness.

Thus, these Undead who had slumbered since the Poison Fog Epoch were the absolute best choice.

Not only did they possess the supreme and wonderful traits of being fearless of hardship, fatigue, heat, pain, and death, while demanding neither wages nor food, but utilizing them also solved a group that was bound to pose a catastrophic threat to all living beings on the Beastmen Continent.

It truly couldn't get any more mutually beneficial.

Without the Undead, they probably would have had to trick players into helping... cough.

Ah, if only they could round up the Evil God cultists to dig the channels as well.

Shang Feifan thought greedily.

The excavation speed of the Undead far exceeded that of ordinary workers; they required no rest, suffered no heatstroke, and never retreated out of fear. In a single morning, a flood-relief channel three to four thousand meters long was already taking shape.

"At this rate, we can complete the main channel leading to the Pengshi City abyss in three days," Lang Mu reported, standing beside Shang Feifan. "For the first phase of the project, the Undead will excavate along the passage you discovered, guiding the magma flow into the abyss outside Pengshi City. The magma pool you found will be the first to erupt, and it must be dealt with first."

That bottomless rift valley, once a scar left by the wars of the ancient gods, was now destined to become a giant maw swallowing the disastrous magma.

"Afterward, we will divide the Undead into five major brigades to work simultaneously, digging five channels to connect to the five most unstable eruption vents. Once the channels are completed, we will finally breach the areas near the vents to transfer the pressure, letting the magma flow along the channels we've prepared and keeping it off the surface as much as possible."

"There is an ancient underground riverbed here that has since changed course; we can utilize it, which will drastically cut down the trench-digging time..."

Lang Mu concluded, "Presently, the Undead casualty rate is within expectations, and the reserve of backup corpses is quite sufficient."

He then paused, "When will the people from the Royal City arrive?"

Lang Mu felt a tinge of worry.

Shang Feifan patted his lover's shoulder: "Rest assured, they will definitely come."

If the First Prince and his faction couldn't even take the news they sent seriously, then the Tiger Kingdom might as well just give up, pack it in, and wait for his little A-Dai to grow up and take over.

Upon receiving the message sent by Shang Feifan and Lang Mu in the Royal City, naturally, no one dared to take it lightly.

Inside the Royal City's council hall, an expedited top-secret report was presented.

"This is an urgent dispatch sent by Raphael Lang Mu! The letter states that the Lord of Pengshi City, Ebenezer, is plagued by lingering resentment and has suffered a mental breakdown. He has brutally slaughtered his subjects and arbitrarily stripped citizens of their rights, making him entirely unfit to continue governing Pengshi City."

Lang Mu was still a Special Investigator, possessing the authority to directly report to the ruler of the realm. Now, he had been promoted by the First Prince from Rank One to Special Rank, and the letters he sent were delivered directly to the First Prince without the slightest delay.

Upon reading the letter, the First Prince immediately summoned his ministers: "The matter of the Pengshi City Lord is secondary; the most critical issue is the impending magma eruption!"

"The letter states that magma is about to pour into the Pengshi Basin. If there is no evacuation, the entire city will inevitably be destroyed."

"Additionally, the direct bloodline of Pengshi City's former lord still survives, having been occasionally rescued by the Alchemist Grandmaster Ares Shang. However, various factions within Pengshi City appear intent on confusing the lord's bloodline. We should dispatch palace priests to verify their identities and prevent petty villains from usurping Pengshi City."

"Pengshi City itself is unimportant if it truly transforms into a volcano as the letter predicts. Whether Pengshi City will even exist hereafter is questionable."

"Correct! The immediate priority is to dispatch people to notify the local populace to evacuate immediately."

"But where are so many people supposed to evacuate to? Are there any neighboring territories willing to take in so many citizens?"

"Have you forgotten that Lang Mu is now the new Lord of the Black Water Wasteland? He stated that the new city he is about to build can accommodate these refugees."

"That settles it then!"

Although some individuals resented seeing Lang Mu, the new lord, acquire so many subjects so quickly, nonetheless... both Lang Mu and Ares Shang had bared their fangs before. Anyone wishing to oppose them or secretly stir up trouble had better weigh their own strength first.

Besides, taking in refugees wasn't merely about seizing benefits; on the contrary, the initial outlay of supplies was astronomical.

Those who loathed seeing Lang Mu succeed were praying that this batch of refugees would plunge them into a severe shortage of supplies.

"Keep dreaming. Lang Mu will lack anything except money. Don't forget who is standing behind him!" Someone sneered.

Everyone had a sudden realization: That's right. With an Alchemist Grandmaster capable of crafting spatial storage tools standing behind him, how could Lang Mu ever lack money or supplies? As long as Ares Shang announced he was auctioning off a few storage tools, countless people would voluntarily deliver money and supplies to his doorstep.

The First Prince waited very calmly for everyone to finish arguing, then made the final decision: "Who is willing to travel to Pengshi City to deliver the message? I will dispatch the Royal Cavalry Regiment to provide support."

"I will go!" Yimanchester stood up.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第249章 王城派人至彭石城 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
在一边旁听的宫廷祭司蚪海潮也站起身，“我也过去一趟吧。彭石城主的怨气缠身我也听到了一些传闻，听说他找了不少人去看，都没能解决。”

各国宫廷祭司只要确认没问题，基本都还留在各国宫廷内继续他们原本的职责。

不死尸的工作效率极高，短短三天，一条长达十多千米的深渠已经成型。

最后只要挖开喷发口，岩浆就会顺着沟壑流淌。

八级不死尸就站在商非凡身边，等待他下达命令。

商非凡正在等待郎沐通知。

郎沐现在就相当于总工程师，他得确保挖出来的渠道有一定安全性，不会让岩浆流到渠道以外的地方，或引起其他不必要的变动。

“可以了！”郎沐传来明确信息。

商非凡嘴角微扬，对八级不死尸一点头。

八级不死尸身体一闪，快速离开。

不久，喷发口被挖掘开，郎沐在那里小心施展魔法，促使地底岩浆按照他所设定的方向喷发而出，随后沿着泄洪渠倾斜而下。

赤红的火龙滚滚而来。

商非凡就站在深渊附近。

他负责监督和总控，不但监督不死尸的工作，还要监督彭石城和附近村镇人口以及生灵的转移。

早在不死尸动手前，转移就开始了。

郎沐是位受到自然之力青睐的魔导师，他只要警告这里的生灵们，告诉它们这里即将发生大灾难，不再适合它们生活，这里的生灵就自发且迅速地离开了它们的家园。

兽人们一直和自然界的生灵有着极为密切的交流，尤其他们身边的巨虫坐骑和战兽伙伴。

当荒野中的生灵们开始奔逃，巨虫坐骑和战兽们也开始焦躁不安，不断试图逃跑和拱着伙伴催促他们逃跑。

兽人们自然察觉了自然界的变化。

“地震？还是其他可怕灾难？”

有经验的兽人们聚集，开始商量。村里的长者安排人手去彭石城询问和请教该怎么办。

可没等问询的人回来，就有人带来了准确消息。

“王城派军队来了，正在到处通知，说我们这片即将发生大型灾难，地震加火山爆发！”

“什么？这是真的？王城真的派人来通知了？为什么彭石城那边还没有任何传音？”

“千真万确！这还能有假？不信你们出去看，王城来了一支军队！那些军兵分成一个个小队，到处通知我们这样的村镇。他们主队此时也正在赶往彭石城，这会儿说不定已经到了。”

“快！收拾东西，走！”

“可我们要往哪里走？”

村镇的兽人们刚露出茫然之色，刚才跑回来传话的兽人就得意说：“我听到了，那些王城的军兵有在喊，让迁移的人跟着黑水荒原领主走，说黑水荒原来了新领主，他们准备在黑水河的入海口那片平原建立新城，现在欢迎任何地方任何种族任何身份的兽人前去落户！还说第一批过去的人会有落户的优惠政策。”

“什么优惠政策？你知道吗？”

“呃，我没听到，就听到咱们这里要完，就赶紧跑回来通知大家了。”

“哎！你怎么听话听一半哪。”

“好了，大家先回去收拾，那些军兵不是挨着村镇通知吗，他们肯定也会来我们村，到时大家再和村长村老他们一起去问个详细就是。”

众人一听也是，纷纷散去回家准备大迁移事宜。

有人舍不得离开家园，但这是大型灾难，等到通知的兽人士兵们前来，就跟他们说得很清楚，说留下九成九就是一个死。负责传讯的兽人士兵又把黑水荒原新领主关于新城的落户政策一说，不少不想离开故土的老兽人也心动了。

那可是一个人头就给予半亩地的可耕种田地！不问幼崽还是老人！

半亩地以兽人们的劳动力来说真的很少，但那可是能耕种的田地。

就问除了那些贵族大户，现在有多少平民能拥有可耕种土地？

虽然分给他们的田地并不完全属于他们，他们没有资格转让和买卖，但只要他们活着，他们就可以免费承包，每年出产只要交纳二十分之一当人头税就可以。

如此优惠，就问现在的兽人大陆哪里有？

如果家里人口多，连娃娃和老人都算上，十个人家里就能有整整五亩的可耕种田地！

如此优惠，不用其他优惠政策，就足够让兽人们趋之若鹜。

更何况新领主还承诺除了人头税，其他农业税丝毫不收。而做买卖的和当工匠的也不用担心，都有各自的优惠政策，总之都比其他地方要宽松得多。

最最让彭石城附近村镇乃至黑水荒原各处兽人心动的是，新领主还要公开招聘各级各业的管理人员，通过考试来决定谁来“当官”。

也就是说原本由贵族垄断的管理阶层，现在他们这些普通兽人也有机会跻身进入。

而为了幼崽的兽人则听说新城会开办学校，凡是未成年兽人都能享受免费教育——商非凡和郎沐有钱，他们负担不了一个国家的免费教育，但一个黑水荒原的幼崽，他们还是负担得起的。

如此多的优惠政策简直炫晕了黑水荒原的兽人们。

不少日子过不下去（包括生活很好）的兽人都在寻找黑水领的办事处，要么跟着黑水领的领路员一起走，要么拿上地图，与整个村子或与全家族一起摸过去。

彭石城附近的村镇居民就更不用说了，地震和岩浆都要爆发了，不走留着等死吗？

同一时间，一支声势浩大的王城队伍抵达彭石城。

五百名王骑禁卫骑着他们的战兽伙伴，愣是跑出了五千人的架势。

不等他们人到彭石城，兽吼声已经震彻云霄。

彭石城的人都听到啦。

何况那么大那么显然的一支队伍，怎么可能没有人看到。

彭石城主也早早得到消息，心里各种猜测和惶恐不说，先着装整齐地带着城中贵族和官员们出城迎接。

伊曼切斯特架势摆的很足，他还是和宫廷祭司同行，为了响应信件中提到的最好“大张旗鼓”这个词，那是旗帜飘扬兽吼阵阵，乘坐的车辆更是曾经公爵府最好的车，拉车的兽都是皮毛统一体型巨大的驯兽，就差锣鼓喧天宣告他这个钦差大臣和宫廷祭司的大驾前来。

这样夸张的阵仗，除了让彭石城及附近兽人全都知道事情不小，不敢轻忽。还有就是为了让埃比尼泽不敢反抗——疯子也许不怕死，但他一定怕“王权的威严”。

果然，当伊曼切斯特绷着脸宣称自己带着王令前来，埃比尼泽虽然满眼血丝，却无法公然违抗王命。

“奉王命，彭石城盆地大难即至，命所有城民及附近子民即刻迁移！城主埃比尼泽因精神失常，暂且押往王城受审！”

“什么？！”埃比尼泽变脸。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 249: Royal Envoys Sent to Pengshi City (Part 2)

Dou Haichao, a palace priest who had been listening from the side, also stood up. "I will make the trip as well. I've heard some rumors regarding the lingering resentment plaguing the Lord of Pengshi City; I heard he sought out quite a few people to examine it, but none could resolve it."

As long as their allegiances were verified as sound, palace priests of various nations generally remained within their respective royal courts to fulfill their original duties.

The work efficiency of the Undead was astonishingly high. In just three days, a deep canal over ten kilometers long had taken shape.

All that remained was to breach the eruption vent, and the magma would flow along the trenches.

The Rank 8 Undead stood beside Shang Feifan, awaiting his command.

Shang Feifan was currently awaiting word from Lang Mu.

Lang Mu was acting as the chief engineer, ensuring that the excavated channels possessed a certain degree of safety to prevent the magma from overflowing outside the channels or triggering other unnecessary disruptions.

"It's ready!" Lang Mu transmitted a clear message.

The corners of Shang Feifan's mouth curled up slightly as he nodded to the Rank 8 Undead.

The figure of the Rank 8 Undead flickered, rapidly vanishing.

Shortly afterward, the eruption vent was blasted open. Lang Mu carefully executed his magic there, compelling the subterranean magma to erupt precisely in the direction he had set, after which it cascaded downward along the flood-relief channel.

A crimson fire dragon came rolling forward.

Shang Feifan stood near the abyss.

He was responsible for overall supervision and control—overseeing not only the work of the Undead, but also the evacuation of the population and wildlife from Pengshi City and the surrounding villages and towns.

Evacuation had begun even before the Undead took action.

Lang Mu was a Grand Mage favored by the power of nature. All he needed to do was warn the living beings of this region, telling them that a major catastrophe was about to strike and that it would no longer be suitable for habitation, and the local creatures spontaneously and swiftly abandoned their homeland.

Beastmen had always maintained an extremely close communion with the creatures of nature, especially their giant insect mounts and battle-beast companions.

When the creatures of the wilderness began to flee, the giant insect mounts and battle-beasts also grew restless, continually attempting to bolt while nudging their partners to urge them to run.

Naturally, the beastmen perceived these shifts in nature.

"An earthquake? Or some other terrifying disaster?"

Experienced beastmen gathered together to deliberate. The village elders arranged for people to go to Pengshi City to inquire and ask what should be done.

However, before the messengers could return, accurate news was brought by others.

"The Royal City has sent an army! They're spreading notices everywhere, saying a massive disaster is about to strike our region—earthquakes combined with volcanic eruptions!"

"What? Is this true? The Royal City actually sent people to notify us? Why hasn't there been any transmission from Pengshi City?"

" Absolutely true! Could this be fake? If you don't believe me, go outside and look; an army has come from the Royal City! Those soldiers are divided into small squads, notifying villages and towns like ours everywhere. Their main force is currently rushing toward Pengshi City; they might have already arrived by now."

"Quick! Pack your things and let's go!"

"But where are we supposed to go?"

Just as the beastmen of the village wore blank expressions, the beastman who had just run back to deliver the news said triumphantly: "I heard it! Those soldiers from the Royal City were shouting, telling the migrating people to follow the Lord of the Black Water Wasteland. They said a new lord has arrived in the Black Water Wasteland, and they're preparing to build a new city on the plain at the estuary of the Black Water River. Right now, they welcome beastmen of any region, any race, and any status to settle down there! They even said the first batch of people to move over will receive preferential settlement policies."

"What preferential policies? Do you know?"

"Uh, I didn't catch that part. I just heard that our place is finished, so I ran right back to notify everyone."

"Hey! Why do you only listen to half of what people say?"

"Alright, everyone go back and pack up first. Aren't those soldiers notifying villages one by one? They'll definitely come to our village too, and then we can all ask the village chief and elders for the full details."

Hearing this, the crowd agreed and dispersed to their respective homes to prepare for the massive migration.

Some people were reluctant to leave their homeland, but this was a major disaster. When the notifying beastman soldiers arrived, they explained the situation with utmost clarity: staying behind meant a ninety-nine percent chance of death. When the reporting beastman soldiers then recounted the new lord's favorable settlement policies regarding the new city, even many elderly beastmen who had been unwilling to leave their ancestral soil felt their hearts stir.

That was half an *mu* of arable farmland granted per person! It didn't matter whether they were children or the elderly!

Half an *mu* was truly very little given the beastmen's labor capacity, but that was *arable farmland*.

Just ask: apart from those aristocratic magnates, how many commoners nowadays could own cultivable land?

Although the farmland allocated to them did not entirely belong to them—they had no right to transfer or trade it—as long as they remained alive, they could lease it tax-free, with only one-twentieth of the annual yield paid as a poll tax.

With such generous terms, ask if anywhere else on the Beastmen Continent offered the same!

If a family had many members, counting even babies and grandparents, a household of ten could secure a full five *mu* of cultivable farmland!

Such preferential policies, without needing any other perks, were enough to make beastmen flock there like ducks.

Moreover, the new lord had also promised that aside from the poll tax, no other agricultural taxes would be levied whatsoever. Those engaging in commerce or working as artisans needn't worry either, as there were respective preferential policies for them. In short, everything was far more lenient than anywhere else.

Most thrilling of all for the villages and towns near Pengshi City, as well as beastmen throughout the Black Water Wasteland, was that the new lord would openly recruit management personnel across all ranks and industries, deciding who would "become an official" through examinations.

In other words, the administrative strata previously monopolized by the nobility was now open to ordinary beastmen, giving them a chance to climb upward.

As for parents concerned for their children, they heard that the new city would establish a school, where every underage beastman could enjoy free education—Shang Feifan and Lang Mu were wealthy; they couldn't afford free education for an entire nation, but the children of the Black Water Wasteland were well within their means.

So many preferential policies simply dazzled the beastmen of the Black Water Wasteland.

Countless beastmen who were struggling to get by (along with those living quite comfortably) began searching for the Black Water Territory's offices, either traveling alongside Black Water guides or grabbing maps and making their way over with their entire villages or clans.

Needless to say, for the residents of the villages and towns near Pengshi City, with earthquakes and magma about to erupt, who wouldn't leave and instead stay behind to wait for death?

At the same time, an imposing procession from the Royal City arrived at Pengshi City.

Five hundred Royal Guards riding their battle-beast companions managed to project the overwhelming aura of a five-thousand-strong force.

Before they even reached Pengshi City, the roars of beasts shook the heavens and earth.

Everyone in Pengshi City heard it.

Moreover, with such a massive and conspicuous procession, how could no one see them?

The Lord of Pengshi City had also received word early on. Putting aside his internal speculations and panic, he quickly dressed in formal attire and led the city's nobles and officials out of the city to welcome them.

Yimanchester struck a grand posture, traveling alongside the palace priest. To echo the suggestion mentioned in the letter to make things as "pompous" as possible, banners fluttered while beast roars echoed endlessly. The carriage they rode in was the finest from the former Duke's estate, pulled by uniformly coated, massive trained beasts. It lacked only gongs and drums to announce the grand arrival of the Imperial Envoy and Palace Priest.

Such an exaggerated display served not only to make the beastmen of Pengshi City and its surroundings realize that the matter was grave and not to be taken lightly, but also to ensure Ebenezer wouldn't dare resist—a madman might not fear death, but he certainly feared the "majesty of royal authority."

Sure enough, when Yimanchester declared with a stern face that he had arrived bearing a royal decree, Ebenezer, despite his bloodshot eyes, could not openly defy the king's mandate.

"By royal decree, a great disaster is imminent in the Pengshi Basin. All citizens and local subjects are ordered to evacuate immediately! City Lord Ebenezer, due to mental instability, is to be temporarily detained and escorted to the Royal City for trial!"

"What?!" Ebenezer's expression changed drastically.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第250章 继承城主府财产 (Part 1)
chunks.chineseText:
第250章 继承城主府财产

埃比尼泽当然不甘心就这么束手就擒，但伊曼切斯特压根就没给他反抗的机会——手一挥，就有一支小队的王骑禁卫围住了埃比尼泽。

埃比尼泽想让手下和他一起反，但他抬眼望过去，就见包括他的心腹在内，所有人都避开了目光。

埃比尼泽心里发冷：怎么会这样？

但他心中又隐隐知道为什么会变成这样，就因为他这段时间的“发疯”。

不！他没有疯！

埃比尼泽不知道自己喊了出来，他还试图冲出禁卫们的包围圈。

这下好了，原本还在怀疑他是不是精神有问题的人现在也笃定这位城主肯定是精神出问题了。

在他们看来正常来说，如果觉得自己被冤枉，难道不该是先解释吗？

可这位城主却大喊大叫双眼赤红，不顾包围他的王城骑兵，就想要脱逃——逃跑也是讲究策略的嘛，而埃比尼泽现在做的跟自寻死路有什么区别？

伊曼切斯特果然冷声喝令：“违抗王令者，立地斩杀！”

“吼！”骑兵们齐齐一声吼，再无顾忌，出手都是杀招。

埃比尼泽一边施展杀招攻击骑兵，一边疯狂喊叫，甚至高喊出：“我知道这一切都是假的！这是噩梦！这是梦中梦！我一定还没有醒过来！”

“石狲悦！石狲坤！你们给我出来！不要以为这样就能逼死我！我不会死！我能杀死你们一次，就能再杀死你们一次！你们给我滚出来！”

埃比尼泽疯狂嘶吼着叫骂着。

王城来人和许多城民：……这算是不打自招吗？

伊曼切斯特看向宫廷祭司。

蚪海潮轻轻点头，表示他都看到也都听到。

伊曼切斯特一抬手指，其他未动的王城骑士再次分出一支小队，这次全都是远程攻击者，而且他们无一例外都是血脉天赋者，手上都戴着能放大他们天赋能力的炼金佩饰。

不过半分钟，也许半分钟都没有，埃比尼泽的脑袋就被一道攻击给炸成了碎片。

当埃比尼泽倒下时，他的心腹和彭石城的官员们全都低下头，不是在可怜和同情他们这位城主，而是在为王城的力量胆颤心惊。

伊曼切斯特目光扫过这些官员和贵族，心中冷笑，现在他还没工夫去收拾这些家伙，当即命令这些人立刻向彭石城全体城民传达王城指令，说明火山即将爆发、地震即将来临，想要活的人赶紧收拾东西撤离出彭石城。

当然，真有那不怕死想留下的，那就自便，不必强求。

撤离点分两处，分别为前往黑森林城和前往黑水荒原新领主建立的新城。

只不过前者什么优惠政策都没有，去到那里就只能当难民。

后者则正在接纳新人，哪怕没有一技之长，也不用担心到了新城没有饭吃——新城还没有建立，那里有很多活干。

伊曼切斯特只有一个要求，那就是务必在半个小时内把他的命令传达到彭石城每一处地方，确保每一个城民都听到要撤离的消息。

彭石城官员们恐惧王城骑士团的威力，不敢有任何屁话，连拍马屁都不敢——敢上去拍马屁套近乎的都被撅了，全都飞快地跑出去传达王城指令。

伊曼切斯特又下令让王城骑士进入彭石城，在各大主要干道张贴撤离通知。

不远处的一处高地，阿呆站在他商爸的肩膀上，额头蹭了蹭他商爸的耳朵。

商非凡单手把他提下来：“要去见见他们吗？你可以给那位王庭祭司一滴血，他会当着城民的面验明你身为前任城主直系血脉的身份。等王城那边登记你的身份后，你就能成为新的彭石城城主。”

想要成为一城之主，自然不会这么简单。

就算王城承认继承者的身份，一个幼崽想要当城主，至少身边要有能辅佐他的能干人，还要在彭石城有一定声望，能压得住当地权贵。如果没有还能坐上城主之位，那九成九都是王城弄的傀儡。

阿呆飞快摇头，拒绝三连：“不见，不验身份，不当城主。”

商非凡逗儿子：“真的不要？那可是一城城主，有豪华大房子住，有大把的钱花，还有很多仆人听从你的命令。”

阿呆眼睛倏地一亮，小兴奋：“爸爸，当了城主会有很多钱很多物资吗？那我们去拿来，都给你和沐爸爸呀~”

商非凡满脸欣慰：“不错，长脑子了。那么多好东西怎么能凭白便宜其他人？儿砸，记住了，你郎沐爸爸什么都好，就是有时候有点傻，有好处也往外推，你可不能跟他学这点。”

阿呆人生打开了另一扇窗，想法跟之前截然不同，反过来催促：“那爸爸我们快去找那个祭司，赶紧把那个城主家里……不对，是我爷爷和妈妈的东西都拿回来。哦，那个死掉的城主是我爹，那他的东西也都是我的。”

商非凡老怀大慰，抱着儿子就去给他儿子讨家产了。

伊曼切斯特和蚪海潮见到商非凡出现，半点不惊讶。

蚪海潮甚至没要商非凡多说，就主动说要给阿呆验证身份。

找来几个城里的老牌贵族和城主府管家，当着他们面的验证了阿呆的身份，确定他就是彭石城城主府所有财产最名正言顺的继承人。

阿呆可既是前任城主石狲坤的亲孙子，又是现任城主埃比尼泽的亲儿子，真的是再没有人的身份比他更根正苗红。

那做了准备的老贵族压根就没机会辩驳，更没有机会把自己的孙子推出来。

他们找的那个杀手已经来了彭石城，但在他被引荐到埃比尼泽面前时，王城钦差已经到达。

这些全都打了某些人一个措不及防，他们都没有反应过来，更不知道是谁把埃比尼泽精神有问题的事给捅了上去。

等看到一个高大的成年兽人抱着一个石狲幼崽出现，要验证其身份后，这些想要谋反的人还在心中想：螳螂捕蝉黄雀在后，看来王城那边早就瞄上了他们彭石城。看，连继承人都准备好了！这要不是谋划已久，他们就把眼珠子扣下来！

商非凡对上那个老贵族愤恨的目光，还对他笑了笑。

那笑容在那老贵族看来，简直是意味深长。

老贵族心里又怒又气，更害怕。

他怕王城那边已经知道他的打算，怕王城在解决了城主埃比尼泽后，还会对他们这些彭石城的老势力动手。

有了这个担心的老贵族是屁都不敢放一个，只求王城来人不要注意到他。

如果没有王城派来的骑士兵团，如果没有宫廷祭司亲自前来给阿呆验证身份，这些彭石城老贵族们还能挣扎一二，至少拖延时间，让他们能有机会转移城主府的财产和整座城的物资，但现在一切都变成了空。

确定了阿呆身份后，伊曼切斯特当即命令城主府管家交出城主府的所有财产清单。

为了防止管家有所隐瞒，伊曼切斯特还找了城主的心腹下属另外询问（审问）。

几人的口供交汇到一起，城主府的财产就大致明确下来。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 250: Inheriting the City Lord's Estate (Part 1)

Ebenezer certainly wasn't willing to surrender without a fight, but Manchester didn't give him the slightest chance to resist—with a wave of his hand, a squad of Royal Cavalry Guards immediately surrounded Ebenezer.

Ebenezer tried to incite his subordinates to rebel alongside him, but when he raised his eyes and looked around, he saw that everyone, including his most trusted confidants, deliberately avoided his gaze.

A chill gripped Ebenezer's heart: How could it come to this?

Yet deep down, he vaguely knew why things had turned out this way. It was entirely because of his "madness" over this recent period.

No! He hadn't gone mad!

Ebenezer didn't realize he had screamed it out loud as he attempted to break through the guards' encirclement.

Now look at him—those who had previously doubted whether he had mental issues were now completely convinced that the City Lord's mind had indeed snapped.

In their view, normally speaking, if someone felt wronged, shouldn't their first reaction be to offer an explanation?

Yet this City Lord was screaming at the top of his lungs, his eyes bloodshot, charging blindly at the surrounding royal cavalry in a desperate bid to escape—escaping required strategy, of course, and what difference was Ebenezer's current behavior from marching straight to his own execution?

As expected, Manchester gave a cold command: "Anyone who defies the royal decree shall be executed on the spot!"

"Roar!" The cavalry let out a unified battle cry, casting aside all hesitation as every strike they unleashed was meant to kill.

While executing lethal moves against the cavalry, Ebenezer shrieked madly, even shouting at the top of his lungs, "I know all of this is fake! This is a nightmare! This is a dream within a dream! I must not be awake yet!"

"Shi Sunyue! Shi Sun-kun! Get out here! Don't think you can drive me to my death like this! I won't die! I killed you once, and I can kill you again! Get your asses out here!"

Ebenezer roared and cursed like a madman.

The royal emissaries and the gathered townspeople: ...Should this be considered a confession without torture?

Manchester glanced toward the palace priest.

Dou Haichao nodded slightly, indicating that he had seen and heard everything.

Manchester flicked his finger, and the remaining royal knights who had not yet moved split off into another squad. This time, they were all long-range attackers, every single one of them possessing bloodline innate talents, and all wearing alchemical accessories on their hands that could amplify their innate abilities.

Less than half a minute—perhaps not even half a minute later—Ebenezer's head was blasted into pieces by a coordinated strike.

When Ebenezer fell, his confidants and the officials of Peng Shi City all lowered their heads. They weren't feeling pity or sympathy for their City Lord; rather, they were trembling with fear before the terrifying might of the royal capital.

Manchester swept his gaze across these officials and nobles, a cold sneer hidden in his heart. He didn't have the time to deal with these fellows right now, so he immediately ordered them to convey the royal command to the entire populace of Peng Shi City without delay: a volcano was about to erupt, and an earthquake was imminent. Anyone who wanted to live should quickly pack their belongings and evacuate Peng Shi City.

Of course, if anyone truly had a death wish and wanted to stay behind, they were free to do so; no one would force them.

There were two designated evacuation destinations: one leading to Black Forest City, and the other to the new city established by the new lord in the Blackwater Wasteland.

However, the former offered no preferential policies whatsoever; those who went there would simply live as refugees.

The latter was currently welcoming newcomers. Even without any specialized skills, one didn't need to worry about going hungry upon arrival—the new city was still under construction, and there was plenty of work to be done there.

Manchester had only one requirement: they must ensure his command was delivered to every single corner of Peng Shi City within half an hour, making certain that every last citizen heard the news of the evacuation.

Terrified by the might of the Royal Cavalry Regiment, the officials of Peng Shi City didn't dare to utter a single word of nonsense, not even daring to suck up or flatter—anyone who had tried to curry favor or cozy up earlier had been rebuffed and dismissed. They all scattered like the wind to spread the royal decree.

Manchester then ordered the royal knights to enter Peng Shi City and post the evacuation notices along all major thoroughfares.

At a nearby vantage point, A-Dai stood on his Shang-ba's shoulder, rubbing his forehead against his Shang-ba's ear.

Shi Feifan picked him up with one hand: "Do you want to go see them? You can give a drop of your blood to that royal priest; he will verify your identity as the direct blood descendant of the former City Lord right in front of the citizens. Once the royal capital registers your identity, you can become the new City Lord of Peng Shi City."

Becoming the lord of a city was naturally not that simple.

Even if the royal capital recognized the heir's identity, a child attempting to become a City Lord needed, at the very least, capable people by their side to assist them, as well as a certain level of prestige within Peng Shi City to keep the local power brokers in check. If someone managed to sit in the City Lord's chair without these prerequisites, nine times out of ten, they were merely a puppet set up by the royal capital.

A-Dai shook his head vigorously, delivering a triple refusal: "I won't see them, I won't verify my identity, and I won't be the City Lord."

Shi Feifan teased his son: "You really don't want it? That's the lord of an entire city, you know! You'd get to live in a luxurious mansion, spend piles of money, and have countless servants jump at your command."

A-Dai's eyes suddenly lit up with a flash of excitement: "Daddy, if I become the City Lord, will there be lots of money and supplies? Then we can go take them all and give them to you and Mu-daddy~"

Shi Feifan beamed with absolute satisfaction: "Not bad, you're starting to use your brain. How could we let all those good things go to waste on other people for nothing? Remember this, my boy: your Lang Mu-daddy is good at everything, but sometimes he's a bit foolish and pushes away benefits when they come his way. You must never learn that from him."

A window had swung open in A-Dai's young life, and his perspective had completely flipped. Instead, he urged, "Then Daddy, let's hurry and find that priest! Let's go get everything in the City Lord's house... No, wait, everything belonging to my grandfather and mother back. Oh, and that dead City Lord was my biological father, so all his things belong to me too."

Shi Feifan's heart swelled with aged satisfaction as he scooped up his son and marched off to claim his boy's rightful inheritance.

Manchester and Dou Haichao showed not the slightest bit of surprise when Shi Feifan appeared.

Without even needing Shi Feifan to elaborate, Dou Haichao proactively offered to verify A-Dai's identity.

They summoned several veteran nobles of the city and the steward of the City Lord's estate, verifying A-Dai's identity right before their eyes and confirming beyond a doubt that he was the most rightful and legitimate heir to all the assets of the Peng Shi City Lord's estate.

A-Dai was not only the biological grandson of the former City Lord, Shi Sunyue, but also the biological son of the current City Lord, Ebenezer. Truly, no one's lineage could possibly be more orthodox or direct.

The veteran nobles who had prepared schemes of their own didn't even get a chance to argue, let alone push forward grandsons of their own.

The assassin they had hired had already arrived in Peng Shi City, but just as he was about to be introduced to Ebenezer, the royal envoys had already arrived.

All of this caught certain schemers completely off guard. They hadn't reacted in time, nor did they have any idea who had leaked the news of Ebenezer's mental instability to the capital.

When they saw a tall, adult beastman carrying a young stone-monkey cub and appearing to verify its identity, those plotting a rebellion were still thinking to themselves: *The mantis stalks the cicada, unaware of theoriole behind. It seems the royal capital has been eyeing our Peng Shi City all along. Look, they even have an heir prepared! If this wasn't meticulously planned for a long time, they'd pluck out their own eyeballs!*

Meeting the venomous glare of the old noble, Shi Feifan simply smiled back at him.

In the old noble's eyes, that smile was simply filled with profound, inscrutable meaning.

Inside, the old noble was furious, outraged, and above all, terrified.

He feared that the royal capital had already uncovered his intentions; he feared that after dealing with City Lord Ebenezer, the royal capital would turn its sights on old established factions like theirs in Peng Shi City.

Plagued by this fear, the old noble didn't dare to let out even a single fart, praying only that the royal emissaries wouldn't pay any attention to him.

If not for the regiment of royal knights sent by the capital, if not for the palace priest himself coming to verify A-Dai's identity, these veteran nobles of Peng Shi City could have struggled and resisted for a bit, at least buying enough time to spirit away the City Lord's estate's treasures and the city's entire stockpile of supplies. But now, everything had vanished into smoke.

Once A-Dai's identity was confirmed, Manchester immediately ordered the steward of the City Lord's estate to hand over the complete inventory of the estate's assets.

To prevent the steward from concealing anything, Manchester also brought in Ebenezer's trusted subordinates for separate questioning (interrogation).

When the confessions of several individuals were cross-referenced, the wealth of the City Lord's estate became roughly clear.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第250章 继承城主府财产 (Part 2)
chunks.chineseText:
阿呆成为城主府继承人，下达的第一个命令就是：“属于彭石城的公用物资交给愿意安顿彭石城城民的接纳方，且这批物资只能使用在彭石城迁移城民身上。”

这下好了，彭石城那些贵族和官员连想要趁机贪掉彭石城公用物资的可能性都没了。

伊曼切斯特直接派出王城骑士团的人去接手城中公共仓库，并查账和封印。

所幸埃比尼泽还是很在乎彭石城的公共物资——在他看来，这些东西都是他的，谁敢贪污那就是在贪他的东西，抓到就是死罪。搞得彭石城管理公共物资的人谁也不敢贪墨，尤其在埃比尼泽近期发疯以后。

所以这批庞大的物资都在原地，接手得也比较轻松。

黑森林城那边也有专门接纳难民的官员跟过来，他将根据前往黑森林城的难民人数来分得一定比例的物资。

公共物资由伊曼切斯特那边看管起来，就不用阿呆操心了——只要有人愿意前往黑水荒原新城，那里的东西就必然也要分他爸一部分，他急什么？

阿呆急的是接收城主府的所有财产。

石狲家族经营彭石城可不止两百多年，那是从大繁华纪直到现在。只不过大战纪时期整个彭石城缩水得厉害，石狲家族不得不躲起来，之后的毒雾纪则靠着强大武力和幸运保护了自己的财产。

说彭石城幸运，那是因为毒雾纪时不死尸到处肆掠，但古怪的是彭石城附近却不见多少不死尸。

彭石城人活到现在压根就不知道就在他们城池不远处的地底下沉睡着几十万的不死尸。

埃比尼泽弄死石狲悦，当了城主后，自然也没必要转移财产，所以城主府的财产保留得十分完好。

阿呆抓住他商爸，拿着几方供出的财产清单，一一清点查收。

管家对埃比尼泽忠心耿耿，城主府里的人也惧怕埃比尼泽的手段，倒是没人敢偷盗城主府财产。当然如果埃比尼泽持续疯下去，那就说不准了。

管家原本还想隐瞒部分财产——也不知道他存的什么心，但在和埃比尼泽心腹口供对照后，他隐瞒的小库房和部分被埃比尼泽当做风险备用的秘密物资都暴露了出来。

管家自然没有落到任何好处，直接被伊曼切斯特给处理了。

商非凡带着儿子喜滋滋地把整座城主府积累不知多少年的财富全都搜刮到自己的荷包里。

钱，材料，药材，食物，衣物布料，古玩奇珍……

这对父子俩不禁对石狲家族积累财物的能力大为佩服。

还有完全隶属于石狲家族名下的矿产、地产、位于王城等地的商铺等等。

这些东西暂时无法收取，不过阿呆拿到了文书，以后去取就可以。

搜刮到后来，就连阿呆都不由感叹：“爸爸啊，幸好我聪明了一下下。”

商非凡被逗笑，摸着他的方脑袋说：“是啊是啊，否则你看你就要错过多大的一笔财富了。”

阿呆眼睛亮晶晶：“爸爸，你说我会不会还有一个人渣爸爸在别的什么城啊？或者人渣爷爷？”

商非凡：“……”

“哈哈哈！”身后传来大笑声，是伊曼切斯特找来了。

伊曼切斯特见到父子俩就竖起大拇指：“你这个儿子，了不得！是个人才！不愧是你和郎沐的儿子。”

商非凡骄傲：“那是。”

伊曼切斯特吃吃笑，对商非凡使了个眼色：“你和祭司？”

那位宫廷祭司在商非凡出现后，明显几次都想和商非凡说话，但商非凡都无视了。

商非凡单手抱着儿子，空着的手摆了摆：“你不用管。”

伊曼切斯特确认周围无人，还是压低了声音：“听祭司的意思，似乎这里原本不会爆发自然-灾害。”

“嗯，他没算错。这里的自然-灾害是人为，因为我和阿沐把整个黑水荒原的岩浆都会集中到这里。”商非凡的语气就像是在说家里院子要挖个小鱼池一样。

伊曼切斯特：“……需要帮忙吗？”

他好歹也是一个魔法师，手上有魔晶，他就能发挥出实力。

商非凡摇头：“不用了，我们已经找好工匠。麻烦你那边安排好全城迁移就行。”

伊曼切丝特也担心自己胡乱插手会不会打乱商非凡的安排，就只点点头说：“那行。你们想要多少人？”

那意思就是你们如果想要全城人，他也可以安排过去。

商非凡再次摇头：“新城确实需要人手，但我们需要的是到那里就能干活的人。像是什么贵族、想要享受和摆谱的富商和官员，想要谋夺新城权利的野心家，就让他们有多远滚多远。”

伊曼切斯特懂了，但他还是确认道：“你真的不要那些有资产者？那些人虽然讨厌，但也能帮着新城快速建立起来。”

商非凡嗤笑：“如果真有人想要去新城，你就问他们担不担心新城主到时候只要物资不要人。”

伊曼切斯特懂了，商非凡他们不缺物资，只缺能正儿八经干活的人。

那些有物资有家产的人跟过去，虽然能一定程度让新城快速建立起来，但这些人靠着带过去的资产也能完成极快的原始积累，成为新城的新贵。

而这显然不是商非凡和郎沐他们想要的。

“放心，除了普通城民，我保证那些贵族和不能做事的官员一个都不会混入前往新城的迁移人口中。”

伊曼切斯特从小在贵族堆里长大，他真的太知道那些人想要的是什么，又最惧怕什么。

商非凡当即拿出一个袋子递过去，还催了一下：“赶紧把彭石城的人全都弄走，最好在今天内。”

伊曼切斯特接过，不客气地当场打开看了。

随后，这位王城“新贵”笑了，商果然知道他最想要的是什么。

有了这一袋魔晶，他能做的事就更多。

而彭石城的人还不知道有人背着他们完成了一场肮脏的PY交易，等到贵族和官员们大多数选择前往黑森林城，绝大部分的普通城民都选择了前往新城碰运气时，他们还以为这都是出自他们个人想法的选择，却不知道他们的想法早就被人有意暗中引导。

之所以说是大多数和绝大部分，是因为也有一部分选择去了其他地方，还有少数人选择了留下。

比如那名谋划想要推出孙子当彭石城主继承人的老贵族，他和少数聪明人以及顽固派，坚信所谓的火山爆发和地震等都是王城想要逼他们离开彭石城的阴谋。

至于王城为什么想要接手一座空城？

那些人理所当然地想：空城才好安排人手，更也许彭石城下有他们不知道的秘密，而这个秘密必定牵连到极大的一笔财富。

说不定所谓的迁移就是黑水荒原新领主和王城那边做的一个交易，因为找不到人口，就直接转移一座城的人。

为了不给后来者让位，也为了找到这笔秘密的庞大财富。这些人自然不愿离开彭石城。他们甚至还嘲笑那些被忽悠走的权贵和富商们，认为他们都是大傻子。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 250: Inheriting the City Lord's Estate (Part 2)

As the newly minted heir of the City Lord's estate, A-Dai's very first decree was: "The public supplies belonging to Peng Shi City shall be handed over to the receiving parties willing to settle Peng Shi City's citizens, and this batch of supplies must be used exclusively for the displaced citizens of Peng Shi City."

Well, that put an end to that. The nobles and officials of Peng Shi City no longer had even the slightest possibility of embezzling the city's public supplies.

Manchester directly dispatched members of the Royal Cavalry Regiment to take over the city's public warehouses, audit the accounts, and place seals on everything.

Fortunately, Ebenezer had always cared deeply about Peng Shi City's public supplies—in his eyes, all of these things belonged to him, and anyone who dared to embezzle them was stealing from him, a crime punishable by death. Because of this, no one in charge of Peng Shi City's public supplies had ever dared to misappropriate a single coin, especially after Ebenezer descended into madness recently.

Consequently, this massive hoard of supplies remained completely intact, making the handover a relatively smooth process.

Officials specializing in refugee reception had also followed from Black Forest City, and they would receive a proportional share of the supplies based on the number of refugees heading toward Black Forest City.

With the public supplies placed under the guard of Manchester's forces, A-Dai didn't need to worry about them anymore—as long as people were willing to head to the new city in the Blackwater Wasteland, the resources there would naturally have a share going to his dad anyway. What was he rushing for?

What A-Dai *was* rushing for was taking possession of all the private assets of the City Lord's estate.

The Shi Sun family had ruled Peng Shi City for well over two hundred years, stretching all the way from the Great Prosperity Era down to the present day. Granted, during the chaotic Era of Great Wars, Peng Shi City had shrunk drastically, forcing the Shi Sun family into hiding, and during the subsequent Poison Fog Era, they had relied on formidable martial might and pure luck to protect their wealth.

Saying Peng Shi City was lucky was no exaggeration; during the Poison Fog Era, undead corpses had run rampant everywhere else, yet strangely, very few undead were ever seen lurking beneath the earth near Peng Shi City.

Until the day they lived, the people of Peng Shi City had no idea that hundreds of thousands of undead corpses lay slumbering in the earth just a short distance from their city.

After Ebenezer murdered Shi Sunyue and became City Lord, he naturally saw no need to transfer the family's wealth elsewhere, meaning the treasures of the City Lord's estate had been preserved in pristine condition.

A-Dai grabbed his Shang-ba, holding the asset inventories wrung from various confessions, and began checking off and claiming them one by one.

The steward had been utterly loyal to Ebenezer, and everyone in the City Lord's estate lived in terror of Ebenezer's ruthless methods, so no one had dared to steal from the estate. Of course, had Ebenezer's madness continued much longer, that might not have remained true.

The steward had originally intended to conceal a portion of the assets—who knew what he was plotting—but after cross-referencing with the confessions of Ebenezer's confidants, the small private treasury he had hidden and the emergency backup supplies Ebenezer kept for crisis situations were all brought to light.

Naturally, the steward received no reward whatsoever and was promptly disposed of by Manchester.

Shi Feifan and his son happily looted the accumulated wealth of generations within the City Lord's estate, stuffing it all into their spatial pouches.

Gold and currency, raw materials, medicinal herbs, food, fabrics and textiles, ancient artifacts and rare treasures...

Father and son couldn't help but marvel deeply at the Shi Sun family's talent for amassing wealth.

There were also mineral deposits, real estate, and commercial shops located in the royal capital and elsewhere that belonged entirely to the Shi Sun family.

These items couldn't be collected immediately, but A-Dai had secured the deeds and documentation, allowing him to claim them later on.

As the looting continued to its final stages, even A-Dai couldn't help but sigh in admiration: "Daddy, aren't I glad I used my brain for a second there?"

Shi Feifan chuckled, rubbing his square head: "Indeed, indeed! Otherwise, just look at what a massive fortune you would have missed out on."

A-Dai's eyes shone brightly: "Daddy, do you think I might have another scumbag dad in some other city? Or perhaps a scumbag grandfather?"

Shi Feifan: "..."

"Hahaha!" A hearty laugh echoed from behind them; it was Manchester who had tracked them down.

Upon finding the father and son, Manchester gave them a thumbs-up: "This son of yours is extraordinary! A true talent! He truly lives up to being your and Lang Mu's child."

Shi Feifan said proudly, "Obviously."

Manchester chuckled softly, shooting Shi Feifan a knowing look: "What about you and the priest?"

Ever since Shi Feifan had appeared, that palace priest had clearly tried to speak with him on several occasions, only to be completely ignored by Shi Feifan each time.

Holding his son with one hand, Shi Feifan waved his free hand dismissively: "Never mind him."

Making sure no one else was around, Manchester lowered his voice anyway: "Judging by what the priest hinted, it seems that the natural disaster here wasn't supposed to happen naturally at all."

"Mhm, his calculations aren't wrong. The natural disaster here is man-made, because A-Mu and I are going to concentrate all the magma from the entire Blackwater Wasteland right here." Shi Feifan's tone was as casual as someone talking about digging a small fish pond in their backyard.

Manchester: "...Need any help?"

He was a mage, after all; as long as he had magic crystals on hand, he could unleash formidable power.

Shi Feifan shook his head: "No need, we've already found craftsmen. Just trouble your side to organize the evacuation of the entire city."

Fearing that meddling blindly might disrupt Shi Feifan's arrangements, Manchester simply nodded and said, "Alright then. How many people do you want?"

That implied that if they wanted the entire population of the city, he could arrange for them to be sent over as well.

Shi Feifan shook his head once more: "The new city does need manpower, but what we need are people who can roll up their sleeves and work the moment they arrive. As for those nobles, wealthy merchants who only want to indulge and put on airs, and ambitious schemers looking to seize power in the new city—let them crawl as far away as possible."

Manchester understood, but he still wanted confirmation: "You really don't want those people with assets? As annoying as they are, they *can* help build the new city up rapidly."

Shi Feifan scoffed lightly: "If anyone genuinely wants to go to the new city, just ask them if they're worried that the new City Lord might want their supplies and labor, but not *them*."

Manchester got the message. Shi Feifan and his group weren't short on supplies; what they lacked were individuals willing to do honest, down-to-earth labor.

If those wealthy asset-holders tagged along, while it might accelerate the initial construction of the new city to a certain degree, those same people would also leverage their brought-in wealth to achieve rapid primitive accumulation, transforming into the new aristocracy of the new city.

And that was clearly not what Shi Feifan and Lang Mu wanted.

"Rest assured, aside from ordinary citizens, I guarantee that not a single noble or official incapable of honest labor will slip into the migrating population heading to the new city."

Having grown up surrounded by nobles, Manchester knew all too well what those people desired and what they feared the most.

Shi Feifan immediately produced a pouch, handed it over, and urged, "Get all the people out of Peng Shi City quickly, preferably within today."

Manchester took it and, without any false modesty, opened it on the spot to take a look.

A moment later, this "newly rising favorite" of the royal capital smiled. Shiye truly knew what he desired most.

With this pouch of magic crystals, there was much more he could accomplish.

Meanwhile, the people of Peng Shi City remained utterly oblivious that a dirty PY transaction had been completed behind their backs. By the time the nobles and officials mostly chose to head toward Black Forest City, and the vast majority of ordinary citizens chose to try their luck at the new city, they still believed these choices stemmed entirely from their own personal free will, completely unaware that their thoughts had long been subtly and intentionally guided from the shadows.

The reason it was described as "mostly" and "the vast majority" was because a small fraction of people chose to go elsewhere, while a tiny minority chose to stay behind.

For instance, that old noble who had schemed to push his grandson forward as the heir to Peng Shi City's lordship—he, along with a few other clever die-hards and stubborn traditionalists, firmly believed that the talk of volcanic eruptions and earthquakes was merely a conspiracy cooked up by the royal capital to force them out of Peng Shi City.

As for *why* the royal capital would want to take over an empty city?

Those people reasoned with absolute certainty: An empty city is much easier to repopulate and control; perhaps there was a secret buried beneath Peng Shi City that they knew nothing about, and that secret was bound to be tied to a colossal fortune.

Who knew? Perhaps this so-called evacuation was just a shady deal struck between the new lord of the Blackwater Wasteland and the royal capital, executed simply by relocating an entire city's population because they lacked the workforce.

Unwilling to yield their ground to latecomers, and driven by the desire to unearth this immense secret treasure, these people naturally refused to leave Peng Shi City. They even sneered at the gullible nobles and wealthy merchants who had been duped into leaving, considering them all complete fools.

chunks.chapterTitle: 第250章 继承城主府财产 (Part 3)
chunks.chineseText:
伊曼切斯特和祭司对这些人的选择似乎很无所谓，随便他们留下不留下。

这让那些留下的人心中生出一丝不安，但他们认定这就是王城对他们的忽悠，是想要断他们这些城中老牌贵族的根，还是坚持留在了城中。

商非凡对此也只能叹息：“儿砸，你觉得我们在火山爆发前打劫了他们如何？”

思想长了翅膀的阿呆用力点头：“可以！否则那么多物资等到火山爆发后就全都浪费了。”
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 250: Inheriting the City Lord's Estate (Part 3)

Manchester and the priest seemed entirely indifferent to these people's choices, letting them stay or go as they pleased.

This induced a trace of unease in the hearts of those who chose to stay, but convinced that this was merely a royal bluff meant to uproot the established old nobility of the city, they stubbornly dug in their heels and remained.
